reviews.comment: Very kind, responsive, and accommodating with late work. However, the workload felt excessive to the point of being impossible to manage, with multiple textbooks, quizzes, discussions, and projects feeling never-ending. The D2L layout was also disorganized, making it even harder to keep track of assignments and know what you need to complete.
Assignment directions are very unclelar. His class is very confusing.I dont reccomend.

Overall this class has way too many quizzes, discussions, and overall too much work for the class level. Not only is it too much work for the level but as an online class this is just too much information to grasp alone and in person would be better. Andrew is a very kind professor overall
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Was a very tough grader! Too much work for a level 200 class, and many text books that you do not even use. Very nice professor, and responds quickly to emails. Eagar to help students but still grades super hard.

The professor is honestly a great guy who wants you to succeed. Super nice person to talk to overall. He's very much old-school even if you take his class online. His assignments can be very tedious, and you are going to be writing a lot. As long as you just participate in class and put in actual effort in his class, it is an easy 4.0.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Too many assignments and pointless readings. Very passionate about the class but it's too much for the average student. Most of his grading comes from these video journals that have to be minutes long. Seems like a nice guy but his responses to the discussion boards are very critical. I would try to get out of this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I did bad on a lot of his quizzes because the questions and answers are highly subjective rather than factual. The final assignment is a 20 minute presentation or a 2000 word essay. This is not honors college. No hate to the teacher; I can tell he put a lot into making the class what it is, but we're undergrads, not experts in this field like him.

He seems like a nice guy who cares about his students. It is just an impressive amount of work for a general elective class that most people take to check off a box. Lots of readings and quizzes that are hard to understand wording, he is very critical with feedback as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His course is way too much work for a pointless elective class. Can be a smart aleck when leaving comments on your work and is very belittling.

I am sure he is a nice guy but for a basic IAH class I was taking as an elective it was an unnecessary amount of work. He also leaves comments on work that are very unsupportive and it seems like unless you put insane amounts of effort into this course you are doomed to fail.

There is a fairly heavy amount of workload and reading expected each week but he will grade most of your assignments based on effort, so if you do the reading and your work you will do fine. However, the reading quizzes are unnecessarily difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor McCullough was my favorite professor this semester, while it was a requirement for my degree I learned a lot of useful information I will use as an adult.  Yor are graded by effort, so all these people who gave him negative reviews probably didn't do all the reading outside of class....which is a lot but college is literally all reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tough grader, along with a tough final project and pointless readings.

Do not take his IAH 209 class unless you like reading pointless information that is very difficult to understand, enjoy getting feedback that makes your self-esteem tank into the ground, and love being graded like you are in medical school trying to become a doctor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This was my favorite class this semester. While you have a lot of reading, the assignments are easy. You can email at any hour of the day, and have a response in a short amount of time. Always willing to help, give feedback, and is super understanding. Due dates are not a suggestion, but there is wiggle room for them.
He is a d1 yapper. Also, the exams are more difficult than he leads them on to be. The exams ARE harder than the homework questions, despite what he says, but besides that, he's chill.

He does not allow his students to use calculators on his exams. If you know anything about economics, especially Macroeconomics, there are many calculations involved, and it seems unfair that you can't use a calculator on the exams when they have complex formulas. Other professors allow a caclulator so I suggest you take one of their courses.
Exams are tough, but Jeff is spectacular.

Professor Ackermann successfully (jokingly) catfished me into becoming an economics major. He actually made economics interesting and fun to learn, which in turn made me think the department was all like that. Boy was I wrong, almost every other Econ professor outside of him is monotone, boring, and old. I enjoyed Econ when I had him, now I don't.

I would say that this class is pretty doable as a freshman. He gives a lot of resources and I believe that the homework assignments (both completion and accuracy) and especially the study guides both give a lot of information to help when it comes to exams. This class demands a lot of effort though so make sure you're staying on track.

To succeed in this class I would review all my notes after the lecture and make my own sheet for each unit of all the really important concepts and definitions. I also constantly reviewed the homework's and practiced them as well as the practice problems and practice exams. If you study those a lot you will do good on the exams.

Very nice and funny guy. Really like his teaching and personality. In his class however, he didn't allow calculators or cheat sheets like every other professor. His 3.5 was also 4.0 in other classes. Despite him being a very good teacher, I'd rather have easier access to a 4. Recommendation is to choose a different one. Attendance is manditory.

Professor Ackerman is an incredible economics professor. If you pay attention in class, use the workbook, and actually study for the exams, you will have no problem succeeding. His comments in class are funny and do actually make sense if you are paying attention to the lecture.

Professor Ackerman was one of the BEST professors I have had at Michigan State. These comments saying this class is tough and he is a bad teacher, y'all do not know what college is. All of these comments saying this class was awful, you seriously have never taken an upper level class before.

do not skip the lectures or else you will know literally nothing. the exams are some of the hardest i've ever taken so stay on top of it. if you want a good grade you neeeedddd to do well on the tests.

Took this class online and had a great experience. The lectures are easy to understand and connect well to the homework. Provided practice problems/exams are extremely helpful and usually pop up on exams. One exam drops and the grading is more relaxed than most classes. As someone who has never taken econ I really enjoyed this class!
He is better than all the other econ professors, very difficult online and he is not very accessible. Grading is easier than most other classes.

Literally the funniest prof ever. Such an amazing guy and you can really tell that he cares abt the class and has passion for what he does. I was undecided before coming to college but after taking his class, made me want to pursue an econ degree. Funny lectures, 3 midterms and 1 final exam but only 3 exam grades count, really helpful study guides.

PROF. ACKERMAN'S CLASS WAS MY ABSOLUTE FAVORITE! I highly recommend taking his class if you are needing an Econ credit. He is super funny and his exams are respectable, considering the course criteria. The workload isn't heavy at all, and he truly wants to help students succeed.
test heavy (you get to drop one exam) so you have to do REALLY GOOD on at least one to get 4.0, this material and the horrible way he explains it gives me a headache every time I try and study

The exams are very difficult and the way Ackerman teaches the content is very difficult to understand. The exams are also a huge portion of the grade so if you do bad on them it will drop your grade significantly.

DO NOT take this class online. If you end up in it, get a good tutor to explain everything he doesn't. He gives workbook pages to follow along the videos with, which is nice, but they are vague. The actual exams are different from the practice ones, too. He also says to not reach out to him, which is strange to me, as he's literally the professor.

Its very hard to manage the workload while also trying to study and really understand the material. Ackerman is a nice guy! but the lecture topics aren't explained in a fully coherent way. It feels like every question on the exam has a double meaning and designed to trick you rather than test your knowledge.

He is one of my funniest professors, and is always energetic and excited to teach. However, you really need to do well on the exams to get a 4.0. Overall, fun guy to be around, and the class isn't terrible so long as you stay on top of things.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mr. Ackerman is great! He always has a positive attitude and presents his lectures in an engaging manner. He provides very helpful guided notes for lectures and great resources for studying, especially for exams. Overall, this course is difficult, but he makes the workload manageable and definitely looks out for the student's best interest.
For the online class its tests and homework for correctness. Thats it. If you're not a good test taker, then don't bother.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I just thought it was kind of stupid that we couldnt use calculators or aa note card on the exam but in my micro class we could. idk the math is divison with big nubers and multiplication, just saves so much time when you get to use a calculator, and there are many formulas to memorize.

Don't take this class online, as a matter of fact, don't take this class if you don't have to. Its hard to figure out what to study for the finals because instead of a practice exam, there are practice questions on every single unit, like I'm not going through all those questions just for only half of them to be on the exam.

Ackermann is great, he just explains everything in very specific ways. If you take him I highly recommend you go out of your way to learn concepts in YouTube or any other way that will help you in specific!

Ackerman is a decent guy and can be entertaining, but I would not recommend taking EC 202 ONLINE. He did not keep up with posting the lecture videos and often left you hanging. Homework would often have mistakes as well. The class itself is easy, regardless, but the professor isn't the best. I would recommend it in person or not with him.

I loved learning about economics in high school. Unfortunately, this professor has now ruined the subject for me. He somehow found a way to make it a mundane, boring chore. It is extremely lecture-heavy, and I felt he explained things in an unnecessarily complicated manner. Ackerman is extremely inaccessible as well.

Typical tenure prof- all heavy lifting is done by graduate students and he doesn't even want you to email him with a question. He will say you can, but if you do he doesn't answer the question and instead directs you to contact the TAs...also has history of changing certain course cutoffs AFTER the last exam to make his "teaching" seem effective

For the online class he isn't bad you just have to actually watch the lectures and use the workbook pages to follow along. He updated almost all of his lectures so they're no longer just recordings from covid like some people said. That said, if you're a bad test taker don't take this class because they're 60% of your grade.

i took EC 201 with him asynchronously and got a 2.0, but i took EC 202 with him in person the following semester and got a 4.0. it'll suck going to class three days a week but if you want to succeed in his class i'd recommend the in person layout. his asynchronous course videos put me to sleep every night but his in person lectures kept me awake.

If youre someone that learns by teaching themselves the material you should be okay but he goes off on tangents a lot and uses lecture vids from 2020 that are to focus bc he talks so much about other things. If you can take an in person i would recommend it over this course!

Before you read. No I'm not going on a tangent because I was lazy or didn't pay attention bc I passed this class with flying colors . .However you can tell this class was structured heavily by graduate students. Insane amount of typos on the homework, lazy test questions, asynchronous students left with no chance of ec, poorly made packets.

Professor Ackermann is hands-down, the funniest professor I've ever had. My top highlight was when he asked an open-ended negative externality question on the worst thing your roommate has ever done. After submitting my response, my roommate chased me out of class which ultimately resulted in me finally being able to switch roommates.

super funny guy. enjoyed this class a lot, was a bit harder for me than my other classes and I would find myself confusing Micro and Macro a lot. Exams were simple if practice tests were done and you went to class. Final was at 8pm on a Thursday though, so that was a little irritating but great class altogether.

I took the class online asynchronous. It was fine all of the lectures are prerecorded from 2020/2021. Homework is pretty easy and the exams are fine too. Make sure you keep up everything because once you fall behind it's pretty hard to catch back up because every week there are 1 or 2 new units being taught.
This class was SUPER hard to me and prof ackerman lowkey taught things very confusing. I was online so maybe the in person was different.
In general, Ackermann is well-liked by most students. If you pay attention in class, complete all your assignments, and practice regularly, you'll be all set.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not hard at all just watch the video lectures and do the practice problems and the exams will be extremely easy as a lot of the questions are reused from the practice problems. Ackerman is a silly little guy also lots of lols to be had
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Emailed him instead of the TA because it was an urgent question and the TA can take a bit to reply. Instead of simply answering my question, he proceeded to type out a paragraph of why I should be going to the TA instead of him and did not answer my question at all. I think that's pretty petty. Also makes unfair changes to course cutoffs at the end

Do NOT take Econ with Ackerman, he was by far the worst professor I have had. He only grades by tests and homework, so not much room to improve grades, and they're both super difficult. I tried getting help from him outside of class and he told me to find friends in the class then, but it's an online class... Avoid this professor if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class online, but the lectures were very engaging where you really actually understand the material. Exams are locked down browser but if you study the practice problems it will be easy. He is a very nice professor!

Ackermann is a very funny and passionate professor. There is a textbook but you don't actually need it for the class at all so don't bother buying it. Attendance isn't mandatory either but the material can get confusing if you miss because he does to many examples in class.

worst lectures ever. so boring and dont help with the homework. quizzes are confusing and exams are hard. he is really bad at explaining things and preparing you. too many concepts he doesnt go in depth and just reads slides. don't recommend, but couldve just been that class was hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, he offers a dropped exam and there's very little work for this class. The lectures are actually enjoyable to watch too and he does a great job at explaining topics that aren't initially straightforward. Just a really nice guy overall.

Definitely don't recommend his class. Unfortunately he's the only EC 202 prof which is why I got stuck with him. His tests are very hard and there is lots of homework worksheets. Your only graded on those two things and the tests are heavily weighted. So if you do bad on the tests your grades gonna be low.

I took this course online and I shouldn't have. Powerpoints are confusing and super long. Homework is really easy, but doesn't prepare you for tests. Tests are only 30 questions and so hard. I don't think I would've passed any tests even if I had help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this course online and thought it would be easier than in person. I was wrong. The homework assignments are not that bad but the lectures are longer than an in person class. The exam questions are worded weirdly and not easy to understand. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. You are better off taking Econ 201 or Econ 202 at LCC for less money and better

Prof Ackerman was a pretty fair professor. He explained things clearly and stopped to answer questions when needed. He made lectures very interesting and really tried to connect with students individually. My main concern was with exams. Since there were only 30 questions per exam, there wasn't much room to make mistakes.

May be a friendly and fun professor but I find him to be quite an unprofessional and rude person. He has continuously been extremely uncommunicative and unsupportive on email and he seems to care more about following what is exactly in the syllabus then hearing what you have to say and at a min, recognizing it. DO NOT TAKE if comm matters to you.
Very funny, fun class, lectures were kept interesting through use of real life examples and his humor. Top 3 professors I've ever had.

You can tell that he genuinely loves teaching and tries to build a bond between him and his students. 60% of your grade is 4 exams (one dropped). He writes his own exams so you'll find that he often reuses the same questions he assigns homework give or take a few different numbers. He has helpful online lectures if you do miss class. I recommend.

Very entertaining professor. He used TopHat to incentivize coming to class (it's a small part of the grade). 70% of our grade was midterm and final, so be sure to understand the material -it's easy to stuff don't sweat it cause you will get practice with the problem sets and non-graded exam practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor that had light homework and easy to follow lectures. You need to show up to do well, if you do this class is extremely easy. Ackerman was enthusiastic about his material and wanted people to succeed, those who did poorly were those who did not attend lectures.

Lowkey don't take this class in person or online. He is not that funny. To be completely honest he doesn't explain things. Most of the students that I've taken this class have said that their exam scores did not reflect their actual knowledge in the class which is very concerning.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but his teaching is so bad. Most of the time he just reads off his PowerPoints word for word and doesn't explain. Homework assignments are graded by completion. Exams are heavily graded on and are way off from what the homework is.The study guides never match the exams.

Good guy. Can tell he really cares. Course is not that difficult you just have to be on top of things and you will succeed. It is very easy to get behind so if you procrastinate you should take the in-person version of the class.

I took the online version of this class and all the homework was due the day before tests. The homework is through an online program that recycles the same questions over and over again so they're easy to memorize the answers for. However, the homework is no help for the exams and if you want to do well you HAVE to do the practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: These other reviews must have cakewalk classes bc this was neither hard or easy. Textbook isn't required but you can find it online for free. Attendance isn't REQUIRED but you're still graded on it. 1 of 3 exams is dropped. It's not supposed to be easy. I showed up 50-75% of time and got a 3.5... A 4.0 IS ONLY 89+ do the practice problems and hw
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The asynchronous class for this was strictly video lectures and McGraw-Hill homework. Exams were most of the grades. Exams were also on lockdown browser.

This class is absolutely horrible. The tests combined are worth 75% of your grade. The exams, which he writes himself, are the hardest things. He says to look over the practice problems he provides you to study with, except they are so easy and the test questions are nothing like it. He is a nice guy, but I do not recommend his class.

The only downside of this course is that exams are worth 70% of your grade. Prof Ackerman is great, but there is a lot of material covered on each exam. As long as you pay attention during class and do all of the practice problems before the exams you'll be fine. I found this class very interesting as a non-econ major, and would recommend it.

All he gave us for lectures were his old recorded lectures from 2020. The homework assignments took hours to do and hardly had anything to do with the lectures. The exams make up 75% of your grade, were very difficult, and were not given enough time to complete.

Econ is not my major so take everything I say with a grain of salt. I thought that he cared about students, was pretty funny when it came to the overall class period, but there is not much to base your grade off. There were the exams and the homework's that were essentially quizzes, nothing else really determines your grade besides the exam.

Really hard to succeed in this class, not much accommodations made. Exams make up the majority of your grade. SO much material and really hard to understand. The concepts are applied to one example an then your supposed to just understand it. I struggled in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: you either love or hate Jeffery Ackerman, he does a great job of keeping students engaged by trying to be relatable or funny but it gets In the way of his teaching. I could tell you more about his kids and his love for Fortnite and Panera charged lemonade than I could tell you about what I learned in this class.
took online, lockdown browser and the lectures are so monotone it is hard to listen to. homework is easy but has almost no relevance to the exams.

The curriculum isn't necessarily easy, however, there are lots of resources that will help you succeed so long as you put the work in. The Econ help room, reading all of the chapters covered, watching lectures from his summer course, and doing as many practice problems as possible essentially ensures a 4.0. Ackermann is a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ackerman relied on lockdown browser and webcam for all exams, and they had mandatory time slots in which they would be taken. We took 2 exams and each exam had 7 or 8 chapters of content that were on it. His lectures posted on d2l could range from 10 minutes to over an hour. And you would have to watch 1-2 videos for each chapter.

Horrible. His lectures are boring and full of random facts about his family or pop culture references. Attendance is mandatory. Exams are so difficult, you will not pass if you don't do a significant amount of preparation. Cracked out on charged lemonade. Some say he's nice/ funny, I personally would never step foot into his lecture hall again.
funny guy, exams are difficult without studying & practice, uses iclicker for attendance, homework assignments were long but helpful to learn material, easy-ish class if you're determined enough

-lets you drop an exam and four homework assignments
-funny
-study and you will be fine
-not boring
-best econ prof

Horrible HW. For our class we had online homework through SIMnet. It was awful, the assignment would loop the same questions over and over, most assignments had around 300 questions, being the same 20 questions looped. A weeks worth of homework would take anywhere between 1-5 hours of completing the same 15 questions over and over again

Professor Ackermann is very mid at best. He tries to keep lectures relevant and up to date but the actual content is not very helpful for the class. I took him for EC 202 and exams are a huge part of the grade and very hard. Be prepared to spend countless hours doing online homework that is barely relevant to the actual class.

Funny dude, horrible professor. Lectures make no sense and just uses graphs that he only understands. Exam questions are near impossible and have nothing to do with anything we learn. The class did horrible, there is not much homework and he is a nice, laid back guy but if you truly want a good grade avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ackerman is a great professor! It's a hard class but he conveys the information well and gives lots of practice problems to help you do well. It is lecture heavy, but he uses lots of examples that make it easier to understand.
He's fine. Not the worst but not the best.

Provides lecture playlist that covers the same material as classes, so attending is optional. Online homework textbook is a mess but it is easy to get full points and he gives a few homework drops. Exam content comes from lectures, not the textbook.

This is one of the worst classes I’ve ever taken. The exam questions are nothing you can prepare for and his lectures don’t teach you anything. I showed up to class everyday, did my homework, took notes, studied and still did horrible along with other people. I’m not one to fail classes but this may be my first.
Lectures made graded material easy. I recommend the work book and really thinking about and doing the work he offers. it makes the exams much easier.

VERY DIFFICULT EXAMS that are monitored and not open note. He is so boring! The class did really bad. Do not take him. He doesnt care about the students. His lectures are too long and he doesnt clean them up when he messes up. Expect bad grades.

Jeff is the man. He makes econ as best as it could be. The course has a decent amount of homework which is much harder than the exams, so they are good preparation if you actually do them. The lectures are great, and Jeff makes an effort to know you. The lectures are perfectly paced, as he will wait a little bit after each slide for typing.

This guy is the man. One of my favorite professors at MSU. I struggle deeply with math and, by extension, Economics and Ackerman made it pretty accessible and understandable to me. He is an easy grader but is still effective in getting his material across. Plus he is a genuinely enjoyable person with a good sense of humor.

Not the best communicator. A lot of people did not finish a group of 4 assignments and he refused to give credit back partially because of the system he uses, and partially because he thinks he's not in the wrong.

Very very lecture heavy, most of the grades come from tests. Didn't offer any extra-credit opportunities, doesn't curve grades. He's pretty nice and fun during lectures, talks about his experiences, and shares any stories he has. However, he isn't that interested in getting to know students (probably because it's a super big class).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Such an awesome professor! He teaches material in a very easy to understand manner and has immaculate online lectures. He makes the class stress free by relating to his students and giving life advice. I learned a ton about econ.

I'm not even an econ major and I took a second econ class so I could have this dude as prof again. The homework is super easy and it teaches you everything you need for the test so you really don't have to study much more. Jeff knows his memes and got a victory royale over the summer so he's a man of many talents.

Professor Ackerman is a really nice and accommodating instructor. His class isn't bad as long as you do the practice questions and look over Top Hat questions before the exam. People who do not take tests very well might struggle a little more. The homework is relatively easy as long as you give it some effort.

Ackerman is caring and quirky! Great human being. One of the things I wish I did more of during the semester would be to go to his office hours and dedicate more time to studying. I will say if you are NOT a good test taker like myself, you might not want to take his class. Your results from your exams and test will be your entire overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Ackerman is a great guy- very nice and approachable. 75% of your grade in this class is made up of two exams. There are three total exams but he lets you drop one. The exams are very difficult. Overall, it is easy to earn points outside of the exams with the homework and in-class tophat questions, but it doesn't make up a huge part of your grade.

Spends a lot of time during lectures talking about his personal life. Also uses way to many examples to explain concepts, and often we fall behind. He also gets stumped easily by questions in class which makes me think he isn't very knowledgeable about the material.
She's a great professor, and this is an easy elective course to take in order to get some credits in without it being too time consuming.

I could say the class is easy, or I could say that the material was explained so well and so well understood that the class seemed easy. Isn't that the goal as a good teacher to ensure students are learning all the material? Mission accomplished.

Clearly passionate about her lectures and it shows, they were all super easy to follow and interesting. The 2 Homework assignments are fun and don't take much time. In class participation assignments create interesting discussions, and students go to the MSU bug house at the end of the semester!

I adored Professor Lorenz! She was incredibly gracious with RCPD extensions, and provided stress-free assignments. Every quiz and test was open resource, with plenty of time to complete the task. Lectures were engaging and interesting. She felicitated a calming learning environment while also sharing her passions. I cannot recommend enough!

LOVEDDD Dr. Lorenz! She is very sweet and funny. This is an online class held over zoom so you'll have daily in class participation and pre-class readings, 3 home work, and 4 exams (all of which are open note). Genuinely enjoyed this class as her lectures are interesting and you can tell she is passionate about her work. Could not recommend enough!

The class is good, it is pretty easy and she is clear on student expectations. Dr. Lorenz is kind and very passionate about what she teaches. The only thing I struggled with is the way she talked about politics and was pretty divisive

Prof Lorenz is super friendly and clearly loves teaching her class. All you have is 3 exams which are open note, 2 homework assignments, 3 question preclass quizzes, and in class participation. She teaches well so all the information is easy to understand and you visit the bug house at the end of the semester. 10/10 prof

Super fun and interesting class. Next to no homework, and what we had was super easy. Exams were open note. Lectures were collaborative and not just her speaking to us. Very good professor, really fun class. Would definitely recommend taking this class.

Dr. Lorenz has a clear system of operation for her class, but it is easy, fun, and engaging! She has a lot of love for the material she teaches and it shows. Her lectures are very clear and informative and the in-class participation that she requires is good review of topics discussed. Pay attention in lecture and you will do well :)
This class made me enjoy exploring the outdoors once again and I had so much fun admiring all the bugs she brought to class to shows us. 10/10 Professor
Amazing professor. Very obviously passionate about her work and the subject being taught and will always answer questions if asked.
Dr. Lorenz is a great professor. This class was an easy A, just attend the zoom meetings and do the participation. Slightly boring but you can tell Dr. Lorenz is very passionate about what she does.

Awesome prof and person. Super kind and receptive to questions. You can tell she's very passionate about entomology and that directly translates into her teachings. I wish grades were updated more frequently, but besides that, she's amazing.
Dr. Lorenz is a very kind professor and cares for her students. She let us take our exams at any time of the day and only had two homework assignments. She gives many points for attendance.

I have struggled in every high school science class I have ever taken and this teacher truly turned that around for me! She breaksdown concepts Into digestible material. if you really care about how you do, so will she. If you put in the work, you will do great. Definitely an easier science for those of you who are not chemists. Sweetest professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Seriously one of the best teachers I had. For being an online class, this teacher truly cares so much about her students. She is responsive on email an always accessible out of class. Science is not a strong subject of mine and I was nervous to take this class. I can seriously say I have learned so much and enjoyed it all because of this teacher!
I learned a lot of things about bugs in Dr. Lorenz's class both interesting and things that will be useful to know for my future career! The bug house visit was especially enjoyable!

Dr. Lorenz was great!! Her lectures are easy to follow, assignments are few and far between, and exams are short, usually multiple choice, and open note. You can tell she is very passionate about what she teaches, and is genuinely excited each day to teach her students. Would 100% take a class of hers again.

Before every class there is a reading quiz that is 3 questions based on a short article you have to read. In class there are in-class participation questions you have to answer in zoom chat. Every class is worth 5 points, and you get 3 drops, exams are online and open note, you have the entire day to complete it. Take this class for ISB requirement

Dr. Lorenz was by far one of the best professors I've had a Michigan State. She is very personable and her lectures are entertaining and engaging. Her passion about the material really shows and makes lectures really fun.

great professor. i took this biology course as an easy A, and i got that easy A. she's very laid back and relaxed and her teaching style reflects that as well. the material and the course is easy, and she's very caring and understanding. ellie was also a wonderful guest to see from time to time.

Great professor and cares about students doing well. You can trust that she has the best interest for everyone and the class is pretty easy. Weekly reading assignments that take less than 5 minutes, and a few exams that are online.

Amanda was so sweet and I loved listening to other lectures. Super short quiz with articles before each class, 2 homework assignments, and open note tests throughout the semester. My favorite part of the lectures was getting to see her dog Ellie. If you have the chance to take a class with Amanda, do it!

She is a great professor and I loved her lectures. The course is very easy and simple, but I still learned a lot. My only complaint is I do think she's a bit hard to reach which can be quite annoying as it was an async class. Though, nothing that was make or break with my grade.

Sooo nice and caring, clearly loves her students/teaching/this class, super fun lectures. Much of the class is completion/participation based, and the tests are very easy. The 2 major homework assignments are fun or at least not difficult. At the end of the semester you get to visit the MSU bug house during class hours which is so much fun.

Very lenient and caring, she asked what topics were difficult before the final exam and adjusted the exam accordingly. There's like 2 homework assignments, open-note tests, and participation grades. Took it online and she showed lots of enthusiasm for the material!
This class was interesting and would be hard to fail. Prof. Lorenz is awesome, funny, and a compelling lecturer. Visit the bug house!

She never answers emails. Like hellooo what's ur job. she takes forever to grade. not mean or difficult but she annoying for never answering my emails or anyone elses. like your not the president of the united states. andwer emails
Very good lectures, not much homework but the homework that you do have is honestly pretty interesting.

Prof Lorenz is the sweetest! She teaches clearly and answers any and all questions. She loves to discuss with students, and keeps lecture interesting. Attendance is needed because a lot of your grade is in class participation. There are extra credit opportunities, but you might not even need them! This class is fun and easy to pass.
Absolute gem, and her dog is adorable. Class is an easy A.

I loved her!! This class was somewhat interesting because she is so much fun and wants everyone to learn. She makes every class fun and she is also so funny so that makes it more fun. There are 3 exams which include the final. There are 2 homework assignments and before every class, you have to do an easy reading quiz. Super easy and she is so nice
Exams were easy and open note, Lorenz is a good lecturer and I never had a problem hearing back from her.
Class is extremely easy and she's lenient with her grading on the homework's. Class should be an easy 4.0

Took this class online for Fall 2021, one of the easiest class I had so far, there are 3 unit exams and 1 cumulative final exam in which are all open book test with multiple choice questions; theres one or two assignments, the assignments are easy to complete, took me about 20 minutes. Dont really require much memorization, just general concept.

She is a very good professor and easy grader. I had technical difficulties and emailed her and let me turn in the assignment late without grade deductions. Highly recommend taking her for ENT205 for the bioscience credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Lorenz is truly the most caring professor I have ever had! She truly cares about her students and their success. Very easy class- easy 4.0. Exams were open note/open resource. She is very willing to help students outside of class. Would take her class again!
I don't even really rate professors but she was so good I wanted to go on here and give a good rating :) Really easy class as long as you participate
Assignments are easy (at least online they are). Professor is so nice and understanding.

Lorenz is an amazing professor. Had her for ent205 and the class was very easy and I learned a lot. Never thought I would be interested in bugs but she makes it interesting and fun to learn. Most of the grade is determined on in class participation, so if you show up you're in good shape. She's very well educated and kind.

She is very caring and demonstrates her enthusiasm during her lectures. Combines videos along with her powerpoints to make the lecture more fun. Exams are easy as long as you study. She does not try to trick you on the exams they are quite simple. Easy 4.0 as long as you do the work.

Easiest ISB 201 class if you are willing to show up to class. She does in class papers for attendance (so easy you barely have to pay attention) basically your entire grade is attendance, a few 1 page papers & exams. The exams are very very easy. Super kind prof! Highly recommend her but dont get stuck in the 8:30am you wont make it.

reviews.comment: Dr. A is one of the most respectful and reasonable professors I've had. She makes the material very interesting and fun to learn about. I will say that she does ask the class questions about the films and asks you to discuss with peers, but overall this class was great!

I loved the class and the professor! It's pretty easy, and homework is usually small writing assignments. She counts attendance, but is understanding if you need to miss class and will email you questions to still get points. Overall, she is so nice, really cares about her students, and wants them to do well! I highly recommend her and this class!

Great Professor!! Loved the class, and it was fairly easy. There is a lot of group discussion and one group project. Attendance was mandatory but you're allowed 2 skips. 5 pop quizzes throughout the semester on the course material. I would recommend this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: This was an extremely easy class. The lectures are easy and are mainly just watching videos and then discussing them within a group. She cares about all her students and gives them multiple chances to make up assignments!! If you need an IAH TAKE THIS CLASS.
She is a great professor, Easy A and cares about her students. Overall I would take her again.

this class is so dumb 
easy A but so boring and a lot of writing and reading 
the professor is nice tho and accepts late work and gives extensions
Easy A and worth the while

I took this professor last semester for IAH 207, and now I'm in her IAH 231 course. She is an AMAZING professor. She explains everything so clearly and she is lenient with her students. She cares about them, respects them, listens to them. She deserves a RAISE. I absolutely adore going to her class. I've never skipped any of her lectures.

She is a great professor! Most of the class is discussion based so you have to talk to people around you and then share with the class. There are typically weekly assignments, but it is a fairly low workload.

Alena was very nice and you could tell she cares about this class! I enjoyed the content but the class but too long imo. Lots of participation, group work, and talking with the person next to you so get ready for that. I often felt bad because not a lot of people would participate during class. But super easy class and assignments, highly recommend

Alena was an amazing professor and I was actually looking forward to possibly taking future courses with her. Be prepared that her lectures are group discussion heavy and lots of turn-and-talk. Overall she was very understanding and such an easy course!

Prof Aniskiewicz was great! I had awful groups for projects in this class but she was very responsive and helpful with dealing with them. In all, this class was super easy and she is not a harsh grader at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was for IAH 231A. This professor clearly knows her stuff and has a passion for the topics covered. I'm a STEM student and was only taking this class as a requirement, but I wish there were professors in my major that cared as much as she did. All writings are gradely very easy and it was nice to interact with people in the class.

Alena was an amazing professor. For this class, you watch 12 different films each week and only write responses on 8 of them. There are five random pop-up quizzes. We also had three reflections and three group discussions. She wants her students to succeed and is very understanding and helpful when it comes to questions. It is also IAH 231A.

Dr. A was very kind, and always there to help. She was on top of questions and emails she would receive. The class was very writing and reading heavy. Attendance was not mandatory, but she would take attendance everyday. I was not a fan of the class personally, but it is a simple IAH to take.

IAH231A** 
Professor Aniskiewics is very sweet and respectful. This was her first time teaching the class, so we were kind of test guinea pigs, but she tried to make it enjoyable for everyone!

reviews.comment: She's so clearly in love with her subject and it really rubs off on her lectures. Super sweet and incredibly helpful. Will write well-thought out, prompt feedback for assignments. reviews.comment: I only decided to take this because it was hybrid, 100-level class, and it's a CAS requirement. I read the reviews on here and thought, "Surely it can't be that bad". Trust me, it is that bad. She really needs to be reevaluated because this class is ridiculous. Be aware that if you miss a single thing on an assignment its an automatic 0.
Really bad class.

I really liked Professor Allen. She has a wonderful personality and seems to care about student's well-being. She also cares about the deeper meaning behind what she teaches. Class work is a lot, but if you set some time aside to do the work, read instructions, and ask questions, this class is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She treats students like children and does not care about them, uses jingles to get their attention and does pointless exercises that actually stifle creativity. She tries to be all sunshine and roses but you can tell she doesn't want to be there because she is treating it like free association. One of the worst classes I have ever been in.

Probably one of the most lackluster classes I have ever taken. I have no idea how this syllabus has been approved. It is all over the place and the professor talks about being progressive but does not offer accommodations if you experience an emergency. Truly performative in the lectures and in practice.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. The hw is not difficult, but it is EXTREMELY time consuming. It's only 2 hours, but it somehow manages to feel like the longest 2 hours of your life. The students are often treated like children; with name tags and jinglebells to get our attention. If I can save one poor soul from this class, then my mission is complete.
JeanaDee Allen means well, but for a level 100 class I do more work in some of my 300/400 combine. If at all take another CAS class.

reviews.comment: Professor Allen is awesome. The assignments may take a long time, but she is incredibly understanding and wants the best for her students. I highly recommend taking this class and the lectures are always worth going to. Professor Allen gives out a ton of extra credit, but you will get an easy 4.0 in this class.
lot's of workload and she played ecco2k in class

This professor was professional and responsive, making the online asynchronous CAS 110 class engaging. The course included quizzes, activities, and assignments, but for a 100-level class, the workload felt time-consuming. Graded on a 1000-point scale for a 4.0, the class was fun, useful, and covered a unique topic that changes every semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This asynchronous course featured creative assignments, weekly quizzes, and a midterm interview that emphasized experiential learning. The professor was fantastic—always approachable and ready to help with questions, providing great support. Perfect for students seeking a well-structured course that fosters creativity and critical thinking!

reviews.comment: allen is a nice lady but eccentric and IMO annoying. she does genuinely care though. this class is an introvert's worst nightmare; when u meet, u are forced to talk to everyone in the class. work is fairly easy and the assignments can actually be fun. no tests or reading. light work. only complaint is that her grading seems very random

A great professor and I enjoyed the class. There are a few homework assignments but nothing hard to complete. My class was hybrid so the times we met once a month in class were important because it's a big part of grading. Overall, it was a good class and easy to complete.

Alex is a nice person, but she is very political. I took her for International Education and I learned more about her political opinions than any curriculum. I do not think I actually learned anything from the syllabus in her class. It is very skewed towards one end of the political spectrum, and she is not open to other ideas in her class.

Alex was an amazing instructor who clearly cared about her students and the material she taught. She kept the class engaged and knew how to pull us back in when attention drifted. The freedom she gave us in assignments was deeply appreciated by my peers and me. If you have the opportunity to take a class with her, take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Alex was a great professor, and I really enjoyed her class. She was so caring and respectful of everyone in class and what they thought. She was very understanding about late work and gave great feedback. All the content assigned felt necessary and meaningful to the course. Participation and group work were highly encouraged in every class session.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Alex cares very much what her students think. She works hard to make sure everyone understands the homework, but she also expects you to bring your perspective into the discussion.

I took Alex's TE 353 class, and she was awesome! Super interesting lectures and in-depth discussions. She clearly is very knowledgable and passionate about our material and is so caring for us and our needs. Classes were dynamic and so fun to attend every time, plus she brought food every week. I loved this class and would love to have Alex again!!

The contents we learned about are very interesting, and even though I don't like reading, the articles and books assigned are some of the best. Alex was very considerate of us and was always making sure to give us extra credit options and grade in a timely matter. Along with that, she's just funny and loving; definitely my favorite prof so far!
Alex was an amazing professor! She was very understanding and I enjoyed her teaching style!

Alex is one of the kindest people I've met. She is great and takes the needs of students into great consideration. She deeply cares about people, and this class makes you actually reflect on some tough topics. I could not recommend Alex enough.

Professor Allweiss is an amazing professor. I loved going to her class because everything she taught made me think. She was super understanding and I cannot stress how kind and caring she is. I actually learned in her class and enjoyed all our discussions in class. If I could have her as a professor for all my classes, I would.

Alex is amazing. Easily one of the best professors at MSU. She takes class feedback and directly implements it into our work for the week. She cares about us and caters the work we do to the overall mood of the class. She teaches tough topics, but always makes sure we have a great understanding of them. Highly recommend this class!

Alex is amazing! . Her class is easy to follow along with. All the work is apart of the class besides some outside activities. She is very supportive of her students needs especially when they are going through a hard time. She wants all of her students to succeed and is willing to help students out when they need it. HIGHLY RECOMMEND HER.

Alex is a perfect example as to how every professor should teach during a pandemic. She is kind, understanding, considerate, etc. Everything that she assigns is essential to your learning and is very easy on grading. She is super passionate about what she teaches and is the most organized professor I've ever met. Highly recommend taking her classes

He is super nice and caring. His class is so boring, and exams are difficult. No final, but the unit exams cover so much content that it is difficult. His grading is weird in D2L, and it's hard to calculate your final grade. He is a good teacher, but be prepared to hate your life on exam days.

Course uses R-studio which is the coding portion. For exams, his coding portion will be taken at the same time frame. Other STT 231 professors allow you to take home the coding portion. He is super nice and gentle, but overall a boring professor. His lectures can be confusing due to the accent but he does offer some extra credit points.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIM! Actually so boring, horrible, hard to understand. In person R studio exam unlike every other STT 231 professor. I've heard take Horr, from everything I hear the class is nothing like Zeleke's was. He was really sweet just shouldn't be teaching.

Dr. Zeleke is a super caring professor who will do what he can to help you succeed. Although attendance isn't mandatory, it's vital to attend lectures as he works on a chalkboard & doesn't post his notes/lectures online. He offers lots of practice problems & extra credit, & his exams are fairly similar to the practice offered. I highly recommend!

Dr. Zeleke is an incredibly kind and enthusiastic professor. However, in my opinion he is not the best teacher and studying for exams can be increasingly difficult and stressful. There is lots of homework too. There are many opportunities for extra credit too. My advice: Go to every class you can, do the homework, and go to office hours.

I enjoyed this class especially trying to refine my statistics skills. I took a stats class in the summer at OCC and I found that some stuff was the same, but the formulas were slightly different. In this class, I would personally say that I struggled with the R-studio part because I would always get error message when I was typing in command.

He seems like a nice guy, but I could not grasp this class well. I am a good student and I enjoy math but he made a lot of the concepts quite confusing. There is extra credit, but doesn't help your grade a ton. His lectures are boring, I was warned of this prof and was told not to take him. I thought I would be fine but I was wrong.

I like Professor Zeleke as a person, but lectures can be kind of boring. There are peer writing assignments which aren't fun if you have a bad group, but they aren't hard. 3 lecture attendances, 1 recitation, 1 PW, and 1 HW are dropped at the end of the semester. 3 tests which aren't too hard-- the final isn't cumulative, and there's lots of EC.

Zeleke is a nice guy, but he just can't really grasp teaching very well. He is quite confusing in lectures. Catch him quite a bit seeming like even he doesn't know what he's talking about. You have so much hw in this class, individual and group hw. The individual hw usually lengths within the 30's for questions. Gives out a lot of extra credit.
Professor Zeleke followed a course-pack and shared many resources to help students succeed in his class.

Professor Zeleke is such a kind man but he cannot teach well during lectures. Asking him questions about homework may lead to more confusion. The homework is difficult and there are so many questions. Moreover, no feedback is provided for homework. Coding section is not hard. Extra credit is provided, so make sure to do all of them when possible.

Very nice professor but his class was awful. Struggled to reach a 3.0 while other students in other professors recieve over 100% on their tests. This class ruined my 4.0 gpa. Do not listen to the reviews saying he is a good professor. I don't know a single person in this class who wasn't struggling.

This Professor is very articulate on most concepts in Calc III. He is very accessible for office hours and study groups outside of class. Exams are very similar to material learned so if you give effort you will do very well. Very interesting class and very simple for those who are interested in the course.

I loved Dr. Zeleke. I am historically terrible at stats, but he got me through this course with a 4.0. He can be difficult to understand, but he wants you to do well and will always try his best to help. Great teacher, do the homework/practice problems/mock exams and you will do well. Attendance is mandatory but he is understanding. Very kind prof.

Professor Zeleke was a ver kind professor. He truly wants his students to do well. I, however, am not very math brained and some of the harder concepts were not explained well leaving me to have to re-teach myself. I ended up pulling a 3.5, but if you understand stats it would be an easy 4.0. homework every week and group essays every other week.

Zeleke is a dawg. By far the best class of my semester. Attendance is mandatory, but class gets done early, and participation isn't normally necessary. There is a "mandatory" textbook, but he provides the same information during class time or alternatively on D2L.

Okay (normal) lectures, but very nice guy & knowledgeable. Always happy to help outside of class, has a good attitude, flexible, offers extra credit. Do the homework, look at the mock exams (just like the real exams). Easiest 4.0 of my life. Excellent mentor for UURAF/Honors Opt if you're a more motivated student. Wants you to do well!

Dr. Zeleke is one the best professor at MSU. I had him last fall for my calculus I and he is always helpful with my questions. His office hours was one of the best thing. Moreover, he is a linear grader with lots of extra credit. Just practice the homework and sample exam paper to get a straight A in the Final.
He is an awesome professor! This isnt high school anymore. You gotta keep up and be responsible for yourself!

Nice guy, talks slow, really goes through material thoroughly & office hours were helpful. But tests were nearly impossible and he teaches calc like you took AP calc already & even those kids had a hard time. for example he taught us 2nd derivative test, but asked us to do 4th derivative on exam? had lots of extra credit but take a different prof
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: tests are kind of challenging he puts true and false questions that are conceptual not a fan, but he gives extra credit on each test and the homework isn't much and it is easy

Class is very very challenging because everything is multiple choice even though stats is very up to interpretation. As a professor, he does a really great job and is very caring. He makes him self available to help and wants all of his students to succeed.

reviews.comment: Test are incredibly hard.
