reviews.comment: He's amazingly clear and willing to go out of his way to help you as long as you show that you are willing to put in the effort.
I LOVEEEEEE HIM AS A PROFESSOR!
Harsh accent, horrible lecture

The class is taught as if the student took AP Calculus in high school, so it was pretty challenging. He was really helpful if you took advantage of his office hours. Meeting one-on-one made things make a lot more sense.
Good professor, for stats. does a decent job of explaining the material that is pretty easy to begin with.
He teaches his calculus class like you took AP Calc in high school. Doesn't explain anything. Had to retake the class with a different professor the next semester.
Very nice and helpful. He really explains everything well and you never feel rushed.
I am a math major and thought his class was definitely good. My friends who were not math majors like him as a prof but have trouble understanding the material.
Tests are tricky, loved calculus before I had him for calc III.
I felt that he thought we all knew everything already so he expected us all to do fine when we gave him blank looks. Not a very good class.

PLB106 was a very intensive class. Every class, you were tasked with a lot of busy work. You don't really take much away from the class. There is also a group project that lasts the entire semester, and you'd better hope you get a good group. Although the class sucks, if you have any questions, he is easy to approach and will answer any questions.

This is a flipped learning class meaning you have to watch pre-class lecture videos, and you do not actually learn in class. They expect you to know everything before, but the videos are super un-helpful. Class is just un-graded group busy work, making Jameel nothing more than a glorified babysitter
Very difficult 1 credit class heavy work load

Please for the love of God and your sanity do not take this class. It's only week 4 and it makes me want to die. Its unorganized, poorly structured, too much going on, and classes are overwhelming and vague. Please just don't take this class.
Good professor, cares about his field and wants to make sure you understand content

He is a very nice guy and is willing to help, but the class feels like a waste of time, its reaching the end of the semester and he still hasn't graded past the first notebook. His lectures and instructions are also pretty confusing at times overall would avoid this class if it is not required.

His criteria contradict themselves all the time, so it's hard to get a good grade because it's hard to understand what needs to be done. The class feels like a mess, and it's tough to understand the work that needs to be done. He will help you out a great deal and is very nice to talk to. Just not the best instructor.

The lectures were pre-recorded videos to be watched outside of class where Jameel read off of a powerpoint. The lectures took a few hours even on 2X speed when I took notes. There were pre-class quizzes and weekly post-class quizzes as well. Jameel is a nice person but is not great at explaining lecture content for a 2-hour long class.

This man takes absolutely forever to grade anything-- even if it is just releasing scores from a multiple choice D2L quiz. He is also very nit-picky when grading. Most of the material must be learned before the lectures, because he is going to go on ten tangents and cover maybe 25% of the material in class. If you have to take him, best of luck.

Ugh, please avoid this professor if possible. He seems like a great person and is caring about students but cannot grade things in a timely manner. Also, you have to earn a 93% or above in the class to earn a 4.0 but must earn 80% or above for a 3.0. So kinda like a curve that is helpful to nobody. Very tough grader too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A really funny professor who is really knowledgeable and passionate about the course material +beyond. Always willing to support students with assignments and make the course fun/engaging.

Dr. Al-Haddad is one of the toughest graders I have experienced at my time at MSU. Not only is he a tough grader, but he has only graded a handful of our assignments this year and class is already over. Despite this he is actually very helpful when you ask questions in class and is good at helping students with their work.

I found professor Al-Haddad to be a great and engaging person who cares a lot for what he teaches but is very slow to grade coursework which makes it extremely hard to know what you need to do better/ different for he next assignment. We have completed 5 notebooks this semester and only one has been graded and it's the final week of classes.

It is finals week and he just started grading notebooks we did at the beginning of the semester. Even if you follow the rubric for the notebook, you'll still do poorly and you'll have no time to make improvements. I have no clue what my grade is and grades are literally due in two days. He is an incredibly boring lecturer for an almost 3-hour lab.

We only have a few days left of finals week and half of our assignments haven't been graded yet. We don't know if we are completing assignments correctly, which also makes it especially difficult to submit any final drafts for lab proposals and presentations because there is no criticism telling us what we need to fix.

Overall a hard class, Dr. Al-Haddad is a really nice guy who is open to help. But for it being a 1 credit lab, there is a lot of work. On top of that it takes him the whole semester to grade the lab notebooks, leaving you lost as to what your grade is at the moment.

Hes very nice and knows what hes talking about but is VERY unorganized. Its the last week of the semester and 1 grade has been put in. The class is a lot for a 1-credit lab and not much feedback is given at all

He's nice, but unorganized. Homework is 15% of your grade and we only had one official homework that took him the entire semester to grade. The class is group oriented, so hopefully you get a good group. The class was hybrid but the quizzes and exams were online, and they weren't to difficult. He's not a bad professor just a little unorganized.

By far my least favorite professor and class here at MSU. Himself and his lectures are a mind-numbingly boring. There is an unholy amount of work. Often takes days to respond to emails. Always unorganized, instructions rarely clear. If your group mates drop, you won't be placed into a new group. Terrible experience from getgo. Would not recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: I still don't know what a notebook is. I have asked in class multiple times along with others and he just says "watch the videos." The videos do not help in the slightest. Everything seems very unorganized and I don't know what's going on half the time.
This class is an ungodly amount of work for one credit. My 5 credit math class had less work.

This professor is one of the most unorganized people I have ever met. He cannot make D2L quizzes properly, he fails to grade work, and announces significant class changes last minute. Overall, he makes the class an awful experience, despite his otherwise nice personality. I would advise not taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Azadnia doesn't come around much; TA-based. TA is either super critical or lenient. In my experience, TA explained the procedures so vaguely and we were confused most of the time. Really unfair that we're graded on purity/yield when the syllubus procedures are inaccurate and outdated. Difficult to prepare for labs. Goodluck!!

TA-based. Lab reports are short, and labs are mainly repeats of CEM 355. Literature assignments are annoying but easy when you know what you're doing. The last two labs (finding unknown compounds) take the most amount of time, so make sure you get comfortable with taking IR, NMR, and the melting point!

ta-based, there's like 3 different versions of the procedure so u have to ask ur ta about every step 😭 lab reports are easy. idk how many semesters tas stay with the same class but if u have indrajit he's goated

TA-based, but if you have Jenna Lepek, you'll do great! Gives you the procedures before class and helps you perform them. Some labs are based on attendance, while others on yield and appearance. Overall, a simple class if you come and do the procedure. Dr. Azadnia himself doesn't teach, but he grades your final paper at the end—pretty fair graders
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: TA based. Lab reports are mostly based on effort, but some labs (and they tell you) are very important to get right. Must prepare to know what you're going to do before class. Lab reports are due a week after which is nice. If you have Tommy Reason as your TA, you'll love the class! Albert himself is an easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Doctor Azadnia runs the overall course so you will likely never run into him; however from my interactions he is very kind and easy-going. This course is entirely based on your TA for most of the grading involving labs and etc. Lab procedures can often be confusing and you basically have to attend every lab to get a 4.0.

Dr. Azadnia is great! This is more a review for CEM 444 because as others said, you don't interact with him much in CEM 355/356. 355/356 are labs so it's pretty standard that you only interact with the TAs. 444 is an easy 1 credit lecture taught by Dr. Azadnia. He is very chill and funny. He's like a kind grandpa who tells chemistry stories

TA runs the course—Shoutout to Nikitia for being an amazing and chill TA. I also had him for CEM 444 and he was funny and chill (granted, it was a 1 credit class). You don't really interact with Dr. Azadnia much.

Like alot of reviews say, the class is heavily TA graded. Your sections TA grades all but two labs, so if you have a chill TA the class is pretty easy, despite how disorganized and vague some of the labs are. Azadnia only grades the green chem project at the end of the semester, and gives mostly everyone a 100. He also responds to quick to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Had to show up to every lab in order to 4.0. Was very nice, but rarely every saw him as the TAs run the entire lab, but my TA was amazing. The course was barely any outside work from lab and lab reports weren't super serious, but that could've been the TA I had who grades them.

TA led labs. You cna finish the course early, and so you can do additional labs as an honors option/extra credit. The final project is very time consuming but not very difficult, and the grading is fairly lenient tho.

TA led course. Textbook is helpful to understand procedures beforehand but not necessary. Only time interacted with the proffesor was when giving final presentation. If you do your work, you will do fine in this course.

She explained things very clearly and in an interesting way. Very easy to follow along and didn't go too fast for the notetakers. Very knowledgeable about the topic and was always very prepared for lecture.
She's a good Prof, however exams are worth %60. Final exam will replace your lowest grade but exams are tough.
Attendance mandatory. Pay attention in class or you wont pass. She moves pretty fast in class but lecture videos are posted. Put in the work and youll be alright.

Dr Pollock is an amazing Professor; her teaching style is good, and she tests what she taught with iClicker questions. She gives opportunities for extra credits as well, 4 total exams with 1 Final exam that will replace your lowest grade from the other 3. I had previous experience doing A' Level Chemistry, so the class was very easy to understand.

Mrs. Pollock was a good professor and explained topics thoroughly. 
-iClicker every lecture with questions for attendance 
-Homework twice a week graded by completion
-Recitation is mostly groupwork but is fairly easy and mostly completion

The exams were very lecture and recitation heavy. As long as you went to class and truly understood what she was talking about and could apply it to other concepts, you will do well in this class. I also recommend going to the help room for more clarification and exam prep. Overall, she was great and super nice.
Dr Pollock is a very knowledgeable person, and you are able to understand the lectures pretty well.  (I unfortunately don't do good in chem no matter what) But she is an amazing professor.

Amy Pollock is a great professor who truly wants her students to learn. PAY ATTENTION to her lectures and TAKE GOOD NOTES. These will be your best friend for the exam. DO NOT slack off on the BeSocratic HW or in the recitations. These are basically mini-reviews for the exams.

Absolutely amazing professor. The way she taught the class made everything in chemistry just click. All homework, recitation activities, and exams will be very easy if you show up to lectures. Made learning chemistry enjoyable.

Dr. pollock was seriously genuine about us succeeding in her class. she would give homework twice a week, but even those are done within 30 minutes. she would tell you everything to do in order to receive a good grade, provided tons of resources, and made it engaging. she is very educated on the topic at hand, and is very kind and considerate.

Professor Pollock took subject that I'm not very good at and simplified it enough for me to get a 3.0. Overall, a good, not great professor. But she can sometimes go a little fast so definitely be sure to stay up on the readings or at least use the help room.

Amy lowkey the goat at teaching, even for a difficult class. It was easy to take notes as she lectured and we would do iClicker for attendance points. Show up to lecture and recitation, take notes, try your best, and you will be fine. I literally got B's on all my tests and A's on everything else, giving me a 4.0 in the end. CEM 141 survivor.
She gave good explanations and clearly cares about students' learning. She has a lot of resources and tips for studying.

This class is taught in a big setting so not very personal. Everything you need to know will be taught in class which is mandatory. Lots of material to study for the test with. Class is not hard but she loves trick questions.

Great prof and made the course very easy to understand if you pay attention in lecture. Homework isn't bad and she goes over it in lecture. Attendance is mandatory with IClicker. Completion worksheet in recitation.
Great lecturer!
Made this class really easy to understand and she's good at explaining topics in a clear and concise way.

Amy is amazing. She is a super kind and a cute lady. However, if you do not come to the lectures, you will fail. Class material is basic chem and Amy teaches it super well. She is very passionate and explains every thing in great detail. There are about 2 easy homeworks a week.  Overall, if you come to class and pay attention, you should pass.
Super great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved Dr Pollock. She explains things very well and made confusing concepts easy to understand so make sure to pay attention in lecture. I got a 4.0 in this class. I never did amazing on the exams but the homework and extra credit help a ton. The final is super easy too. I would recommend taking CEM141 with Pollock.

Love Dr. Pollock! She explains things well in class better than my high school teachers. I never went to office hours since they conflicted with my classes but I've heard that she explains things very very well there. Just make sure you shown up and pay attention in class!
Very informative lectures, she teaches you exactly what is going to be on the tests and how to approach it. Definitely make use of the practice materials before each test.

You really just have to attend lecture and pay attention. This class is a general chemistry class, so the concepts are fairly simple. Go to class, study, get what you pay for. The only con I have is that the due dates for homework can be somewhat random, leading me to miss two of them because it slipped my mind.

Amazing at explaining the WHY for concepts, wants people to succeed and is good at telling us how to, makes lecture interesting, easy to understand. SUPER organized which was the reason for my success, posts lecture vids. Doesn't waste a second of lecture, definitely memorizes her speeches. Use learning objectives to study for exams! I'd recommend!

I studied for 9+ hours on every exam and never received anything better than an 82%. One exam I got a 69% even though I studied for 9 hours. She's a decent teacher, but this course just sets people up for failure. I do not understand how people 4.0 this class.
Very good lecturer, explains topics well. She does a very good job explaining why the concepts work the way they do instead of just giving us rules to memorize. And the homework load isn't too crazy.

Very good lecturer, explains topics well. She does a very good job explaining why the concepts work the way they do instead of just giving us rules to memorize.
And the homework load isn't too crazy.

Dr.Pollock is a very good professor. She is well experienced and makes you really understand concepts that can be challenging. She goes slow over materials (which I liked) to ensure that everything is clear. I wished she taught upper-level chemistry so I can retake them with her.

Professor Pollock was a great professor and explained the material slowly and thoroughly. She was very accessible outside of class and told you exactly what you needed to know to be successful. CEM 141 is a tough class but if you put the work in and go to all the lectures you will succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof is very aimed towards students success and education, but you can't really miss a lecture. Multiple extra credits and clear learning objectives. She is very clear with the material and easy to learn from, gives many suggestions on how to succeed in the class and if you follow you will. The exams were straightforward but at weird times.

Amazing professor, genuinely so nice and as long as you go to lectures and pay attention, you'll be fine. The homework is completion and the tests are hard so make sure you go study EVERYTHING on the slides and go to the help room!

Dr. Pollock was one of my favorite professors of the whole semester. I don't love chemistry, but she has a great teaching style. If most of the class got a lecture question wrong, she wouldn't show us how we answered and would reiterate from a different approach with more detail, then ask the question again and it worked every time. Great prof.
Professor Pollock is a great teacher. Highly recommend taking CEM 141 with her.

Lectures are SO important please go! Pay attention and ask questions, she is more than happy to help! She wants to make sure students succeed and even though it is a general course, still wants to make kids love chemistry. Overall, a wonderful professor!

I love her class. CEM 141 is typically hard but the way she explains things helped me understand. Homework definitely helps with understanding the material. I recommend utilizing the learning objectives. Exams to me were easy. Don't be afraid to use the help room too!

I absolutely loved having Dr. Pollock! She lectures in a manner that is easy to understand and she does look for participation a lot in lectures- but I personally didn't mind. If you follow the learning objectives, and are good (and quick) at taking notes in class you will be just fine. She makes expectations very clear and is very kind overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is a solid professor and conveys information in a digestible manner. If you pay attention and take notes in class, do the homework, and use the PAs for help as needed in recitation then you should be able to pass.

Goes way too fast in lecture. The TA's do a better job at explaining things than her. Extremely harsh grader especially on exams, which are worth 45% of your overall grade. I hated this class and struggled with it, which is weird because I did very well in previous chemistry classes I have taken.

She's great. I took this class with another professor and got 1.5 because the concepts are difficult and I couldn't understand. Now I'm taking it with Pollock and I think she's great. She goes fast but if you're gonna take this class every teachers gonna go fast. I have like a 3 in her class

she goes extremely fast and changes the slides before you have a chance to write anything down. plus, all the slides have so much info on them, which makes it easy to fall behind. she talks in questions, a weird teaching style. hard to follow, hard to understand. the exams are difficult, and she doesnt drop any of them. overall a difficult class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She talks in a way you can understand chemistry! She records every lectures (posted) so it's helpful if you missed class. She gives extra credit for homework. You get a point for each lecture/recitation you attend. I think she takes attendance by iClicker. Go over lecture videos and your notes (that's what helped me) cus exams are a bit rough.
Professor Pollock makes the material easy to grasp, but the exams are challenging. With diligent studying and using resources like Unstuck ai, you can ace this class.
She Is awesome, does a great job explaining and breaks down concepts. I struggled in the class still, but she made it better and looking back now, one of the better chemistry professors

Pollock was a great Professor. Her lectures were very informational and easy to follow. Although chemistry is a tough subject she explains it very well. If you do everything you're supposed to do, you should have issues with this class.
Nope. Just no

Great lectures. May be a little fast-paced for some, but the unit notes are posted ahead of time. The environment is more focused on learning than being graded by using iclicker, so feel free to be wrong, but be prepared to show up to class!!! Lectured are recorded and uploaded after. Easy to reach via email and great at answering questions.

The homework she gives are decently challenging, but she grades them in terms of completion and not correctness. Exams are pretty difficult so you'll want to take good notes and study well. She offers recorded lectures and things to make it pretty easy to study. With effort you'll be able to 4.0 and with minimal effort you'll 3.0-3.5. Great prof
The professor ensured to explain topics and concepts to fulfill students understanding of the material. The exams are easy as long as you keep up on the material and attend help hours!

Professor Pollock is so sweet and caring when it comes to helping you during class or office hours. She always makes sure to explain everything clearly if anyone has questions before moving on and will not make you feel dumb for needing clarification. She really cares about making sure everybody can do well in her class. USE OFFICE HOURS!!!

Professor Pollock was great when it came to thoroughly teaching topics.  However, you MUST show up to lecture or you will miss a LOT of information.  She was also very straight forward with her teaching.  There were many extra credit opportunities and grade drops offered, so do it all and you should be ok.

Professor Pollock was amazing! Professor Pollock made everything extremely easy to understand and learn. She is easily one of the best teachers I've ever had. However, that doesn't mean you can slack off. Make sure to pay attention and take notes and I promise you can easily 4.0 this class. Best of luck!!

I absolutely loved Dr. Pollock. Her class was always engaging and you can tell she cares about her students. She would review iClicker questions when the majority of the class got them wrong. However, the exams were extremely difficult. I think this class is mores difficult because of the tests, not the teacher.
She was very nice and easy to talk too, but the exams were pretty hard. You have to really study for them. It's more of the material that can be difficult to learn and not the professor.

The professor is great, offers many resources for help (take advantage!). I did a lot in this course to keep up, but if you are not a good test taker like me, this class may be a little harder as I would say even if you do great in everything else, the exams will still ruin your grade. She still does a great job at teaching a lot of content.

Dr. Pollock was an amazing prof. She's a very calm and collected professor, just the material can be overwhelming. The chemistry department at MSU is a creature in itself so just take things one day at a time and you will make it through. Attend her office hours, help rooms, and take advantage of study groups. That's what got me through!

Dr. Pollock is a very passionate professor and seems to care about her student's success. If you pay attention in lecture you will do well in this class, she posts the lectures online after class, but attendance is still required. This class moves quite slow, so lectures can be long and a bit boring. I would take Pollock over the other professors.

Ms. Amy ate her outfits up every single day. On top of that, she is spunky and organized. Very kind and very prepared and it's obvious she enjoys the material she is teaching. The exams were a bit on the difficult side, but nothing the right preparation couldn't fix. A few extra credit opportunities, and ICLICKER is used in just about every class.
coated

Professor Pollock is a wonderful teacher and ensures that her students understand the content. She is also very helpful during her office hours. The class content itself was definitely difficult, but she always made sure that we understood the material to be best prepared for the exams. Would definitely take one of her classes again.
Kinda Boring
Overall good teacher just beware of the first exam and then the rest of them
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was a tough class for me. There are 3 exams and a LOT of course information. Despite that, the teacher is wonderful and committed to helping students learn and master chemistry. There were many TAs walking around in lecture ready to help as well. The teacher offers many resources to help students be successful.
Takes her job very seriously, pretty repetitive homework assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's a great professor. Do the homework (especially ALEKS for 141), go to recitation, go to class, and you get a huge amount of easy points just from showing up. Tests are hard but doable - the first one is the easiest so study hardest for that (IME). Go to office hours if you've got questions, she absolutely takes the time to explain very well.

Professor Pollock clearly has passion for chemistry. The exams are very difficult, almost all my friends failed at least one exam. The final is worth a lot as well as the pre chemistry assignment of ALEKS, these two things will determine if you pass the class. Brush up on your prior chemistry knowledge before begining this course.
She was a very good professor, she tried to make a large classroom still interactive and wanted students to participate and ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Outstanding prof, truly cares about your success/emotional health. Go to office hours (not many do!) Clear lectures, brief HW, never wastes your time, & positive attitude. Exams are difficult but lots of prep material provided & only covers material in lect/recitation. I've taken AP chem, LBC chem, etc: this is the experience you wish you'd had.
Overall, great professor, easy intro class. Lots of easy points: participation, homework completion, attendance. She makes content understandable and truly wants her students to succeed.

I am not a chemistry person but I really enjoyed her class and would take it again. The class (CEM 141) does require some hard work, but that is at no fault of Dr. Pollock. She provides a lot of resources for her students.
Would take another one of her classes in a heartbeat

This professor did an amazing job. I am not a chem person at all and I have an A in the class. Always has resources available for you to get help, if you are failing it is on you because this professor provides you with so many resources.
She's okay, attendance is graded, no personal connection, teaches like an elementary teacher, the lectures are critical, and the practice exams are just like the real ones.
If you pay attention and take notes it is pretty easy to do well. Lectures are very helpful.

She is amazing! Not much work or reading for the class and she is so organized and easy to understand. She records all the lectures so you can watch them later or go back. There is so much opportunity for additional help but it's not even needed. She is the best chemistry teacher I've ever had. Tests aren't hard but need a little studying for.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Inconsistent and drastic grading harshness by the TA's. The teaching method failed to follow a linear path of thinking which made concepts unclear and confusing. When discussing grading with the professor, a clear answer was rarely provided while circular thinking was unfortunately common.
If you have her for an online class. Drop out
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed taking Dr. Pollock for general chemistry. She explained the material slowly which helped me a lot. The hw assignments are graded for completion but are easy to forget about. The quizzes and exams are hard but the graded assignments aren't too bad. Recitation can be annoying but it's for participation points and it helped my grade.

everything was open note even quizzes, lectures were online and not mandatory so you could do them whenever. Most things were completion grades and the material was very similar to high school chemistry. Professor Pollock was very nice and sweet and explained everything very well, available after every class to answer questions.

She explains the concepts well, but the rest is terrible. TAs grade everything, and never hand out high grades. If you ask the TA about the assignment, they provide no feedback and do not know what they are talking about. Everything is open note, yet half the class still failed every quiz. Highest quiz grade I ever recieved was a 60%. DO NOT TAKE!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very easy to fall behind and hard to catch up. TA's are nice and will help if you ask but she is the worst and seems stuck up. Quizzes and graded assignments are open notes but grades very. Hard class would not recommend taking chem in general if you can avoid it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's super great at explaining all the concepts and connecting everything. Beware of graded assignments because they're graded by TAs and the grades vary a lot. The quizzes are open note/book which make them manageable. Definitely go to lecture and take notes.

This class made me lose the last of my remaining brain cells. You need to attend every lecture and take notes on everything. Pray to the lord you have a good recitation teacher, those are your saving graces.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great Professor
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I've never understood chemistry until this class. She explains things so well and the materials/homework she gives benefits your learning a lot. I wish she could teach all my classes

Homework after every lecture, but she reviews the answers at the next lecture so do it for participation, not accuracy. Weekly recitations where you have to work with a small group to do a few practice problems. Bi-weekly quizzes. Fairly easy if you don't fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is really nice but she lectures a little fast. You go over a lot of stuff in class so pay attention and rewatch lectures to do well. The lectures are long. The TAs and professor are helpful for answering questions. Reading the book and looking at the learning objectives are good ways to do well in this class.

She is not very understanding. She doesnt care if you have technical issues. Her multiple choice quizzes are harder than S.A quizzes. I was so confident with every quiz but apparently she uses words that she doesnt mention during lectures.

Very clear with lecture material and makes them interactive without making you feel pressured or uncomfortable. Frequent homework assignments but easily manageable and always helped with understanding course information as opposed to just being busy work. Records the lectures live and always uploads them same day to D2L along with lecture slides AM

Dr. Pollock is one of the sweetest professors I have ever had. It's chemistry, so it is hard for a lot of people but she does her absolute best to ensure everyone succeeds and she cares about her students. There are a lot of resources outside of class to help and she will always answer your questions.
Amazing professor! Her lectures are very easy to follow and helpful. If you do what is asked receiving an A in her class is very achievable.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took this class Fall20 and I was never great in chemistry but I enjoyed this class. The way she taught was very clear, and what was due was basically spelled out for you, great for online. Office hours and the help room were easily available and if you put in the effort and attend lecture your set. I think recitation was required but not lectures.

Despite being online because of COVID, I really learned a lot from Dr. Pollock. She is a great lecturer and keeps the class engaged with polling questions and chat discussions. Pay close attention to details because they will appear in quizzes. There was a free textbook available online which would be useful to those who study best by reading.

Good professor. Lectures weren't always easy to understand. Quizzes consisted more of the book readings than the stuff discussed during lectures. Professor Pollock was easy to get ahold of outside of class and was always willing to help. Overall, I enjoyed having Professor Pollock and I would take another class of hers.

Dr. Pollock is a great professor! The whole gen chem department at MSU is very organized and I really believe all the gen chem profs, Pollock, Cangelosi, Kijewska, and Stubbs, are really good. I had Pollock for 142 and she was amazing! Always helped and very great lectures! She is super clear with instruction and she explains material very well!

I had Dr. Pollock for CEM 141 as well. She's a great professor who knows her material. Be prepared as exams are difficult if you don't know your information. Go to her office hours! She cares!! Just put the effort in for the grade you want to receive. She's great, but concepts are difficult and confusing! Take advantage of resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Pollock was such a great professor. I had her for both 141 & 142. She really knows her material, and always wants to see the student succeed. She's very accessible and you can go and ask questions whenever. Exams are difficult, I recommend taking her advice in preparing for exams, don't wait until the night before.

She is an amazing professor and knows how to teach the subject extremely well. She is kind and willing to work with all of her students to ensure they understand the information because she wants her students to succeed, especially since this is a required course. I love her so much, pick her for chem.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's a really good prof for CEM 142. The tests are not that hard as long as you study for them and do the mock exams. She's available during office hours to answer any questions and tries to ensure that you understand the concept.

Pollock is a great prof. She's super interesting. I used to think I hated chemistry and was bad at it, but it turns out I just didn't have a good teacher. If you are taking university gen chem, TAKE POLLOCK. She is easily the best professor. She makes the most sense and is the most willing to work with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: CEM 141 is a challenging class, but professor Pollock does a great job at teaching this course. I hated chemistry in high school, but I really enjoyed her class! I always left the lecture feeling like I knew the information and always came to exams overly prepared. I took CEM 141 last semester and I already miss professor Pollock!

Pollock actually cares about teaching and is very thorough in her lectures. She will stay on a topic if you don't understand it and is just an overall very nice and welcoming person. She is my favorite professor by far.

Pollock was a great teacher. The lecture hall is powerpoint based. As she teaches, she addresses the common problems of the group. She also places emphasis on study skills that will help. If I truly applied myself and did a bit better on some exams I would've 4.0ed. But with respect to grading go to recitation & do the homework and you'll be fine.

Overall great professor. She explains the content well and is always available for extra help. However, the exams are VERY difficult. You can miss up to 3 classes and 2 recitations without penalty which is nice, but attendance is definitely recommended. No opportunities for extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Overall, the class is super difficult and it's very hard to really know where you stand before the final grades come out. THE FINAL IS EXTREMELY DIFFICULT!

Her style relies on heavy emphasis of the topics discussed, which got the job done. Overall, Professor Pollock made this an easy 4.0 if you pay attention. To be honest though, shout out to my TA Ben, he really explained what was covered in lecture in simple terms. Had the 1.5 hour lecture so mileage may vary, but hard to get through sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Pollock knows her information very well and never makes a student feel stupid for asking questions. She comes very well prepared to lectures and includes all valuable in formation. I 100% recommend attending or you will not pass the class. I did not read a page of the book and preformed well on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Never miss any of her lectures and or iclicker question
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Pollock is a very good professor. Her exams are designed to be difficult but as long as you attend every lecture and take good notes and know whats going on in each lecture you should be good. But if your lost and don't know whats going on just go to the prof. office hours and ask for help and she will help you in any way that she can.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Pollock is a great chemistry professor. She really makes sure that any questions are answered throughout the lecture and takes time to ensure a majority of people are understanding what is going on. Her lectures are informative and helpful and if you show up, take notes, and study a few days before every exam diligently you will be completely fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is hands down one of the best professors that I ever had. The lectures were very easy to follow, but to understand the posted slides, you most often had to attend lecture. The exams tested your knowledge, but if you go and get outside help the exams are a piece of cake - and you can get extra credit. I would highly recommend her as a professor.

You need to attend lecture to understand anything, and then outside of lecture you need to look at the slides and make sure you understand what is going on. Study... a lot. The exams are nothing like what's done in lecture or recitation so make sure you look at the practice exams before hand and make sure you know how to do everything on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Good professor. Lectures are well prepared and executed.
Very active in class, allows questions and explains in strong detail, doesn't treat you like an idiot for the question, explains things in a way everyone can understand but not at a pre school level.

Once of the best professor's I've ever had. She is extremely competent and knows exactly what she is talking about. She explains things in a way so you actually understand and can connect different concepts, rather than struggling to simply memorize topics. She cares about her student. She is a powerful, intelligent woman, and a great teacher!

Pollack is hands down the best chem professor for CEM141 and 142. If you come to class, actually listen in lectures and do the practice exams to study, you WILL do well. She cares about her students and gives you pretty good hints at the exam review sessions about what will actually be tested. Great teacher!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She dumbed things down in lecture, nothing seemed hard at all. All of the exams after exam 1 were very hard in my opinion compared to lectures and homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great professor, all of CEM 141 classes are given the same exams so I would chose her to take the class with. Hard class, but I would pick this professor in order to do your best. She wants you to succeed and will help.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Did not care when I went to her struggling on over 3 different occasions. I went to her when my exam score was a 61% and she told me to go slower. terrible professor! really mean and not helpful

Very clear when teaching, best cem prof to have
Hands down one of the best profs I have had at state so far.

She does a great job of doing examples, and explaining chemistry clearly to the students

Pollock is an amazing lecturer. She really knows how to explain things well. People skip their lectures with other CEM professors just to go to her's. Highly recommended to take her

Pollock it by far the best professor i've ever had. The class is tough, but she's amazing

The best professor I have had so far. I didn't do so well in chemistry in high school, but she explained it so well and was very clear and easy to understand, and I received a 4.0. She is definitely one of the best professors on campus.

Explained the material very clearly.

Pollock is a really good professor, very clear in her lectures and the best teacher for chemistry. If you don't get her, you'll regret it!

Awesome teacher! I switched from another prof and my grades increased dramatically, she is very helpful, her lectures are awesome and she has great office hours! Would recommend for any CEM class at MSU

Great professor!
She was very helpful and clear.  The class requires a lot of work, but she does everything she can to help

Great Professor, I hate the subject but she got me a 4.0

No Comments

Awsome teacher

reviews.comment: 4.0 is a 94 lol. 5+ hours of reading and course work every week. An arrogant prick yes, but a respectable one at that. makes a gen ed course more than It has to be. will make you work your @** off for a 3.0, just take the Africa IAH, its 20x easier, lords knows I dont need to read about the coming of christ, and I don't even believe in him! ;)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: For a 100-level ONLINE summer class, Liam took it way too seriously. The ego/god complex is intense with this guy. Had us read the textbook, which gave us everything, and then still wanted us to watch his 30-minute lectures. I guess he wants to make sure he didn't waste thousands of dollars on a history degree cus I never watched those lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Brockey gave some sharp feedback on the first college paper I wrote. I deserved it. Talked at office hours. After I was able to explain that I didn't want my grade changed, he helped a lot. I never got less than a 3.0 on a history paper from that day until graduation. Comes across a bit arrogantly, but knows what he's doing. He has my thanks.

I've had Dr. Brockey for three classes now and honestly he's one of my favorite history professors. One quiz is generally based off of a reading so make sure to read your assigned texts, quizzes are easy, but will ask students how they're feeling and gives hints during lectures to answers. Amazing, cares about students, in-person final.

Professor Brockey was a great lecturer who cared about his students success. He was understanding that majority of students taking IAH202 were not in it by choice, but to fill the university requirement. Because of this, he made sure that students had multiple opportunities to 4.0 the class by giving out various extra credit opportunities.

IAH 202 would not have been as bad if students knew what was involved before. Random attendance quizzes as well as quizzes based on lectures which are hard to remember. However, he drops quizzes all the time, gives random points, and the best extra credit opportunities a student can ask for. It's honestly not that bad, I got A's on every paper.

Everyone giving Professor Brockey a poor rating are just lazy. I wrote 2 of the three papers and went to all the lectures. 6 of the lectures had attendance (that went towards the quiz grade) and 3 regular quizzes. I bombed the regular quizzes but still got a 100% in the class. Surprise that you ACTUALLY have to go to class to get a 4.0
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dont buy the books! A majority of them can be found online. If not they are free via the MSU library. I recommend making a reading group, this makes the readings easier to do as a group rather than just one person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Anyone who says they do not like Brockey's IAH 202 class because he is 'mean' is being lazy. If you attend class and pay attention at recitation, you will easily do well in the class. I cannot promise it is the most interesting class ever if you do not care about history, however with minimal effort you can get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Honestly hated the class.The class requires you to be on top of attendance for lectures and the recitations, in which you have to read 50-100 pages for every week. If this class wasn't mandatory and I was trying to learn history, he's an exceptional teacher. If you have a passion for history, I highly recommend him as he's truly a great teacher.

IAH 202 is a required course and Brockey laments that just as much as the students do. I would say he does a decent job with what little motivation he has from non-history major students. Do the Bonus assignment and try your best on the two essays and you'll 4.0 this class. Also, show up to recitation, since its like 30% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: This course is very doable if you're willing to put forth effort. As long as you show up for class and pay attention you will do fine on all the quizzes. There is a lot of reading but the essays are solely based on the books so I would recommend doing it. He's a funny guy with a wealth of knowledge so if you listen to him you will learn something.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 0/10 would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very lecture heavy (it's a history class) but it's fine because he's a really good lecturer. Expressive voice, answers questions, makes jokes, and he clearly knows his stuff. Gives great feedback on papers too. Glad I took the class, and I learned a lot.
I am not a history person at all and took this class out of curiosity. Best decision ever! Professor Brockey is smart, engaging, and easy to listen to.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Brockey was excellent this past semester. The lectures could have been a bit faster-paced, but they still were good. He was nice and completely understanding of unexpected circumstances. The class definitely makes you work for the four credits, but as long as you focus and do the work, you should be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Offers extra credit & honors option, hilarious, good pace during lecture. Lecture info is informative and fun, but you don't have to go to pass; all quizzes (no tests except final) are writing papers or picking out quotes from the reading material (you'll see) but don't fall behind! gives lots of time for quizzes, made me enjoy 9am class time :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Brockey made HST293 a great course to take, given all of the struggles of online school. His lectures were always funny and easy to understand. He wants to see each of his students succeed and that comes across both in and out of scheduled class time. There is quite a bit of reading, but it is worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He is a very bad professor who doesn't care about individuals at all. Talk about himself during lecture and think he is smarter than everyone. Very bad grader, class average grade for three essays are 78, 70, 68. Section participation average grade is 73.

Brockey is the most entertaining professor I have had at MSU. His lectures have a nice flow and his ability to pull from his own research to supplement the content was refreshing. He made the course interesting with his enthusiasm and I have no complaints about him. There is a lot of reading but it isn't laborious or nonsensical. I would recommend.

You can tell that professor Brockey really cares about his students enjoying the course & actually learning, rather than just grades alone. The class does have a good amount of reading, but if you keep up with it the class is fun & interesting! (Dont be worried about the bad ratings on here, its the exact opposite of my experience!)

Yes, there are a lot of lectures, but Brockey does a great job keeping them interesting and funny. He has done a fantastic job transitioning to online, and he is super responsive to students' needs at this time. There is a manageable amount of reading each week, but it is all engaging and relevant. If you do the work, you will 4.0.

What a great class! I have never taken a history class so this was a "for fun" class for me. Prof Brockey really cares about his students and is very understanding. He is much more concerned about his students being able to learn something rather than just stressing them out with busy work. The content of the class was also very interesting. 10/10

Very arrogant professor who talks about his own success too much as well doesn't teach anything specific. His lecture slides are useless and you'll have to buy like 12 books to pass the class. Doesn't care about individual students or their success or their circumstances. Very condescending if you talk to him through email or in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: not a hard class at all, the notes are irrelevant to the take home essays but you still need to pay attention to get a good grade on the quizzes. he doesn't pay attention during in class quizzes so you can cheat on them. the essay prompts are easy and if you just try really hard on only two short essays you'll easily 4.0 the class and no final.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Brockey is a great professor with a very mature sense of humor. He has little patience for immaturity and he is not afraid to call anyone out on their laziness. Show up, and do the work and you'll do great. Anyone that claims he's a poor professor are just lazy ass students that never show up to class yet expect to pass.

Arrogant, all the lectures notes do nothing for your grade. The essays are entirely your grade. He doesn't really care about the individual students. Talks about his own success a ton. No One Cares. Honestly an awful teacher. Do not talk this class, if you enjoy your life at all. Nothing about his class is interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Brockey does not know you to teach. Do not take this class if you are not extremely interested in Europe because you will not understand what he is talking about or what he is going on. The slides he puts out has little information, and he just rambles about Europe the whole lecture period without any specific points.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory for recitation, but not for lecture. Dr. Brockey is a smart man. He is pretty funny and understanding, but beware that he does not have patience for immaturity. You can learn a lot from him if you put in the work.

Brockey is a fantastic professor. I never expected to get excited about Jesuit missionaries in Southeast Asia, but I genuinely looked forward to going to his class and hearing his lectures. As long as you show up, you'll do well. He's a great lecturer and is very knowledgeable He says in class in doesn't care if everyone gets a 4.0 so do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Brockey's lectures were always fun and entertaining they aren't really necessary to attend but they are helpful. Lot's of reading but you'll be fine if you only finish about half of each book. Best history class I've had at MSU. It also helped that John the TA was awesome.
Lots of lecture, very strong-minded and not much group discussion
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I love Brockey. His lectures are always interesting and easy to follow, and every once in awhile he cracks a joke to make sure they aren't dry and clean cut. The class is REALLY heavy on reading, so make sure you plan out a few hours every day to commit to the books.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests? Not many--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Do not take unless you are a devout catholic. This is not an objective course whatsoever.  You will feel left out of the lecture, and unable to participate in the limited time for participation.  The entire course is lecture based, and the professor never stops talking to allow students to give opinions.  There are three papers, graded very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Definitely a man of his words. Wouldn't get on his bad side. Just show up to class, don't be disrespectful, and you'll have a decent time. Brockey can definitely be funny at times. A man of knowledge to say the least.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: POP QUIZZES. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory but he has pop quizzes that are part of your grade. Need to read to do well on pop quizzes. You can get through the papers by skimming through the readings/taking down notes in recitation. Personally didn't do well in the class because I wasn't interested in the topics at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Lots of reading but you don't have to read all of them to get a good grade. Brockey is a great lecturer and the class is interesting if you like history.

Pro:  Knows what he's talking about. Hilarious, his lectures are amazing. The main textbook is virtually useless. I didn't read it at all yet I got a 4. You can save some money. Very helpful tips and feedbacks.  Cons: A decent amount of reading assignment. His ppt only helps you understand the lecture. You can't skip and just count on ppt

I really enjoyed how Brockey approached this course. It is a lot to try and squeeze in a semester (being world history up to 1500), but I thought he did an excellent job. He has a good sense of humor and is clearly passionate about his area of study, which is great.

Bob is very engaging and clearly cares about students' success. The projects and assignments may seem intimidating at first, but they are manageable if you stay organized and ask questions when needed. The class is well-structured, easy to follow, and enjoyable overall.

Professor Gould has lots of knowledge in news production and would be a great professor for any high-level class; however, for a 200 level class, he often didn't do enough to make sure the entire class was up to speed on the skills we were learning for the first time. Overall, he was very helpful and you can tell he cares deeply about his students.

Bob Gould is one of the best professors I've had. He's a tough grader with high expectations, but if you participate and engage, the class is very enjoyable. His fun, goofy personality makes it interesting. The required video kit is expensive, but I would take this class again.

Bob is a good professor, but he switches up. One day he likes you the next he is so rude to you. The projects are a lot outside of class, so make sure you have time for that. He also teaches and grades like this is a 400-level course even though it's the beginning of journalism for a lot of students. Does get frustrated easily. Overall, a 6/10.

Bob is a charming and funny guy, he sometimes likes to talk about fun things at the beginning of class, which created a very open and welcoming environment; everyone seemed comfortable talking. He kinda expects a lot from a 200 level class and might get frustrated if everyone missed something, but he is very helpful and accessible outside class.

He is very passionate and has a good personality. I think he fails to take into account this is a beginner class and some of the things he has us doing is very complicated and he grades pretty harsh. If you miss one lecture, especially on a day were editing, it will be very hard to catch up. Also he is hard to reach outside of class.

He really does mean well, but towards the end of semester he will give you 2-3 projects to work on at the same time and they aren't super easy. Also he will only let you have 2 absenses or he will knock your grade .5 GPA.

One the most difficult graders I've ever had and grades as if it isn't an entry level course, expecting students to already be experts and grades just so. The equipment required is also very expensive, and the course is not well-organized or easy to navigate as a student. Don't take this class if you don't have to. Ruined my GPA.

I think Bob is a fantastic professor and cares a lot about students and their learning. His grading can be harsh, especially when you don't follow instructions EXACTLY, but he wants us all to succeed and create quality content rather than allowing us to put out something we aren't proud of. He's not easy, but that's why he's a great professor.

Seems like a nice enough guy, but the course organization was horrible. Very hard to navigate syllabus, find course instructions etc, and even then they were very unnecessarily complicated. He also seemed like he didn't know what was going on lol. It's easy once you figure out what you need to do, but just a very weird organization

He is a tough grader and attendance matters to him a lot. If you miss 2 classes, your final grade will go down .5. He gives a lot of projects and grades them tough if you don't do them exactly how he wants them. It is a 200 level class but feels like it is a 400 level class with the expectations.

Bob Gould is a good professor, but this class can be difficult. There is only one exam that you take at the end of the semester that covers everything. There are are weekly quizzes you take at home on D2L, and the writing assignments are relatively easy. He certainly makes the class interesting.
You'll think that you're doing well until you get your final grade. He's picky about details and doesn't take into account that you may be a beginner. He ruined my GPA.

Out of the 4 big projects, 3 of them were groups projects. Rubrics were hard to follow and not entirely clear. She is a tough grader. The first couple units were easy to follow, but as the course progressed, it became harder to follow along and take notes because she would ramble on a lot. Not an easy 4.0, coming from a student with a high GPA
This professor never has a clear schedule or assignment list. You have to use four different websites for content. Tophat is used for mandatory attendance. She is passionate but demeaning.

I greatly enjoyed Dr. Burnleys class, I don't understand her low rating. Get to know her and you'll do way better in this class. It is lecture heavy and we use a ton of different websites, but the pop quizzes you can do with your friends. And beware of group work! Plus all the movies we watched were great!

Burnley is a kind and approachable professor. She grades generously as long as you carefully follow the rubric. Attendance is required through Top Hat, and her lectures are heavy. Most days she'll talk for the full time. All quizzes are online and unproctored, but group presentations make up a significant portion of the course. It's a an easy 4.0

Easy class, boring lectures. Get a good group together, and you will receive the easiest 4.0 of your life. Be prepared to spend some money on software to do attendance and some work with (tophat). The lectures feel excessively long, and as previously stated, are boring. She is a very lenient grader, follow the rubric and you will do very well.

She seems like she is very nice, but the overall class is just VERY boring. If you hate group projects, you are in for a ride. Majority of the class is just sitting through the most boring lectures ever, and attendance is mandatory... If you have a good group then the work is fairly easy, but be prepared to read and watch things outside of class

This class would be interesting if it wasn't so mind numbingly boring. No one pays attention in this class and it is only easy if you have a good group, its all group work. She gets off topic easily and is really opinionated. Attendance is mandatory so you have to go to her lectures which is irritating because you don't learn much from her.
Extremely boring and long lectures I honestly sat on my phone the whole time but it isn't too hard of a course I got a pretty easy 4.0.

Sandy is lovely, class is...not. The 3 platforms are super confusing and if you get a horrible group like I did- get ready to WORK. I definitely could've done better if I actually showed up to class but the lectures are mind numbing. Great content, poor execution. Would take again knowing what I know now, but take a different ISS if you can.

Class is hard to follow. The use of 3 platforms is very confusing and hard to keep up with. No one in the class know what is going on. She's nice but wouldn't recommend as a professor. You aren't told when you have homework or a quiz you're just expected to magically know when you have it and when it's due. I would recommend avoiding this class.

uses many diff websites for work in every class it was confusing and annoying, would post many discussions but never a prompt, hard to know whats expected. participation is heavy and lots of quizzes, she was a nice women but got off topic sometimes, engagement was hard, over all the class was easy but an 82% in the class is a 2.0 grade. no tests.

Lecture was boring more often than not and the 3 different platforms for assignments were annoying to keep up with, but I barely showed up to class and still managed to get an A. 
As a person, Professor Burnley is a delight once you get to know her! As a professor...I'd pick a different ISS if you can. I'd take it again if I had to though.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. I am typically a 3.8 student, and this class ruined my gpa, the professor uses 3 different platforms and the questions on all tests are confusing. Not to mention lectures are long and boring.

Class is easy but very boring, but caught Burnley and her TA literally laughing at my group's presentation we were doing, while we were doing it. "they clearly don't know what they're talking about" Um... it's a 100 level course and I am literally doing a presentation about coal right now. Nobody in this room knows what they're talking about.

It was a really easy class, an easy 4.0. It was very lecture heavy, but she wasnt the worst teacher ever. There are a lot of group projects that are graded by your classmates, so you want a good group. The lectures are just really boring and hard to pay attention too, and you have to go because she takes attendance.

Very easy class, you watch movies then discuss sociological issues depicted. The idea of the class is interesting, but the lectures are very boring and they rarely relate too much too the movies. Ideas are not revolutionary, despite being treated as such. Easy class, but not terribly interesting.

She wasn't a bad professor but she wasn't particularly good either. the lectures are extremely boring and the topics are simple but she acts like they're revolutionary. The group projects are the worst part especially because the way others rate you on it affects your grade and if you come to her with problems in the group she barely does anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Main thing is TONS of group projects. The content itself is very strange, kinda tries to focus on too many things at once. Overall, the weekly quizzes are pretty difficult, but her grading of the group projects is lenient. ATTENDENCE MATTERS! Essentially, it comes down to if you get a good group, your set. If not you're in for a rough semester.

Very easy and straightforward class. Lectures were boring, quizzes are open note and online. You get weekly discussion submissions on PackBack. There were two big group projects. My main horrible experience about the class is the people in my group. They always procrastinated and I always had to push them to hurry and they never spoke to me.

Very very sweet, but was incredibly boring. Theres two group assignments worth most of your grade which is annoying. Attendance is mandatory and you only get three unexcused absences. Honestly just slept in her class every day.
the class was alright....only thing i despised was packback and the group projects other than that professor Burnley was cool

A lot of people on here don't like this professor, and I don't really understand why. Her class was pretty chill. While I do give some people benefit of the doubt with her quizzes because those are hard to get a high grade on, the rest of her class is pretty easy to pass. All you have to do is show up, do the pack backs, and you get an easy 3.0 :)

This course is extremely unorganized, and the grading criteria is never clear. The quizzes are always about something completely different than what we discussed in the lectures. I would not recommend taking this course with this specific professor.

I am not sure why she is rated so poorly! I took ISS 215 and I loved it. Despite if you like the material or not I think she was a great professor and had a lot of personality! The class was a pleasure to take. At times the material could seem a little silly but I wont reflect that on her because the class is a university requirement. Easy 4.0.

Since ISS is a graduation requirement, people with no interest take it and then rate her low. She is not a bad professor and truly cares about what she teaches. The class was super easy, so it can get boring sometimes. The quizzes were annoying, and the final and midterm are both group projects, but you'll be fine just do your work.

I had Professor Burnley for ISS215, she is very enthusiastic and I found lectures to be interesting! However, you'll work in a group for your midterm and final. My grade ended up relying on people who never came to class, never communicated, cheated, attempted to steal work, etc. If you have a good group you should be fine, but that's up to chance.

This class feels like having a mildly annoying friend who's really passionate about something you could care less about. You want to be polite and listen but it's really hard to pretend like you care. But the class is pretty easy and at least she's nice.

Every time i went to the class i had no idea what is going on. Most of the whole class is talking about actually nothing, projects are all over the place, and as well as the d2l page is not good either, i don't recommend this Professor at all.

Professor Burnley is a decent professor, the work is not super hard, but it is tedious, and the material is pretty useless. The final is not super hard like everyone here is talking about, but it is really oddly made for a class such as this. Everything before the final is mind numbingly easy and you can get away with skipping most lectures.

Idk what these other reviews are talking about. This was the easiest class ever if you don't slack. It was confusing at some times just because the topics don't go together, but that doesn't matter. It's interesting nonetheless. There are 3 or 4 group projects and a few quizzes that are open note, so make sure to take notes in class. She's so nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quizzes that had questions we did not go over the class, group project and most students don't care.
Dr. Burnley lectures are very long and heavy. Her explanations are very confusing. The class is extremely project heavy! Take notes in her lectures because you will need them for the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the most confusing classes I've taken. Nothing makes sense, the lectures are so boring, the quizzes are hard, and have questions that aren't from the slides. All the projects are group based, so be ready to have lazy group members. She was very nice and is highly intelligent, but her forced opinions and grading is awful.
Horrible

Horrible professor. Could tell she tries to hard to be liked and 'woke' but it comes across as forced. She will make her opinions known and argue if you disagree. Class material was disorganized and confusing in terms of order. Heavily group projects, which can be good or bad. Lost all respect from the class early on. Do not take her if you can.

I don't know if these people took the same course I did because I had a completely different experience. I will admit the lectures were sometimes a little time-consuming but the course is what you put into it. Professor Burnley always tried to make class fun and enjoyable. Quizzes are a bit challenging but overall it was a good class.

Very irritating class. The lectures are useless and not important to anything relevant. Very easy work except she grades the midterms (all projects with a group) pretty harsh. Biggest issue is she makes it impossible to know what is due and when. Everything is hidden in her wreck of a d2l. Unbelievably frustrating.

Do not take ISS210 with professor Burnley. This class is a complete waste of time and jumps around so much I'm not even sure what I was supposed to learn. She is very opinionated during her lectures and makes sure everyone is aware of that. Also the majority of your grade is based on group projects so if you get a bad group you're screwed.

My experience with Dr. Burnley was a good one! I always found her lectures very interesting and she was always good at keeping us focused. She asks for students' opinions on topics and persuades us to engage with her. The quizzes can be a little tough, but they are open-note. Overall, a really nice lady and passionate about  her teaching!

Most of the people who dislike her honestly are just lazy or don't like what she is talking about. I found the class super interesting and easy. My only complaint is the class is super group project-based and a lot of times your group members don't pull their weight. Other than that I really liked this class and Ms. Burnley.

The course is easily 4.0-able if you put in some effort. Very group project based, so be prepared to work with others. Despite what others were saying, I found the final relatively easy as the professor makes a clear template of what lines of code were needed in the website. She is an enthusiastic professor and I would take a course with her again!

Burnley is an okay professor, I didn't understand why her quizzes were set up to have one correct answer when during lectures we talked about multiple point of views. The final group projects (theres a group project for every midterm and then some) was coding a website which didn't make sense for the societal issues and this being an english class.

Didn't have a problem with Prof. Burnley, her lectures were okay and nothing special really popped out. Class has a bit of busy work and group project based. Quizzes had unlimited attempts and overall should be a 4.0 if you just but some effort in.

This class was all over the place. Good luck on the quizzes. She doesn't try and hide her views and her lectures are very opinionated. Lots of class discussions that don't really make sense. 
But, the course is easy as long as you show up (required attendance) and enjoy group work because that is all you do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: My experience with Dr. Burnley was a good one, on contrary to all the other reviews. Her lectures were well put together and genuinely interesting. There was a lot to learn about the REAL world and why the world is the way it is today. I recommend this course. The classwork was easy and this course is easily "4.0-able". Overall very positive!

Course was pretty organized for the first part of the semester. However, after the school experienced a tragedy, the course became disorganized, and some projects were likely given due dates that were extended a little too far. The university offered the pass(take credits) or fail(class won't count towards GPA), but course organization still helps.

Do not take this ISS!!!! Unless you want to struggle the entire semester. Hardest class, the readings did not make sense, she did not post slides until before the exam and talked very fast. The last project was CODING??? In a ISS? Do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Her class was all over the place. Made us buy a book just to read only 10 pages of it. Her class is so unorganized to the point I don't even know what I learned from this class. She absolutely cruises through her lecture slides so you cannot take notes. Coding and creating a website was the final and it was impossible. Avoid at all costs.
was worried going in to the class after seeing her ratings but i honestly enjoyed the class besides the final project. very stupid and had no relation to the course

This course was all over the place. It was not structured at all, half the time I had no idea what we were talking about because it jumped back and forth so much. It was manageable up until our final project where we had to CODE our final. Also there were lots of notes and long quizzes that barely had to do with the material on the slides.

This class was so Woke and her opinion is the right one. It's never a discussion. She isolated me on one side of the room to take shots at my opinion and this is common, where she splits the class into two opinions, picks her side, and destroys the other hopelessly. The other is anyone conservative, right-leaning, or white. Heads-up: retaliation
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is nice, and she knows what she is talking about, but the assignments did not really make sense with the curriculum. There are a ton of assignments with your group, in which was only switched two or three times throughout the entire semester. The final involved coding, which does not make much sense as this is an ISS class.

There was so many projects that we had to do with out group which were okay because you aren't struggling on your own. But what really bothered me was our FINAL was a coding project. As someone with no coding experience this being the final was incredibly difficult, and coding was not taught at all.
