reviews.comment: Took HST140 fall 24 and genuinely loved this professor. The class was entirely paper and exam graded and attendance was required which I'm not a huge fan of but the lectures were amazing and the assignments were clear and not difficult at all if you put in the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: I don't know what those other posts are about. This was my favorite class of the semester, maybe ever. Sure, there was a lot of reading and films, but they were interesting and we always discussed them together in class. He clearly likes teaching and brings so much energy to class! I hope to teach like him some day.

This was one of my favorite classes at MSU! Dr. Segal really took the time to get to know students. He didn't just lecture but always included time for us to discuss the readings together. I learned a lot in the class and he gave us study guides to help prepare for the midterm and final. I hope to find time to take another class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Gives very long readings and entire movies to watch during the week, without much of a care for the lives of his students outside of class. Not accommodating of students with not visually apparent disabilities. Likes Japanese people a bit too much, to an uncomfortable and weird level. The class did have some interesting readings, not a good prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof is alright, but absolutely insane amount of homework, most of any class ive taken in my 4 years and my major is definetly not easy. like 7 movies, 4 books, 2 essays, 300pgs of supplemental reading, final project, final exam, pop quizzes, class discussions. If you have a heavy semester, please reconsider taking this class.

Unless you have all the time in the world to spend reading upwards of 100 pages a week, do not take this guy! He's extremely rude and condescending to students in class. Study guides are about 50 questions long and half of them will be on the exam. Has no consideration for students having lives outside of class. Avoid!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Segal really bonds with all of his students, even in huge lecture halls. His lectures were very interesting and there were many opportunities to receive extra credit. The only downside to this course was his grading scale which was 93-100 is a 4.0. Thankfully I managed to get that but most of my other courses are 90-100 is a 4.0

This guy blows. He refuses to post his slides even if you miss class, so if you miss class for any reason you are essentially screwed. Guy has no flexibility at all for anything, I'd avoid him if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Segal was an incredible instructor. He genuinely cares about all of his students, and makes consistent effort to learn all of the students names and to make sure they are not falling behind in material. If you are willing to read a good chunk, definitely take one of his classes!

He is very knowledgeable on the topic and more than happy to answer any and all questions we might have had on the subject. The pop quizzes were usually implied ahead of time and even then, were not difficult if you did the reading. The study guide given for the final and midterm were great and included everything you needed.

Nice guy, just way too much reading to complete for me with my busy schedule. There was also random pop quizzes to check to make sure students were doing the reading. The final was also writing three short essays in two hours. The films were interesting tho to watch and learn
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Segal was by far my favorite professor I've had at MSU. Each week we had bookwork and then we had weekly response papers where we responded to the readings, but it was a max of 600 words, then an hour-long class discussion where we spoke about the readings. Segal really knows his stuff, especially Asian history, he was a lot of fun.

Professor Segal is a respectable person that understands what he is teaching at a deep level. Although I don't enjoy history, he made the information bearable. The class structure fits well with what he is teaching but beware of quizzes at the beginning of class. If you have not done the readings that he has assigned, you will not pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Segal was awesome. Even though we were in a pretty big lecture hall, he made the class feel small and personable. He was very knowledgeable, but he wasn't afraid to admit the areas he wasn't as familiar with which was really nice and transparent. I'd definitely take a class with him again.

Great Professor. Dr. Segal knows his subject matter so well. He never really briefs from the slides, he explains them in so much detail. Attendance is mandatory, as it should be. I was just so interested in the subject matter and learned so much. I loved the recitations also, the short stories were great. If you try and care, youll do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This was my favorite class at MSU so far. Learn about Japan through film, novels, manga, and sports. Get ready to watch LOTS of movies, but most were interesting (inclu anime). His class presentations were good. 3 papers was a lot, but he gives good feedback. Coming back to campus for evening films wasn't my favorite, but still a great class!

Lectures were interesting - well organized, lots of pictures, and he never put me to sleep.  He gives a lot of reading, but you expect that in a history class.  At least he always discusses the reading, and is good at explaining things that aren't clear.  He clearly cares a lot about his students and will help if you go to his office.  Great class!

This turned out to be a great class. I wasn't sure when I signed up, but I learned a lot and the discussions were good. It's about Japan, and I didn't care that much about Japan before this class, but prof did a good job of relating things back to the U.S. and our problems here. It was way better than 299! If your IDS, and willing to work, take it!

Overall, I was not a fan of him. He is rude and down-right boring. He thinks we are tired every time we come to class,but he is the one that puts us to sleep! The reading assignments are ridiculous. They are frequent, long, confusing and boring. The pop quizzes are frequent too and considering the readings are so confusing.. good luck on those.

Extremely knowledgeable about his subject. He is quite detailed and likes to give a good amount of info in lectures. Reading/attendance are musts. He uses pop quizzes and readings are discussed in class. He really wants you to know your stuff and was always willing to help, but he expects effort too. Good prof.

One of the worst professors I have had at MSU. Only reads off of slides and doesn't speak clearly or loud enough for people to hear and she teaches like she's annoyed to have been teaching us the class in the first place. Quizzes/exams do not reflect the material in class and doesn't release review materials in a timely manner.

The worst professor I've ever had. Every single lecture was based off slides that she would read in the most monotone and quiet voice. She seemed annoyed to be there and would frequently sigh and mumble. Sometimes she writes on the chalk board and the chalk doesn't even show up and when students ask questions she gets annoyed.
She cares about her students so much and will help you patiently.

This is the first time I have actually taken the time to leave one of these reviews, and Professor Yakasai is the worst professor I have had at MSU. Lectures were awful, she used slides that she did not make herself, she did not explain anything well or even show enthusiasm for it, none of her practice reflects actual exams. You will teach yourself

Professor Fine is a great professor, but some topics are hard to make interesting like labor history. Also having 90% of the class exams seems not right to me. Though she grades nice still be ready to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: HST308. Overall grade is based only on 3 exams and one essay. No guidance or instruction is given on the essay. Lectures and slides are messy and unorganized. She has a very outdated teaching style.

As an exchange student I found the final paper difficult but the other exams and quizzes were easy (define 2-4 terms and write 1-2 essays among various choices). She is a good teacher and her class was very interesting!

HST 308. First time course was taught, and while course is very interesting she needs to wildly reduce what she is currently expecting to go through. Grades are determined entirely upon 5 exams at 20% each, 4.0 grading scale for 1 essay, and 4 "short responses". She has an outdated teaching pedagogy, which is strange considering her background
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: So hard for no reason
Grade is based off of only 2 quizzes, midterm, final, and paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Super amazing class would take agian.

Great professor. Uses in-class activities and explains concepts simply, making the content really program into your brain. Homework is consistent and actually helps a lot with studying. If you go to help room she's really personable and very nice to talk to.
Amazing professor. She is so helpful and caring.

This was Dr. Furqueron's first time teaching this class, it didn't seem like it at all. She is so knowledgeable of the material and made sure everyone had a clear understanding of the content for the exams. Her lectures were engaging with group work. She is just a caring, encouraging person. Definitely one of the best professors I've had so far.
Very nice and passionate about her students and class.  You could tell she really cared about everyone as well as their grade. She was an amazing professor!
She slayed!

She makes the lectures super interesting, which cannot be said about most professors. She cares if you understand the material and is super helpful when it comes to questions. It is very easy to get points off on all of the assignments in here but overall she is an amazing professor.
Dr. Furqueron is quite actually the best instructor I have ever had! Her class is set up in a way where you really learn the material and it's enjoyable to go to class!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Many reviews seem overly harsh, often from students upset about not getting a 4.0. She isn't easy, but her class isn't the hardest at JMC. Go to office hours! She values students who ask thoughtful questions and actually do the readings. Overall, she's a great professor and one of my favorites.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I don't feel that the rest of these reviews do her justice. She was very professional, gave clear guidelines, and assignments and lectures were very engaging. While the class did require all of the readings to be printed, she was open to conversations about accommodations. I would definitely take her again; this class is what got me into my major!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Extremely vague and unclear with assignment directions, which made it hard to know what was expected. Responses to questions often came off as passive-aggressive, and the feedback provided was not helpful or constructive. The course also required printing a large amount of material, which ended up costing a lot of money throughout the semester.

All expectations were so unclear and if asked about them, she would be passive aggressive and borderline offended.
