Hates teaching undergrad and it shows. AVOID!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Do not take this class! Not good at all with communication and passive aggressive when communicating. You have to print out every reading, so when it's 60 pages, it's extremely expensive. I practically went into debt printing her assignments.

Literally don't take her if you don't have to, avoid at all costs. Not only is she not a great professor in the sense of teaching, she also is just a not very nice person and is super condescending towards any participation.

She has a power trip that reaches an extremely unprofessional level. Her instructions are often unclear, and she becomes frustrated when students do not understand her vague guidance. She dislikes having to “repeat herself,” even though the information she claims to be repeating is not included in the syllabus or clearly addressed in lectures.

DO NOT TAKE HER. Terrible person. Does not answer questions in emails. "it's on the syllabus" bs. ONLY HAS ONE DAY OF OFFICE HOURS?? If you ask a question on an email she'll send a class announcement acting as if answering questions is not her job. Terrible essay feedback. Has a superiority complex against her students?? ruined my gpa; avoiding her
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is very understanding towards students and is passionate about her teaching.

I loved having Professor Flaim as my professor for MC 201. She can be a difficult grader and rarely gives "perfect" scores, but she will help you improve your work if you're struggling. Note: Her office hours can be busy. She's passionate about the topics she teaches, make sure to participate in class!!

Flaim is nice, and passionate. She cares for her students and her cause. However, she frequently goes off topic, which stops you from getting answers to your questions. She also grades harder than the other professors so you will probably have to work harder than your fellow classmates.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: felt incredibly babied and micromanaged. Specifically, rubrics had word counts for specific paragraphs, and she would walk around the lecture to make sure you were paying attention and didn't have your laptop out were some things that really pissed me off. She brought valuable information to class but I felt  like I was in 6th grade
Changed my mind, avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Tough grader, all readings are similar and not interesting. The class is tailored for specific people. It is unorganized and good luck getting a 4.0 on a paper. Her grading makes absolutely no sense. Would not wish this on my worst enemy
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Flaim is perhaps the greatest professor I have ever had the privilege of taking. She understands that students have a life outside of her class, and adjusts due dates accordingly.  There are a TON of readings , but it is JMC so it's not surprising, and she takes a while to answer emails but she is very busy so also not surprising!

Her classes are hard, I wont lie, but she cares for her students and will hold your hand throughout the whole process. If you are really trying, it is never too late to try again. I once did poorly on a paper and because I went to office hours to ask for help she just offered to let me rewrite it. I didn't even ask. Take her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Flaim is one of the most helpful and respected professors at James Madison. Yes, her grading can be difficult. However, every JMC class holds its students to high standards. The difference with Flaim is you will receive the grade that you earn. If she sees you're putting effort in and show interest to learn she will make sure you succeed.
Best start to JMC at state I've had!! Tough grading for sure, but she'll help you through it!
Very very caring and will work with you if you happen to miss a big assignment, I missed a midterm and she let me write a paper to make it up even though I missed it for a dumb reason.

Very passive-aggressive when asking questions, almost rude even. Not good at teaching and with the most unclear grading criteria possible. I legit couldn't see my percent grade all semester. Expect lots of meaningless group projects and busy work. Weekly quizzes that are pretty easy, but oftentimes hard to understand. Do not take.

A nice guy to talk to, but awful teacher. Does not give any instructions and expects you to know everything before hand. Does not grade until the last minute and does not grade resubmits fast, so you don't know what you get wrong.

I took LB 117 online, for the most part it was the same content as my high school calculus class but he either never elaborated on what he wanted us to do on the labs, or briefly went over what material he wanted us to turn in and always took so long to grade stuff. Overall horrible experience.
I would not recommended taking this class. This professor briefly goes over material and expects 100% understanding and some. There are also labs in this class?? A math class.

Dr. Fessler does not teach, but rather reads equations and makes you solve them all class. He does not handle criticism or suggestions at all. Makes you buy a new calculator for the 3 tests that we have. Be prepared to teach yourself everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: horrible horrible horrible never ever take mth103 with chuck fessler. he may be the worst teacher i've ever had in my entire life. his grading doesn't make any sense, the exams do not correlate with the material we learn in class whatsoever and he does not respond well to criticism or feedback and blames everyone failing on us not being prepared.

super nice guy but grades lab reports insanely. it is insanely hard. extremely tough grader on the lab reports for the pre-clac equal. for exams in MTH 103, it was very hard to gauge his expectations on tests/quizzes. i felt like i never knew what he was looking for

I took calc in high school, and struggled with his class. He does not explain well, and examples we do in class are completely different than assessments. I turned in an assignment in the beginning of October and it was not graded until early December. It was also nearly impossible to tell what your actual grade was throughout. not a good time

Dr. Fessler was always very nice and supportive for me. I went to his office hours often. He pulls some questions from the book for quizzes and exams but you can never be prepared enough. Seek as many sources as you can for studying. I did have to study very hard for his course but I managed to 4.0 with never taking calc in highschool!

professor fessler is a great guy however he was a terrible professor. he left me and my classmates very confused after every class and expected us to know everything presented in front of us. he didn't teach properly and all the homework that was assigned per unit didn't correlate with anything we were "learning" in class.

Would give 0. Didn't grade majority of assignments until end of semester. Never taught in class + majority of the class was always confused. Tests and online homework did not match examples done in class. Hard to succeed unless you have a strong calc background. Never helped w/ problems and didn't seem like he knew what he taught. Save yourself.

Nice guy, but can't teach at all. He works very fast in class and expects students to already have some background in calc. I was also having medical issues this semester and he was very hard to work with on this. He also lost one of my exams after I took it in his office hours. Don't recommend at all

If I can give Fessler a 0 I would. He doesn't teach any of his subjects and expects you to know everything already. You have a a quiz every week that's 50% of your grade and there is no dropping but only 1 retake of an exam at the end of the semester. The homework is on webwork and doesn't really correlate with what he is "teaching".
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Fessler is an amazing guy to talk to, but he is not a very effective instructor. I often found myself leaving lectures confused and unsure of how I would be able to succeed in this course. Once again, he is a very caring, but please try to get an override if you have to take one of his courses. I left Briggs because of instructors like this.

Chuck is a great guy but should not be teaching math 103. He changes the way he grades constantly, gets irritated at students for asking questions, and barely teaches. He just makes us do the notes and expects us to be math wizards. He is very kind but if you get stuck with him for class, I would recommend taking math 103 through the university.

Nice guy, awful professor. His grading is harsh and confusing and forces you to do most of the work in terms of determining your actual grade. He does not teach the material well if he teaches it at all, and the questions seen on assessments are ones not previously discussed, found in the notes, or in any of the hw or review problems. Do not take.

Terrible professor do not take him! Grades very tough and gives weekly quizzes on material he barely covers. Treats this introductory Calc 1 course like a upper level course. Do not take him no matter what you do.

Does not teach. Once got annoyed with students for asking questions and not understanding content, which was only the case because he teaches way too fast or not at all. Sometimes is unsure about his own questions. Practice exam material does not always match actual exam content. He is friendly and a good person but not a good teacher.

Very good person and could have been a more effective instructor. He is a great guy to talk to, but when it comes to course material, I am always left confused, and so are my classmates. He is accommodating but also really likes to talk, which is inconvenient when you need help with class activities.

Great guy, terrible teacher. This class was genuinely one of the worst experiences I had in college, I would come into class and leave more confused than when I had entered. You can easily learn the content online (organic chem tutor) rather than in his lectures. His teaching style just did not resonate with me and friends who took his class. 3/10

The professor is very nice and sweet, but he's not good at teaching math, as he demonstrates how to solve things fast with barely any explanation. He also grades extremely hard on tests and quizzes, giving some problems that are barely within the range of what he taught. Everyone's left confused after every class period

Incredibly nice guy but occasionally difficult to work with. He is not the greatest at explaining material, and many questions end up being taught to yourself because it is challenging to understand them in his lectures. Would  honestly make a better English or history professor
Chuck is a great guy who wants you to succeed if you demonstrate to him that you care. He is very helpful and understanding!

I had him for both trig and calc. I will say I saw improvement in his grading between the two semesters, but it is still very difficult to succeed if you're not already good at math or have had no prior calc experience. Quizzes every week, you can't miss them without a doctor's note. I liked him as a person, but he isn't the greatest professor.

He's a nice guy but take someone else for calculus. He means well by standards-based grading but it makes it more difficult to get a good grade. Quizzes are every week in recitation and I felt like I didn't learn concepts in lecture. Our ULA would go over content before the quiz and that's when I'd grasp the subject.

He is a good person but that is it. He teaches terrible and gives you quizzes every week during recitation. He gives problems and questions that you never really learn in class. The TAs felt bad for us because we would all be so lost in his class. I would try to take calc through the university. The grading scale makes it impossible to do good.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very nice person, but I would recommend taking Calc through university. Quizzes every week during recitation. LA's always felt bad for us because of the immense struggle we all had. Grades based on standards and I had no idea what my grade was all semester. Some questions on the quizzes 1 exams I had never seen before.
Just so bad, so so so bad. do not take. take university calc and do not take lyman calc. or u will be screwed. best of luck!!!

Actually a horrendous professor (nice guy though). Ended up teaching myself everything because of it. Study guides do not help, and a very misleading grading system. You will have quizzes every week (on and off independent and group style) in recitation which is required. You cannot skip these quizzes without a doctor's note (same for exams).

HORRIBLE class. He is a nice guy but I dont think teaching math is his thing. take calculus through university you get online exams.  if you don't want to watch your grade drop every week take it outside. really bad grading his teaching style is also wack.  the exam study guide doesn't correlate with the exam. Nice guy needs to consider changing su

Whatever you do, do not take this class. He changes the way you're graded constantly and literally cannot teach. If you are not already a master at trig, STAY AWAY. He overcomplicates everything and will take points away if you don't do work the way he wants it. He's actually a pretty nice guy, but worst prof I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is such a fantastic, knowledgeable lecturer who has a deep passion for the topic. He explains these topics so well and with such excitement, it gets me excited to learn. I learned so much from this class without it being difficult.
Very nice guy that seems to care a lot about his students. Easy and fun class to take, good elective.
Cool teacher with easy class

He made the classroom a fun environment, and was very understanding near the end of the semester. His grading is very relaxed and the weekly assignment was a paragraph on whatever I wanted. I really enjoyed understanding music i'm gonna miss that guy
He seems to actually care about what he is teaching and that makes the class so much better.

Very nice professor, you can tell he likes teaching about music and he's also very passionate. One of my favorite professors I've had at MSU. Makes essays fun because you write about almost anything you want related to music. Great choice for an elective.

It wouldn't let me choose the correct course but I took IAH 241a with Professor Fields, which was Music and Society in the Modern World. I loved this class, especially for an IAH. Prof Fields has such a caring, kind demeanor about him which made me want to participate even more. Easy workload as well. This was the way an IAH course SHOULD be.

I took this class very last minute not knowing anything at all about music. One of the best professors I have ever had so far at MSU. He is really engaging and cares that you pass. Not even a music major! I am business but was my favorite class this semester.

Sweetest prof. ever, poor teaching style. Made many mistakes, not tech-savvy, wasted time. Wanted us to succeed, helpful 1-on-1 but should be teaching a smaller class. Content shouldn't have seemed so dificult to understand, I didn't like the way she overcomplicated things/underexplained things. She deserves to teach a subject she's better at

Lectures and recitations were quite confusing. I thought that the lectures were a bit all over the place, and it was hard for me to follow what we were learning. She is really nice, but I do not think that she is the best teacher and I found the course difficult due to her teaching style.

Professor Fairbourn genuinely made me like a math class! She is so kind and answers any questions! One homework assignment per week, 2.5% added to your final grade if you do all the EC, my TA was amazing and helped me understand the content. The Stats Learning Center is such an amazing resource if you're struggling, I highly recommend utilizing it!

Very kind professor, uses great comparisons to get the lesson across. Attendance is a grade but you can always get at least half points and it is not weighed too heavily on your final grade. The final exam is cumulative, but the midterms are okay. Stats overall is hard so thats the main thing.

Her lectures are always confusing and her TA's are no help and make everything more difficult to understand, I would not take her class if your not the best at math because of the way she attempts to teach the material

I would try to take another professor. She makes the lectures very confusing, and most of the time, you are just doing examples and not actually learning the content, which made me have to learn it outside of class. Attendance is mandatory, but she offers make-up attendance questions at the beginning of the week. I wouldn't retake it.
Teacher didnt give me a 3.5 by 0.07% and would not round up. Other then that very boring lectures, and tests are heavily graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor is fine, class material is just hard. Starts off very easy and then quickly becomes impossible

Was definitely my toughest class of the semester, but I was still able to get the 4.0. Tophat and WebWork every single week, so make sure you do that. Taking notes is crucial and her lectures were good enough to where I could follow along, although I definitely got confused at some points. Use the very usuful practice tests and study for exams!

Prof Fairborn seems like a sweet woman but it almost felt like she knew too much for a base level stats class, it got confusing at times. She goes through slides fast and it was hard to keep up during lectures. If you feel confident about math you'll be fine. If you struggle with math, then you may want to make sure you can find outside help.

Fairbourn is by far the best stats prof. She is very caring and if you put in the work, you will get a good grade. Also, if you are having problems I would recommend going to the SLC. They walk through everything with you until you fully understand.

Super easy class, lectures are pretty easy to follow, only three exams; all very easy if you do the practice exams and study guides, don't necessarily need to go to class but you would need to do the top questions online if you want to get the points, definitely would recommend to anyone who has to take STT 200

Pretty easy 4.0 if you go to class, do the webwork, and do the study guides. Webwork and TopHat are required, along with a course pack. She was a great professor and I understood every lecture. Going to class is so important because she has TopHat questions for participation points! Overall would recommend
Great teacher for STT200, the lectures were valuable and the practice tests made the real test super easy.

Easily one of the best math professors I've ever had! She made statistics so easy to understand and was so nice. Grade was based on attendance (she usually gave us extra points or ways to gain back the points we missed) via Tophat, homework, recitation attendance, and 3 exams. All the exams were exactly like the study guides and practice exams!

This is the average STT class that colleges provide. It wasn't very hard, however, it could take time to get the concepts down. It wasn't extremely enjoyable but that isn't the fault of the professor for the most part. There is Tophat and Webwork due every week, so be prepared for that. Exams can vary in difficulty but they aren't very tough.

Fairly easy course and she tells you all the shortcuts possible. Course is not very difficult and she tries very hard to make your time enjoyable. She does well at not talking at you and talking to you instead. Very kind and compassionate lady.
I love camille. She is very sweet. Lectures can be confusing but if you go up to ask a question she affectively re-explains it.

Camille Fairborn is a good professor, but her lectures are hard to understand. She goes pretty fast through the slides and does not give a lot of time with required attendance top hats. Her tests are easy though as long as you do the practice exam and the study guide. Going to the lectures is very important if you want a good grade!! Shes good tho!

I liked Professor Fairbourn, but her lectures weren't great,so go to helprooms. Her tests are pretty easy as long as you understand how to do the practice exams she gives you, they are basically the same exact thing just different numbers. Attendance is graded on tophat and if you miss any lectures she has makeup questions you can do every Monday.

She does TopHat in class for attendance, however, she goes quite fast and gives us limited time to figure out the answer. She also goes a little fast in the lectures so you have to pay attention. But, Prof. Fairbourn has been great at answering questions and emailing back quickly as well as making the class fun on Thursdays with TopHat questions.

She is terrible, and when I say terrible, I mean it. By far the WORST math teacher I've ever had; not only does she have horrible lecture slides and fails to articulate what she means, she flat out completely fails her students as she cannot grasp the idea of how to teach math. I've had plenty of not-so-great math teachers, but she takes the cake.
Professor speaks and lectures but does not being concept to the main topic. Very hard to understand have to relearn everything in recitation.

Professor Fairbourn was awesome! She cares about her students and tries to remember names even though there's 300+ students in her class. Exams are easy if you regularly attend lecture and complete your WebWork. Have access to a TI-84 calculator because the majority of the course is just memorizing how to use the different functions on it.
Very organized slides. She knows her stuff as she is the course administrator for the class. You will need a TopHat account for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Fairbourn is super sweet and does a lot of interactive parts during class. TopHat questions will count for attendance so you could get away with skipping if you're paying attention to the classroom, but the content moves fast. Each class goes through roughly 10 pages of the course pack. Stay till the end for Thursday fun questions.
The lectures actually make sense and the whole course is clear and organized. The tests are just like the study guides and the homework is relevant. Overall such a good class!

Professor Fairbourn is the sweetest professor ever. If you got to the lectures and put in the effort you will do fine. She always asks for feedback and adapts to the class to make sure everyone is on the same page. The schedule of due dates and everything is super clear. She is super caring and will help you with anything if you ask.
Lectures were amazing. If you actually listen in her lectures you will understand the whole course.

I took this class online so I never interacted with her. But, from her lectures, I could tell how passionate she was about stats. The large homework load in this class is painful and tedious. I now hate stats but that's not Camille's fault lol her lectures taught the material clearly and concisely.

Although I did four point the class, the class required LOTS of homework and studying if you weren't the best at math. Had her for an online stats class and the homework would sometimes have questions that she never went over so sometimes it was difficult. She seemed nice though.

Prof Fairbourns' lectures and notes were incredibly helpful in being successful in this class. Watching them is a MUST! Hybrid-flex class made balancing the workload in this class manageable. Content is difficult at times, but the notes prepare you well for homework/exams. I enjoyed how the class was setup. Attendance was mandatory for recitation.

I took the flex-hybrid course and it was really manageable and easy. There was a lot of practice work and extra credit that helped me prepare for exams. Also, the videos were easy to follow and no longer than usually 15 minutes. Professor Fairbourn is a great person and lecturer and she's great at explaining things.

Professor Fairbourn is amazing! We were given the option to either go in-person or do the class asynchronously. I did the class asynchronously and had no issues at all! Each lecture video never exceeded 15 minutes so they were super manageable. I recommend printing the lecture notes as it made note taking so much easier.

I love this woman. I am awful at math and barely passed all of my other required courses, but her lectures make it so easy to understand! She breaks down her lectures into manageable videos and puts helpful references and tools in between the videos! She also uses great examples :)
Professor Fairbourn is great, be sure to do the homework, don't be afraid to ask questions, you've got this!

This class was strictly online but was performed perfectly by Professor Fairbourn. The course was extremely well organized, easy to follow, and she broke down hard to understand concepts very well. Watching all of the lectures is key as well as doing the homework every week, if you do that, you're bound to get a 4.0!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I never talked to this professor as the class was online, but these are the most straightforward and easy to understand lectures Ive ever had. There are many many opportunities to do well in this class, and the lectures outline everything in perfect detail. If youre ever confused, the team of professors responds to emails quickly.

I had Professor Fairbourn during a COVID year so our stats class was completely online and I never had an actual one-on-one conversation with her, however, her lecture videos were really good and I think she is a good teacher, especially for a tougher class like statistics.
Professor Fairbourn was very thorough with her lectures and explained each concept in great detail. Pay attention to the lectures and the class will be a breeze.

Not a bad intro to stats class, took it online asynchronous and it was easy to do well in and to get help. Her lectures are nice, lots of examples and easy to understand even if you've never taken stats before. Very lenient with technical issues this semester too, gave extensions for that sort of thing. Overall good class and I usually hate math

I took STT200 all online asynchronous. I really liked the way prof Fairbourn set up the material on D2L. It was very clear to follow and hard to miss anything. I liked how she split up all of the lecture videos into short 4-10 minute videos that go by section. The detailed lectures follow the notes packet so you never get lost.

A solid instructor for an intro stats course. She explains things in a way that you can understand. Sometimes it is still hard to keep track of everything you're learning but she does her best to keep it manageable. One of the better classes I've taken for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: best math teacher i have ever had. very easy going & she explains everything. i was scared to take a math class during a pandemic but her set up was by far the best of any of my profs. she made things super easy & made it asynchronous so i can do it on my time. wonderful teacher, really cares about her students. take her classes !!!!!
Really great lectures which made the course a lot more enjoyable.

She probably never learned that you learn the best from your mistakes. The dumbest part of this class was the practice exams. You could complete them up to 10 times but you never got to know what you got wrong. How am I supposed to learn from my mistakes if I don't know what mistakes I made? so I ended up doing bad on the exams. Also, no late work.

Professor fairborn is a great teacher! Her lectures are easy to understand, and the class itself is nothing too difficult. She gives great examples, and I was able to learn very well from her. I highly recommend her.

I took this class online and LOVED professor Fairbourn. She posted video modules for each week, breaking them into smaller submodules. She was very thorough with her teaching and used relatable topics to help you understand the material. Take advantage of the workbook because it is a fantastic reference as long as you followed along.

I never met her once because there were 1,800 other students taking this class this semester, but from her lectures she seems like a nice lady. She explains things easily, but I benefitted from putting the recorded videos on 1.5x speed.
The most understanding and personalble professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The GOAT. 1of1 professor.

Love this guy! The class was very easy, and there were only 4 assignments the whole time. Guys, please laugh at his joke of the day it makes me sad when people don't! Kinda quirky, but a very passionate teacher and someone who would help you in the future in a heartbeat.
Such an amazing professor! Genuinely made every lecture so engaging and enjoyable. He is so funny and goes out of his way to accommodate and help students, could not recommend him enough!!
He is the best. He is so nice and funny. He genuinely cared about each student. The class was so easy too.
He is so kind! This was such a fun class and I would definitely take it again

My favorite professor by far! He truly cares, adds humor to keep lectures engaging, makes students comfortable asking questions, and is always responsive to emails, even if you're a former student. He truly helped me love the class and want to be there and engaged. You have to write your name on a piece of paper when you go, but it's not mandatory.
George is AWESOME!! So helpful and truly just wants the best for everyone

George is one of my absolute favorite professors. Super engaging with the students and genuinely cares about his students' learning. You'll have to study for his exams but nothing too difficult. Also a little bit of homework but totally managable
Very respectful and has your best interest in mind. 190 is extremely easy.

I took this class only because Professor Harnick was teaching it, he is the best professor Ive had at MSU! He is so passionate, entertaining, and funny. All the content is super useful and he makes it easy to learn. If he makes a joke, LAUGH!!!
GEORGE IS MY GOAT. BEST KIN PROFESSOR IN THE DEPARTMENT.

When I say George is the best professor you will ever have that is an understatement. He is super nice and is really excited to teach his students. His work does require a bit of work but everything he assigned was pretty easy. If you have a question he will gladly answer it and help you if you don't understand something. George you are amazing.
I fking love George Harnick.

THE BEST PERSON EVER. he genuinely cares about every student, and he knew everyone in my class by name. though I only showed up to like 5 of the lectures, I still managed to 4.0 the class. most of the material is common knowledge. he is really passionate about kin and make the class interesting. I would go out of my way to have him again.

George made the class fun. He is very caring and respectful. He is also a good source for any information, KIN related or not. The class is half a semester long so a rather fast-paced class, but you learn a lot. It is also a pass/no pass grade. Attendance isn't mandatory but highly encouraged to get all the information and they are also fun.

George is awesome. Teaches you so much about the world of disabilities in the lab, and he is extremely patient and caring about both the participants and the students. Top three profs I've had at MSU.

Very passionate about his job and kinesiology in general, which makes it easy to pay attention in class and makes you actually want to go to class and learn. He is also a great source of information if you have questions about anything kin related, he's a huge help and always willing to answer questions.

George is THE best, if he makes jokes just laugh. The class is kind of annoying because you lecture for almost 2 hours once a week and then have a gym class for 50 minutes twice a week but it's a requirement so just do it. The exams are a mixture of easy and hard.

He is one of my favorite professors here at MSU. You can tell that he loves what he does and is very accommodating to students. The class is easy and the labs are super fun! It is not hard to do very well. The only thing i wish was different was better feedback on assignments especially our presentations from the labs!

Super amazing professor. He truly cares about his students and is genuinely a great guy. The class is the easiest I have taken ever. I studied one hour before the exam and scored above average. TAKE THIS COURSE WITH HIM!!!!

This class is a bit annoying because the recitations are basically a PE class, but the lectures are good and the material is interesting. Professor Harnick is a great and passionate lecturer who cares about us learning the materials. The class has three exams but he gives study guides that outline what it is on. Grades are very attendance based.

Prof. Harnick is an awesome guy. He has a great personality and is always happy during lectures. He is always open to asking questions, and loves engaging with students. Lectures are important, but the textbook will help you if you missed anything. The lab for this class was also super fun, literally just a high school gym class. Fun class overall!

Prof. Harnick was by far one of my favorite professors so far. I never missed a single lecture and he always knew when to give breaks. You can definitely tell he is passionate about what he does and knows how to teach the content. Notes are the most important part of the whole class and before an exam always study the exam review!
He was one of the best professors I've had at MSU. He really enjoys teaching and is very clear when teaching material. He's also super understanding and is super nice.
He is a professor that genuinely wants you to be successful!

Professor Harnick is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is super funny and I enjoyed going to class. It is a note heavy class, but he makes it easy to follow along and understand. Professor Harnick is super easy to reach outside of class and usually responds super fast. Overall, one of the best professors I've ever had

As course coordinator, I thought his weekly quizzes were rough since they have the same number of questions as the exams, and the exams also cover old material which was annoying (exam 3 covers material from exams 1 and 2). The quizzes caused so much un-necessary stress, and prioritized short term memorization over actual learning

Took online Fall 25 w/ in-person recitation. Excellent lecturer, explains things extremely clearly, obviously passionate about math and responds to Piazza questions/emails quickly. Didn't like how some units felt physics-heavy. Exams are pretty easy. Offers 4% extra credit, optional recitation. WW is heavy but it's the same across all sections.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Handwriting is a little tough to read and accent can be a bit distracting. Quizzes and midterms are cumulative, which is strange. Weekly quizzes were overly difficultly formatted. Textbook is written by him and is a free PDF, which is cool. Accepts late webworks for 90% credit until the end of the semester! Recitation is extra credit.

The professor himself is nice however the teaching is kind fof bad. He basically records his hand written notes (not like MacCombs he actually handwrites them) and all the videos are an hour long. But it takes you 2-3 hours PER video (3 times a week) to actually even write it down not understand it because he prefills and then reads right off it.

I took the online version and his recorded lectures weren't bad. He doesn't provide structure for the notes he just writes it all down on a blank page which makes it hard to take notes for at times. His handwriting can be hard to read, but you get used to it. He seemed nice enough. The class it hard, but I think he was a decent professor.
difficult to be difficult

Do not take for MTH 235. For a 3 credit course I found myself spending more time on webwork doing homeworks during the week versus previous Calc classes. All midterms are cumulutive and most quizzes often covered material from a couple chapters in the past. He makes the class require too much effort for a 3 credit math class supposed to be "easier"

the most boring class ive ever taken. pretty good lecturer though, it's just a lot of boring dull content as opposed to difficult content imo and the hardest part is getting through the lectures w/o falling asleep. posting on piazza feels like bracing to be patronized. easy exams reflective of lectures and quizzes, ww is way harder for some reason
Good lectures sometimes a little dull
lecture not very helpful and heavy on self-teaching

While he was very organized and never missed a single lecture, his teaching style is like an AI chatbot. He only describes the same basic overviews of course topics over and over again and rarely shows the class how to solve problems that may appear on exams and WebWork. He is way too broad in his explanation of things and expects a lot.

This professor has a thick accent but you'll get used to it fast. This class is very self-taught, your expected to watch video lecture and complete accompanying lecture notes before attending the actual lecture, which is quick review. It's not ideal for this kind of class.

If you are coming in as a freshman and did not do any math over the summer do not take this class. He does have an accent but which can make it hard to understand him sometimes but if you focus you can understand him decently but the main problem is that he does not explain things well at all, he just does the math and kinda moved on right away

Professor Nagy was great given the circumstances. Lectures broke things down into simple steps. VERY exam/quiz heavy class, and lots of homework. The class focuses heavily on "concept" understanding and not actual problems, which makes it difficult to know what to study. However, my TA was wonderful and probably the reason I did so well.

terrible class, terrible professor. not one person i knew did well in the class. hard to understand- topics from lecture and recitation do not match. no feedback on any test. TA's were clueless as well
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Could be very snarky when students asked questions about the course setup. Used a lockdown browser unfortunately. 3 lectures a week and a quiz or midterm every week. At least two webwork assignments every week. Generally just a lot of work for the course. Unfair quizzes with written response questions each worth 20% of quiz/midterm grade.

Expect LOTS of time to be spent on this class. the class is passable as long as you know where to look for help. piazza response times are quick which is nice to ask questions. most of the homework problems have a solved example problem in the textbook when lecture notes don't help. it's as difficult as you would expect a 200 math class to be.

Class is doable if you expect minimal help and can learn by yourself via outside resources. Prof wrote the textbook for the class so that sucks. He will respond to piazza posts, but it will probably be a rude or snarky comment, nothing of actual use or helpfulness. Doesn't really seem to care if students pass, but did end up curving final grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nagy was always quick to answer questions and I thought his class as a whole was very fair. His lectures were pretty boring but it's differential equations so you can't expect much. If you do the homework and look at the textbook for examples, you will be fine in the class. Quizzes and exams were pretty easy to predict and fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Just a lot of material is covered. Study a week in advance for quizzes and exams

Absolutely wonderful class. I was in the honors section and loved how interesting our deep dives were, especially the last one on quantum mechanics. Differential equations is not my preferred mathematical poison, but the course was fun and not too hard. Many chances to score bonus or extra points. You don't need to go to class, just read the book.

His lectures were near impossible to figure out, no matter what I did I didn't seem to be able to dig myself out of this class, would absolutely recommend going with another professor for 235. No hate to Nagy as an individual he seemed like a cool guy, but just nit my favorite teacher.

Nagy makes the online lectures, and the videos can be difficult to understand and are often an hour or longer. The class itself is hard because it is Calc 4. Lots of homework every week through Webwork and the usual weekly quiz like most math classes at MSU. Not my favorite professor but not my least favorite professor.

Nagy was a good professor. Super quick response time on piazza and email. Nice grading structure. Lectures can be a bit boring, but not too bad. He is a nice genuine person. Most of the quizzes and exams were very fair. Overall a good professor that I would recommend.

This class was very well organized and all of the lectures are put on D2L so you don't actually have to attend any lectures. I thought he was really good at explaining the concepts but most of it can be self-taught. Tests and quizzes can be tough but they are based on the homework and lecture quizzes so if you do well on those they aren't bad.

Not the best at pure teaching but otherwise pretty great.
- Well organized class
- Reasonable Exams, quizzes and grading
- Was possible to self teach using the internet and the homework

Not that bad of a choice if you don't care for lectures and would rather teach yourself the material.

Textbook was a PDF written by the professor that kinda sucks

this class is hard and the prof is semi-helpful. Lectures are pretty clear but they move fast and prof is passive aggressive if you need help on homework. Quizzes every week and exams are HARD so prep yourself to cry

Professor Nagy is mediocre in my view. Lectures were lackluster and the tests were tougher than they needed to be (though not horrible). On the other hand, we were given a 2% extra credit opportunity which was very generous and the course is very well organized. If I had to take the class over again I wouldn't take it with him if possible.

The class and content is difficult. I was able to do well by watching all of the lectures, and never used any outside additional help. By only watching the lectures I obtained a 4.0 and asked him for a favor once and he provided it. For those reasons I think he is a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Nagy, Oh professor... The lecture videos were extremely dull and long, making it almost impossible to pay attention. He also was very rude to the students making it seem like he definitely didn't want to help them. Many students did not make it through the semester, as he tests HEAVY on things we barely covered/learned right before exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nagy always was able to answer your question in the class forum. It doesn't mean that he was nice about it. There was usually a "you're dumb" tone to his responses. To be fair he usually gave useful feedback. If he cares about how his class does he does not do a great job of showing it.

I emailed him about an exam problem and how I don't remember covering it and asked him what unit it was so I could study, and he almost cussed me out because "he's tired of people" I apologized to him. Then he kept emailing me till I agreed with him it was a fair problem
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Nagy was always answering my questions on piazza within a reasonable time and he will answer follow up/ clarification questions as well. His lectures are pretty straight forward, I highly recommend printing out his notes and following along with his lecture.

I have taken this class online with this professor and all I can say is that this professor has proven over and over again to be outwardly rude and arrogant to students asking for help, as well as making attempts to embarrass them. The course itself has a heavy workload with multiple video quizzes weekly as well as section quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took his DiffEq class, was it hard? Yes. Did I have to work hard for my grade? Yes. Is he a great professor? YES! Prof Nagy has a propensity to explaining complex topics in an elegant way, simply put, if you pay attention during lectures and do the homework, you'll be fine.
Nagy is the best math professor I've had at MSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great guy. Replies to emails quick and always willing to help. Definitely a lot of homework and quizzes but that is expected for a math class and it would be really difficult to understand if you werent forced to practice. Lectures are all you really need for the homework assignments but the book (he wrote it and its FREE) has some extra examples

Notes are very proof based. Could definitely make his own notes but basically copies word for word from the textbook. Class itself isnt too bad but with online format, and video quizzes (mini assessments after watching lectures), the class becomes a little longer. His videos also become longer ad you get into the semester. Should be a 4 credit clas
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This course is not difficult. The course was very consistent throughout the semester. The practice exams and quizzes were pretty similar to regular exams, with many opportunities to improve your grade if needed. It's not necessary to watch the videos, instead just use his electronic notes, much easier and takes less time.

Gave an obscene amount of assignments, including four quizzes every week. Made TAs do most of the work and often refused to help students or respond to emails. Lectures consisted mainly proofs with a few examples. Didn't really seem interested helloing anyone succeed

I stopped attending class and hired a tutor. He is in charge of webwork so everything is done on webwork. If I did not have a tutor, I would not have passed this class. The MLC did not have any tutors that could help me in this class. Unfortunately he is probably better at teaching this class than any other professor at MSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The AMOUNT of school work we have to do throughout the week is unbelievable. TOO much work for a 3 credit class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: No, just no. Very mediocre, does NOT care about your grade and success. Dont take the class online, he doesnt do anything and he just makes his TAs do all the work for him.

This professor is mediocre at best. The lectures will contain almost entirely proof and sometimes during lectures when students have asked questions, he refused to answer at the time. The exams are very tough especially because the multiple-choice will be like "Choose all that Apply" with no partial credit which was unfair for a test quesiton.

Textbook was only used for honors projects, but he also supplied it as a PDF for free, which was GREAT. Class is tough, and you definitely don't want to skip. His lectures were dull, but very well organized and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great guy. His lectures are kind of dull but are good. This class is very doable but has lots of webwork to do. My one complaint is that he didn't finish the practice test until the day before the midterm both times, which was annoying for everyone who didn't want to wait until the last minute to study.

Very intelligent and its clear he knows what he is talking about. Has an accent but still easy to understand. Lectures are boring and can be difficult to sit through. Still can learn a lot from his lectures though. So much webwork. If his lectures improved, he'd be an easy 5 star.

He reads directly from the book that he wrote. There are a significant amount of quizzes on webwork, that you get to take up to 3 times. While his lectures are not good, you are given enough homework and assignments to pass. All of your exams are done AT LEAST 50% on webwork. The final is 100% on webwork. Do you webwork and you will pass
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He just reads off the notes
He was excellent at explaining topics! Best math professor ever!

Very intelligent but lectures are very boring. Has an accent, but he is very easy to understand. All of the material is found online and you can learn it that way much easier. Overall, my TA was fantastic, so that helped a lot as well. Quizzes are easy, exams are a bit harder.
When proving something goes wrong.... "and then your toast" Really enjoyed his class :)
great guy
Hard to understand. Smart guy but not much help when it comes to learning. Better learn how to teach yourself.

While the grading guidelines were VERY forgiving and allow almost unlimited retakes, Urquhart is just a bit confusing to understand when it comes to lecture as he always seems a little confused/lost. Poor guy is also very stressed out. Otherwise he's a great professor and teaches very interesting material!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor!  Really loves the content he teaches and has a passion for it. He was always understanding of circumstances and gave clear criteria of what was expected of his students.

Dr. Urquhart is a great professor! His class is very straightforward, he makes it clear what is expected of students. He really cares about student success, and even offered my class an opportunity to get points back on an exam we had a low class average on. Very caring prof!

Dr. Urquhart is great! He is super approachable and happy to answer questions. He tries to make lectures fun and usually we get out early. The class is straight forward and has a pretty light work load. Exams are mainly free response with some multiple choice. He offers a few extra credit opportunities too. Good class, great teacher!

Had fisheries and wildlife 101 with prof U (the course code was unavailable), online in the summer so maybe that's why the class was as lecture heavy as it was but I've taken other summer classes and this one was not it. 4-5 different hour long lectures a week. Easy class but I hated the long boring lectures. He is accommodating too which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I was out for mono for 3 weeks and Dr. U completely excused me from all lab assignments I missed. very short lectures then complete worksheets in class. Leave about an hour of time for pre classes, they're recorded lectures that you have to take notes on. tests mostly short answer, some multiple choice.

Dr Urquhart was one of my favorite professors at Briggs. He was so caring and he was focused on making sure everyone understood the material and were doubting themselves. The tests are a little difficult, but if you study the right material they were not bad. I wish I could have him for all of my Lyman Briggs classes

I did not have him as a professor although I turned to him for help as he is the assistant dean of lyman briggs. He offers amazing help.  If you have any issues in lyman briggs I highly suggest turning to him first as he knows what he is doing. I only have good things to say about Urquhart as he is amazing and very knowledgeable.
Lecture format was great, interesting topics. Exams were always straightforward and easy to pass. Do the pre-class assignments and study for the exams and it is an easy A.

A great professor! There are quite a bit of assignments for this course, but they are not hard at all. A few papers, weekly Cengage assignments which are unlimited attempts, and the exams. As long as you do your work you should get an A. overall a great professor whose caring, flexible, and wants to see his students succeed.

He was AMAZING! I loved going to this class not only because I love bio but because he truly made it fun and entertaining. His lectures were full of personal stories and videos and his exams were not hard. He gave out a study guide and if you put effort into that you had no issues. He really made my life easier and I learned a lot.
Professor Urquhart really cares about his students. I love this class and he makes the class really easy to understand.

Dr. U is an awesome biology professor! It is clear how much he cares about the subject, and he makes the class very doable. Tests are based almost exactly off presentation slides. Get ready to hear a lot about his trips to Nicaragua! Lots of extra credit is offered which is beneficial when the end of the semester creeps up on you!

Dr. U was by far the best professor I have had here. He made LB 144 a breeze. He provided note outlines from which he made all of his test questions. Don't bother buying the book. He told us exactly what to study for the exams. He gave an insane amount of extra credit so I didn't even have to worry about the final. Dr. U sets you up for success.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: amazing

He is extremely smart and try to be as clear as possible. if there is something you do not understand he will work with you to figure it out. In the class I had I could turn in hmk a week late for 10% less credit and turn it in a week before finals for 50% less credit! There is something very attractive about him too.

Dr. U was probably one of my favorite professors this semester. He clearly explains all of the material and if you as a question, his response is very clear. He is also a great person and interesting to talk to.
Definitely one of my favorite professors, will help you with problems, and has more personality than most professors.

Dr. Urquhart is awesome!!! He teaches exactly enough to make you understand, just go to class and pay attention. He lets students (like me) work on special projects with him outside of class, and even has class field trips!!! 4.0'd the class easy. Just beware of 155's chem portion.

Ms. Griffin was great! Always very positive and easy to talk to. Explained things fairly well and color-coded almost all of her work. Only expected you to know the things you should know going into a college math course. Gave us so much extra practice like her own additional exam review & answer key.

Literally the worst class I've ever taken in my life. Profesor Griffin is extremely harsh and shows lack of care for students. There's a good chunk of homework, but it's only worth 10% of your grade. I can't believe I even passed this class.

I would do everything to get out of this course. To her credit she does give you a lot of resources, but her lectures are extremely fast paced, and it's difficult to comprehend the material she gives you. The bigger issue is the structure of the course as recitation is basically just a place to take exams and test tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Griffin is very quick in lectures and follows the syllabus strictly. After reviewing the videos, webwork, and practice problems on D2L, my grades improved. I would highly recommend doing all the possible "learn it" and "practice it" objectives in D2L. She does teach new material right before an exam when the new material isn't on the exam :/

Won't talk to you about grades, tells you not to email her over many things, talks really fast and you can't understand her, is basically the only one who teaches this class at available times and is so bad I had to take her class twice.
She is very nice and super outgoing. A very fast-paced class but if you come in with prior knowledge you should be totally fine.

Griffin is nice and approachable, but she moves quickly through lectures. She speaks fast and only leaves notes on the screen for 15 seconds. The course includes WebWork hw and quizzes every recitation. Unlike other professors, she rarely holds math exam reviews, so I usually attend Allen's review sessions. I would definitely recommend Allen.

Although it is a fast paced course, Ms. Griffan does a great job throughly explaining material and her videos on D2L and extremely helpful. Go to your lectures and put in the work outside of class and you'll be fine (coming from someone not good at math).

RUN from this professor. She rushes through everything in class and in her videos, but at least you can pause those. She solves problems without explaining the steps or giving students time to try them. Recitations were basically just quizzes and tests.
Please for your sake avoid at all costs.

Talks too fast during lectures and has NO REVIEW during any of the lectures. Even when an exam is coming up, she will be teaching new information you need to know that wont even be on the upcoming quiz/exam. Be ready for a quiz or exam every week. Wouldn't recommend.

The class of MTH 103 itself is bad, not necessarily the professor, but regardless she did fly through the lessons VERY quickly, according to MSU-grades there was a 25% fail/drop-out rate last semester, i got through the course with a 2.5, although barely. Unless your already very comfortable with Algebra, you will likely struggle.
Very clear explanations during lectures and videos. Very strict with syllabus.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Ms. Griffin's a nice lady, she is engaging in the lectures. But she talks very fast and seems to rush through things. Some units are easier than others but attending the lecture is a massive help to understanding the content.
You WILL feel like you're drowning. She moves too fast to understand a thing. You're better off skipping lectures and teaching yourself, honestly.

Griffin herself is a good and nice person, but teaching MTH 103 is hard because there is so much content to shove into one semester. avoid taking 103 with all you possibly can, and if you must take it, just know it will be your hardest course even if you were decently proficient in math in highschool.

I thought Dr. Griffin was a great instructor for a beginning math course. She has good lectures and is very involved during class. Although attendance isn't require, all the quiz and exam information are from lecture, so I would advise you to go if you want to pass.

I took her MTH 103 lecture/recitation and I failed. I retook it this semester with a different professor and got a 4.0. I missed a quiz because I was sick. I went to spectrum and got a note. I sent it to her and her response was that I needed to be hospitalized in order to retake the quiz. Doesn't teach, just has you READ about MATH.
Very kind teacher. Her videos are very helpful. Don't be afraid to attend her office hours to get extra help if you are struggling or just have questions!

Attend her office hours!!! Ms. Griffin is there to help you and is willing to help you learn if you put in the effort. I hate math but Ms. Griffin helped me find the confidence in myself to do well and learn. For a hard course she is a very kind and understanding teacher. She will push her students, but she does care about how you do.

God forbid you miss one class you are behind for the whole semester. She is a nice woman but is not very good at teaching. She just writes down everything barely explains it at least enough for others to understand. You better hope you get a good TA because that is your only chance of understanding this class.

Did not attend one single lecture and still managed a 3.5. The videos are really helpful, as well as the recitation activities, reviews and worksheets. Not a complicated class if you have taken algebra 2 or precalc/calc in high school. Dropped one of the quizzes (every week during recitation). easy to talk to outside of class and my TA was perfect
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do yourself a favor and take MTH103 A and B. I know more people who failed this class than I do who passed, including myself. Second round taking it, and it is hardly easier. Quizzes every Friday, four exams, tough grading criteria, and SO MUCH HW! Unless you pick up math like a second nature I DO NOT recommend.

I missed one class at the beginning of the semester and never was able to get back on track because she covered entire units in each lecture. She speeds through it like she's got places to be. There were several occasions where she straight-up invented new math terms. She uploads videos explaining each lesson on D2L, but they're absolutely useless.

Mth 103 is a hard class for anyone, Professor Griffin does the best she can. She cares about how you are doing and cares about the class. She wants you to pass and gives you the best tips in the short amount of time that is given for lectures. My TA is terrible tho.

yes I did poorly but she was a professor that I couldn't learn from. I had my friends in high math classes help me and they said the way she thought was backwards. I would highly recommend you pick a different professor

The course is hard(multiple homework assignments due weekly, quiz/exam at almost every recitation,  lots of notes). Although it can be challenging, Ms. Griffin is so sweet and helpful if you take advantage of her as a resource. I went to her office hours every week, and she always made sure I understood the concepts.
If you want to pass don't take this class. Doesn't explain anything, goes over 5+ lessons in 50 mins. Quiz every Friday.
If you can't deal with a fast paced environment, go for 103A&B
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: JUST DO YOURSELF A FAVOR AND TAKE MATH 103A&B. Professor Griffen was okay, but she didn't really teach, just gave us skeleton notes. I'm begging you to just take a&b. All the teachers are like this.

Not good. Goes WAY too fast and does not explain concepts thoroughly. I along with other students just watched the videos on D2L and basically learned the material ourselves. Very thankful my TA was helpful and knew what he was doing and actually explained the concepts to us. Just bad. Terrible. Would not recommend this professor to ANYONE.

She's very sweet but also knows what she's doing, she'll do pop up attendances if she sees a lack of students in her lectures, and likes to interact with us. I would take her classes again for sure. The main issue I have with her is that she goes fast, which sometimes isn't her fault, and her d2l can be hard to navigate through.
Doesn't teach or explain. She simply just tells and writes it down. This class was absolutely horrible

The class material is incredibly difficult, especially for an entry-level class, though that isn't Professor Griffin's fault. She talks SUPER fast, and doesn't go back to repeat problems, so your attention better be focused.

Dr. Griffin gets a lot of unnecessary slander because she teaches mostly freshmen. Dr. Griffin's teaching style is very clear and makes sense if you go to class. Attendance is mandatory if you want to pass, but I got away with missing a few and was fine. All tests are in person, paper pencil, during recitation. Easy to reach outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Griffin is a very kind and funny professor and I really enjoyed her personality. However, I feel as though maybe it's the combination of her talking fast + her teaching a very fast paced course that made me struggle. Quizzes are nearly every week, and they don't look at all like the webwork/notes. Grading policy is very good though.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This lady is the goat. I never even had her as a professor, but she was the one who created all of the online notes for my class. She went through the lessons really well in the videos. My teacher often went too fast with the notes in class, so it was nice having her online lessons to help me understand much easier.

Griffin is very nice, but as someone who excelled in math before college, this class was unreasonably hard, especially in terms of quizzes. We go over topics very fast and she often skips review problems that would have made homework and quizzes so much easier. Most people don't even show up because the online resources teach much better.
Never again.

This class gets a bad rap because it's taken mostly by freshman who are new to college classes. Don't get me wrong, it's fast paced, so in order to succeed you need to put in the work. Go to office hours weekly. Go to the math learning center! Ask questions in recitation. The ULA's are there to help! Mrs. Griffin wants to see her students succeed..

Griffin is a very nice lady, she definitely cares for her students and is willing to accomodate, but she is not a great teacher. I really struggle with math and I'm worried about failing, although I frequently go to lectures and office hours. Her exams and quizzes are really difficult and sometimes not what the review material is like.

MTH 103 has quizzes or tests every week during recitation. Griffin is kind but it's a huge lecture with like 100 people so don't think about asking questions until your recitation. She loves what she does but goes through extremely quick, and rarely goes back if you missed anything. Good luck but it's college algebra so it's not too hard.

Ms. Griffin was a very straight forward gal.  She made it clear that her job was to simply teach.  There is a quiz every week in recitation, so don't miss it.  There is a lot of partial credit offered on exams and quizzes so write down everything you can for more points.  It is homework heavy but if you get it all done it helps boost your grade.

although she seems like a very genuine person, it is very hard to understand this class if you are not a math person. she moves extremely fast, and you take notes the entire class period. there is a quiz almost every week, and they are tough. when taking notes, there is no explanation, you are just expected to know how to do the problems.

Math 103 should not be this challenging. I passed this class by 3 points. The professor was nice and willing to help but her quizzes and exams were never like the homework or the reviews. Honestly, save yourself the money and choose a different professor, other classes seemed to have a better success rate...
Very nice, funny professor but she is not a very good instructor. Her lectures are frustrating and confusing. I found myself learning better when i taught it to myself.

I am not good at math to begin with, however even my friends who were good at math struggled in this course. Ms.Griffin is so kind and funny but her course is difficult, again math is not my strongest category. Be sure to review class notes, and pay attention to the reviews given by TA before quizzes and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Taking this class Fall of 2023 there was an issue with resources available to help all the students who were struggling. Just look up this teacher's average grades the past few years on msugrades, the average never went above a 3.0. At this point, this is a curriculum issue, grading. Im sure she is a good woman at heart just not meant to teach.

This class gives no credit other than homework, quizzes, and very heavily weights exams. There is no credit given for attendance or participation. Professor moves incredibly quickly and does not stop for questions. Does lecture notes byd and her hand blocks the projector camera. No time to copy notes. Very challenging if not a math person.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For the love of God be weary of taking this class. I came in as a confident freshman and left as a broken man. While Mrs. Griffin is nice and caring as a person, the math curriculum along with her lectures is bound to fail you.
Good luck!  Hardest class at MSU

Don't take this class unless you hate yourself It's so hard and the professor makes it even worse. She is a horrible teacher in lectures she goes way too fast it's almost impossible to keep up with her. There is way too much homework for one student to keep up on. This class is so time-consuming there is also a quiz every Friday.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not a bad teacher, just teaching a hard class. Homework multiple times a week, with quizzes and exams every Friday. Extremely fast passed class making it very hard to understand the topics enough to pass the quizzes.
Her lectures are very fast-paced. A lot of homework on Webwork and weekly quizzes. Great person, she's just a tough teacher.

Nice lady but with class she goes through problems very fast and doesn't quite explain them well. Class is test heavy. Tricky test problems worth a lot of points for short amount of questions. If u r an incoming freshman, I would honestly take Susan Allen's class.I had to go to her lecture just to better understand the work. She's much better.
She was just mean
lecture heavy and test heavy

Dropped this class about midway through the semester as it was horrible. This professor speeds through lectures and will on the regular ignore students raising their hands. The homework she assigned was completely different than other classes of 103 and much more difficult. I had an easier time in my asynchronous 103 than here.

The class is very fast-paced, but she offers office hours for multiple days every week. Listen... you need to go get help outside of class, that's the only way you will pass this class. Overall, she is a very nice lady.

Attendance is mandatory and she will go out of her way to make sure it is taken again if too many people leave the room. A large portion of your grade relies on the 4 Exams (granted you drop one). She allows crib sheets during exams for examples, definitions, etc. Personality wise, she's a nice lady, but you have to be on top of your work.

Professor Griffin is a sweetheart - nevermind all the freshmen reviewing her. As a junior, she is amazing. She talks fast because the courseload is heavy - she stays after class to help and discusses everything in detail as needed. She offers a ton of office hours to help if you need it, too. Reach out if you need help!
Her class was much more difficult than the other math 103 sections
she talks so fast its almost impossible to keep up with lectures while filling out notes
Ruthless- she will rip you apart. Be prepared to work hard.

Goes way too fast and will not slow down or answer any questions during lecture. Homework load is absurd considering this is entry level algebra. No make ups and no retakes. She will not do a single thing to help you pass her class... in fact she will make it easy to fail. Tests are difficult and her video reviews don't help in the slightest.
she goes too fast and will not allow makeups for tests/quizzes even if you are sick.

She goes quickly through the lecture. You need to pay attention because like all other math courses you will need to be able to apply the information you learned to other problems. She makes some jokes in class that keep you engaged. If you have trouble with pacing they offer 103A and 103B for a reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Griffin is definitely my hardest professor. You would think that college algebra would be easy, right? This is a very hard class, even though I go to every lecture, I complete all of my homework, and spend nearly 2.5 hours in the math learning center every night. She is nice, but not very understanding. Her exams are very difficult.

She goes through lessons pretty fast in order to get everything done in the 50 minute lectures. The class wouldn't be terrible if the exams and quizzes were worded similarly to the lesson notes and homework.
I love her
She literally moves so fast you wont learn anything by going to lecture

She talks to fast in lecture she doesn't go over a lot of the stuff you see on exams and quizzes you have to buy a subscription to web work and the homework you are assigned there are nothing like what you see on quizzes and exams. Overall just pick a new professor for math 103

Awful lectures, sped through with no care for students and for what? I have to pay for this? I don't even bother taking notes anymore, just show up to the lecture for the attendance credit. My ULA (Chen) is worse, confuses the entire class with her reviews before the exam. When we ask questions we are told "it just is." Should be online only.

This class was the only class I got a 3.5 in during my freshman year. This class progressively gets more difficult throughout the semester, despite being about topics I already learned in high school. There is a learning center available, and I regret not taking advantage of it. For me, the amount of time given on the exams were not enough.

She seemed nice but I went to every lecture and still failed the exams. The class was unnecessarily hard, it's been my worst class at MSU so far. I thought chemistry and calculus were much easier to pass.

Very very bad class, the professor did not teach well, as she went too fast, and did not care for students trying. The webwork is worth a really small amount of the grade, and the quizzes and exams are worth the rest, and they are not even related to the content being taught, Don't waste your time. Go or not go to the lectures, you will still fail.

Well How About the fact that the class average was a 2.0 for the course in the fall. More people have failed this class under her than any other Math 103 prof at MSU. Don't waste your Brain Cells in her class. Especially don't waste the time and money doing Math at MSU. Go to LCC so much better!!

I absolutely love Ms. Griffin. I think many students anticipate her classes to be easy and they are if you attend class. She is very accessible to students, helpful, and really cares about her students. She is a teacher who pays attention to her students and knows who cares about her class and who doesn't! Reach out to her and connect!
You will be teaching yourself this course by yourself seven days a week. VERY test heavy. Four exams with one drop (fall 2021) that are all worth 66.7% of your grade. Webwork is useless.

The form of application used on homework is the complete opposite of the tests, and because of this I was always reteaching myself how to do the material just to complete some questions that didnt help me prepare for exams.
Literally awful, prayers to the ones who will take her class. She made me wanna rip my hair out. The actual worse.
worst teacher ever

The math department at MSU is honestly messed up. This is the only class I would study for, had a tutor, went to every lecture, did the notes and all the homework and still couldn't manage to get better than a D in this class which that was even hard for me to get. I learned more from my RA teaching me in the study room at 2 am than I did in class
Not much to say just read the ratings. Homework and lectures don't prepare you for the exams. its just a struggle to learn and do anything well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not much to say you can put in all the work in the world into this class and fail.

Had her fall 2021 online. I thought her lecture videos were okay because my math teacher in high school taught like Griffin, but I dont feel like I can ask the questions I need to, being online. This was definitely a class for students that can take initiative to study on their own and often.

Worst class I have ever taken. I entered this course with math being not only my strongest subject but also my favorite, unfortunately, I will be leaving the course with a hatred for it that I never thought was possible. The exams and quizzes are much harder than any of the material presented in the lectures. Props to you if you actually pass.

The tests and quizzes are harder than the material learned and the professor is not very accommodating. This year we had 2 quiz grades dropped as well as a test, this may sound like enough I am not sure I personally know anyone that is happy with their grade in this class. Professor Griffin is nice during lectures but does not meet people halfway.

Terrible professor. I'm usually a straight A student and now I probably won't pass this class. Her exams are extremely hard, so much homework, and her lectures aren't helpful at all. Won't respond to emails, won't help students. Seems like she wants us to fail. Avoid taking her at all costs. Worst professor ever.
If you pass haha I will be shocked. Not worth the time or money spent. I will be retaking this class somewhere else. Please stop using web work its not worth it!!

There is a lot of lectures and readings so if you take this course make sure your semester is has 4 classes including this one.
