Professor Veit is a great professor but the ways she structures the class is stupid. The GPA Requirement to get a 4.0 is 94% which is already high paired with the fact that you have 7 Unit Exams and a Final it's quite hard to get a 4 unless you get an A on every exam. The final is also cumulative of all 7 units and you aren't given a study guide.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: While I enjoyed the class it was overwhelming at times. You will have a test per section along with a final exam, recitation and lecture quizzes that will be the bulk of your grade. I did well on them but I feel like its almost impossible to get a 4.0 in the class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Veit is one of the best professors at MSU. Expectations are clear and easy to follow. There's a strict no-tech policy in class, and although it may seem strange, it was super beneficial. She is very passionate about what she does, and I would encourage everyone to take her class. Exams and quizzes are VERY easy as long as you pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I adore Professor Veit! She's one of the best professors I've had. She holds students to high standards and fosters engagement with her no-tech policy, which helped me connect with amazing peers. This class isn't an easy A—you'll work hard—but it's so worth it. I'd 100% recommend her to anyone seeking a challenge and meaningful connections!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great professor, amazing class. She really knows how to teach a subject. Great at encouraging discussion among students, great at encouraging thoughtful engagement with the subject. Yeah she's a tough grader, but it makes you want to work harder at it. Don't do it if your handwriting sucks like mine, it's all paper.

Professor Veit was the worst History professor I have had at MSU. I received the worst grades in any class I have ever taken at MSU, and it's not due to my work. She holds students to a ridiculously high standard. No electronics in class (not even before class) means everything, but papers are handwritten. If your handwriting sucks, do not take her
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The material in this course is so eye opening, everyone at MSU should have a class like this. Professor Veit is very passionate about the subjects, but she is an EXTREMLEY tough grader. This class is also extremely heavy in projects and readings, but most of them are interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Veit is generally a great teacher she cares a lot about the things she teaches and she cares about the atmosphere of the class room as well. She is a bit quirky but honestly, it makes the class entertaining, one of our big assignments is to recite a poem. But overall I would highly suggest her!

Taking History of Food and Alcohol with Prof Veit was great. She's very knowledgeable on it, she provides very interesting topics to discuss, and class was always enlightening. Just don't skip, because she has quizzes every week or two and you don't know when exactly they are. Homework outside of class is minimal, probably 2 hours a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This was an honors section, but either way this class was HARD. So much reading assigned. Also be prepared to write any paper with the rubric side-by-side. She's a tough grader. But she's knowledgeable and insightful. The topics she chooses are so interesting. I totally recommend taking a class with her, but just know you have to PUT IN THE WORK
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Veit is extremely opinionated. If you do something she doesnt like, your grade will reflect that. She is close minded and unreasonable. Dont take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Veit is by far the best professor I've had at MSU. She is very knowledgeable and makes the information so interesting. Fantastic teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's a great professor that makes learning boring American history more exciting. I wouldn't say its an easy course, you will have to work for your A but it doesn't seem like too much work. Actually really enjoyed her and HST 202.
She is very knowledgeable and she presents information in a very interesting way.
AWESOME professor.  Not very interested in History before taking the class and she made it interesting. The best professor I had this year! Take her class, I hope to have her again!

Fantastic Professor! She was always interested in the subject matter and everything was very clear. Show up, do you work, participate and you will have the 4.0 no problem. I easily 100'd my midterm because of the study guide she provided, and I would not consider myself an exceptional student by any means. Awesome awesome awesome prof!
As long as you show up and do the assignments, you're good.

She is very clear on what will be on the tests and how they will be laid out, and she gives some freedom on how to write your papers. The only bad thing is that she goes through the lecture really fast and it can be hard to keep up. She also puts a lot of minutiae into her lectures, i think to throw you off. Good prof tho.

Great Professor! This class was so much fun and very interesting. I never got bored during one of her lectures. Very clear on what to study, she even gave out study guides. I hope to take many more of her classes in the future! Highly Recommended!

enjoyable class, funny sarcastic prof! difficult material but she explains it in a way that's easily digestible. wish there was more homework to boost my grade because the exams are kinda hard! i've learned so much cool stuff about animal behavior so far! she calls on people sometimes, if that makes you anxious maybe avoid eye contact lol!

She is clearly very passionate about this subject and I found the lectures very interesting and useful. I wish there had been more opportunities for homework or other study materials as I felt like I needed to review every single thing mentioned in class to get a good grade on exams, which made studying take very long.

She is not a nice lady. Her classes are very difficult to grasp information and give notes that are very difficult to study. She talks unprofessionally about other professors. And she is disrespectful to her students. She makes you feel very small. She is not nice when you come to her to help or any advice on how to succeed in this course.

This class was fairly hard, but I really enjoyed it. She talks really fast but is really receptive to feedback and if she needs to slow down. She's super sarcastic which I think can come across as rude but whenever I met with her one-on-one she was super helpful and wanted us to learn the material.

Difficult to receive helpful feedback due to her rude manners. Unable to ask questions in class without a snarky remark. Pulls the most niche/hard topics from lectures to use on the exams. Very clear she is not passionate about educating and would prefer only to do research. Overall, she creates a poor, hostile learning environment for students.

Not enough grading opportunities to accurately judge a student's ability on the subject at hand. His lectures also follow a random pattern with no chance to study correctly due to his lack of assignments and withholding proper study materials, such as the slides.

ISS 320 consists of three exams, 1 extra credit opportunity for 5 points (usually a random lecture midday on a weekday) Exams are poorly written, shows up late, gives indirect answers to questions, and studying effectively is nearly impossible because he doesn't post slides. Goes on unrelated political rants. Exams are opinion-based, not an easy A.

I was so surprised to see negative reviews on Dr. Hourani. He was truly one of my favorite professors, and while his classes are reading heavy, he is very patient and understanding. If you make an effort and have open communication with him about any problems, you will do well in this class. He is engaging and makes the class feel connected.

He is a good professor, but he expects a lot from his students. There are at least two readings per week (and I mean long scholarly readings). Most of the class periods are discussions so I would at least skim the reading because he does call on people. He is very knowledgeable but not the best at communication basically never tells you your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is not a bad person, but not a great teacher. Never tells you your grades and the readings are impossible unless you have prior experience with dense readings 20+ pages long.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Is this a professor for real or just a guy with ego trying to feel powerful and condescending on his student? I felt so abused in the class! Such low class IMO. Such incompetent's (teacher) I would say not a professor. Real Professors manners, they treat their student with respect and professionalism. We need better management in this "college".

I enjoyed Dr. Hourani's class a lot. I found the key was to take notes on any topic from the reading he mentioned in class. I thought he was usually pretty funny, but his exams were definitely a lot of work. The TA had given us a couple extra credit papers to write which def made the class easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took a course in "Special Topics in Urban Design and Urban Regeneration" with professor Najib in the German Jordanian University, and he is wonderful! Gives a lot of amazing readings, holds great discussions, he is very competent, really knows his thing. He gives great feedback and motivates everyone to do their best. Definitely taught me a lot.

If you are looking into whether or not you should take a class with this professor, consider yourself lucky that you went to rate my professor first. I studied my ass off for this class and barely came away with a passing grade. This is the type of teacher that would read this review and be proud of it. Heed my words, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!!

This was by far the worst class I have ever taken. Exams are tough, and the only thing you're graded on the class is exams! This class is very lecture heavy, and there are rarely any power points to look at. The Professor easily gets off topic for most of the class and the concepts he is teaching are very hard to grasp. Do not take this class!

This class is called "World Urban Systems", so if for some wild reason that's what you're expecting, do NOT take this class. The entire course content is up to the jurisdiction of whatever Dr. Hourani wants to talk about that day & issues/history in the Middle East. Hourani seems ok, but he is very closed-minded to those with opposing viewpoints.

Dont get me wrong he is a good guy (hence 2 not 1), but the class quickly transitions from Urban Planning to being a class about his interest in Islamic culture and "relevant" topics in the middle east. He says you wont pass if you do not read, but if you take good notes on the review sheets you will pass the exams with ease. I would NOT recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not a good professor I recommend DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!! He is the worst professor I have ever had and that is not an exaggeration. When you think you've done everything you can do to pass, professor Hourani finds a way to write a test that you are not prepared for. I was an honor student, don't make the same mistake I did. (I actually took ISS 320 but it wasn't an option)

I took ISS 320 with him. The class itself was about "urban planning." However, rarely have we talked about any cities, and when we did, we only talked about Arab cities. He has mentioned several times how he is from Lebannon and that is mostlyall we learned about: Lebannon and the Arab world. Only grades are 3 very difficult exams. I HATE HIM!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The reading load is heavy, and the exams are insane, but this class has been the best I've taken at MSU. If you want an old-fashioned course experience, take this class. No powerpoints or busy work, so if you want the easy way out take a different class. If you're interested in social & cultural theories  of anthro and you want to learn, take it.

I took his class based on the reviews here and he is a good teacher but he is kind of a dictator in the class. He gives lots of reading and you have to be ready for class discussions, the first exam was easy but the ones after that were hard. All I can say is keep up with the readings and GO to class most of the exams are from class discussion.
He's a really cool guy! But geography is not his thing. He should stick to antropology. Assigns a lot of readings and you have to be ready when you come to class, gives points for participation.
No Comments
He challenges you and makes you think. However, he's a bit scatter brained, quite disorganized, and often appears to be on the verge of a breakdown!
She's pretty good

She is not that bad. Sometimes she can be a little unclear or confusing, but overall it doesn't really matter since she grades so easily. Like a month into the class she started saying we can just talk in English for most discussions so that we can have better comprehension. She's also pretty kind and funny.

She's not as bad as the other reviews say, but she's definitely not great. Her class is pretty tough and there is a lot of online homework and participation is required for every class, but she's pretty leinent on grading essays, assignments, and there's no proper tests. She can be a little bit rude, but will give you help if you ask for it.

Definitely the worst spanish professor I have had here. She is unclear with directions, not understanding of personal life events, and makes fun of her students when they mess up pronunciation or spelling. She does not make learning this language enjoyable. I have considered no longer minoring in spanish because of her. Do not recommend.

This professor caused a lot of stress and frustration for me and my peers. She was very unclear about expectations during class time and would frequently make people feel uncomfortable by singling people out for not understanding what she thought was basic knowledge. She would also make fun of/mock our language skills and culture.

Easily the worst Spanish teacher I've had. She was consistently passive aggressive and abrasive with students and always had a condescending tone. She also often contradicts her own directions and is super unorganized.The class was easy but I learned so much more from things I did on my own outside of the curriculum. I do not recommend her.

She contradicts herself constantly and doesn't understand why students are confused. She will criticize and single people out, creating a judgmental and passive-aggressive environment. 
The class itself is fine. It's department-run so there is a lot of online homework. Being in class often felt redundant and pointless, but attendance is necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Her class itself was fairly easy, but she would give unclear/confusing instructions a lot of the time and get frustrated when we didn't understand. Also, her attendance policy is very confusing, and even when you are sick with a doctor's note there isn't much leeway.
Don't let these other positive reviews fool she is very passive aggressive, shifts blame, and not helpful at all.
Very difficult to deal with. Doesn't seem to understand her own attendance policy or her attendance form.

Very easy class. It is somewhat like high school because she will stop the lecture to tell someone to put way their phone. Very strict tardy policies and will even mark you late for being 30 seconds past. Other than that the class was easy and repetitive

Her SPN 202 class was a breeze tbh. The class had a lot of hw but besides that as long as you attended every class (besides your 3 skips) I don't see how you couldn't 4.0 because she gave ALOT of leeway on written and oral exams. A lot of people in that class probably couldn't conjugate into the past tense and she didn't really care Take her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Irma was a wonderful professor to have for my second semester at MSU. Her class was more tricky than I expected, but it was still one of my easiest classes that semester. She was an excellent teacher AND an excellent person, and I would love to have her as my professor again!

This is more of a warning for the actual SPN 202 class. It's department ran and a teacher is placed to teach the course. This means class will never be canceled as they can just find a replacement, skipping class requires filling out a form and all the homework is accuracy based. As for Bartolo, she's a nice person, just strict on participation.
Profe Bartolo was great! Would definitely recommend for students starting to learn spanish.
great professor
She was amazing. I almost wish I had to take Spanish again so I could be in her class again. If you need to take SPN 201 or 202, take her class.

Like any language class, you have to participate to pass the class. This isn't a negative but don't expect to sit quietly the whole sem. There is a lot of busy work, composed of short quizzes for reading comprehension. These are extremely redundant and, in my opinion, insufferable as a weekly thing.

I did enjoy this class, Irma was nice & funny and wasn't afraid to go off topic. A couple negatives were that there were a lot of assignments that were very time consuming & sometimes hidden, and some seemed opinionated but there was only one "right" answer which she refused to see otherwise, some directions were also confusing, but otherwise good

She is a really understanding professor that is supportive in the students efforts to learn Spanish. Shes patient and pushes participation to improve learning. The class is focused more on understanding in context rather than memorization.

Only graded on hw, in class assignments and attendance. No huge finals, just short speaking & writing tests that are about 80 -100 words. You are allowed 3 free absences and then everyone after that deducts 1% off of your grade. She really pushes for participation! The class is more conversation heavy rather than grammar. Overall great profesora!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: great teacher

Dr.H is funny, and stays after class to help people and is open to it. I asked to talk with him because I missed due to illness and he said no, thought that was weird but otherwise chill and communicating through email. I failed the class but I'd def take Dr.H again!

He uses tophat for attendance which you can do remotely. Overall if you attend lectures and recitation, understanding the content is really easy. Exams are a huge portion of the grade so you have to prepare for them. There's some extra credit built into the homework too.
Really well taught course. Dr. H is a good professor and makes this course easy to understand. Pretty easy 4.0 if you go to lectures and recitations.

He was a great stats professor. If you go to recitation and go to class everyday, you will do great! One thing that annoyed me was him letting people go early which was super distracting to people like me who stayed all of class. Overall, super easy math requirement with only 3 exams and a lot of extra credit offered to bump your grade 2.5%.
He is very nice. As far as a Stats class goes this one wasn't bad. He does a lot of things to help you succeed so just stay on top of your work and study for tests and you will be fine.

This class was sick! So to start off im one of those laid back chillers but me and hairy long lets just say we live on the wild side. To start off were both diabetics and we would wake up and shotgun dr peppers like dawgs and I swear me and the boys would be buzzing off the peps like no other. Will Long is a lifetime friend.Class is mid ngl.
He was a good professor
Great professor and very personable, as long as you pay attention in class, attend the recitations, ask questions, you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Go to his lectures and do the tophat participation questions. If you miss them, you can make them up the next week for full points. Would have probably gotten an A instead of B if I showed up to all his lectures

Friendly professor for STT200, down to earth and tries to make his lectures fun. Class becomes fast paced after first month. One hw assignment a week (hr to complete) and one recitation a week. Complete both and attend lectures and the exam material will come to you very easily. 2.5% grade boost for extra credit

Going to class is important because its easy to fall behind. Lots of extra credit. If you show up to lectures and recitations and do your homework and extra credit you will be fine. Tough grader however, Would not round me up .2 to next highest grade which was frustrating but like i said there is a lot of extra credit opportunities getting me close

He is a quick teacher, and there is a note-pack. Attendance is kind of mandatory since he asks questions on TopHat during the lecture, but he also has makeups for the attendance open for a week after. To succeed, stay on top of homework and do all extra credit after completing homework.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Don't need to go to class can do top hat makeups from home and still receive credit. 
Complete extra credit and an extra 2.5% is added to final grade. 
Course isn't hard go over lecture notes, he moves pretty fast.

STT 200 exams/curriculum is all the same but Dr. H is the right professor to choose. He is kind, funny, and very clear in lectures. Make summary sheets to make sure you remember everything. Extra credit can up your grade by 2.5%. Only one homework assignment/week. He posts all the lecture slides & info so don't worry about missing a few classes.

Dr. H was a very nice and friendly man, but I felt like his lectures were too fast paced and at times he didn't fully explain the material. I would go to study for exams and would teach myself the whole exam material the week before the test. The content was not difficult it just took time to learn. There are many resources to get help such as SLC.

Dr. H was a great professor and super down to earth. This class was so easy it literally just requires you to do the bare minimum of go to class and do the webwork. Lectures are only 50 minutes but are 3 days a week so it's a little annoying but nonetheless, super easy class and exams are EXACTLY like the study guides

Overall, I found Dr. H enjoyable to listen to and learn from. If you follow along in the textbook/workbook, you will not have a problem taking his class. The homework is almost entirely things learned in lectures, and he posts the lecture notes after every class in case you miss a lecture. I would recommend taking Dr. H.
I just could not understand the way he teaches. He would bounce around from page 30 to page 120 in the span of 5 minuets, lectures were all over the place.

Super clear lectures, accent isn't thick at all, don't worry! tests were hard, 3 exams, all non-cumulative which is good. Class gets really boring though. DEFINATELY recommend the printed lecture notes, you WILL need them.

Overall the course was easy as long as you attend lectures and get top hat points. I landed 0.33% below the 4.0 grade. I emailed Professor H and he proceeded to give me a 3.5. Just thought he would be more caring then that so make sure to do all extra credit homework assignments, may save you in the end!

Dr. H's lectures were a bit fast paced as the stats classes have to adhere to a strict schedule, but he'll post the lecture slides after and there's a stats help room as well. From what I heard, he's one of the stats professors who tends to cover content slower in comparison to the others. If you complete all the extra credit, you get 2.5% boost.
Dr. H is awesome!! He made the material very easy to understand, and he just is such a nice guy. He was my fave professor this semester. Would highly recommend!
So sweet and great at explaining. Every thing is so straight forward and coincides very well with the exams and homework. If you have to take STT200, make sure you have Dr. H.

Dr. H is a fantastic professor. His lectures were super easy to follow, there was not a lot of homework, and the 3 exams were super easy. You can tell he really cares about what he teaches and is always willing to help. If you go to recitation and class, it's an easy 4.0. There is also extra credit that adds a whole 2.5 percent to your grade.

This course requires a lot of time and effort, especially if you get stuck with a bad recitation teacher. I recommend going to the SLC if you're struggling because that was the only way for me to pass since the lectures were fast-paced and confusing. Exams are similar to practice exams and study guides, but the questions tend to try to trick you.

Overall, Dr. H was quite good, but occasionally his accent made it difficult for me to understand the material. Also, the lectures were fast-paced, as he tried to cover a lot of content along with the TopHat questions. However, the recitations were very helpful and managed to review most of the lecture material in just one hour.
Not a very organized lecturer. Rushes towards the end of lectures because he's on a timeline and things get lost in between. Overall, an easy course tho.

Dr. H was a fantastic professor for statistics. Attendance is mostly mandatory, there will be participation questions throughout the lectures but the points can be made up with extra credit opportunities that come every week. Very helpful and knowledgable. He basically gives you the exams beforehand so preparing for them is extremely easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. H's classes were amazing. He would randomly talk about little stories he has (mostly about his cats) and he would teach the content very well. Show up to Classes and Recitations, do the HW with the Extra Credit and do the practice papers before exams (they are EXACTLY like the actual test) and it's an easy 4.0. I ended up getting a 101.5%.

If you're taking STT200, defo take Dr. H. I had a great time in his classes and he's very funny, always talks about his cats. Show up to classes, recitations and do the homework with the extra credit (extra credit is actually more helpful than you think) and it's an easy 4.0. Also, the practice exams are EXACTLY like the actual exams.

This class was overall very easy. Lecture attendance is mandatory as there are multiple participation questions throughout each one. Review sheets before exams are identical to exams. Overall he is a very nice guy and often makes jokes.

Very good professor who teaches statistics very well, you have to go to class to get points every week but the lectures are only an hour long. There is weekly homework that isn't very long. If you go to the lectures the class isn't very hard, Dr. H is also a nice guy so the class doesn't get boring.

His classes are too fast, leaving little time for the in class and timed questions, which require calculations and written answers. Only 30-60 seconds per question makes it tough to keep up. Lectures are less helpful compared to recitations. Good beside that. Exams 2 and 3 are harder.

Good prof, probably the best one for intro statistics. Ensure you get a physical copy of the coursepack at the beginning of the semester. It makes things so much easier. Go to all the recitations/lectures and you will get a good grade.

My favorite professor thus far! He's a very personable guy, and I felt very comfortable in his lectures and always made sure to go to them. He was a very clear teacher and made sure to explain everything thoughly. When they print out the notes and bind them it's super useful, and I 100% reccomend! He really made me enough learning stats!

The class isn't easy and imo very boring but it was a box I had to check off, if I could go back in time I would have showed up to more lectures as it's very easy to get behind.  Show up to every recitation or you it will negatively effect your grade and you cannot make up points.

Go to lectures or you'll fall behind and be confused real fast. Exams were like the practice exams and study guides. Homework was confusing but do the extra credit homework first and it'll make it easier plus that is the only extra credit you will receive so that helps boost your grade

Dr. H was a very straightforward, fair professor in my opinion. As long as you do the homework assignments and show up to lectures/recitations, you will get a 4.0. He provides a "study guide" and "practice exam" before each midterm and final, which was almost exactly how the tests were on exam day. Those were super super helpful.

Great professor who explains things clearly. With each homework assignment there is a corresponding extra credit assignment with unlimited attempts, meaning you should do the EC before the actual homework to ensure you get a good grade on it. Exams are fair. He WILL hold you right up until the end of class with Top Hat questions so be warned

this class was honestly easy if you paid any attention to the lectures, showed up to recitation, did the homework and extra credit, and then did the practice exam before the real one. I have never taken stats and did not think this class was hard. When he talked too fast I would go to SLC tho just to get extra help.

Professor H was a very good teacher. He explained the material very well and was extremely responsive to any questions you had. It is clear he wants students to do good in the class and succeed. The homework goes with what you learn in lectures so make sure to go and pay attention. Do the practice exams to help you prepare for the exams.

There are many things your grade will count towards (ie. recitation activity, tophat, webwork, exams). The content itself is not too hard I'd say as long as you go to the lecture and do the notes you should be fine. However, the professor was too fast-paced and did not want to slow down when asked.
everything was easy but makes you second guess yourself. grades are based on 3 exams, top hat in class, webworks, and recitation activities.

I loved this class and that was definitely because of the professor. He's always prepared and has a positive attitude. I thought the layout of the exams was easy to predict because of a lot of preparation materials. One of my fav classes I've taken!

He talks SO FAST and I don't know a single person who could keep up with him. Lectures are mandatory to get TopHat points. The notes they recommend you buy don't follow the slides super well. He's a nice guy but the class is so chaotic and I never have a clue what he's talking about. Exams are a carbon copy of the study guide though.

Exams are worth 70% of your grade so beware. They were somewhat difficult but also exactly like the study guides. He was a fast talker and I relied on having friends on the class to do homework and pass overall. He is super nice and tries to connect with his students.

He reads off of slides that he creates himself with one example done in class on TOPHAT. 30% of the class will get the correct answer and he assumes the class has the concept mastered due to the 30% getting it correct. He does not give adequate time for exams either.

He often teaches in a fast paced and confusing manner, and without having prior knowledge of stats I would have been lost. He is kind and professional, randomly discusses his cats which is nice. Recitation TA answered any questions I had. Quite a lot of material is covered, Middle of semester most difficult, I wouldn't recommend missing lectures.

My largest problem with this class occurs in the middle of the second semester. I took this class in fall 2022, and halfway through the second semester the professor around the Thanksgiving break the classes jump around the coursebook and introduce some of the most important parts of the semester which got very confusing and tanked my grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you did well in AP Stats, you'll be totally good for this class. Class is kinda fast paced, but there's just a lot of material. I had to study a lot on my own. Prof is nice and funny and good at lectures, talks about his cats a lot. Tests are very important, but they're not too hard if you keep up with the class. Once a week homework sets.

He is a good professor. You should go to the lectures and PAY ATTENTION especially during the middle of the semester bc it has the hardest content. The practice exams are just like the actual exams, If you put in the work and understand the concepts you will get a 4.0

I took this course online asynchronous. It was pretty easy for me. There is extra credit that you can complete with every week of homework through webwork. The site isn't the best but not the worst to use. There were lecture videos that went along with the notes. As long as you completed everything every week, you should get a good grade.
Poor professor

I took this class during MSU's first full Covid semester. This comes from the heart lads. I took this class during the summer while trying to do a full time job at the same time. Not a good idea, and poor decision making lead to me getting hit with an ADR. Not good. Shaken, but not stirred, I retook the course and got a 4.0. This class is a labor of time friends, sometimes your entire weekend. Good luck.
guys I'm so tired of this, please make it stop

Guys don't trust ANY of those good reviews, they are all lies. Get ready to work very hard and not get any recognition back for it. I got a 4.0 in this class and let me just tell you, neither of the professors helped with that. Sorry to those who have to take this class in advance, I salute you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Imen Zaabar is a good professor who is willing to help if you ask for it. If you put in the slightest bit of effort, you will be able to get a 4.0. I'm saying this as a person who had ~1 day of actual experience with Python before the class. And I didn't read the book even once; I just did the assignments without using ChatGPT and got a 4.0
just dont for your own mental health sake, its not worth it, ive lost like 20 pounds starving myself for these projects

Are you a fan of ambiguous online grading of assignments, leaving you stranded hopelessly staring at Codio desperately mulling over the endless things that "Code Co@ch Buddy" claims could be wrong? Then this class is for you! I would criticize her somniferous lectures, but she was hardly ever there to give them. Thank you, Imen!...for nothing.

Every week the students are given material to teach themselves, then once a week in class it is reviewed. She was always an hour late. Why pay money to teach yourself something? It doesn't make sense. Everything in this class is a confused mess and it's way too unnecessarily hard for no reason.
Doesn't teach. She makes her students teach thensekve
Good luck to those required to take this course. If you don't have a significant history with coding before taking this class you're screwed.

Imen is the one professor I have had that went out of her way to help me simply because I asked for help and put in the effort. Way too many people fly under the radar but then get upset when there is little profs can do when they have shown no effort. Put in the work, go to office hours - it will go a long way. Such a caring, inspirational person.

Class isn't as hard as it's made out to be, but for ME it can be very difficult. I highly recommend taking this elsewhere over the summer because it takes up so much time between the projects and preparing for the exams. Given the fact that you can use AI on projects and have 2 attempts on the exams, there is no reason you should fail though.

This class isn't as bad as others make it out to be, They have made it significantly easier to 4.0 the class recently as of 2024 (Automatic code grading system, 60 points of extra credit weighted out of 1000 points, two chances to take each exam.) Do not underestimate the class; do your elbow work outside of class, and you should be fine.

It seems like Dr. Zaabar gets a lot of hate for students not putting in the work. If you complete projects ahead of time and actually try to learn the material instead of going straight to AI, you will be successful in this course. You get two chances for exams which I found to be very helpful.

The person who commented saying people are just learning that college gets hard is the dumbest thing I've ever heard. I took 10 AP's in my high school career before this and I graduated with a 4.1 GPA. Yet I'm learning college is hard and I'm not trying enough??? I got a 4.0 in this class ON MY OWN, ALL SELF TAUGHT. She contributed nothing to that.

Kind, respectful, knowledgeable. Went out of her way to talk about related and tangential concepts to the class, even un-related. Super easy to talk with and great to listen to. Amazing hard working professor that goes above and beyond her colleagues in dealing with a large mass of students and snarky faculty. Keep it up, we need you.

She gets a bad rap because this class makes students realize they're in college now and need to be responsible for their own success. She is strict but has a kind side, a little respect goes a long way. Just show that you are putting in some effort. Yeah the class is hard so prepare yourself and stay well ahead of deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: CSE 231 is exam and project heavy.  She has office hours on zoom and help hours aside from office hours are available for CSE 231. I don't like the way she structured the grading. Projects are hard, and 30% of our grade is based on projects. If you have zero coding experience, I do not recommend taking this class. Exams are not too hard.
I hate my life and it's all her fault.
I did well in this class but Zaabar made me consider dropping out. She's the worst.

Imen was one of the worst professors i've ever had, she may seem nice on the outside but she's cruel. She barely taught anything and always responds with, "Well everything's easy for me...".She's horrible and relies on her TA's for everything, I don't think she does anything but talk in slow motion on the bad lecture videos she tries to teach in.
Do not take this class! Take it somewhere else over the summer

I got a 4.0 in this class. Because of her, I transferred out from MSU. The whole CS department is a joke here, especially because of her. Thank you, Imen, for your great effort in prompting me to leave this university! Not to even mention her horrible TAs. Can't solve your questions but at the same time will berate you over a small single mistake.

Difficult because it is an online class that needs lectures. You don't see professor Zaabar often. The TA's teach the lab and they are ok. Videos are boring. 

Grades: the class is 30% projects (very difficult and you get 1-2 weeks per project), 60% exams (all coding, not to bad), 5% homework assignments (easy), and 5% quizzes (easy).

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. Do not come to this school if you want to study CSE. Please just leave. I am actually losing hair over this class. There is a special place in hell for Imen and I'm not just saying that. She is horrible and deserves the worst. This class is uncompletable. Look up the grade distribution for this class.

Very unkind to new learners, very tough grader, lots of tough assignments, and so unfortunate to be around. MSU needs to revise this class and not make it so hard for a beginner class. Turns many off of coding as a whole.

This is my second time taking this class (because i failed it the first time), and things need to be changed drastically. The professor was okay I suppose, but there is no reason for there to be a lot of homework/projects just for the majority of it to not matter because the exams will either make you or break you, even if you do well on hw/projs

The WORST class of MSU. I have over two years of coding experience and yet this class was equivalent to climbing mount everest. the professors aren't teaching at all, and the TAs are useful only in the helproom hours. tbh you cannot score in this class and do not bring your morale down or change your major if you're barely passing this class.

very nice if you talk in office hours. class is hard just because learning computer languages is a new topic to lots of people. The way the professor teaches isnt the problem, its the way the grading is set up. Sometimes the written questions feel like an all or nothing kind of point system. start projects on time and get help when needed.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Advice for anyone taking CSE 231: start the projects early and study for exams. You'll be fine if you can learn quick.

Had no python experience and struggled all the way through. I spent all of my free time in the help room, where every TA knows me by name. I understood the material, but the quizzes and exams (totaling 70% of grade) were all or nothing, ruining my grade. She should be more interested in improving the curriculum instead of researching pavement.
I'm a 4.0 senior Physics major, and this class just ruined my GPA. It also ruined my hair. Thanks.

CSE 231 is NOT A CLASS FOR BEGINNERS. I took 2 years of computer science in hs and am still struggling to get an 80. Prof. Zaabar is however a very kind professor. I have had issues arise from unclear instructions in regards to coding projects, but she is very quick to respond to emails, and help in person if needed.
If you want to 4.0 this class, you either need 2+ years of previous coding experience or you either need to sell your soul.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Sands and her both make the TA's "teach" all the classes, even though the TA's explicitly said they wouldn't teach the material. The lecture videos only explain the bare minimum and don't help. This class has a lot of homework even though exams are 60% of your final grade. Save yourself and take this class anywhere else. Worst class at MSU.
I don't think this professor wanted many students pass this class, because most people I know, who picked this class all failed in the coding exam.
Wasn't too bad. If you pay attention and do projects her course shouldn't be hard

she was a very good professor always responded to my emails, and consider my requests it was a easy class 
for me and if you study hard it will be easy to you.
i went bald

She's a really tough professor and doesn't offer much extra credit or help. She's never really around except during the last 10 minutes of class during the weekly quizzes and at that point doesn't help much at all. She is also a harsh person in general.

When I initially saw the rating for Dr. Zaabar, I was scared for this course. However, I feel like it is super possible to do well in this class, you just can't be afraid of work! Leaving this class I genuinely have a much better handle on Python and found Dr. Zaabar very helpful on Piazza, when she was around in class, or on her hosted reviews!

reviews.comment: This is the worst class I have taken in my academic career. my MSU advisor even told me not to take it. Only saw the professor one time, the TA's run her class. The exams are graded so harshly and are weighted at 60%. when the projects are a measly 25%. Do not take this class. Take it at a community college, I wish I listened to my advisor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: shes bad. unhelpful, condescending, and makes the class unreasonably hard. for the amount of effort the projects take, they should really be more than 4% of the grade for 12 hours of work.

Imen Zaabar was the worst professor I have ever had. She doesn't teach students at all, TAs do. The worst thing about the class is the unfair grading. Quizzes and tests are all or nothing. You can go from 100% to 0% based on a grammar mistake. This is not an Intro class, it's more about exams than actually learning. Codeo doesn't even let you debug
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is such a sweetheart and a kind person. Some people may think that she is rough or mean, but in my experience this is tough love rather than her being rude. Her class was alot of work, but she was supportive, office hours she was always helping students, as well as going to help-rooms and responding to Piazza quickly and respectfully.

I understand this is a weeder class but there should be no reason an intro level CS class should be designed so poorly. The content is completely self taught and mostly online. The weighting is very unnecessary and the professor herself only does review sessions and comes to some labs, and most of the content is taught by TAs.

Ever wanted to take an intro class that required absolute perfection? No actual grading (or very very minimal) is done on the exams/quizzes, that would require the profs/TA's to actually do something, so it's all auto-graded and must match the instructor results PERFECTLY. A grammar mistake or missing word can take you from a 100% to 0% quiz grade.
womp womp, drop this class

She's one of the most beloved people on the MSU campus. Her empathy, resourcefulness, and helpfulness have changed my perspective on life. I beg each and every one of you to take her class. Witness her greatness in person! You'll be left in tears for sure.

Zaabar has shown up to a couple of my labs. However, she has not actually participated in any of the course content. 

The review videos are hard to grasp and dragged out, the textbook is absurdly expensive and underutilized, and the quizzes and tests are excessively difficult for the course content taught. The HW projects can take 20+ hours to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Zaabar is the most inspiring person I've ever met. I mean it. No one has inspired me more to jump off a cliff and kill myself in a slow, antagonising, brutal way than she has. Her unnecessary in-lab quizzes and exam-heavy policy is prob the reason 90% of my class will eat batteries for breakfast, dinner, and lunch. Mission accomplished?

She doesn't give partial credit at all. If your code does everything except print a space wrong or something like that and fails the check, you will get no credit at all. My exam grade dropped off a cliff because I couldn't get it to perfectly do the checks. Not to mention that you have so little time that you have to rush through the exam.

By far the worst class I have ever taken. I had no knowledge about coding and took the class because I was interested, but the amount of tears and hours spent on this class not even a month in has not been worth it. Maybe the in person sections are a bit better, but good luck if you have never coded before.

Only 3 weeks in, and I already regret it. I read that this was an intro to coding class and thought that this class couldn't be too bad. I was wrong. There are so many assignments with so many tears, I am very new to coding and have received very little help. The only people that teach are the TAs and you receive no feedback from the professor.

It's hard to evaluate Dr. Zaabar because this class is primarily run by the TAs, and most of the content made by professors no longer involved with the course. For an "introduction" class, the exams are unnecessarily difficult and brutal. Be prepared to grind on the projects to absorb the damage from exams. Be sure to pirate the $120 textbook.

It is truly an impressive feat that the professors for CSE 231, including Dr. Zaabar, have accomplished: taking an easy-to-learn concept (Python) and making it a struggle. If you want to do well in this course, you must read the textbook and take thorough notes. You will not do well if you don't understand the concepts taught by the textbook.

As a student finishing the summer semester, and taking it for the second time, it was much better the second time. Weekly review videos and exam review videos were helpful, but will not be enough to pass. Zaabar responded to questions quick at the beginning of the semester, but that did not last for long. If you fail one exam, pray for help.

As a CS major, I would rather touch grass than retake this class. When I asked her about getting credit for one of the mistakes in the exam she told me that her "mistake" wasn't a mistake as there were better academic ways to "trick" us and told me how I should have known the intention behind the question.

The class structure is absolutely horrible, because how is it that everytime there is an exam there's no project that week but for the final exam which is the heaviest and most important one, there is a project due and a penalty added at the last minute. This is ridiculous
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Every week I need to do four assignments. Pre-lab, lab, exercise, and project. Each project spends almost 2 or days and worth almost about 60 credits, and if you lose 100 credits, you will get 3.5, lose for the second 50 credits you will get 3.0 and go on. That means if you want to get a good grade need to finish all the projects and get full score

Capable of teaching just chooses not to it feels like, no lectures, just crappy textbook and videos. Also course policies are hyper unreasonable for an introductory class, 1 hour to code four problems on an exam, you have so many projects that your grades in other classes slip and you are still struggling to get a c in this one. 0/5 if I could.

Weekly programs are quite tough, and sometimes I feel like they are trying to give us headaches purposely. Atleast lecture every week could fix this everything, and I would definitely not miss those lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Exams are AWFUL. 50 mins to code 4 separate questions, despite the lab (where you take the exam) going for 2 hrs, and often several definitions in those blocks. Wildly unhelpful, was told to "think about it" after asking a question about a project. Some projects taking more than 30 hrs a week to complete despite me having lots of coding experience

To me it was an easy class. There was a recap of the material that should have been studied before class. There was an in person lab every week with a chunk of code due at the end. Exercises due every Saturday. Project based off of lab concepts that were upscaled due every Monday night.

If you already know ANY coding language, you'll be fine. If not, prepare for hard (but manageable!) work. Tips on how to succeed: 1) start your weekly projects early 2) ask questions 3) form a study group. There are plenty of resources provided (old exam questions, online videos, extra credit...), you just have to be resourceful and use them.

There are projects due every week. It's not unmanageable if you put in the work needed and start it couple days before the due date. Tests are not difficult, as long as you study the past projects/labs. You can bring in 1-page cheat sheet, which will be a lot of help. No previous coding experience needed, if you put in 5-10hrs of work each week.

If you have never taken a coding class before this will be difficult, but manageable. The prof isn't the best, but you will only be dealing with TA's anyways. The profs don't want you to fail so they give many help and review sessions. The class is tough but if you put in effort you will pass.

Dr. Imen always responded fast to emails and piazza posts. I took this over the summer so it was a lot of work per week, but her videos and my previous experience with python helped me through. The exams were easy because she lets you put whatever you want on your cheat sheet.

Dr. Zabaar teaches CSE 231 with Dr. Enbody. To be exact, Enbody has the most control over the class structure, so I don't blame Zabaar for the dismal quality of CSE 231. Zabaar hosted weekly hour-long review sessions which helped somewhat for the exam. She did her best to answer them. It will be a lot better if Enbody was not there in CSE 231.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: don't take this course asynchronously. if you have no other choice, start learning python right now or else you're going to struggle A LOT. the weekly review sessions help but most of the time you're left to fend for yourself. i'm literally begging all future students to reconsider this course, it's genuinely so hard.

Dr. Zabaar teaches CSE 231 alongside Dr. Enbody. As far as I can tell, Enbody has the most control over the class structure, so I don't blame Zabaar for the dismal quality of CSE 231. Zabaar hosted weekly hour-long review sessions which helped somewhat with the difficulty of the class. She was patient with questions and did her best to answer them.

Loham and Stofluz are professors for one lecture time. In all honesty, do this class at a community college. So many people complained to Kruger (who created the class structure), and she hasn't done anything about it. The majority of your homework is outside of class, even the actual lectures. Please save yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I do not think Prof Lehman was a problem except I need heard anything that he said because he would let students talk over him. I do not like that you I have to teach yourself everything and the iClicker was so stressful due to it because for accuracy. Overall, it wasn't the worst it was just structured horribly and the TA's were the save in grace.

BS161 isn't bad at all and everyone is overdramatic. If you are a bio major and don't do well in this course, you should probably rethink stuff. Prof. Lohman is helpful most of the time and will always answer questions in class. He also responds to emails really quickly. Overall everyone is way too rough on Professor Jere Bear.

BS161 is the worst course I have taken at MSU. The structure of it is terrible; you have to teach yourself everything before class, in class group assignments, and iclicker graded for accuracy. Professor Lohman is so quiet it's hard to hear or retain anything he says. He also was not helpful when asked questions, the TA's were a lifesaver.

NO DROPS on exams worth 50%! Do all learning objectives, ICAS, GO TO THE HELP ROOM, and utilize TAs. The learning in this class is active learning so you do everything by yourself and attend class for the activities. It can be easy to get confused, so utilize all resources for help. Extra credit opportunities offered throughout the course.
He spoke very quietly and was not helpful when you asked questions. The exams were hard, and the whole class structure was difficult.

Genuinely awful, has no care for any student in his room and just does his lectures to get through the rest of his day. Would take 30 seconds on iclicker questions that need maybe 2-3 minutes and makes you feel dumb if you ask him any questions and was no help whatsoever.

Going to a lecture was a joke but mandatory. A TA will do video lectures that you watch BEFORE class, then in class you will do activities in a group with iclicker (graded off correctness). These activities and lectures did not reflect onto the tests and quizzes. They could've made this class so much better and more engaging, but instead it's hard.

The professor himself was okay, but this class is stupidly difficult. All the lectures are done before class, and take a long time. He doesn't teach at all and we just do in class activities. Hate the set up of this class

This professor CAN'T teach! The class is very participation based with in class iclicker quizzes, group work activites, and per-class lectures. The class itself isn't that hard, but the professor refuses to answer or explain the iclicker quizzes or help struggling students.

This guy does not know how to teach. Content is not THAT difficult but he does not know how to properly teach or test the content. Also does not take feedback into consideration at all. His response to everything is telling you to go to the help rooms.

Dr. Lohman and Professor Hsu co-teach a flipped class. Dr. Lohman was consistently condescending every time I spoke with him. He didn't even teach anything; the whole class is group work and iclicker quizzes. The lecture videos were made by some random, and in class he was unintelligible. This class is hell, take it at community college if you can.

I'm not sure if I am just good at accounting or not, but I didn't find her class too hard. The biggest thing was that the course packet for the class didn't match the actual slides, so it was kind of hard to follow along in class. The exam setup and process to get to the answer are very similar to the practice exams in Connect.

Lori is SUPER nice but I genuinely have not learned a single thing since coming to this class. Every day I go to her lectures I stare at the slides and have no clue what's going on - and I think this is because she didn't create any of the material she uses. The workbook makes no sense and half the time doesn't even correlate with the slides.

She is a nice lady, but her lectures are all over and hard to follow. She doesn't show much energy, has bad slides, and overall the class doesn't seem full ready to be taught, since the course book isn't complete and HiTa isn't set up. Be prepared to learn the material yourself.

Very nice teacher but it's impossible to understand what she's teaching. The notes packet doesn't match the slides and I can't tell what she's trying to get across most of the time. First exam was easy but after that it's downhill.
Absolutely loved this professor, she is so sweet and genuinely passionate not only about accounting but also about her students' success. By far one of my favorites, especially for a required course.
I don't know what I was taught the entire semester. The teaching wasn't on point.
Beware! Didn't have a nice time doing this course. Kinda difficult to understand what is taught.
Great professor, content can get challenging at some points.
Super nice professor, online exams, attendance not mandatory, one group project at end of semester. very caring. Curved everyones grades at end of semester.

He split a class with Jeremy Loham. The class set up is horrendous and no one will change it. There's stuff on the quiz that is only brought up once or twice. If I was you, I'd take the class at a community college.

He was a good teacher when explaining things but the way this class is set up...you basically teach yourself, also TAs are wishy washy, it depends on who you get. I'm just glad it's over and I passed.

Professor Stoltzfus was an amazing professor. The class itself carries a lot of work load, but if you put in the work it is definitely manageable. The exams cover content in class and do not stray off on tangent topics. I highly recommend going to office hours and making sure you understand the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class was reversed. The actual class was group participation going over questions that were graded. My group sucked, but the TA's and professors all tried answering any questions we had. The class isn't hard unless you don't do the work. Be prepared to teach yourself and put a lot of time into this class. Help room hours save your life though.

Stoltzfus never actually taught the class, we would have to watch video lectures on our own time and then come to class and just do iclicker questions for the hour and 20 minutes. Very disappointed because I thought the class would learning everything in class and taking notes but it was nothing like that. NOT a GOOD professor.

He never actually taught the class, we had to watch videos before lecture then come to lecture. He was good at explaining but I wish I got a class that was where you would sit down and learn everything in lecture instead of finding your own time outside of class. We did iclicker questions for the hour and 20 mins and that was it. Very disappointed.

He taught the 1, 3 and 4 units. You get pre recorded lectures to watch, all you do in class are in-class activities. He never made things understandable, it was always confusing. I would avoid taking this course with him. The textbook is required but we center used it even though there were chapters that could be read.

He's a nice man but the way his class is set up is messy. Trying to navigate his D2L page is harder than the actual course material. Attendance isn't mandatory which is good because he spends majority of lecture rambling about how magnificent AI is. Exams being online, open book, take home made this class tolerable.

The lectures, textbook (expensive and mandatory), and exams are completed unrelated to each other so much so that it feels like taking 3 separate classes. The exams appear to have been AI-generated, with frequent spelling errors and questions that don't make sense to the point where he is forced to comp them since it's literally blind luck.

The simulation assignments were some of the most frustrating assignments I have ever had the misfortune of doing, exams are absolutely awful and none of the questions on any of them had what we studied, his continual A.I glazing got tiring and overall I would never ever take this course again
This isn't a hard class at all but he is so disorganized and confusing that the class becomes hard.

MSU is number one in the nation for supply chain, but our intro course is terrible. Spink is passionate about SCM, but that does not translate into his aptitude for teaching. Disorganized (D2L is horrible to navigate), grades terribly (everything is a zero, confusing labels, always behind), presentations are cluttered. Needs a full course revamp.
Awful class. Avoid if you can. Lectures were long and boring, and useless. Exams were so hard. Extra credit and open-note exams saved this class. Spink was genuinely awful.

D2L is set up beyond poorly, complete cluster and mess. Exams are 75% of the grade, just an unheard of and rather blasphemous percentage. Expects you to know precise word by word definitions of terms, which are contradictory to what is written in the book and slides. Nice person, but horrible class. Very unfortunate that this is a requirement.

Exams are NOTHING like class or notes. If you don't know the word for word definition of the EVERTHING you will not pass the exams. They are online and open note and that does not help. Sucks that it is a required class.
Unreal......

SCM 304 is by far the worst organized class I have ever taken. Information is scattered everywhere and what shows up on quizzes doesn't match what shows up in lectures. Taking this class is incredibly frusturating! Avoid at all costs!!

Go to lectures + do other homework, keep good notes from the (expensive) readings.
Lecture was him telling us about how he will tell us stuff. 
Said he would "teach us how to use ChatGPT", a model designed to be as user friendly as possible. Filled lectures with him telling us to ask AI instead of teaching us. 
Completely unorganized and rambley.

The other reviews are spot on with the disorganized lectures, but this semester, this class has basically become AI (mainly Copilot) glaze. 80% of the class is either talking about AI or Spink telling us to look things up on AI to "facilitate discussion" instead of doing his job of teaching. It's just promo for his and another prof's new AI class.
Brutal class but has taken steps to make it more barrable

This man's class is impossible to understand. His organization is abysmal and his lectures are worthless. Good luck trying to figure out your grade at the end. Exams made no sense. I made it through but I don't think I really learned anything. Sucks that he's the only one that teaches SCM303.

Professor Spink is a good guy, but this class is so unorganized. I attended the lectures for the first 10 weeks, but honestly they were not very helpful. The book is where I learned everything for this class. The exams are hard, but he let us use our notes which was very helpful to refer to.

This class was so easy I don't know why everyone complains about it. Lectures are not mandatory and the exams are basically just re written homework questions (open note, open book). Never went to class except for a few when he offered extra credit. Smartbooks are a pain tho but it's just busy work and the homework is fine.

Spink is one of the worst professors I have had at MSU. His online material is impossible to navigate. You never know exactly if you are doing good or bad in the course. His lectures are about nothing related to the content and you never know what will be on the exams. I would not recommend him to anyone unless you absolutely have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Spink is sweet, caring, and passionate about teaching. However, the class could benefit from restructuring for better cohesion and accessibility. The D2L is disorganized and hard to navigate. While exams were online, which was convenient, they were tough, and I personally didn't learn much in the class.
This class needs major restructuring. Set aside $100 for the textbook and go to class only on lecture days after each exam to get extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He really cares about his students, but D2L is super unorganized and hard to navigate at times. You do weekly readings, and homework assignments that aren't too difficult. Its just hard to study/stay motivated in this class.
Lectures aren't super informative, but he does care about his students. He's also a fair grader and the class isn't very difficult.

Lectures are repetitive and boring. We had online, open note tests, probably wouldn't have passed without that. He thinks his D2L is organized, but there is so much unnecessary garbage on it.
