reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He is literally the most inspirational man I have ever met in my entire life I love him so much. He genuinely cares how his students do and wants to see them learn and succeed. Please take his class it will make you love going to class and hes just a great guy to talk to.

He rocks, he's passionate, he'll try to connect with you, and he'll do his best to make it enjoyable. His exams are tough, he's the type to give options A-G where D is A&B, E is A&C, F is B&C, and G is All the Above. So you gotta know your stuff and be prepared to explain in detail. He assigns homework and give pop quizzes but he warns you.

He's the toughest grader I've ever had. This class is so unnecessarily and excessively difficult for a required freshman level class. I'm a senior graduating this semester and this class is going to ruin my GPA for the term because his grading is bogus. Even with knowing the material and studying I almost failed every exam because of his grading.

You do have to pay attention and really learn the material to do well, but he's pretty funny, makes a lot of jokes, and is really helpful. If you have to take an ISB, I'd recommend taking 201 with Ryan. You'll do well and he makes it interesting even if you're not big into biology and environmental science.
Ryan is awesome. It's an easy A if you attend lecture. No book, so that's nice. Occasional pop quiz, but rarely ever. He's very funny and makes learning fun, interactive, and valuable.

He truly cares about the learning of his students and makes class extremely interesting. Would take again! Attendance is not mandatory however there are occasional quizzes at the beginning of class covering homework or last lecture. No textbook for this class.

This is a flipped learning class, meaning that you will need to watch all of her pre-class videos before doing un-graded group busy work in class. I think the flipped learning structure is un-helpful, and I found her video explanations weren't good
The way she said "Hello scholars" was triggering to me

She is honestly super sweet and likes to engage with her class. there is a-lot of bust work to prepare before class and you are expected to know it for the in class activity and quizzes that are every day. I learned a-lot overall though! do not skip class

Suuuper sweet professor, she learns almost everyone's names! Super kind and will sit with you till you understand. She is also super open for any questions and work you need help with! The only thing is the class is structured really weird... definitely not a lot of fun, a LOT of homework, and 70% of it is work you have to do on your own.

She is sweet but I HATE how this class is a flipped course. Honestly believe if it was like a regular lecture, many would know what the heck is going on in class. The pre class activities are understandable but the in class activities are confusing. Quizzes every Monday from last weeks units. Every assignment is graded on accuracy and completion
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Kruger is amazing! She is very passionate about the material and easily approachable if you need help. The TAs and ULAs were very helpful as well! Make sure to study hard for this class since there is a lot of material in the units, and attend the help rooms for additional help.

I loved Dr. Krueger, while she has a thick accent if you listen she is clear and describes the material well, especially if you talk to her 1 on 1. BS161 is a lot of work however if you read directions on the in-class assignments carefully you get points for format. The material can be tough, but everything you need for exams is in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class is moderately difficult. Everything is based off of some kind of test, which makes the workload a bit higher than other 100-level courses, but it forces you to actually learn the material, which allows you to do well on the exams. She provides a lot of really good study materials on D2L and there are multiple office hours with great TAs.

Dr. Krueger is a phenomenal professor. She is kind and passionate. She is super approachable, so talk to her if you have questions. There is a good amount of work with in-class activities, pre-class activities, and quizzes every week. But you are allowed a one-page cheat sheet! So, if you put in the effort, it's an easy A!

I had a very pleasant experience with Prof Krueger. BS161 is a flipped course meaning most of the learning leans on you, but you do not need a strong biology background to succeed, and she and her TAs are constantly helping out in class and enthusiastic about their field. Study hard for the free responses and multiple choice quizzes out of class.

You watch the lecture outside of the class and come to class to work with a group of students to complete in-class activities. The lecture videos are not the most helpful and if you don't have a strong background in biology you will struggle. She's a nice professor but I haven't learned much through the course at all.
She knows what shes doing.

I LOVED Dr. Krueger for BS161! She is so kind and really helps facilitate good biology thinking and knowledge  and she set up her course in a way that things build onto each other (which is great for the cumulative final)! There is help outside of class so if you are stuck there are so many resources and ways for you to succeed.100% recommend!

Professor Krueger is such a sweet heart. She is super helpful in class and will make sure you understand the iClicker if you ask her. The class is a hard class so be sure to do the online lectures. Her help rooms and very helpful and she is more than happy to help you.

Dr. Krueger was a wonderful professor to have for BS161. She certainly knew what she was talking about in regards to biology, and she also made an effort to actually get to know her students (even though it was just her and one other prof in a lecture of 300 students). The grading was *slightly* strict at times, but overall very fair.

It is very hard to get a good grade in this class  grades are solely based off of how much of the information you can retain. RIQ (quizzes) ask there questions in really confusing ways. But this professor was very kind and always made an effort to help you understand. If you need to take this course this is the professor you want.

When I say this course is test-heavy, I mean there isn't a single graded assignment that doesn't involve you answering some series of multiple-choice or short-answer questions. She gives good feedback and is helpful, but the layout of the class was very inefficient and I wish she defined/explained terms and processes more.

The was no teaching that occurred in the lecture and most of it was groupwork. Most of the time the groups are lost on the clicker assignment and the ULAs don't do a great job on clarifying the doubts. The pre-lecture videos are somewhat disconnected to what happens in the lecture and it is frustrating.

This class is a flipped format which I did not like. You will have to watch an hour of lectures before every class and take a preclass quiz, Hard Iclicker graded questions in class, weekly quiz with exam level question and 4 exams with 0 drops. Class is very easy to fall behind in but if you stay on track and watch the videos you will be fine.

Lots of resources for this class which can students if they choose to use them. Professor Krueger is very understanding and she gets to know all her students. This class you do have to stay on top of the work since the class is not a traditional lecture class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures do not apply to what is required to know for the homework and exams. You have to teach yourself the topics from resources on the internet. Their resources do not prepare you for what you are graded on.
Great

Literally such a sweetheart and is very passionate about learning. Highly recommend attending help rooms, as it helps so much w/ understanding of content. This class is reverse classroom teaching and very work intensive, but helpful for any health majors.

Dr. Krueger was very knowledgable about Biology and I could ask her questions not necessarily pertaining to lecture topics but about things related but beyond the content, and she knew the answers and loved to help. The class was hard but I really enjoyed having her and her teaching team everyone was very helpful.

BS 161 with Krueger was very well organized. The class is flipped, so you watch video lectures on your own time and then you practice what you learned in class. People complain about the amount of quizzes but you get 2 or 3 attempts on the pre class quizzes. Wish upper level STEM classes were like this one

BS161 is a really hard class. You have to watch the lectures outside of class, so there is very little instruction during class. Dr. Krueger in BS161 was helpful, and could answer almost any question. The only downside about her class in 161, is that as of Fall 2022, her class is flipped. So the lectures are to be watched outside and before class, and you work in class, meaning LOTS of homework including videos and worksheets. She helps if you ask though!
Dr. Krueger was an amazing professor. She gives good feedback and responds to emails quick.

reviews.comment: This class is kind of inverted, so the homework is usually just to watch lectures before coming into class. There are also a LOT of quizzes, some of which are easy and some that are quite hard. There are review sessions every week on zoom, which were super helpful. This class is hard, but if you pay attention and ask for help you should be fine.

Great teacher however, the riq's and exams are very difficult. Some contain material that isn't even covered in class. This makes it hard to study because studying the notes from the lecture does not always help. Also, there is not enough time given to finish the exams and riqs. They do offer extra credit, which helps a little.

Dr. Krueger is a very sweet teacher! While the class is very challenging, she hosts review sessions often as well as the TAs. The tests are pretty hard and do make up for most of the grade. Each class is required and you work in groups the entire time.

reviews.comment: Dr. Krueger was a really good professor and actually has good lectures. She is good at explaining the content and is also very helpful to everyone. She is an understanding professor but has her rules and deadlines that need to be followed. She is very organized and structured and I'd definitely recommend taking BS171 with her.

Worst class I have ever taken. Before every class you would have to take a 15minute 8 question quiz on the UPCOMING class material that you were supposed to memorize before the class time when she was supposed to be teaching it. Each one of those quizzes counted for 4% of your FINAL grade. You had to participate through the whole class.

Dr. K was an awesome prof! She had good lectures and instead of exams, we did daily 10 question quizzes. reviews.comment: I found the workload really manageable, and none of the assignments or exams were especially challenging

reviews.comment: Great professor, doesn't use much technology and instead outlines work very well in class. Very easy to keep up with as long as you pay attention in class. Highly recommend.

Amazing Professor. In my first semester of college, I enjoyed his class the most by far. I wasn't always focused, and it was okay; he and his TAs were there to help whenever needed. Doesn't take attendance, but we had random pop quizzes, and as long as you did them, you basically got a 4.0. Very kind and accommodating to anything you might need.

This guy is great, highlight of my semester. Lots of interesting reading and lots of essays. The essays are fantastic as they make you think and, as long as you mention the broad points you can write about it anyway you want. 

Its a very intellectual class.
The professor has dry humor but if you like that you will find him funny.

Not a fan of Professor Lambert. For an IAH class that has almost zero benefit for anyone taking it he is way too serious.  You have atleast one essay a week if not more, and they are graded on a 4 point scale. You do one thing wrong and your grade is automatically a 75%. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I loved Dr Lambert! Attendance was not mandatory, so unfortunately, no one ever showed up for class, but they were to be honest missing out. Had him for fall semester, great class, and super knowledgeable on the material. Very clear guidelines for each assignment on the syllabus, so as long as you follow it you should get an easy 4.0. Decent amount of writing and 1-3 readings every week, but easily manageable.
LOVE LOVE LOVE, very understanding and really connected with this class. Great professor, gives good feedback, and easily gives out 4.0s
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Class is super easy. Attendance isn't required, but you won't be able to write critical thinking questions or papers if you don't have an idea of what he talks about in the lecture. He is very passionate and can come off a little harsh but overall hes a cool guy

Really enjoyed this class, 6 weekly reflections that you can do over 14 weeks, 5 critical thinking questions, 2 short papers and one final paper. reviews.comment: Dr. Lambert can come off as intimidating at first but he is a really caring and passionate person and wants you to do well. The grading is very clear cut, if you do what is says on the syllabus; you will get a 4.0 easily.

I really enjoyed Dr. Lambert's class. Dr. Lambert is very passionate about his feminist views, so if you share those views take this class. If you don't, do not. He assigns readings and holds discussions about them in class, so make sure you do the readings and participate in discussion. A few very short written assignments and no exams.

reviews.comment: Boring lectures and gets off topic very easily. Goes on rants about things not related to the readings or topic of his lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures are long and take up the entire time designated time. Class is easy and interesting as long as you put a little effort into reading some of the content. I would recommend this class.

He recently redesigned the class and made it much easier. The content is incredibly interesting and his lectures are fun to attend. Dr. Lambert is clearly passionate about what he's teaching and it shows. He really wants to see you put in effort, but honestly you don't have to to get a good grade. I loved this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: do not take this class in the morning, while its interesting material it is also incredibly boring. attendance is not taken but there are a lot of in class assignments with no warning to catch skippers (me) and it can hurt after a few. dr. Lambert is a nice guy though and really cares about his students, if you miss something he'll be cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I had him in the Fall of 2022 and looking back at it this was by far my favorite class and my favorite professor. Starting that class thinking I would hate it but ended up loving it. Class is easy if you show up and actually listen to the Lectures.

I'm not even done with this class yet, but I want to make sure he gets the rep that he deserves on here. He is very personable and remembered my name because he's seen me at work a few times, even though I'm quiet in class. IDK if it's just my TAs, but I put minimal effort into writing (never full essays!) and have aced every "paper."
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His class is two hours long which felt so long but they always made you actually think about the world we live in, and he seemed to care. The beginning seemed kind of slow with book but towards the end I probably learned more in any of my other classes. If you try on the papers and take your time, you get a good grade. Forces you to talk in class.

Professor Lambert always grades and assigns work with the student's best interests in mind. The assignments for the course are not difficult, but force you to think. He gives clear feedback and guides you to improvement on the next assignment. Professor Lambert provided intellectually challenging material interesting and/or relevant to the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Loved this class and would take it again with him. I would make sure to read the material. If you read the material you will do good in the class. Lots of class discussions and a couple of random assignments (sort of like pop quizzes but really easy). Definitely go to class because you will develop a deeper understanding of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I've never felt the need to rate a professor before but I'm taking his upper level IAH course next year because I enjoyed his course so much. Reading wasn't super heavy and usually reasonable. The way he lectures and speaks gives incredible perspective of racial and gender inequalities and gave me a greater perspective on my own identities.
The class is not confusing if you actually pay attention, go to recitation and office hours. He is a funny guy and very passionate about what he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: So insightful and straightforward. There are basically only 12 assignments in total.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment:
-i didn't read and still did well
-as long as you turn in the assignments and actually try you will be fine
-very liberal and will tell you his views
-go to class, he does in class assessments which basically serves as a pop quiz
-allows you to drop one assignment from each category 
-2 hours long
-easy
-always changing due dates
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: On the first day of class, he claimed that nothing he lectures about is his opinion, yet has lectured completely biased every class and pretty much invalidates any opinion that contradicts his. Basically if you don't have far left liberal views, you will not be right in his class.

You're going to want to do the readings for his class, if you do the readings you don't really need to go to the lecture. His grading is not very hard, just know what you are talking about! Most of the quizzes are on Quizlet but not all, the PowerPoint really help with quizzes.

Wonderful man and wonderful professor. If you are willing to listen to others and discuss ideas, you will love his classes. If you are not open to other ideas and diverse perspectives, you will not like him. Overall, best PHL prof I have had at MSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Class was easy and the papers don't take long as long as you write down what he says during class and put it in ur papers. Problem is is that we have the same conversation over and over and it can be really frustrating when the same question is asked in different words a lot.
The best professor I have ever had. Very engaging and respectful with material. Loved this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Just, no. Dont waste your time with this class. Probably the harshest grader Ive ever had. One little thing wrong with your paper turns into a D grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Horrible
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lambert completely controls all lecture discussions and also grades papers in a completely subjective way. That is, he looks for a correct interpretation of the text and if youre not spot on (in his mind) you will be marked down for it. Discussions are boring and only consist of his own notesnot discussion. Not a way to teach a PHL class IMO.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He says attendance isn't mandatory but then gets very angry when people don't go. I understand he cares about what he's teaching, but he doesn't get that people are enrolled in his class because the university makes us take 2 IAHs, and makes it more difficult than necessary. Cool info to learn about though.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you are thinking about taking his class... just dont do that to yourself. He tries to make kids that dont go to class fail and chooses favorites. If you look at the wall you should be scared for him to yell at you. He says this class is not about opinions, but the whole class is based on his opinions. He thrives off of the power that he has.

Lambert was a good teacher overall but there were so many books to read and essays to write. He says attendance is not required but you should definitely go because he asks questions on the exam about videos he showed in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Lambert was a good professor, his lectures were very interesting and easy to stay tuned into. You aren't graded by much though and half of your grade is made up of the final and the last paper. Overall, the class was not too hard and he was a good professor. You HAVE to go to lectures, though, or you are going to have a rough time on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Enjoyed his lectures, does grade somewhat tough but the final was set up to boost your grade.

Professor Lambert is a nice guy but gets on your nerves. My class started to not show up halfway thru so he made attendance mandatory or else he wouldn't share his slides at the end of the year. Don't let him catch you on your phone he WILL single you out. He opened my eyes to a lot of things concerning race so his class was important and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Easy class, no homework just weekly quizzes.
Dr. Thompson is sweet, and her lectures are inspiring and straightforward. Attendence was not mandatory. The exams were harder than I expected, but she allows multiple drops.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: a really great prof! A lot of drops which is really nice, but if you don't want to go to class I would get the book or vise versa. However I will say it is so lecture heavy and I did have to fight my sleep demons more times then I would like LOL. I do wish there were more discussions and more diverse voices and opinions were heard.

The class wasn't hard and the workload is reasonable but it's extremely biased and one sided. Almost everything is taught through a single political lens, and the course often pushes specific societal and feminist solutions without leaving room for other perspectives. It also rarely covers actual women's psychology like biology and cognition.

Dr. Thompson is fantastic, she is so kind, knowledgable and accessible outside of class. You do not necessarily need to go to class, but it certainly helps! If you ever want to talk about something you found interesting pertaining to her course, she is more than willing to chat about it with you because she is so passionate. I would take her again!
Attendence is not mandatory. She does include items from the textbook in her mini exams. Overall, an easy class if you show up.

Ms. Thompson's class was very lecture-heavy. I often felt bored and overwhelmed trying to copy each slide before she moved on. The nearly two-hour lectures were tiring, and the exams every two to three weeks were all memorization-based. The homework was simple—two short quizzes and an assignment every week.

Amazing professor, really cares about the subject and is super easy to talk to about anything. Tons of drops for homework, attendance, and exams. Lectures can be long but making it through them is the only hard part of class.

Dr. Thompson was nice and had interesting stories sometimes but her whole lecture was reading directly off of slides. If you are able to read through textbooks and make quizlets to learn rather than note taking I would recommend this class but it was not enjoyable and I was often stressed about writing everything down as she clicked through slides.

Engaging professor who cares about her students. The lectures are long, but she explains the content clearly and makes it easy to remember. Take good notes and study the homework questions and you'll do well.

It's not hard to pass PSY 101 but it is a hassle to try and get a great grade. She's pretty whimsy and her lectures can be boring if you don't like the content but she knows what she's teaching. Theres attendance interactives locked via password gotten through lecture. About 3 assignments a week pre+post test and then hw and decent deadlines

Lectures are long & attendance does matter, however, the class is very manageable as long as you do not slack off. Not much extra credit. Exams are SO straight-forward and not tricky as she provides study guides. Just memorize key terms and vocabulary and you can easily get 80% on the exams. Lots of homework and quizzes that can EASILY be redone.

Dr. Thompson is a very nice lady that is passionate about her teachings. However, the class is long and boring and hard to engage in. There are a lot of assignments, but they aren't hard. Exams are ok, study and you'll be fine. It is nice before every exam you have the class before off.

I'd say the only bad things about the class were the super long lectures and the study guides. The study guides were just an overview of the notes and were not very helpful. She also curves the tests which is nice, and if you do well you don't have to take the final. Overall, very nice and passionate prof, long and boring class.

She's a very nice Professor and knows what she's talking about. But the way the exams are is too much, there are 4 exams. Not spaced out well, with material not in the study guides she provided. Lots of homework too. You have to come to class and sit there a full 2 hours to receive participation credit.

Thompson is an good prof, not a great one. It is a very lecture heavy class and the lectures are long. She sometimes goes on tangents that will just never help you on any assignment you do for this course. It is somewhat hard to pay attention. With that said, it wasn't like she was a bad prof. She cares about the students and is passionate.

Has very long and boring lectures that take up the whole class period. Get a buddy for the attendance code and you get credit. Grades are off of a point scale so it is easy to get a 4.0. Only need to average a 78% on all of your tests if you do all the other assignments. Ignore the lectures and study the textbook which doesn't take too long to read
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Thompson is very passionate about her job and it shows. She works hard to make sure everyone understands the subject. The three lowest exams are dropped which helps a lot with grades. Overall the course is interesting.
She's British so if you want to hear that for hours then don't take her.

Good teacher and makes content digestible for students. Clear guidance for students despite the semi-heavy work load. AMAZING grading, very very lenient with drops and will benefit you if you do the work during the Finals Weeks

Prof is nice and knows class content. Really the only issue I had with the layout of this class was the mini exams. The study guides for each were about as long as a regular exam study guide which means there were weeks where it felt like you were prepping for 4 exams in just her class.The questions were often things not on the study guide too.

This was one of my favorite classes this semester. Although attendance was not required, I showed up every single day, as Dr. Thompson was so passionate about what she was teaching. I highly recommend her, as well as this course! I hope I will be able to take another course with her. She was very kind, knowledgable, and understanding. very easy/fun

Dr. Thompson is a great teacher. She gives very interesting lectures. She also has a lot of built in drops for quizzes, exams, discussion posts, and even for the final. I would highly recommend taking her PSY 339 class!

This course offered SONA research experiences for extra credit, along with tests and an optional final, enhancing its flexibility. It included online lectures, Packbacks, and mini quizzes with unlimited attempts, creating a relaxed learning environment. Minimal study was required, making it a fun and interesting class overall.

I loved this course! Extremely easy to understand and genuinely engaging. Exams and assignments make sense even if you don't attend every lecture. Dr. Thompson clearly cares about this field and is very flexible and willing to work with students for deadlines and the like, definitely recommend.

She was very passionate about the subject and I feel like I left the class with a lot more knowledge of the world. She's very caring and interacts with all of her students. She does these things called "mini exams" which are supposed to help with testing anxiety but were overall more inconvenient. Overall I would recommend taking a class with her.
Love love love this professor. Her class is super easy and she is very understanding. By far the best professor at MSU.

I took PSY 101 with her online. The class was very easy to understand and learn about. We had a quiz and one pack back questions due every week. It was one of the stressful least classes I had to worry about over the semester. The one thing I will is that this class has you taking a lot of notes and reading a lot. The textbook was found online.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Enjoyable class and interesting material. Very easy to do well in this class. I had this class fully online so it was super spread out throughout the week and paced very nicely.
Amazing professor! Took this class online, it was organized great, clear directions for the class. Digestible and helpful class assignments. Do the work and get an A.
Easiest class I have every took. Lectures were actually enjoyable and so many free points were given just for trying in the class. Dr. Thompson is also very sweet.

I took this class asynchronous and it was good overall. There were many lectures to watch each week and you had notes as well. The discussion posts on packback were easy and as long as you pay attention to the lectures, you will do well on the tests.
Took this asynchronous, if you do whats assigned its an easy A. She does a lot of discussion boards to get the class talking, makes the class more fun. Fun and interesting class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took psych this semester and I really enjoyed it. In part because of the professor. Dr. Thompson was an amazing professor who cares about her students. The class is really lecture heavy but it isnt necessarily hard material. We do weekly Packbacks which are easy to get an A on. Overall, great professor and its a easy A if you do the work.

For the most part, if you participate in this class, you're going to get an A. Unlimited attempts on all quizzes, and she drops one of each different type of assignment. I never needed my textbook, though it's a free pdf, and I hardly needed to study either.

It was always hard to know what to study. Walker's handouts are very confusing and sometimes even the TAs didn't even know what the answer was. The exams are also different from the textbook and Walker's own handouts. Most questions you couldn't even figure out what he was asking for in each box.

I took CEM 251 back in 2018. Dr. Walker is an incredible professor. I attended his office hours weekly and that really helped. If you put the effort in, you'll succeed in this course. Nothing bad to say about Dr. Walker. I'd recommend taking his course.
Professor walker is a good lecturer despite what others say, if you pay attention in lecture and do his optional handouts you will do fine in this class.

I think his low rating is unwarranted. Mr. Walker is an expert in what he teaches and if you learn through analogy or stories then he will be a great professor. I would understand if his teaching style wasn't for everyone, but lectures are not going to be boring at least. Just attend lectures, study, review: I found outlining the textbook helpful.

He was a pretty terrible lecturer, but grading was quite generous, although you are only graded on like 5 things total. So be sure to do well in all of them. Going to lecture is pretty useless unless you want to participate. Make sure to read the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly I found this class to be rather simple, I finished with a 3.0 but never once did I have to put in any effort to achieve that doing the homework was enough and the first exam is all review from gen chem if you just do the homework and do well on one of the exams you should easily get a 3.0

You know in old movies that take place in the dessert with tumbleweeds and half swing doors and cowboys that have toothpicks in their mouth, that is Kevin. He is the most out of pocket person I've ever heard speak. He talks in circles yet thinks he is explain things. One TA was a cocky weasel and the other was the sweetest guy. Exams are impossible

Most people seemed to hate Walker, but he handed out extra credit like candy and made the class very achievable with an 85% cutoff for 4.0. The TAs are also really good for this class and make the content in lecture easy to stomach. He is so funny in class and creates easily rememberable phrases to describe certain mechanisms.

It was without a doubt the worst class I have ever taken. Kevin is an awful teacher. You were only graded on 5 exams and homework. The only kids who passed his class with a 4.0 were chemical engineering majors. He makes very weird sounds and slightly sexual comments about chemistry during class just made me feel weirdly uncomfy. COLD CALLS!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easily the most disorganized professor ever. Walker does not have sympathy for poor grades, and does not alter his teaching style to accommodate learners. Curves are not offered, extra credit is minimal, and the exams do not reflect any learned material that is taught. Shame on MSU for hiring the literal worst organic chemistry professor ever.

Lectures are disjointed and did not seem to have a specific goal. Quiz class averages rarely surpassed 40%. Walker never addressed this. Just moved on, not changing his teaching style. Would write mechanisms, but not explain what they were for or even what mechanism it was. Nice as a person, but should not be teaching this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is one of the worst professors at MSU. The chemistry department should be ashamed that he teaches. He has been reported numerous times over the years to no avail. He curses (constantly), proceeds to deviate and go on long tangents, is very difficult to follow in lectures and tries to to be “funny,” by making inappropriate jokes/remarks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most people seemed to dislike Walker, but I felt he was a pretty fair professor. His grading criteria was very fuzzy at first for the biweekly quizzes, but it got better as the semester progressed. He was very funny during lectures, but often acted like you were stupid if you asked questions. Curved the final and gave clear topics to study for it.

Walker is funny prof but his lectures are very unorganized. His office hours are the best resource possible as he can actually explain concepts and come up with problems for you to work on- which preps you for his unique style of quiz questions. He offers a TON of extra credit (around 50 points, aka an entire quiz worth) making it a fairly easy A.

he writes notes on the board but he rarely indicates the mechanism or topic of what he is doing. quizzes were obscenely hard since there was no real structure. no clear learning targets. he is all over the place at all times, no coherent train of thought. he does remember his students and tries to use examples and analogies.

Walker has an interesting teaching style. He often begins to explain a topic and gets off track. Quizzes are hard because we aren't prepared well with what is on them. I've tried to follow him in lecture but its just so hard. Lots of homework (50 problems per week) that you have to use the book to teach yourself. Very difficult class.

Uses chalk and board. My notes were just structures & arrows; no real meaning behind it (which is partially my fault, could of wrote some words). He often skips the arrows and makes it hard how he got to the end. Quizzes are difficult if you don't study b/c it's just blank boxes. Likes students who goes to his office hours and knows them by name.

Walker is a good professor. It's obvious he puts effort into teaching and giving the students what they need to do well. He teaches chemistry though, not mindless problem solving, so be prepared to actually try to understand the material.  He supplies lecture notes and is helpful for any questions you might have after lectures and in office hours.

I'm sure Walker is a decent person outside of the classroom, but his lectures are extremely hard to follow, he treats the class like it's a review course and your entire grade is based off of his impossible quizzes, which he does not prepare students well for. I tried really hard to like him in the beginning but his teaching style is just awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I attended every lecture and all my recitations. I spent time trying to teach myself topics that i did not understand but the exams were VERY tough. Don't recommend unless you are willing to go to every office hour PLUS study 1-2 hours after every lecture.

Im sure professor Walker is a great guy outside of class, however, I couldnt think of a single positive thing to say about the way he runs this course. Let me put it simply, Walker refrained from using D2L the entire semester, only used his words and chalk to explain complicated topics, and was distracted the entirety of the class. I wish you luck

His lectures are very confusing and honestly did not help a lot, but there are quizzes every week that you automatically get 100% on if you just go to class. His exams are very challenging. You will have to take a lot of time out of class to succeed in this course. I highly recommend watching youtube videos and doing the homework to study for exam.

I saw he had horrible reviews and I thought I was smart enough to manage, but nope. He's hands down one of the worst profs at MSU. He acts like this is a review course. My biggest pet peeve is that he hardly ever addresses what he's teaching. For example you could be working on stereoisometry, but he hardly ever actually labels what he is teaching.

Walker is a funny dude, but everything I learned in this class was from his amazing TA. This class was ridiculously hard where only the top 5% of geniuses in the class succeed. Grade is only composed of 4 exams and 6 quizzes. But he did round my grade A LOT at the end of the semester which was nice. Highly suggest another prof tho
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Walker is not the best at lectures and goes off on tangents but does care about his students. Don't take his class if you're not willing to put in hours on your own. Use resources and office hours because lectures move quickly and his notes are jumbled. His exams are hard but if you do all the practice problems multiple times, it's not too bad.
This guy is not organized by any means! and he doesn't know how to articulate his theories or the mechanisms of the reactions! prepare to learn everything on your own.

He needs to be taught how to actually teach a class of 400 kids.Made decent mnemonics. This man made me skip class frequently. Do not sit near the front row unless you want to be called on. He makes you feel dumb. I used to love chemistry, but having him as a teacher made me hate it now. Avoid him at all costs.
"VERY unorganized, makes ZERO sense, scatterbrained. I learned nothing in class. Never looked at my notes once to study. Learned everything from TA's.

First of all, I have a 4.0 GPA, I am a lyman briggs and honors college student. I found Walker to be terrible. The second day of class, he called some girl "Red" who had red hair and a red shirt and at the end of class another girl asked a question and he called her "ginger" after he thought his mic was off. He also blows students off, A LOT.

I ended up 4.0ing this class only because I spent over an hour every day solely studying for this class, teaching myself the material. Dr. Walker's exams are definitely tough and sometimes include things that are not clearly covered in lecture. Exams make up a great percentage of your exam, so if you don't do well on those you will not do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He talks to his students, who don't know chemistry like they've been studying it for as long as he has. He also doesn't teach the overarching concepts in class. His practice exams are wayyy easy compared to the actual exams. He does reviews, but when the questions he reviews are not the same as exam questions, it doesn't help much. AVOID him.

He has a lot of aspects that make up a good professor, but I think he does poorly at connecting with/understanding his students (it also doesn't help that exams are 93% of your grade). If you always pay attention and practice a lot outside of class you should see somewhat decent results. I never went to office hours, but I've heard they help.

Lectures are hard to follow as he constantly goes off on tangents, your grade is determined almost entirely by the insanely difficult exams (which aren't curved at all) and you will likely have to teach yourself the material outside of class. However, due to the way the grading scale works it is entirely possible to bomb every exam and still pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid him. Certified gpa tanker and not a very nice person. Does not answer emails quickly or in full. Exams do not resemble his lecture material or the textbook he assigns. Exams make up 93% percent of the grade. 10+ hrs of studying for each exam did not help my exam scores. Talks down on students, has no sympathy and lectures incoherently.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have such mixed opinions of Dr. Walker. it is evident to see he is very passionate about the material, is very knowledgeable, and does want to see his students succeed. I gave a low rating because he does teach the class as if we already know organic chem. If you aren't willing to put in work, then don't take it. He can't do everything for you.
Mediocre professor. Class is easy, but lectures consist of Walker rambling on and on about nonsense.

I honestly didn't learn anything from the class. Material isn't well explained. Tests and other items are not graded in efficient manner. You will teach yourself the information if you actually want to know the material.

Now that I've had a semester away from Walker, I can speak fairly about him. The class is hard, but he decently prepares you. People love to complain when things aren't an easy A, but if you put in the work & try you can do good (I recommend going to his review sessions before exams - super helpful). Prepared me well for Orgo 2 unlike other profs.

While Dr.Walker tries to make lectures fun and bearable it's just really difficult to learn from him and most of my learning has been from youtube and the textbook. The only grades that are put in are exams and biweekly quizzes. I would strongly recommend choosing a different professor unless you're okay with teaching yourself orgo.

Where do I begin. He is a very off task professor - he starts talking about one thing and next thing I know he has completely shifted to a different topic that has nothing to do with what we're doing. His exams are quite near impossible and your grade is mainly made up of solely exams. STAY AWAY FROM HIM!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor at MSU. Lectures are hard to follow and make little to no sense. You have to study for hours after class to make sense of the material. He gets distracted easily and is not open to questions. Exams are pretty much your only grade and he makes them insanely difficult. I have a 4.0, but walkers class is impossible. STAY AWAY!!

I normally don'r leave reviews but for Professor Walker I have to make en exception. He is by far the worst professor I have ever had. I had to teach myself all of the content, and he crammed two very important topics into one class period. Stay away. If you can't, be ready to spend hours on your own teaching yourself organic chemistry.

His lectures are very hard and confusing to understand. Besides points for the in-class quizzes and going to recitation, exams are the main thing. The exams are nothing like the questions we practice in class and they are very hard.

his lectures are so long and he can't stay on one topic for more than two minutes. he never finishes his thought and is not easy to follow at all. he lectures as if you're already supposed to know the material and does not properly explain anything. exams make or break your whole grade so if you're not doing well on those you have like no EC.

I didn't really learn much in the class. Everything I learned I taught myself. Exams are hard and not from Dr. Walker handwritten notes . He doesn't teach very well. He doesn't answer questions very well either. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT! He isn't a bad prof, just not my cup of tea.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Walker  is a very nice professor and is very passionate about the material; however, CEM 251 is a hard course! You need to dedicate hours each week just to keep up with the material and be ready to read and take notes independently from the textbook as well! Attendance is a must. He is a very knowledge prof who gives lots of extra credit!

I hated him at first, but he grew on me. He is usually entertaining, and makes you work for your grade. Slack off, or don't follow his instructions and you might as well drop. Knows his stuff and will help you. This was the hardest class I ever took, and the one I am most proud to say I got and A in.

They either love him or hate him. I don't understand. Know him from couple of semesters ago. HE'S great to everyone. Knows his stuff. Is helpful. Makes chem fun. But you must study. He can't do everything for you.

Dr. Walker is a very funny guy but definitely knows what he's talking about. His jokes are sooo random but they kinda make sense when relating it to chemistry, so it's funny. CEM 251 is hard course. It is 60% on you and 40% on him. So, practice and go to his or TAs office hours.
Dr. Walker is a decent professor. Not the greatest lecturer. Notes are all hand written and they sometimes get sloppy. Would recommend if you don't like homework and willing to study a lot for tests.

It's definitely a difficult course, but Walker makes the content entertaining and accessible. He's genuinely invested in the success of his students. Use the extra practice problems to your advantage - he's not kidding when he says a lot of those practice problems are similar to exam questions. If you have questions, ask!

He is a great professor and a great guy. Teaching sometimes does not seem to be his best suit. He is unorganized and you will not have an idea what your grade is. If you show up to class and do the work and study a little bit you will pass his class and do pretty well. You have to respect everyone's ideas which I liked.

CEM 251 is a lecture-heavy class, and unfortunately I often found Prof. Walker's lectures to be boring and drawn-out. He is a nice person and a fair, quick grader, but I wish I had been more engaged in his class. CEM 251 is not a hard class, but you really need to know all details in the lecture notes. Anything in them is fair game for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Orgo is hard. IF you put in the time and work. Highly recommend doing all the problems he assigns you for homework because that is what the exam will be like.

He can sometimes go on tangents here and there about what somethings can be used for but overall he is pretty good at giving examples in class and always holds review sessions and encourages his students to come to office hours
He gave extra credit after students asked for it; he has evening review sessions every Tuesday.  I managed to get a 4.0. It is a tough class, but doable.

Professor Walker is a fantastic lecturer, he made use of analysis and comparisons that can help with understanding otherwise vague and new concepts. reviews.comment: I'm convinced the last 4 positive comments on here are made by bots or paid for by Professor Walker. Avoid at literally all costs if you're not expecting to put hours upon hours upon hours into orgo and still see no results in your grade because of the exams.

reviews.comment: Hard class material but nothing much you can do about it. Allows honors option, answers emails fairly quickly. Quizzes and tests are kinda hard but he doesn't try to trick you, answers every question during lecture, lots of opportunities for extra points.
Good class. I was challenged but I learned a lot. Going into this class I thought I was going to hate it but now I actually enjoy organic chemistry.
It's orgo, it's going to be hard. There is lots of studying! All lectures were posted. He's slightly hard to understand but he knows his stuff.

Walker is very passionate about chemistry and prepares his students well for future Chem courses. He uses lots of helpful analogies, and honestly tries to help his students succeed by offering lots of extra credit. Be prepared to study, because the tests are hard and make up the majority of your grade. Think twice before taking the honors option

If professor Walker were to teach the tale of the three little pigs, he'd tell the story backwards and forget to say that the wolf was bad. Absolutely horrendous "teaching style", which involves spending time regurgitating irrelevant information that will never appear on any of his self-made exams. Not there to help you, just to make jokes.
This class has driven me to therapy.

reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

Don't take his class if you care about grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Walker is a nice person but a horrible professor. Absolutely HORRIBLE. Please, avoid taking his class if you want a good grade in orgo. For the last two exams, the averages were a 58% and he still refuses to curve. Your grade is solely based on exams and the only content material you receive from him to study are his crappy handwritten notes.

VERY DIFFICULT. I don't recommend unless you want to teach yourself. He is very difficult to understand because he is extremely disorganized. Notes are all over the place and often goes off on tangents in the middle of problems. He is a good guy and tries but I do not recommend him as a prof as he is extremely difficult to follow.

Over the semester you have 3 exams & a final and those 4 exams make up 450/500 points total for the class (90% of your grade). His notes are all over the place and make no sense and the only way to learn is khan academy or a tutor. 2nd exam we took, average was a 57% & no curve because 1 person got 100%. reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He canceled an entire exam the day on hours after it was supposed to take place because he could not figure out how to use the same software we had already successfully tested on. He uses heavy terminology. The only reason I passed was my tutor and the fact that he had to change the grading scale to 74% to get 4.0 since he dropped an entire exam.

Genuinely an awful professor and human being. Calls on people randomly. Will make fun of you during lecture if you leave early. Spends half the class telling unfunny jokes and irrelevant stories. Constantly makes mistakes while teaching and his notes are horrible. Khan Academy does a better job teaching ochem than this guy ever will. Avoid.

Professor Walker does not deserve the amount of hate that he gets. He is very knowledgable. It is just misfortunes of switching to online that became a problem. His grading scale helps you a lot, I 3.5d this class and I didn't deserve it with how little work I put in. He also gives more extra credit than any other chem class!

Everyone is tough on Dr. Walker but he really tries his best to accommodate everyone with exam curves and accessibility. exams long so study! best things are the practice quizzes in class and the end of chapter textbook questions. everyone that complains about Dr. Walker probably wanted their grade handed to them. He's a nice guy and likes to joke.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: THE ABSOLUTE WORST PROFESSOR AT MSU. he does not teach, he jokes around the entire lecture. he was so behind this semester that he didnt have time to cover 2 ENTIRE CHAPTERS. if you get him as a professor, if he even has a job after this semester (hes been fired before ive heard), drop the class and take it next semester. save yourself the stress

Knows what he is talking about and is able to explain it in many different ways but his lectures are disorganized and he jumps around a lot. Also, the tests are not at all what you would expected and much harder than what you learn. There is no hw in this class your grade is only the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take CEM 251 with walker. I learned more from the TAs/tutors and by teaching myself than he ever taught me. His lectures are hardly worth it. He does not know how to teach effectively and he constantly jumps all over the place. Hes a nice guy, but could use some guidance on how to teach.

Dr. Walker is a very intelligent man; however, he does not understand how to teach his knowledge to those who have never seen organic chemistry before. Choose other professors to learn the material, because he talks more about trying to make students understand him than actually presenting the material to his students in a way that's easy to grasp.

The students' attitudes seem to change year-to-year--guided by social streams. The practice problems look very similar to those on the exam, save those that are concept problems that require you to THINK. Those who do poorly (they are few) in the class seem to think Walker can be a miracle worker and offer the harshest criticisms.

Would not recommend any one to take cem 251 with Dr. Walker. I feel that he assumes his students know what he is talking about when in reality we are all clueless. He poorly explains topics and claims that his practice problems are far more difficult than his exam problems which is completely untrue. If you're not pre-med or pre-vet, run away.
You have to put the work in. You get deja vu after studying practice problems long enough. When you get the test, you realize many of the problems are exactly the same as what you just practiced.

It seems prof walker has changed his ways. I had him for last semester orgo I and he was a good teacher. It gets sticky when he tries to put things into perspective in his own way. Either way the practice homework he posts is 90% the material on the exam.. he even says so. I 4.0 and I just made sure i understood all concepts and problems on the hw.

DO NOT TAKE ORGANIC CHEMISTRY WITH DR. WALKER! He is a terrible teacher, and doesn't seem to care if the students learn the material. He's rather rude and will make you feel dumb if you don't know the answer to questions he asks. His exams are outrageous. This is the worst experience I've had at MSU.

CSE 102 got completely revamped in Fall 2025,no more TA's just the professor, and she is a very good teacher, the online homework is redundant and boring, I learned a lot more during the Labs/in-person lectures, she will help you if your struggling with the lab assignment. classes are less than 25 people. She is very experienced and willing to help
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The class got harder for me around Nov but the professor was pretty in-depth in her reviews during labs and was always ready to help when needed. It was just really time-consuming
Not that bad if you can learn on your own. Overhated but not great

this class is horrible. TA's never go over quizzes so if u didn't know what u were doing, u still won't! everyones reviews talking about academic dishonesty and cheating are true. This was such a hard class for being a introductory. If you love yourself, don't take this class. While this class isn't necessarily hard, there is so much work that it makes it near impossible.
Would give this professor a 0/5 if i could, doesn't care for the students and gives incredibly hard quizzes and exams

I don't know what the professors do for this course other than hw lecture videos and grading exams, they do nothing to help the students of the class and rely heavily on the TA's to do the professor's job for them. No wonder the CSE requirement was dropped for the business school because the course is so poorly taught I hope the professor is fired
The professors genuinely do nothing and its all on the ta's to teach you the content. Most pathetic and useless professor I have ever had in my academic career

Incredibly hard quizzes and exams doesn't, the quizzes are pass/fail and some of them are incredibly hard for no reason the course is poorly organized and taught and the quizzes are so annoying like why not just use a normal multiple choice quiz instead of heavily tanking the grades of the students

While this course was taught by TAs, Wulfekuhler wasn't very respectful to any of the students. Highly recommend to make a friend in this class to work on HW and labs.
By far the worst class and professors at MSU. Even if I did do well in this class, I would still not like anything about the course. It is nearly impossible, and the professors are 0 help whatsoever.

This class is way easier now compared to what it was, but the "professors" are no help. I don't even want to call them professors, because they have no presence throughout the course, which is carried by TAs. The class isn't that hard if you buckle down and do the work, but don't expect help from any of the professors.
Awful teacher. Doesn't care about students. TA's run the class. MSU needs her fired.

Was an easy course for me since I got 6 for computer science SL in IB diploma. He didn't teach lectures. And, all those videos on codio were not enough. I would say his lectures were not helpful. I ended up with 4.0 but there are many tasks to do during this class. Just get used to the coding. It's recommended to self-learn the theoretical parts.

Literally the worst class I have ever taken in my whole life.  Prof does not even teach the class, it is 100% taught by TA's who half the time do not know how to explain the topic.  The videos were long and tedious and had absolutely no hand in helping me with the content.  The only reason I took this course was because I have to for my major
The teacher really doesn't seem to have designed these lessons very well and is very unfriendly to students who are just starting out
Teachers can't seem to get students to understand the content

You can only watch low quality videos recorded about 4 or 5 years ago in a semester

Also we don't have a good way to ask teachers.
You can only see the teaching assistants in class
But can't seem to understand what they are saying

There are many teachers who teach this class. But they all use an online model
There are a lot of problems with the system this year and it doesn't seem to be working out very well
The content and timing of the exams are completely unrealistic, and students have to waste time changing between two pages constantly.

This class is really hard, but if you keep up with the weekly homework then you should be fine. You will never see the professors, and all of the sections are run by ta's. There are quizzes which are not bad if you've done the homework. Exams are tougher. The projects are the hardest part, but they are only worth 6% of your grade.

This class made me change majors. the class was WW2 History but quickly devolved into Soviet history. We skipped almost all of the allied content in favor of soviet  battles. I can't recommend taking another class enough, please don't make the same mistake I did.

took every thing in me to get the grade I did in this class, I was reading over a hundred pages per class and the only grades we had were 3 exams with very unclear instructions. If you are not willing to put in 15+ hours a week this might not be the class for you.

reviews.comment: I took this class because I love American History, and the class was WWII. However, you learn about things from the European perspective, per say. He packs a little too much information into his lectures so it is hard to take good notes and follow along, but he uses movies occasionally which helps alot. He is more than willing to help students. Beware his midterm is pretty intense but the class is well worth it especially if you are interested in European history which is not my forte.
for ece 410, the longest project i have ever had to do was this class. the professor does not help and grades extremely tough and does not help at all

reviews.comment: I got an average of 87 on the exams and an average of 85 on the homework yet somehow finished with a 2.0. Go to class or else the attendance will tank your grade. Outside of that she's one of the better professors that I've had here at MSU.

This class was overall very easy in comparison to MSU's 201 circuits class. Guided notes, easy lecture, worst part about her was mandatory attendance.

Class is extremely boring. Mostly reading off slides, or throwing on random films/documentaries. Doesn't respond to emails. attendance is confusing, says is mandatory but barely takes it. Says will drop you a whole letter grade for missing more than 3 classes.

reviews.comment: Slow grades (no grades entered more than halfway through the semester), and the course topic is just not what the class is described as. If you want to learn more about Chilean politics, def take this course, but if you're looking for reading writing by women, this isn't it.

McCleese only gave out 5 assignments the whole semester.  She takes attendance randomly so just attend even though it is boring af. Her lessons are so boring, playing minesweeper is more entertaining. She reads everything off of a slideshow, (which that is NOT posted to D2L).

This professor graded everything a week before the course ended. An okay instructor who oddly made the class about food culture. One of the worst professors I've ever had. I was expecting the course to relate to the description MSU put out, but she put an "indigenous food studies" twist to it. Lectures consist of her reading slides in a monotone voice. She gives us useless assingments and hasn't graded anything the entire semester (less than a month left). Stay away.

Very careless about student feedback or incidents. Took random attendance for the first month as a scare tactic, then suddenly stopped, nobody knows when she will take attendance next. Easy 4.0 she didn't really have class a lot and was an easy grader besides that he grading didn't go in till the last day but if you want an easy 4.0 take it with her you also only like have 4 scattered assignments so if you don't really care and are a good writer this class is for you

As an exchange student the class was anything but interesting especially when we had to read a book about a child vampire having relations with adults and we had activities on this without analyzing it in class. Dr.Mccleese is a nice person yet she has no idea how to grade. I have zero grades right now and it is the end of the semester. Dr. McCleese is clearly a great scholar but she CAN NOT TEACH. She only reads off slides the entire lecture and takes forever to grade anything despite promising to grade sooner. She is literally afraid of students and acts very timid.

Other reviews are true, I didn't get anything out of the class, but if you want something easy you found it. I skipped class often and my grade wasn't effected. I didn't put a lot of work into the papers and I just rambled and made stuff up for the final project because I didn't read the book it was about and I got a 4.0 in the class so I'm not mad

My grade on this class was based on 2 300 pnt papers, 1 300 pnt project, and 200 pnts of attendance thats c/nc. Criteria for assignments was unclear and as such they were very difficult to write. Very poor experience. Very late grader, unclear and confusing projects and grading guidelines. Lectures are monotone, unengaging, and unhelpful. Is not accessible outside of class, email regarding course was never returned.

Every one of these reviews is accurate. The course was extremely unorganized and Professor Mccleese often times seemed like she had no idea what she was talking about. DO NOT TAKE CLASSES FROM THIS PROFESSOR. She did not consider attendance this semester due to Covid and tried her best to be accommodating. I liked Dr. McCleese. She was an alright professor for a basic class. There were only a couple projects in the class but she put the grades in at the last couple weeks of class. Technically attendance is mandatory, but she hasn't taken it since the start of the semester. Due dates unclear, often pushed back because she never gives any place for it to be turned in at.
