reviews.comment: Very good professor, you can tell he actually cares about his students and he's just overall very sweet. He's super fair and if you have an issue easy to reach and willing to help out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Penyak truly does care about his students. He has no final cumulative exam, but attendance is part of your grade. Recitations were also helpful review.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She left for 5 weeks mid semester for a trip and had 2 TA's running class and barely knew how.
Professor never answers email and disappears for weeks at a time.

To be honest her class is pretty easy. There are in class questions you must answer for attendance/grade, but class material is pretty easy. Exams are half multiple choice half written but again not hard. She is gone doing research a lot so will have canceled classes/ TA ran classes which is nice. My downfall was not paying attention in class

Dr. Peters is super nice! She taught half of the lectures, and Dr. Peacor taught the other half. I think that she had simpler topics, so it was easier to understand her. The rest of the class was quite difficult outside of her lectures. Something that made things a bit difficult was her lack of study materials for exams.
I love Dr. Peters. She genuinely cares about her students, and I love the way she teaches her classes. I recommend every student take her class.

I loved Dr. Peters! I enjoyed taking her Great Lakes Bio class. It wasn't a ton of work and the quizzes felt fair. This semester, she offered that if you had over a 90% in the class you didn't have to take the final exam so make sure you attend class! There were no attendance drops but a few chances for extra credit.

Dr. Peters is a great professor! She obviously knows what she's talking about and welcomes any questions or comments on the material. She makes an effort to get to know the class and lectures are engaging and interesting. Attendance is not required but participation matters! Exams are written response but easy if you go to class and participate.

Dr. Peters is a good professor and she is obviously very knowledgeable in her field. However, her grading is weird sometimes and her quizzes/tests are all short answer. I would take her class again, but be prepared for it to be slightly unorganized and for her to be gone several lectures.

Dr. Peters cares a lot about her students and works hard to know everyones name. She makes a fairly large class feel close knit. The assignments are varying and cater to many different types of learners. She is readily available to help whenever. I hope I can go with her on the study abroad this summer! She's overall just a great person.
Good teacher easy course
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great prof, super nice, forgiving on missing pts on assignments/exams. Just show up to class, and if u can't email them and u can get points back. Not too much homework, exams were very fair, and lectures were engaging that helped prepare for the exams. Need more profs like her

Dr. Peters is a funny person and makes lectures fun. She rarely assigns homework (BS162) and grades very forgivingly on exams. The ONLY downside of taking her/BS162 is attendance is mandatory and if you miss one day, it takes your participation grade down about 3%, which is annoying but other than that I would recommend her to anyone who asked!

Peters is a great professor. The main reason I liked her class was because the practice exams matched up to the actual exams very well. You never had to worry about not knowing what was going to be on the exam. The amount of homework was very fair and when we did have homework it was not very difficult or time consuming at all.

BS 162 was a lot easier than BS 161. Everything you need to know for the exams Dr. Peters goes over in class. All tests are free response but they are really similar to the practice tests. Attendance is not mandatory technically but there is a google form you have to fill out each class. If you attend most lectures you will get a good grade.

absolutely NO amber slander.  science does not come easy to me. but ive gained SO much confidence in this class. Amber is approachable, shes funny, and shes inspiring. class material is easy to digest yet difficult too. but if you pay attention, ask questions, and do the practice exams  common homework, you'll be fine.

I loved Dr. Peters! She tries her hardest to make the class easy for her students. 35% of our final grade was based on homework (most of them being in-class activities), so make sure you do those. The exams are spaced out well and they are not too hard as long as you pay attention the lectures and do the Common Homeworks.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Honestly, I thought this class was so annoying. The class material is boring, not sure why any pre-med would want to learn it. Tests are all short answers which is so annoying, make it multiple choice like any normal class come on. Also, they take 3 weeks to grade your exams which is absolutely ridiculous. Should consider changing class format.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Peters is great! Her lectures make a lot of sense and her in-class questions really help the material "stick." Peppy and approachable, making the best of online classes. Her tests and homework are fair, just pay attention in class and you'll do fine. Stuff takes a while to get graded though.

One major problem I had with this class was how LONG it took to find out grades for exams, like a good 3 weeks even though theres 5 TAs and lecture is only about 150 people so that bothers me. Other than that, her exams are very easy and Amber relates a lot of her lectures to everyday life and her own life and was a great teacher and person.
Very cool teacher. She was super straight forward and the tests were exactly what we learned in class. However, all tests included short answer!

she is so unorganized and the pickiest grader ever on exams its so ridiculous. exams are all free response. the material isnt hard but shes so picky on grading that in the end she has to curve the class. shes a really nice lady and the final is group which is nice. but still, shes just so freaking picky on grading
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Amber Peter's class. You form a group to work with at the beginning of the year. The final is taken with your group. She gives a lot of study materials for the class. One thing I would complain about is that she posts homework and other useful documents very last minute. Overall great class and much better than BS161.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amber is super nice! There is homework every week and it is posted over weekend, kinda inconvenient but the homework was usually really easy, I usually did Btwn classes. Exams are straight to the point with great study guides. The group work is nothing to worry about, its mostly discussion with each other in class 4 particp, no agonizing projects.

Lectures are kind of long, the class was a bit disorganized, and in-class group assignments got a bit tedious, but the work was fairly simple and the exams/tests/quizzes were near mirrored to practices.

To begin with, Amber has an extremely annoying voice and her voice makes it hard to sit through a 2 hour lecture. She is also very disorganized. If we have a homework assignment due on Tuesday, don't expect it to be posted before Sunday. Everyday in class there is an in class assignment and it can get a little annoying.

For better or for worse, there's not much that I can go into detail about Amber. This course, like most ISP courses, was one I, speaking on behalf of most of the students in the class, was not eager about taking. With all negative remarks and low expectations aside, she elaborated fairly succinctly on the causes and effects of climate change.

This is the most ridiculous class I've ever had the displeasure of taking.  Prof and TAs are rampantly disorganized, the material covered belongs in a high school classroom, and there is a ridiculous amount of busywork assigned.  I become physically ill during labs due to the utter stupidity of the tasks we are told to undertake.  Avoid.
She is an effective, helpful instructor. Her class format was quite good. She's very/too nice. Note to other students: SHUT UP while she is lecturing. No one is paying to listen to you!

easy and super interesting class that only meets once a week. Just gotta go to class and raise your hand 6 times in a semester for full participation so easy again. Readings are through perusall which is annoying but again if you can't read 20 pages once a week you probably should not be in college. a few easy cooking assignments, great prof.

Loved Dr. Qu! I'm honestly not sure why these reviews are so bad… her class is extremely easy. I got stuck with this class because it was the only IAH that fit into my schedule, however, I really enjoyed it. Class was only once a week and I actually found the lectures to be pretty interesting. Easy homework (quizzes) and midterm/final assignments.

There is a weekly quiz on a movie and/or a reading every week which can be annoying. There are participation stickers and you need 10 to get 100%. Attendance is mandatory with two unexcused. Quizzes are not lock down. Has a midterm paper and final online presentation. Nice teacher, didn't have any problems.
Save yourself the trouble and take another class.

Read the weekly course material and participate in class- the course is easy. People love to complain about everything. If you put effort into the essay portion of quiz you'll earn extra credit; I had no problems. 

I recommend this class to anyone genuinely interested in East Asia, b/c I enjoyed the material she provided. The lectures are boring.
Many reviews don't like her but I think the quizzes were not hard and you only had to do projects instead of exams. Also really easy to talk to for help.

Weekly quizzes are hard, and her grading of the "short" answer is strict. A reading or movie/series every week for the quiz that is usually unavailable unless you want to search for a free version for hours or paying. Mandatory attendance but class is only once a week, You need to participate. She also grades very slowly even with little students.
Just save yourself the trouble, pick a different class.

reviews.comment: This class is impossible. Quizzes are impossible and she picks readings and movies that nobody has ever heard of. She's more concerned picking things that people can't look up rather than picking content relative to the class.

reviews.comment: The quizzes are weird and imposossible. I went to class and some of the questions on the quizzes she never goes over, you can't look them up, and quizzes are most of your grade. I hated my life on the days I had this class.

The class literally isn't that hard. Some of these reviews are just overreacting. That being said, I wouldn't take the class if you aren't into East Asia, which I feel like is pretty obvious already. reviews.comment: BEST TEACHER I EVER HAD! She is very concise and has a very clear passion for teaching. I came into the class with no interest in the course and was surprised by the engaging material. If you pay attention, this class is sooooooo easy.

Extremely boring class. Would not recommend it to anyone. Class averages for quizzes are around 75% and don't seem to phase her. Class participation is your attendance grade but doesn't give many opportunities to participate in class.

The professor is ok. I would not recommend this class if you want an easy IAH. I am a big reader, but the readings and lectures were quite long most of the time even for me. The only assignments that are graded is the quiz every week, which she grades harshly. Many of my classmates have emailed her about issues and it was 50/50 for her to solve it.

reviews.comment: well I did get a 4.0, this class was incredibly hard compared to other classes u can take instead. Professor also grades very hard and there is a ton of work. I would not recommend this class ):
Very boring lectures, too much reading for a single week's work, random drawing required for projects that don't relate. This isn't an art class, it's history.

reviews.comment: Lessons cover a lot of the class prep activities relating to the shows watched in class this semester. Very flexible with submitting late work and she if she doesn't allow corrections on summary activities (tests), they're usually given a bit of a curve anyway. Я люблю Жанну :)

Lessons follow the Mezdhu Nami workbook until it's finished, then they go onto prep for the spring semester of 200 level RUS

reviews.comment: Do not take this class if you can. There is lots of reading every week and the stories are boring. I took this class because of the easy schedule but wish I hadn't.

reviews.comment: He is very cautious about plaigarism/ChatGPT so be careful. However the class itself was super easy. You just have to read quite a bit and write discussion posts and take some small quizzes. Thats really it though

reviews.comment: As this class is an online class, I can't say much about the professor but more on the course. I really enjoyed this class and was really interested that I actually want this class to be made in person as well. reviews.comment: I took ANP 429 and it was a very enjoyable and memorable experience. Class is friendly to beginner ethnographers and the professor is caring towards your progress. The readings are not overwhelming by any means and the class structures you well for the final project. Amazing professor with a lot of experience and knowledge in the field.

Prof Quan has interesting material however there is so much reading and additional articles that it was unrealistic for me to actually process the content even though I was genuinely interested and wanted to learn. If he cut out the excess requirements I would have had a much deeper understanding of everything we covered.

reviews.comment: I took ANP 200 in an online asynchronous format over the summer as an elective. I don't remember much from the course other than the materials were super easy and the class required minimal work. If you do the assignments you will have no issues in this course.

I feel bad giving her a lower rating because she is very sweet and kind to all of her students. But her lectures are long, boring, and tough to understand at times due to her strong accent. The midterm was randomly thrown onto us two days before the due date, in which the wrong time was told. Subpar lectures and unclear instructions define this.

(I had Qing for 201, not 202, but it wasn't an option) 

Professor Qing is an exceptional, extremely caring professor. If you want to 4.0 the class, go to her office hours and do her honors option! She gives extra credit (unlike other JMC professors) and show your appreciation for her. Nevertheless, try your best and your work will be recognized.

Professor Qing is one of the sweetest and most understanding professors I have ever had, and she is very knowledgable on a variety of political science and IR topics. Her class is somewhat disorganized and instructions for essays and assignments can be somewhat unclear, but she is usually more than willing to answer any questions you have.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Love her so much. Super intelligent and understanding that life happens.

I appreciated that Professor Qing took the time to make sure we understood her lectures (she recognises that her accent is hard to understand). My biggest problem is that her guidelines for assignments are incredibly vague.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Qing! I really enjoyed her MC 201 course. She was very accessible outside of class and got to know us as people in addition to students. Her research is very interesting. She was a fair grader and attending office hours was really helpful. She is very sweet and I'm so glad to have developed a relationship with her. 100% recommend!
She's an amazing teacher, my favorite at James Madison College.

I LOVED Professor Qing! She is a little hard to understand sometimes but has no problem repeating herself for you if needed. She does not take attendance but I would obviously recommend attending class as much as you can. I enjoyed her so much for MC220 that I am taking MC318 with her this semester!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Qing is very bright. While she is hard to understand, she adds valuable insight into class discussions that you don't get from many professors. MC201 is heavily discussion based. The classes would consist of a student-led ppt, a class discussion, and then Qing would end it all up with how our discussion relates to the reading.

She is a really nice, and intelligent teacher who cares about you being able to understand her and the material. Easy grader. She doesn't post a rubric and you don't really know what she wants you to do in your writings. 70% of the grades happen at the end, so it gets stressful. Class schedule gets wonky, and she isn't good with online stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Qing is one of the most knowledgeable professors I've had at MSU; Her profound understanding of the Sino-US partnership is rare. She possesses a plethora of experience reading, writing, and teaching about Chinese foreign policy and ways to pacify Sino-U.S. relations. She is both competent and caring!
Absolutely wonderful and brilliant professor, she knows a lot and always wants what's best for her students. I've taken 2 of her classes and I would take anything she teaches.

Prof Qing is a wonderful lady. She can be difficult to understand but she knows this. She recognizes the language barrier and will help you to understand. She laughs regarding her troubles with English at times. Not really a tough grader and pretty open with due dates. She is not a very good grader and does take some time to submit. 4/5.

I graduated in 2004.  Dr. Qing is the most compassionate, enthusiastic, fair, and honest professor I've had. I am now a teacher and her spirit in the classroom inspires and informs my work.  I tried to take as many of her classes as were offered and I studied abroad with her in Beijing.   Go to office hours. Be passionate and informed--you'll learn

Excellent Prof.  Encourages Debate and provides good guide lines for understanding the reading.  Accent is a small barrier.  Don't ever underestimate her, she is very smart, and always paying attention.

While Professor Qing's accent may make it hard for some students to learn, she really wants students to understand the material and engage in discussion.  She is more than willing to go over things during office hours and her enthusiasm for the subject shows.  If you study what's on her slides for the exams then you should do fine.

Generally nice-clearly intelligent;somewhat haphazard in teaching style; accent and English as a second language pose a barrier between her and the class. Grading either w/0 rhyme/reason or aiming to hit arbitrary 2.5 bell curve. Many assignments I received had 'excellent work' coupled w/ mediocre grades. Two words: Knuckle Sandwich.
good professor, hard to understand most of the time but very interesting and intelligent.
I agree...  not a good professor.  She basically just wants you to debate in class instead of going over the readings.  Then, by the time you get to the midterm or exam, you get screwed over.
Don't take this professor.  It will be the end of your GPA.
Very nice, and pretty easy, even though grading can be a bit inconsistant and hard to predict. Be careful, or she might give you a "knuckle sandwich!"
Easy class to 4.0. No exams just group work but she's an easy grader. Overall great professor!
Very easy class. mostly connects with some occasional group class work.
She is actually the goat, so nice, amazing actually entertaining lectures, and understanding
One of the best professors here at MSU. Engaging and relevant lectures, clear homework instructions, and cares about students. Make sure you attend lectures.
so kind and i love her and her classes. she doesnt believe in exams which i agree with. a queen

Her lectures are very engaging and each quiz per week follow with the lecture videos. Its important to do all connect assignments since this course is heavily based on assignments and readings. With no Exams at all!!
Prof Sullivan is such a warmhearted individual. She actually wants us to learn and it is evident through our assignments and her grading procedures. I wish more professors were like her!

Sullivan is by far the best prof at MSU. She cares about her students a lot and she shows it with every class. Not to mention she is very funny and makes the class laugh, which makes lectures fun to attend. Take her if you can!

Amazing professor, gives tons of extra credit and no one grade is going to massively hurt you. Her online lectures are actually well-thought out, the slides are genuinely helpful, and the quizzes directly pull from them. She also actively takes feedback on what activities actually help teach the content, take this class with her if you can!

I am glad to have taken this course, with one of the best professors at Michigan State. Professor Sullivan truly cares about how her students learn from her course setup and asks for input on how to improve and help students receive the most from the course.  I can't recommend her enough. if you can take her course jump on it you won't regret it!
Wants you to succeed, really enjoyed this course.

Professor Sullivan is a great teacher for Marketing 300. She allows the class to be structured how the students want (fully in-person, hybrid, fully online, etc.) and allows us as the student body to choose what we want out of this course. She gives a weekly quiz and discussion posts, but you'll be set as long as you go to class and listen.

Hands down the best professor I've had at MSU. Really interesting lectures (even though it's a boring topic) and a great person who genuinely cares about her students. I wish I had more classes from her. Workload is reasonable, but she won't take any excuses for missed deadlines.

Writing this review in advance lol. But Robby is honestly great and makes the class not even feel like it's an upper level 400 class. If you still need to take MI 401 then I highly suggest that you choose this professor. There is attendance every week so just make sure you're logging on/coming to class. Class content is really engaging and in VR

My only problem with this class was the use of AI. He doesn't have lecture notes for the topics he assigns, instead you have to interact with an AI chatbot (Gemini or GPT). Other than that, hes great, the class is hardly difficult and it can be fun at times.
One of my favorite professors at msu, i took his avatar and vr class because of how easy his class is. The only way to fail is literally if you don't do your work

Robby seems like a good guy and the class isn't very difficult but that doesn't give him an automatic 5/5. 4.0 is 94-100. He is super disorganized. Everything in D2L is a link to a google doc. Not sure why he can't just post to D2L like every other professor. Grading expectations were confusing. Responded to emails quick but feedback wasn't helpful

Robby is a great professor who is very passionate about virtual reality and avatars. He encourages a positive, accepting, and inclusive environment. I can't forget to mention how absolutely fun the class is. Having group discussion/activities in VR is SERIOUSLY fun. A class where you learn while flying around on a magic cushion is unforgettable.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Prof Robby makes a clear effort to know his students' names and get to know them well. He is passionate and excited, making his lectures fun and enjoyable. He is always working with students to understand how he can make the class better and make tests go more smoothly. I would 100% recommend him.

Robby is definitely the best professor Ive had. Hes super cool and funny, hes understanding and just a great guy. Lectures are mandatory but theyre really fun and interesting. Hes chill and really cares about his students. Would recommend him and this class.
Great professor, great class. Everything was easy to follow and not hard work. Mostly consisted of papers but they were only 200-400 words. Easy 4.0 if you do the work.

Robby was hands-down the best professor I could ask for. He cracks jokes all the time and he really knows what he's doing. He's also very good at keeping the class engaged. I wish I could retake the class every semester.

Very funny and entertaining, heavily lecture oriented, 2 pretty easy and easily-graded projects, 3 exams and 1 final, get to drop one (so you dont have to take the final if you do good on the 3 exams)
Good guy, interesting topics, good explanations.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This prof isn't even involved in the course. TA's run it, they're unhelpful and rude. This class is more handwriting than chem. Projects are straightforward but little direction is given. >2 hours per session is just writing redundant details. It's run like a high school chem class. Easy to 4.0. All this extra work for no good reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My software glitched and so instead of a complete PDF, only the final page was actually submitted on a team project. After realising the mistake, the professor wouldn't accept the fixed version, saying that it is an insignificant part of the grade, and that it didn't matter. the assignment was worth 15% of the grade...

For 1 credit, this class gives a hell of a workload. All work is due within 48 hours (or less) of your lab time, so it feels very condensed. How easy this class is also depends a lot on your lab group.  Rubrics are available for each assignment type, pay attention to them. The course gets a bit easier once you get the hang of each assignment type.
I love this guy
It all really depends on your lab group and the people actually instructing you, besides that hard to contact and confusing set up

The lab was super fun but it all depends on your group. If you have a bad group then you will do bad in the lab. The ULAs are hit or miss but mine were great and clear. The projects were interesting just a lot of lab reports and writing.

Really difficult to ask questions and get actual answers. Had to contact the ULA to get actual feedback. Would tell you to do one thing and then come back later and ask why you had you lab set up that way. Made no sense.
Lectures are long and boring. This class is a class that most people take for an IAH requirement so it feels too strict and high stakes to actually learn.

Rachman's main focus is that you know how smart he is; nothing else matters. He can be funny and engaging, and he loves to drop in pop culture references every change he gets, but if you have a funnier narrative, what you get is a teenage boy who wants to forever impress his mommy!

If I could say one thing about him, it would be that he needs to acknowledge that his prerequisite classes are not that interesting to most people that are required to take them. He was also a little unorganized when it came to due dates and it's obvious he likes to hear himself talk. Overall the class was easy, but had lengthy and boring content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Rachman was great, you can tell he loves his job. He got to know students and would often remember things we wrote or talked about. He gives informative yet fun feedback and is quite forgiving in terms of grading. It's a reading heavy class, a new text or parts of a book every week, there are some good films in there too. All around a good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took professor Rachman's 221C course and loved every minute of it. Fair warning: there is a lot of assigned reading, most of which are stories and not textbook reading. In this course we were mainly graded on papers and attendance. If you show up and write the papers well you'll have nothing to worry about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Rachman is so smart it's almost unbelievable. Pop culture is such a fun and interesting English class, I would highly recommend it.

Professor Rachman is, to put it simply, the professor you envision having in college. He's funny, caring, and energetic through lectures. He sees potential in his students and gives grace to them when it is needed. I absolutely loved going to every class and hope I can take him again in the future!
Best professor in the English department and it's not even close. He cares so much about his students.

Honestly a really good professor who cares about listening to his students and making sure they are engaging with the material. Most of the class is discussion-based (so do your reading) but Rachman likes to hear himself talk so he'll prompt you on what he wants to hear. Really easy to talk to and accessible outside class. Quizzes are super easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: ENG473A Literature and Medicine- Understanding about attendance if you make effort to reach out or participate on Zoom meetings. Talks a lot just for himself but he does say a lot of thought provoking things. Grading is kind of vague and he dates himself sometimes with things he says. Very good with literature analysis and is enthusiastic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Goated professor who made dense readings understandable. Best professor in the English department.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Rachman is extremely kind and knowledgeable. His class was interesting and the books we read were amazing. I really liked this class. The workload is reasonable and professor Rachman was understanding and worked around deadlines. I would definitely recommend you take this class with professor Rachman.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best profs I've ever had.

This was an online class, so things may be different normally. Prof. Rachman was a good professor. If you read the books and take notes you shouldn't have too many issues on the quizzes once you get used to his style. He did assign a fair number of essays, but wasn't overly harsh grading them. Class was a bit political, but that's college profs.

Dr. Rachman is incredibly smart and assigns interesting readings. His assignments are occasionally difficult, but his grading is reasonable. If you have any issues with the course, I highly recommend speaking with him about it. I found him to be very accommodating and fair.

Rachman was a pretty chill guy. I took ENG 342 Readings in Popular Literary Genres online during the Summer with him and it was a pretty interesting class. His topic is detective books. The readings were pretty interesting and got better as the class went along. The online lectures are a little boring but not too bad. Overall I liked the course.

I've taken multiple classes with Steve. He's extremely supportive and is always willing to give advice. Go to office hours! You need to read the books and articles to do well on quizzes and to be able to participate. Highly recommend. My favorite prof at MSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Ranchman is too smart too teach. Loves to hear himself talk and I'm convinced he dresses up as Sherlock Holmes on the weekends. Attendance is MANDATORY, i had word during his class and he was super pissed about it. There is a quiz ever week on the books and they're tough, so be prepared to read a lot, or use spark notes lol

His lectures are really hard to take notes off of. I just stopped listening about 2 weeks into the semester because I was getting nothing from it. But attendance is mandatory except for 3 absences so I had to go to class and sit there and work on other stuff.

Overall, Professor Rachman is a decent guy. He likes to hear himself talk, but he knows what he's talking about. He's really interested in popular literature. He assigns a lot of readings, even though it's a 100 level course. The exams are difficult, as every question has answer e.) none of the above and f.) all of the above. Be prepared to work.

Professor Rachman is a superbly intelligent teacher. His study in the class of character and philosophy is incredibly interesting. His assigned readings (though there are a lot) are perect for the topics he wants to explore. His is not a class you want to take for a blowoff, but if you want to work a bit and explore a lot take a class with him!

This professor has no interest in facilitating meaningful discussion.  The second a student makes a statement he connects to in some way, he interrupts and inserts his own take on what that student just said.  He seems to love the sound of his own voice, because he answers his own questions again and again.  Where's the meaningful learning?

this class blows and will continue to blow if  taught by this prof again. this is no reflection on the character of the man, but if i wanted to, i could get by without reading the books for the class since he spends the entirety of his lectures READING THE BOOKS OUT LOUD. really frustrating, but if u need a flashback to forst grade, go for it.
The class and work load suck but Rachman is extremely entertaining and hilarious!
Love the class and Rachman too.  Super nice and helpful.  Let with a little crush and an B, but I had to study to make the grade.

Alot of info in lectures and only shows slides for split second so being an expert note taker is a must. Exams need to be studied for. Attendance is 40% of your grade, however, he gives little assignments that graded strictly which are included in that 40 percent, overall a very philosophical class.

Extremely sweet professor and cares about all students who step into her classroom. She provides structured, thought-out feedback and provides interactive lectures that teaches you lessons about everyday life. As an "unmotivated" student, I'd always look forwards to class. If I could retake any class at MSU, it 100% would be this one.

Her lectures are really fun and easy to relate with in real life scenarios and she also addresses present day issues. Grading isn't too strict but will give useful comments to improve on, a lot of group work. If she sees potential, she helps give resources and references how to succeed and do more outside of class. Took the class for fun, worth it!
Really nice to talk to, helps students a lot and if you have issues with grades she loves helping students with where they can earn more points. Also very funny and lectures are fun and interactive

Dr Taylor is very passionate about her class, and she's very caring of all her students. Some of the assignments are a little annoying but she tries to make them fun. She's one of the sweetest people ever, and I would recommend going to her office hours. The only 2 big gradings in the class is the midterm (notecard allowed) and group project.
Sweetest professor ever.

She is very kind and caring and actually cares about her students. Attendance is strict and lectures can be boring but she jumps around a lot which makes it engaging. I wasn't a fan of the topic but she quickly made it my favorite course. Do the in class activities and as long as your group for the final is decent it's easy.

Dr. Taylor is a kind and caring professor. She would always say in class "this is not a building block course and we are going to be jumping around" which is 100% true. There usually always an in-class assignment so make sure to pay attention to the lectures.

Professor Taylor was an average professor. She had some boring lectures/ annoying homework assignments, but was fair in her grading. Group project/ midterm exam make up the bulk of the grade. Final group project was annoying to complete.

She is so nice. I have a 98% in this class its very easy. Just do the work and you're good. She offers extra credit and grades work super fast. I emailed her about an issue and she responded within minutes and fixed the issue. I love her, she's so sweet I'd do anything for her. Please take this class and show her love.

Literally one of the kindest professors I've ever had. Always receiving and listening to feedback, knows all her students and you can tell she loves her job. Weekly homework but it's never difficult and no exam, just a group presentation.

Dr. Taylor is just an alright professor. She explains things very clearly but she can sometimes talk to you like a baby, and other times talk too fast. The homework is pretty easy as long as you pay attention, and the midterm exam wasn't the worst. A lot of guest speakers and their content will be on the exam. No readings though which is good.

She is such a sweet teacher; you can tell she loves her job and teaching this subject. I really like her classes and hearing her talk. She takes your answers from the homework and incorporates them into the next lecture. She's very open to feedback and will adjust her class and teaching format to keep her students happy. I enjoy her class.

Dr. Taylor is my pride and joy. Had her for 202 and 208L, amazing experience in both would take a million times over. So kind, helpful, understanding, funny, smart, everything you want in a professor. learn to use excel beforehand and the class is much easier. If you have the chance to take her, do it! Praise Dr. Taylor, she deserves the world.

Although she overcomplicates the class a bit and is very nit-picky eith grading, she is incredibly nice and understanding. I didn't mind the group work, but having to show up every day or getting a 0 for the in class activities kinda suck. One midterm with cheat sheets, weekly homework and a final presentation/paper. Interesting class

Dr. Taylor is the best professor I've ever had. She truly cares about her students and will help you with anything you need. There's a regular amount of work but it's not too difficult just can be time consuming. Just show up to class and participate.
It is unbelievable how hard she tries to make this class way harder than it needs to be.

The class was setup in groups and almost everything is done with your group. The final is a semester long project which you present and work on in groups it's a good chunk of the grade. There is a textbook but she provides it. There's only one test and it's the midterm which if you don't do well can drop your grade a decent amount.

I so grateful for how this course is set up. you never feel like your wastin your time bc the lectures, readings, hw, quizzes, exam are all related and you feel prepared. she also offers a cheatsheet and it counts towards your hw grade which is a free grade !
Dr. Taylor is an incredibly supportive professor. She provides valuable insights during group projects, ensuring that we meet all the requirements and achieve the grades we desire.

Dr. Taylor makes every class activity feel engaging and exciting. Whether it's a workshop or lecture, she always incorporates interactive elements that keep us engaged while making the learning experience enjoyable and productive.

I really appreciate how Dr. Taylor encourages us during group projects. She's always available for questions, offers constructive feedback, and ensures we stay on track to meet the expectations for the project.

Working on group projects with Dr. Taylor is such a positive experience. She encourages collaboration and offers helpful suggestions to ensure we all contribute and meet the project's goals. Her support makes a huge difference in the outcome.

Dr. Taylor is incredibly supportive during group projects. She goes above and beyond to ensure that we meet the expectations and achieve the grades we want through her constructive feedback. Her guidance helps us stay on track, and she's always available to help when needed.

I really appreciate how Professor Taylor creates a positive learning environment. She always encourages her students to ask questions and gives thoughtful feedback that helps us grow and do well in her course
I love how organized and well-prepared Professor Taylor is for each class. She makes every topic easy to follow and provides helpful examples from real life that deepen my understanding.
I'm so grateful to have had Professor Taylor as an instructor. She is insightful, approachable, and truly cares about her students' growth and success. I always feel supported in her class.

She is a knowledgeable and approachable professor who creates a welcoming environment for all students. Professor taylor provides clear explanations and is always happy to offer assistance when needed during her office hours or after class

Professor taylor is one of the best professors I've had. She genuinely cares about her students' success and goes out of her way to make sure we understand the material by offering workshops and in class activities. Her feedback is always helpful and encouraging.

I have learned so much in Professor Taylor's class. She is patient, approachable, and has an amazing ability to break down difficult material. Her passion for teaching really shines through because of how well organized and constructed the course is. You can tell so much work is put into it to ensure her student's success

Professor taylor is a fantastic instructor who makes every class engaging and enjoyable. She explains complex topics in a way that is easy to understand, and she's always there to help when you need it.

Professor taylor consistently goes above and beyond to create an engaging and informative learning experience. Their enthusiasm for the subject is contagious, and their clear explanations help students feel successful and confident in their work.

professor taylor is both knowledgeable and approachable, making it easy to engage with the content. They offer constructive feedback and make sure every student has the support they need. I feel more confident in my academic abilities after taking this class.

I feel incredibly fortunate to have had Professor taylor as an instructor. They create a classroom atmosphere that encourages collaboration and critical thinking. They always make time for students and offer valuable insights into the material as well as clear up any confusion on any topic.

Professor taylor is an excellent communicator who truly knows how to make learning enjoyable. Their passion for the subject and dedication to students shines through in every lesson. I've gained confidence and a deeper appreciation for the topic.

I am so grateful for Professor taylor's teaching. They are approachable, patient, and always willing to help. I have gained a deeper understanding of the subject thanks to their clear and effective teaching methods.

Professor taylor brings enthusiasm and energy to every lecture. They explain complicated topics in a way that is both clear and engaging. I look forward to their class each week as well as the interesting in class activities that we do

What stands out about Professor Taylor is their genuine care for their students' success. They go above and beyond to ensure we grasp the material and are always willing to answer questions. I feel encouraged and supported throughout the course which i rarely find that with other professors.

Dr. Taylor is one of the best professors I've had!!! She has an incredible ability to make the subject interesting and accessible. I've learned so much from their clear explanations and thoughtful feedback. She puts so much work and effort into her course and honestly, you can see that being reflected in the course!

Dr. Taylor presents material in an organized and approachable way, and they are always available to offer guidance. I feel motivated and confident in my learning because of their teaching style and support

since we have a final project as our final, she is very understanding and supportive if we had group members who are not contributing or delaying the group's progress, and instead, grades your individual work and is very fair.

Dr. Taylor an outstanding instructor who always creates an engaging and supportive learning environment. Their passion for the subject is infectious, making complex concepts easier to understand. I truly appreciate their dedication to helping students succeed.

her lectures are always interesting and makes you more aware about your environment. I really liked the group project because it targets regions in the world that need environmental attention, which puts the spotlight on places of where people are struggling but the media doesn't highlight that.

something i like is that on the midterm, the workshops &in class activites are really a preperation for your midterm so thats why she provides so much detailed and good feedback on them (which is why many people say shes a tough grader)

What I like is that the reading &lectures go hand in hand which is amazing bc the lectures explain things that i might not understood in the readings. shes available and willing to meet with you for office hours to help you on areas where you are struggling as well as offer extra credit to help your grade. She also has a lot of drops in the course!

She is very observant and notices her hard working students and gives out stickers and thanks them for doing so well in the course which is very rare that any professor hardly even recognizes ur face. She also support you so much bc she provides the textbook for you and everything you need for free!

Dr. Taylor is very supportive and is willing to help you to make sure you do you best in her course. She puts so much time and effort into grading and giving constructive feedback. Some people say shes a tough grader, but really, she just wants you to do excellent on the midterm bc everything you do in class is preparing you for it.

Talked during every work time so we never could work in class during the time she had set aside. Class activities often have no meaning or impact. Topics are easy but assignments are often tedious and take a lot of time.
Very caring teacher, just a lot of time wasted in class

Very kind and will like you if you participate and try. Attendance is taken and she is a VERY tough grader but does not take off high amounts of points. Low points taken off but very easy to loose points. Overall great teacher for a mandatory class.

The entire class is group projects, it's awful. She is a REALLY tough grader and if you make even one tiny mistake or you don't explain something enough, you'll fail the assignment completely. She also barely gives feedback, so you usually don't know what you did wrong. The assignments are easy but there's so many each week. She's super nice tho

Taylor's lecture's aren't the *most* engaging, but she is very kind, smart and posts the lectures online if you need to review. There is only one person midterm exam and the final is a group project that you work on throughout the semester. If you put just a little bit of effort in, you should get a 4.0.

Dr. Taylor is super nice, I just was not interested in the class topics at all. If you miss a class you lose a lot of points so you need to  go to  every single  lecture. It was hard to pay attention but if you really like the Earth and the environment then this is a good fit because Dr. Taylor is a great  person.

Dr. Taylor is super nice and very passionate about her studies. Lectures were okay. She gives a lot of in class and outside of class activities/homework. Only one exam, which is the midterm. There is a big group project at the end.

Great professor, only one exam the midterm. Even if you flunk midterm you're still able to get a good grade in class. Lots of group work- the final is a group project. Talking to her helps build a good relationship.

I loved Dr. Taylor's class! She is so much fun and, outside of some of the videos she shows, the lectures are really enjoyable! In-class assignments are worth more of your grade than you think so don't miss class! Slightly challenging mid-term but she does let you have a cheat sheet. Everything is graded to the absolute letter of her rubrics.

Dr. Taylor is a nice and somewhat understanding professor. Most of your grade in that class will consist of your attendance, the in-class learning activities, and the labs she gives to you the night before. If you show up to class and do your work, then you should be perfectly fine.

I loved Dr. Taylor. In a class of over 200, she was somehow able to know my name. Course consists of weekly homework's (Quiz and Discussion Post) which are both take home and fairly easy. Show up to class, take notes, and it is literally the easiest 4.0. After the midterm, there is no need to take notes. Final is a CAP project presentation.
Great professor, homework is very easy. A lot of it is group based activities. Exams are kind of hard, but Dr. Taylor is an accommodating professor who cares for her students success.

Dr. Taylor was one of my favorite professors during the fall. She is super caring and wants all of her students succeed. Her grading criteria is very clear. If you ever have any questions she is always open to ask and provides very good feedback. If you have to opportunity to take any of her classes, do it!
This professor cares about your success and gives you many resources to help you succeed in the class. It's very flexible when it comes to assignments and homework. I recommend this professor!

Dr. Taylor was a solid professor until she started enforcing word counts on discussion posts. She will mark you down even if you are a 20 words shy, with solid content, and then still mark you down when you meet the word count using filler content and dragging it out. She needs to learn to pick one, quantity or quality. You can't have both.

Overall Dr. Taylor is a great professor. You can tell she wants you to do well in the class, and she will work with you when possible. The only reason I am not giving her a 5 is because she does weekly discussions posts, and is a stickler about minimum word counts. Remove the word count minimums and I would easily give her a 5.

Dr. Taylor genuinely cares about her students and how well they are doing in her class. She also adjusted certain aspects of the class based on feedback from us. This class is very lecture heavy but they are all very applicable in our everyday lives. We also are assigned groups at the very beginning of the semester to work in throughout the class.
She really knows what she is doing and had interesting lectures. She has a quick pace, which might not be the best for everybody.

I found this course difficult due to its grading structure and heavy workload. The syllabus categories made it hard to track my standing, and missing grades in a section impacted my GPA. I reached out for help over 2.5 weeks but didn't get the guidance I needed. Stay proactive and clarify expectations early.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

Please do not take if not interested in soccer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Lots of homework

He can point you in the right direction. Effort  success.
What this guy said pretty much sums it up: "he is feast or famine. you'll either be friends with him and get awesome grades, or you'll be a regular student and just pass the class."
Your grade is based on how much he likes you, so play his games. If your class is small, he might invite you to his creepy, trashy house at the end of the semester.

I took him for screen writing and advanced screen writing.  He is one of the best profs at Michigan State.  He is much like the older father figures that you see in clichéd movies and books--a warm and friendly figure.  Just make sure to use proper grammar (it is possible your work will get stomped on during class--leaving the shame of footprints).
he is feast or famine.  you'll either be friends with him and get awesome grades, or you'll be a regular student and just pass the class.
No Comments

Bill is a great prof and knows his stuff. However, if he likes you, you'll get a better grade than if he doesn't. But, the more classes you take w/him, the more you'll consider him a friend than a prof.

He's pretty goofy, but very passionate about what he does.  His eccentricites alone make attending class a must.  As far as learning from him, yes, you can get a good chunk of screenwriting knowledge from him, but he's more about getting creative ideas flowing then boring "traditional" learning
No Comments
Enjoyable but boring.  Taught Sam Raimi way back when, never gets tired of talking about it.  Disrespects animation.  Otherwise decent.

Do not take this class! She is very strict with any electronics (including computers) and WILL call you out in front of everyone for the smallest stuff. Her lectures don't really make that much sense because she goes on random rants about things and interrupts students during discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easy class, easy grader. Class feels like high school (no phones out, must pay attention, participation), this was annoying for a university required class. Her advice was condescending, vague yet overcomplicated, ask lots of questions to fully understand the group project before getting too far in. Don't overcomplicate anything though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had her for IAH 207. She graded everything very easily; I got A's on almost every assignment. She will literally love you if you participate in the discussions, so say anything and she will love it or agree with you.

She approved my article for this presentation assignment and then once I presented, she noticed my article didn't have an author and required me to do the assignment all over again for a different article, after she already approved the other one. Her classes are extremely boring and she is always rambling about something not even related. Easy tho

Dr. Weiss will call you out if you are blatantly not paying attention in class, which honestly I think is fair. She's a great person and her lectures are often interesting if you actually care about what we're learning in class. If you do your work it's such an easy and enjoyable class.
There is a lot of group projects/work, and she doesn't let you use electronics during the class unless she says we can get them out.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. She is rude and constantly called me out in class for odd reasons. Forces you to work in groups and gives horrible instructions for every assignment. She wants you to practically read her mind for half of the criteria. Has a few students in the class that she picks on and a few that she favors. Don't take it!

Very condescending and rude, even when just asking for clarification. It's a simple class and assignments aren't too difficult, but I wish I dropped week 1. The class included a group project and the whole process was just beyond unorganized. If you can, choose another IAH.

Worst class I've ever taken. Professor Weiss is condescending, rude and unorganized. Every lecture felt like torture and every student groans at her assignments. Not a hard class but I would've taken a more difficult class if I knew I would be learning anything. Take any other IAH please.

Professor Weiss is extremely willing to help students achieve success in the class. Grading tends to be pretty lenient, although there's a lot of required reading / watching films outside of class. From what I've heard, one of the better IAH profs here.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class because of her good reviews big mistake. This professor was so infuriating to work w/ directions were never clear, lectures made no since, assigned huge reading before every class and had a whole GROUP project entirely on your own out of class. This class was way too much stress and work for an IAH class but TENDED to grade easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is a good prof and very nice. However, her lectures were dragged out and unengaging. Attendance is "mandatory" but you can easily get away with skipping classes if you participate occasionally. The irritating thing about this class was how you had to attend 5 events from the program that she was involved in which had no relation to the class.

Professor Weiss is very caring. Sometimes, she isn't as clear as she could be, but she makes her class very manageable. If you put even a small amount of effort in and submit on time, class is an easy A.

So condescending. So passive-aggressive. Lectures are insufferable, she drags out every concept unnecessarily. Course work is fairly easy but there is just so much for this type of class. Requires a lot of out of class participation for films. Asked her a question about how she prefers I turn in an assignment and she was so difficult to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is one of the best professors I have had at MSU. She is really kind and understanding of everything. There are some events you have to attend on the weekend but other than that and the reading she assigns her class is really easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Weiss is a very kind professor, she isn't strict about grading or attendance. I would recommend showing up to class often though as it can be easy to get lost in some of the content she teaches. She does post everything on D2L though so if you miss a class you have access to everything you missed. Sometimes she doesn't explain things well.
Dr. Weiss was really kind and accommodating when it came to getting assignments in. She really cared about our comprehension of the topics presented. Great professor and an enjoyable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She made it clear in the beginning that the she wanted her relationships with students to be more peer based rather than professor/student, which made it easy to reach out. She was the sweetest, but also knew when she was being taken advantage of. Most I had to write in this class was 150 words, and a simple group presentation at the the end.

I had Dr. Weiss for IAH 210, I highly recommend taking the class with her because she is such an amazing teacher and is very passionate about the class. The class content is not super heavy and the work load is very manageable. I loved taking her class so much, I am taking a second level IAH with her next sem.
She is the best professor i have seen. She lets you have your our opinions  and  nurtures them. Her classes are very interactive and she is very good in grading as long as you show good effort.

I would not recommend this course to anyone. The professor dosen't express the lectures enough and he will call on you even if your hand is not up. The exams are nothing like the "study sheet" that they provide and the course is extremely hard to navigate. Not to mention a big group project that has no substance to it. Don't take this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Vernon Miller is very unorganized. The course itself is very confusing and the lectures are unncessarily long. Attendance is required in recitation and each time missed is a point deduction. The TA's are not helpful and the workload is extremely hard for an elective. Do not take this class.

This class is an elective but is treated like a mandatory requirement. The tests and recitations are unnecessarily hard and there is no guidance by Professor Miller. He stumbles upon his words and expects you to read 35-40 pages of articles. The course is VERY poorly structured and includes multiple "suprise quizzes" during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class sucks. It is organized so poorly the recitations are horrible almost 2 hours of just listening to the same stuff talked about in lecture. huge group project that you get no time in class or anything to work on, it makes no sense that this is a group project because you do independent interviews. The lectures are so boring no no just no

He was okay overall, but the class often felt hard to follow. Lectures could get off track, and it wasn't always clear what we were supposed to be learning. This made studying for exams a bit confusing since they didn't always match what we focused on in class.
He rambles and sometime you can't take away anything from what he says during lecture. Super caring and wants his students to succeed. As long as you put in the effort its a good class to take.

Lectures are very heavy, and the dude just kinda rambles for 2 hours. I often left wondering "What was I supposed to learn there". There is also a semester long group project that is very unorganized and far too difficult because of that. He also doesn't allow phones during the lecture, and on several occasions took them away from students

Professor Miller is a good guy and he is very passionate about what he teaches but I definitely wouldn't of passed this class if it wasn't for such an amazing TA in Hubert Miller. Lectures were rushed and packed with a ton of information and the structure of the semester long group presentation was confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Worst setup class I have ever seen. Lectures go full two hours and cover an unreal amount of content. His speech is very garbled not articulate hard to understand. He does not take attendance and says the class is optional but he has pop quizzes for grades. There is also a semester-long group project that is extremely vague and unorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I enjoyed the class, professor, and lectures. There were 1-2 chapters of reading each week. We had two group projects where the grading was a bit unclear but helpful extra credit on the exams were offered. Attendance wasn't mandatory although we were given points for in-person assignments. We were often let out early. Good experience overall.

This class was awful. Unorganized, lectures are heavy with information, yet you have no time to take notes because he talks super fast and is impossible to understand (you also have to hand-write everything because he doesn't allow technology). The group project was unnecessarily long and difficult, especially if members don't do their part.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: if you match his compassion for the subject, he makes for an absolutely amazing professor. helped me realize how interesting a class like organizational communication can be!

Professor Miller is clearly knowledgable and passionate but I dreaded going to lecture because of how quickly he talks and there was too much content covered each time. Grade is based off 3 exams and a group project. The lectures are not 'optional' because there is in class assignments and points. You have to put in the work to get a good grade.

Professor Miller has good intentions for his students, his lectures were long and confusing, especially when taking notes. He is always helpful and very nice, but the class is made up of 3 exams (300 pts) and the final project done in rec (100 pts). With very minimal studying, always attending, a great proj. group, and extra credit I got a 3.5
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Class is super lecture heavy and goes the entire two hours. On the syllabus it says the lecture is optional, but there are quizzes for points in lecture. There's a group project which is long and confusing. Professor is passionate about the subject but talks way too fast and there's too much content that's crammed into exams. Final is cumulative.

I took this class as an elective and I do not recommend this class AT ALL. Very hard. Exam heavy. Huge group project that is very confusing. Grades very hard. He is a nice person just the class layout needs to change.

I like Professor Miller as a person; tries to involve all the students and relate to them. I didn't like how lecture heavy it is. lectures always went full 2 hours and were fast paced and not easy to understand what was being said. Group project was a disaster, but if you get a decent group it is an easy A. Lots of EC if you attend let and rec.
Talks so fast. The group project in this class was the longest thing ever. I hated this class it made me almost want to drop out of school completely.

he talks so fast and I wanna fall asleep every lecture because he just repeats the same thing over and over again. I hated the group project we had to do too, this is one of my least favorite classes I've taken
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Miller is awesome! He is kind, funny, and dedicated to what he teaches. He LOVES helping his students! He is very approachable and will answer any questions that come up! The thing I didn't like about this class was the group project. It was very stressful and demanding.

Attendance doesn't matter but you get extra credit if you do show up. The exam are very doable if you go to class and study the information from the lecture. She also likes to get to know her students!

Don't be fooled this course is NOT brain and behavior, it is a neuroscience course. Class is graded by four exams that can have a 6 point bump with in-class questions. Exam content can be confusing but if you understand the content you will succeed. Attendance is not mandatory as long as you complete tophat questions. Would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only graded by 4 exams, lectures is easy with tophat to keep you engaged (she mostly reads of slides) but exam questions are very deep and complicated. Possible to do good if you commit to studying and really understand material not just memorize. She offers some extra credit but its like 3 points each exam so not much to really improve your grade
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: When deciding to take Dr. Veenema's class, please keep in mind that there are a lot of political opinions that are skewing the RMP data. Republicans are upset over an email that she sent out after the election and you can read about it from "The State News"  to form your own opinions. Put effort in this class, and you will pass.

I'm not rating her based on the recent political controversy, she made a mistake and to me that's ok. Professor Veenema was always very nice and passionate. She tries her best to teach, but the material itself is hard to fully understand. I had to drop the class because of the harsh grading criteria, but I would still recommend her as a professor.

Taking this course during a time when the country is so divided really put things into perspective. The content is tough, but she is willing to work with students, even giving an optional final to help boost students grades. There are pros and cons to every instructor, but don't let the current events deter you from taking one of her courses.

If you are coming in as a freshman just be aware that s this class is a lot different than most highschool psychology classes. It requires a lot more commitment and studying.  Professor Veenema herself is such a nice person and I would personally would say she did an excellent job teaching. I loved this class and I wish I could take it again!

Professor Veenema is a very sweet and caring woman. This year we lived through a very major political event, she has never pushed an “ agenda “ or indoctrinated us adults, only allowed us a space to feel grief. Please do not listen to the other comments when deciding if you should take this course, You will take 4 exams to determine grades.

She is a kind professor that cares about her students as both people and academics.  She strives to make sure people understand the content and genuinely wants everyone to succeed.  The entire course is graded off the exams, but she gives lots of extra credit. DONT LISTEN TO THE COMPLAINTS ABT POLITICS, as a woman she is scared rightfully.

Content is lecture heavy and no homework just four exams. Course is difficult but she does her best to help out her students. Overall a sweet and caring professor who watches and truly cares for her students. Recommend her truly so nice!

Her class is pretty difficult, your grade is solely based on the four exams you take and sometimes the questions are worded confusingly or are something we haven't gone over. However, she cares about her students! Class starts with cute animal pictures to brighten our day, and she offered an optional final for those in need of a grade boost!

Dr. Veenma is fantastic! The class was online and only based on 4 exams, but they are open note, and all of the content is only within the slides she goes over in class. Tophat questions during class are for extra credit towards that exam, and it is very easy to 4.0 if you have an interest or any background in the content!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: this class is only based off of 4 exams, the first one is extremely easy but after that they are difficult. she is a good teacher but you need to pay attention and understand what we're learning
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She went superrrr fast during lectures and I could not keep up. Content was a lot packed into each exam.  Wish there was more opportunities than exams

She is super nice, but the class format isn't great. I went to every lecture and took extensive notes, but the multiple choice exams had many questions that had 7 options and you had to pick one and some content not in the textbook. Also, exams are the only part of your grade, and each is 25% so if you do poorly on one exam, you can't recover.

The only things in the grade book were the 4 exams but they are not cumulative and there is no final. The first test was easy but the other you do need to study more for application of ideas learned. The tests are open notes though.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's really nice and shows her dog a lot during lecture. This is a PSY class but is pretty neuroscience-y, so if you're not into that be careful. Opportunities for extra credit during lecture. Exams made up all of the grades but they were open-note and non-cumulative so it was definitely manageable. Pay attention in class because she moves fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is a very nice professor, but it is difficult to contact her outside of class. If you ask her to go over something in class, she tells you to just rewatch the recording. I usually wouldn't have a problem with this but the concepts are not super easy. The grades are only based on the exams as well, so I definitely recommend studying a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very very nice person, but she was not really available to us when we needed help. When asked questions in class, she did not always answer them. She did not seem concerned that the majority of class was  overwhelmed by the content. Exams are hard to study for because topics are vague and there are lots of them.

Very nice professor, only exams are graded and there's no homework, plenty of oppurtunity for extra credit!! She's very understanding and passionate in what she does. Only thing I wasn't a fan of was the guest speakers.

Best prof. I've ever had. She always showed us her dog during online lectures just to cheer everyone up. She doesn't give out homework so grades are entirely based on 4 exams. She is super understanding (especially when it came to internet issues) and there is some opportunity for extra credit. I would recommend her to anyone; she's amazing!

Dr. Veenema is passionate about her studies and is a great professor, but this class was pretty hard. It is only graded based on exams, which made the class pretty miserable. The information is interesting, but it is a lot to take in. If this isn't needed for your major and you just want an elective, I recommend taking a different 200-level class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's a really nice professor and pretty easy going. She uses TopHat for everything & it's easy to get all of the questions correct because she posts them before class so you can just write them down & put the right answer during class. She also uses a lot of those questions on exams. There are 4 exams total & no final exam.

So kind and easy to reach through email. Wants everyone to succeed, and easy to 4.0 if you come to class and watch the lecture videos. She is very knowledgeable and helpful if you have questions. She makes this class run very well and it is not a class I ever worry about. Lockdown exams with no camera too and other assignments boosting your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Go through allllllll of the material, it is a lot, but it will help you because the exams are kind of tough. The exams are pretty similar to the in class assignments

Dr. Hedges is very willing to work with you, and she provides a lot of course materials for you to understand the material. I didn't do too well, but looking back on it, this is only because I was stressed with many other difficult classes. Dr. Hedges gives amazing feedback, make sure to attend class and office hours!!

The flipped classroom style isn't for me, but Prof. Hedges was great. Her assignments are very interesting, and you can attend classes in-person OR online (Zoom). Do the study guides, keep up with assignments, and learn the content well- you will get a 4.0. One tip: Make sure you have a good grasp of the material. Tests are application-heavy.

Dr. Hedges was amazing. This class was super helpful to my learning and it was relatively easy to get a good grade as long as you did the assignments and understood how to do the exams. The class is hybrid which is nice if you can't make it. Be sure to do the in-class assignments and weekly quizzes and you will be able to 4.0 this course.

best professor ive had in all my 3 years. i have never learned as difficult information and actually understood it as quickly as i have in this class due to the way this class is formatted. i got the highest grades on everything without having to study once.

Dr. Hedges is a great professor. She gives opportunities to fix exam grades and it is largely independent based outside of class. She uses class time where we can work together and ask questions on the content. The structure and flexibility is great. She is very clear about the grading policy. Definitely Recommend!

All content was online despite it being an in-person class. If you went to class, you just did an assignment that can be done at home. She stressed how much she was there to help, but when I politely emailed a question, her rude response was off-putting. Basically, she doesn't do anything. Her grading scale is nice and allows you to do well though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: GO TO RECITATION. you will regret it if you dont, as half of the time she gives away exam question answers and is super helpful. Do the in class assignment and the additional practice questions, as they are helpful on exams. However, you have to earn a "strong" score on all exams to 4.0 the class, which is a 32/40 on all of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: She does not help her students whatsoever. I have tried to ask questions in class and they never get answered. I have emailed her questions and she does not answer them. She made me feel worse when I told her I was feeling overwhelmed.

Only a few weeks into the course but reasonable, accommodating, and respects privacy/student autonomy. Treats us like adults. Exams online, no lockdown, no invasive tech. Difficult material, but I want to actually learn it when profs have personalities like this and trust in students. Kind, reaches out when she se's missing work, easy to access.

I love the length of the lectures. She is very knowledgeable and easy to talk to and contact even outside of class. I do feel as if her exams were harder than the content if you didn't understand the recitation and I think the exam times are too short. So many opportunities to make up your grade though

Dr. Hedges is super caring and makes a huge effort to get to know her students. I wasn't the biggest fan of how she organized her classes, but I still felt like I got a lot out of the class. I recommend going to her recitations though, if you take her class.

I had Dr. Hedges for both 301 and 302 and I loved her! The grading scale is a little weird but she has made it better and you have the opportunity to do corrections on all the exams. Also DO THE RECITATIONS! I didn't for the first semester and regret it greatly.

I can't speak for previous years but both of my semesters with Dr. Hedges in NEU have been really beneficial. I find the tests to be easier than quizzes but still good assessments of what was taught in lecture. Lectures are asynchronous and online-might not be everyone's strong suit. She was fun, lenient and understanding.

I really enjoyed her class and the way she teaches. Her class is online asynchronous with a once-a-week recitation where students work on a worksheet. She mades an effort to come around and talk to students one on one and did a pretty good job of clearing up any confusion. Her lecture videos are shorter and easy to follow.

Super clear and concise lectures. There are ~9 lectures per week spanning 5 mins to 15 mins so it's not that bad. The quizzes are exactly what was covered in the lecture. Exams are a bit harder I feel because they tend to reach a little further than the lectures but still doable. She does offer practice questions each week that help with the exams
