reviews.comment: I took this class as a freshman. In my experience, Wiser is really helpful and will gladly take time out of his day to help you understand a concept. On the other hand, he has no time for students that do not take his class seriously. Pretty solid lectures though, if you read and take notes before class its an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very insightful professor!

I made an account just to review him poorly. This was by far the worst class I've ever taken in my entire life. Wiser is the most condescending professor who thinks that a class average of low C's and D's are good. The tests are so hard you can study day and night and still fail because they are not the material. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Wiser is a very good choice for bio lab. He is not bad at all. He makes it challenging by not telling you what to do step by step, which is the whole point of learning. If you talk to him in office hours he will guide you better. Hes a great person from my experience. Just understand his expectations and you will be fine.

the worst ever. RUN if you have him on your schedule. you will regret having him as a professor. he does not teach, you are expected to learn all of the material before class and take a quiz on the material before the class. which is the stupidest concept ever. I have never heard of pre tests/quizzes being graded for credit... switch out ASAP
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Wiser is honestly the worst instructor I've ever had. He is very condescending toward his students and does very little to help his students out. The class itself wasn't hard, but Dr. Wiser made it very unenjoyable and I dreaded going to his class.

This class is hard. You will watch lectures and take a quiz BEFORE the class and do a worksheet with a group in class. Then you take a quiz every week after the classes. Exams were worth 50% of my grade. The exams give you almost no time to answer the short answer parts. The TAs don't really answer questions well. The lectures don't match exams.

Stressful. Says 2.5 is good for the class and releases all exam scores seemingly proud of these 2.5 scores he has produced as the professor. He doesn't even really teach much even though he's the instructor, every class he sends you into groups and does some poll questions, then you're done. Avoid him at all costs.

Dr. Wiser is one of the most condescending professors I have dealt with. He gets really triggered when students pick "E" in the Zoom polls! The amt of work in this class is way too much... we watch pre-class lectures and then take a Preclass quiz! BEFORE every class! Then in class activities graded on accuracy and we don't get enough time to work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Wiser has the most condescending way about carrying himself and his class. Hopefully you never have family tragedy - because he wouldnt let me makeup any of the work (none of it even matched the syllabus). MSU needs to look into professors like Wiser that absolutely destroy GPAS and learning solely for bragging about how hard their class is.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do NOT choose this professor. The whole class is structured so students literally can't succeed. 80% of your grade is based off exams/quizzes & the other 20% is based off assignments graded for accuracy which they barely give enough time for. Don't even bother emailing him because he won't respond to you. Avoid him.

choose a different prof or biolab if you can. He speaks to students and other instructors in a very condescending way. Some policies on the syllabus were not followed. He didn't care when it was brought it up. Heavy on busy work. Based on these reviews his BS 161 class is way harder than the one I took with a different prof.
He was very condescending and did very little to support his students. I would highly recommend to choose a different professor.

The structure of the online course is ridiculous and when I brought up concerns he just said, well we prepared all summer for this structure to be helpful to YOU. Lectures are recorded by a different professor and the meeting times are to work on assignments. Pre class quizzes and assignments as well as post class quizzes and exams. AVOID HIM.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The worst professor I've ever had at MSU. Horrible lectures. People say it's not his fault and the course is structured like this but that's not true at all. My friends with other profs had a fine experience and I had them send me their lectures since Wiser's were so bad. Also the worst grader and never emails back. Just avoid him.

Absolutely hated this class, made me seriously question whether to change my major -- because of one. class. Went too fast in lecture, even when classes went online because of the pandemic. Didn't answer my questions and got irritated when I asked to go back a few slides. 3 Bio classes later and still the worst of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: RIQs are 15% of grade and exams are 50% of grade total. Thus 65% of your grade (online only) is for testing. The questions were over material that we learned for 2-3 questions and the rest were hypothetical situations that were not elaborated on in the textbook. Basically, this class's average is held by those who took AP Bio so don't expect a 4.0

Not really his fault, the class is just structured very badly and the tests are impossible. Questions are not from lectures or from class. Does not really depend on the professor, the class is just much harder than it needs to be.

This class relies on the reading... Or so they say. The tests seemed far off from what we read in the book, and Wisers lectures didnt help whatsoever. The class was more difficult than necessary, with a lot of outside work. This was surprising for a 100 level course. Wiser himself wasnt much help with clarifying the already confusing material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: AVOID WISER! His lectures are a couple slides with a sentence or two on them. When he does lecture, it's with irrelevant information that doesn't help with the exams. I had to ask my friend with a different professor to send me her lectures. The class is so unorganized, and he never emails you back. One of the worst professors. Don't choose him.

If you are a visual learner, this class is not for you. The ppts accompanied by the lecture usually have only one or two sentences on them, and they're not really useful. Prof. Wiser will talk for 10-15 minutes and then give you a worksheet to do in groups of 3, and this repeats until you've completed 3 worksheets. I didn't find this helpful.

It's not necessary Professor Wisers fault for the awful set up this class and the extremely strict grading that takes place in this course. They love giving busy work and make you attend 4 hours a week of class and at least another 1-2 hours of out of class work for two credits. Professor Wiser doesn't give direct answers which can be frustrating.

Lecture format is the worst and hard to take notes when all he does is talk. Textbook is online and is expensive. He is very confusing and sucks at lecturing. There are very few exam questions that are on things you actually learned. Everyone I know that's taking his class is very confused and never knows what is going on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Liang is very kind and flexible when it comes to deadlines, and her lectures really help with understanding the material. The class if very easy if you have any kind of stats background, however to get a 4.0, you need to score >95 overall, so be wary since the HW is graded on accuracy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors throughout college. She made the material easy to understand. Would highly recommend taking 808 with her.
Dr. Liang creates excellent notes that easy for us to understand.

Dr.Liang is awesome!
Her EPI 808 transformed my understanding of biostatistics and inspired me to dive deeper into the field.
While she wasn't a bad professor, she can be passive aggressive for no apparent reason on times and is very harsh at grading with no consistency.

I think she is okay. But she is not understanding. She gives so many assignments and there are so many group projects. Exams almost every week. Do your homework and make sure you understand the material and you should be okay. But she is not my favorite professor.

The lectures are pretty entertaining and help you learn and understand the language, but there is so much homework. At least 4, 10 to 30-minute assignments per week. You get a lot of time off class, but attendance matters in the end. The textbook is pretty expensive, so I would try to buy it second-hand. There are also a lot of group projects.

Professor Hao is an incredible professor. Her lectures are always fun and engaging and she always emphasizes the importance of trying instead of being afraid of getting answers wrong. Mandarin is a hard language, and you need to make a continued effort, but having a professor like Professor Hao makes the content entertaining and easy to understand.

Hao Lao Shi is an outgoing professor who gives straightforward and somewhat entertaining lectures. Getting a solid grade in the class is a little difficult and she does not have clear rubrics with grading. I would recommend giving her a try, however her teaching style does not fit me well.

Yiying Tong is easily a top tier professor at Michigan State University, East Lansing Campus. very helpful for all students, and has clear grading criteria. I would take him over Borzoo Bonakdarpour every day of the week. Inshallah Yiying.

Content wasn't too hard, the professor makes the exams multiple choice and on D2L in person. Only issue I had was that he was a little too slow for my liking, so I would often just go through the lecture slides at my own pace and tune him out. Other than that, gives great examples and makes it fairly easy to get a 4.0

One of the best professors at MSU! It's evident he is passionate about teaching and wants his students to learn and succeed. The 80 minute lectures sometimes got a bit stale, buts thats the only negative thing I can say about Yiying. Looking forward to taking his higher level CSE courses in the future. He's truly an injective (one-to-one) prof.

Was hesitant to take CSE 260 because I heard the other professor (Borzoo) ran a difficult class. I was relieved when after the first few days I realized prof. Tong was completely different. He had clear lectures, reasonable homework/tests, and was accessible outside of class. He's also the reason I bought a Wii to re-live some childhood nostalgia.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I often find myself struggling to stay awake in lecture. However, he's great at answering questions on piazza and explaining the content if you can get past the monotony of the content. I recommend buying the textbook for extra credit, as it'll give you more practice and more room to make mistakes on other assignments (this class is 60% exams).
Lectures are very long and boring. If you pay for the textbook, you are better off learning from that. Not a bad class, but could be much better.

Great professor. Everything about the class was meant to be difficult, but he taught it in a very intuitive way. Fair grading, and easy to score if you study. Helpful, responds to questions fast and effectively on Piazza. 

Inspirational. Also great at Wii Boxing.

Great professor. Everything about the class was meant to be difficult, but he taught it in a very intuitive way. Fair grading, and easy to score if you study. Helpful, responds to questions fast and effectively on Piaza. Textbook not required but is extra credit. 

Inspirational. Also great at Wii Boxing.

Made discrete math super easy to understand. Grading criteria was extremely clear. Also the recitations playing Wii play motion with Yiying were some of the best class memories I've had at MSU. Will never forget the time he cleared all the levels in Wii sports sword fighting… back to back!!

As an international student and a fellow East Asian, I must say that most Asian professors are not good enough. However, Professor Yiying Tong is an exception. He teaches with true ease and enthusiasm rather than being an extremely self-centered person. Lectures attendable online, exams are strict but fair and reasonable.

Amazing professor, lectures are only twice a week, with optional recitation. You can also join lectures online via zoom. homework is not difficult, and due every other week. He uses piazza to answer questions promptly. Book is not required, but purchasing it allows you to get 5% extra credit. Prof. Tong is also great at Mario Kart & Wii Party!

Had some of the best sleeps of my life in his class, with that said, his lecture is pretty boring with the boring material and his soft and slow tones. Everything else is great though, very smart and caring and he made the class as easy as possible despite the the boring class materials. Easy hw and extra credits, would recommend to anyone.
One of the best professors I've had. Very caring, smart, professor. Would 100% take again.

He is the best professor I have ever had. He made learning exactly how it should have been with this course without overly complicating things. He is also super responsive and understanding. Everybody should definitely take.

260 can be a difficult class, but Professor Tong is very caring and gives good responses on Piazza or in-person. The sample exams correlate pretty well as long as you do some decent studying. He also gives 5% extra credit if you buy the Connect book and do the homeworks. The only "bad" thing is that his lectures are often long and he goes fast.

it can be hard to concentrate during lectures, but the professor is very understanding and is always willing to answer questions. the lecture content comes from the online textbook, which you don't have to buy unless you want to complete it for extra credit. overall, the class is a little difficult, but the professor is willing to help you succeed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is an excellent professor, and although some students may find his lectures somewhat dull, he is always willing to answer questions and help students who need extra support. He is genuinely interested in his student's success and ensures they have the necessary resources to excel. He is one of the most caring professors in the CSE department.
He is very understanding and responds quickly to emails and piazza posts. He has practice exams and quizzes that are close to the actual exams and quizzes which helps a lot. Overall good professor.

His lectures were difficult to understand, especially with dealing with such complex material, but if you were to self learn and master the material, he has very lenient grading and even though the homework load is a handful, it is good practice for both the exams and practical knowledge. He handled the aftermath of the shooting very well.

The lectures were not great so be ready to self-learn and search for youtube lectures. Otherwise, the class was quite fair. The exams and quizzes were all based on previous material shown in class and nothing was surprising. Quite a bit of optional XC was available up to 5% of the total grade. And the homework is also fair and self-graded.

CSE260 is a foundation building course, and professor Tong succeeds in doing that. Annoyingly the book was on Connect and cost a decent bit of money, but it was solely for extra credit points - speaking of which, you won't need them. Lectures are not the greatest, but he'll respond to queries fast. I suggest reading the slides and self-learning.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As another user said, the professor was overall very solid.  Lectures were really slow and boring, but everything else was pretty good.  Was very fast to respond to questions and did a good job organizing the course and listening to students.  All in all a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is such a nice guy that listens to student feedback and adapts the class, but he sucks at lecturing. But god bless his review videos. That is were you will learn the material, cause in lectures good luck not sleeping.

Dont take this class alongside other demanding classes. Be very intentful and careful with your homeworks. The quizzes and tests will try to trick you, so please study hard. Read the book and the slides for maximum effect. For the tests make an amazing cheat sheet. Good enough cheat sheets wont work. Find someone to work/check stuff over with.

She is an incredible professor and makes every student feel heard and seen. She always makes sure each student is learning the material in a way that makes sense for them individually, and explains the content clearly. Would 100% take her courses again.

She is an incredible educator! She teaches the content well and makes sure everyone understands by asking if anyone needs a different explanation to grasp the concepts. She is one of the best professors I have ever had. She is incredibly understanding and helpful, I would take her class 100 times over if I could. She is the best!
i thought the TAs were wild. like if you didn't understand something they were just rude. The prof was nice and would help. I would just watch out for the TAs. good luck guys!
She is an amazing math teacher and makes it a very safe space to ask questions. She'll tell you about the quizzes ahead of time so if you study outside of class time you'll definitely pass.

I would recommend this professor. She makes sure everyone understrands the material and is willing to teach it a different way. She is very kind and doesn't make you feel any less for not getting it. This class is difficult in general and she does not pretty fast.
This professor is a very tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Test at least once or twice a week, it's quite hard to keep up at times. Attendance is mandatory and I wouldn't advise skipping any classes because you'd get lost because of how fast she moves, she goes super in depth about what topic she's teaching. Her class is usually 2 hours 2 a week and that can be bit much.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: No professor showed their true colors in the aftermath of tragedy. Not only was there a quiz the DAY OF students returning after the incident, but then said in that same lecture "It's better than canceling class" (??) Her lectures are slow-paced, her explanations were confusing for how many times she worded them, and the grading was tough.
Prof. Zimmerman really cares about the success of students. That means she has to be harsh sometimes, but thanks to her, I drastically increased my study quality and my grade.
Very enthusiastic and passionate about class content. Very easy to work with and genuinely wants students to succeed.

She loves math and is very genuine when it comes to helping other students because she wants everyone to get better at what they are learning. Professor Zimmerman will make math a little easier for you and everyone around you.

I'm not good at math and had to drop, but she is an amazing professor who goes out of her way to help you pass the class. Usually responds to emails within the day and tries to offer as much help or compromises that she can.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She was very nice, wants you to succeed. Very accessible outside of class, encourages questions, I am not the best at math but she always found ways to explain things different ways if you were confused. It wasn't supposed to be asynchronous but MSU said it was and she was very accommodating to students needing their own time to take the course.
Great Professor. Always tries her best to be available for office hours. Make sure you take the participation assignments seriously! Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the best math professors Ive ever had. Shes willing to work around your schedule if you need help in office hours, great explainer, has practice sheets and exams set up for you to succeed. She is a tough greater but thats the best part! It helps you get prepared for calculus. Take her!!! Highly recommended, best professor ever!!

If you can take Zimmerman! She literally designed the course, she is so sweet, and she is super helpful during her office hours. She one of the few math profs I felt comfortable asking questions to. I really loved her as my prof and if I need to take calc I'm taking it with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She was the best math teacher I've ever had! She encouraged us to ask questions and explained concepts so well. I wish I could have her for all of my math classes.

She goes through the notes in a very clear manner each lecture and is even willing to explain certain concepts multiple times to make sure that everyone understands. I can honestly say that I loved this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Zimmerman was the best prof I have ever had. I struggled in math but she really takes the time to make sure you understand the material. If I could take all of my math courses with her, I would do it in a heartbeat! She wants students to succeed!! Both in person and online, she was AMAZING!!

Ms. Z is one of the best Math teachers a student can have. She always makes sure that students are understanding the topic and if a student doesn't understand she will explain during class another way that makes sense. She is also pursuing a PhD so she is also a student at the moment, meaning she understands the current struggle. Would Recommend!!!
Great teacher! Helps with any questions you have and makes sure you understand the content.

Very great teacher, she is helpful. If you need her, all you have to do is email her and she'll either set up a face to face or video chat with you on the spot. She cares about helping you pass. Grading scale is great. She understands the struggles students have and works with you. Love her very much, if you have her you are in GOOD HANDS!

She is one of the best professors I have ever had. She explains the material so well, if you don't understand she will explain it another way. She gives you her notes from class which is really helpful. I wish that I could have her for every math class!

She is an excellent teacher, provides great examples and goes over ones people have trouble on. She runs the MLC so she is very helpful with student. She uses OneNote to do notes in class which makes it easy to read and very organized and posts a blank note sheet so you can print off as well as a completed one after the lecture. Very good teacher.
If you have to take the class take it with her.

She was awesome! She runs the MLC and pulls in examples that students have had problems on. She also used to be a high school teacher so she actually cares if you understand! She makes the calculus easy to understand and tries to relate it to things you already know so you can understand it better. She does reviews before each exam in class.

I can't say much about the professor because I have not had to contact her, but the course itself depends solely on your TA, as everyone else said. The experiments have minimal instructions, and the case studies are where you meet on Zoom with your team, and one person basically completes the entire thing, which is not a great setup.

I got a 70% on a case study I did all the work for. My group got a 95%. Thought it was a mistake; was bc I was late to the zoom meeting (group discussion). Zoom useless. Got a 50% on my final case bc I was late. She was not understanding over email and condescending. Can't believe I failed assignment and got 15% off another bc I was late to zoom.
Super rude and not understanding. Doesn't give clear instructions most times

Very apathetic to student situations, and very difficult grader. 

If you do make the same mistake as me, and decide to take a class with this professor, make sure you do check the briefly mentioned lab manual, as it will be key to your success.

As said, this class relies heavily on who you have as a TA. However, I had a very difficult group this semester which made the class 10x harder, as assignments are created for 4 people to work on, not 1, and when concerns are raised about this, no one really addresses it. The class in general isn't too bad, and if you work hard you should do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This course really depends on who you had as a TA, as well as your group members. Personally, I did just fine in this course by coming to class prepared.

Like the comment below, the class is heavily dependent on your TA. The class is 90% group work, so if you do not get a good group the class will be terrible. Theirs groups projects, presentation, labs, case study's, all of which you probably won't fit in the class time. If you have a free loader in your group get it sorted quickly.

The class is a lab class that is largely ran by TAs, so YMMV there. However, she is in charge of organizing the course. The course is pretty organized and easy to navigate. Also, there are quizzes each week based on lectures she records of herself. Most of the quizzes are easy enough but can have some tricky questions. This class was fine.

Her ISS Lifespan Development Course is her going on Pro-life tangents for almost 2 hours. You could learn the same things she teaches in her lectures by watching Fox News. This woman is unnecessarily difficult and wants you to prioritize her class above anything and everything. Has very little empathy for students and their personal lives.
So boring and the easiest information being explained over and over for hours

Dr. Yelinek is a lovely professor, and SOC 241 is such an easy course! Your grade is made up of (open-note) exams and in-class assignments, but both are super easy. She is a caring professor who facilitates interesting conversations throughout her lectures. I strongly recommend taking this course with Dr. Yelinek - it's an easy 4.0!

It's very easy to four point her class as there's only two things that the grades hinge upon: in class exercises and exams. Both are open note and pretty easy to complete. If you're not coming to class, make sure to have D2L open on your phone or computer at least twenty minutes before class ends!! Lots of discussions but they aren't enforced.

This class was really easy but mandatory attendance (in class assignments and sign in sheet). There are no tests or finals, but one group project which is a presentation. Professor Yelinek is really nice but also lowk a talker and class always goes the whole time.

Amazing professor that presents the information in a way that makes it easy to understand. In class activities are randomly at the end of class and cannot be made up, so thats kinda an attendance aspect of the class. No homework, 5 total quizzes that are open note and not in class. Honors option is a very short in-class presentation - do it!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor is very nice, and she knows what she is talking about. However, she talks for so long that time gets away from her and you will go over the end time for the class. That is really my only issue with her but this is an easy class where you do learn a lot from it.
I absolutely loved Dr. Yelinek! She is such an empathetic and warm individual, and her lectures are very engaging and thought provoking.

Dr. Yelinek was great and I really enjoyed her lectures. Just come to class as in-class quizzes are a good chunk of your grade (but they are super simple and based on the lecture you just listened to). Quizzes were online and you didn't have to come to class for them. Just go to class and you should do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Yelinek is extremely kind. No homework, quizzes online and not taken in class and open note. There is a book you're supposed to buy but you can pass without it. Attendance not mandatory but I would recommend coming because sometimes she has mini pop quizzes at the end of class.

Great teacher but often talks specifically about my culture (and no others usually) as highly conservative and dogmatic. As an atheist and the only person from that ethnicity in class I felt it erased my experience and made it seem like I have to represent my ethnicity/a religion i don't even believe in instead of just be a student in class.

Second class I've taken from this Professor. Quizzes are straight forward and slides were uploaded to D2L. Occasionally short, open note quizzes at the end of the class. Highly recommend if you need an easier but still interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Yelinek is very nice, but attendance is very mandatory and her rubrics and assignment guidelines were pretty unclear. Lectures sometimes got out early and were very boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Yelinek seems strict but just values attendance (don't take if you can't attend classes; expect brief in-class quizzes). All exams were online, remote, and open note, but were, in my opinion, ill-timed (very brief). Lectures were a bit repetitive, but exams reflected the slides and in-class quizzes. Free online textbook.
Started off by saying she didn't believe in race. Would mark you absent even if you were there and had proof, if you had evidence of you being sick she still wouldn't care.

Already signed up to take her course next sem. Very understanding and very caring. Topics are interesting which made me participate in class willingly (and she never calls on students who don't have their hand up). Also is considerate about poor weather conditions.

Her guidelines were very unclear, and she would post conflicting guidelines for the same assignment, making it confusing what was expected. She takes an unreasonably long time to grade assignments, making it nearly impossible to know what your grade currently is. The lectures are boring and long. There were a couple of interesting assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Super easy 4.0 class. NO EXAMS - only open note quizzes (no class on those days). No homework & no projects!

Random "in class exercises" which is a short, opennote quiz at the end of class that usually has a 10 minute timer. They can not be made up and none are dropped. Sit next to the same people since we always turn and talk.

This is okay if you're taking it as an elective. If this is something you actually care about I wouldn't recommend it with this professor. She seems nice, the lectures are just so unengaging and a bore to sit through. She shows a lot of old clips from youtube and TED talks rather than explaining material herself.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is easy, but lectures are painful. Constant clips of outdated TED talks and other BS. Nothing too thought-provoking if you actually want to learn something. I feel like this is what the entire SOC department at MSU has become.

personally, i loved this course. exams were online, open note and typically ?s were pulled right from her slides. she does just read off slides but we also have a lot of class discussions which i enjoyed. attendance assignments are random. i took this as an elective and it was a simple 4.0 if you show up.

She uses slides made by the textbook and just turns around and reads straight from them. No expanding or teaching. She also likes to bring up politics here and there which is off-putting for some. Overall she is a very nice person but not a great teacher.

Too easy and boring for a 300-level class. Learned nothing, and Prof Yelinek clearly doesn't want to be there. Most days, we just watched videos/ movies, and random others took over teaching. If you need an easy elective, take it I guess, but if you're a soc major, you will be bored to death and have wasted your money. DO NOT BUY THE TEXTBOOK.

Very insistent on class participation and didn't excuse the absence of students in a gas leak until people complained to higher ups about being unable to commute to class. Was very rude about her attendance policy and didn't let students do the attendance quiz while they got ready or were walking out the door. Also no sick policy without note
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was not a fan of the way this class was formatted. If you plan on not attending-- you will not pass. I also stopped using the text after the 4/5 week... She will not excuse you (despite what the syllabus says). I know a student had to come to class with a positive covid test. It was hard to talk to her as well, it was draining. Super easy though.

I took this as an elective and loved Professor Yelinek. She is so caring and considerate. Attendance isnt mandatory, but she would do random VERY easy quizzes in class that if you missed you could not retake. She had quizzes after each topic and they were decently lengthy, but easy open-note and taken from home with no class those days (amazing.).

Attendance is VERY mandatory. Sign in sheet at every class. A good chunk of the work is done in trios You all get the same grade regardless of what portions you do and what portions your partners do. Choice of a presentation or a paper as a final. Rarely answers emails. Is mostly understanding of personal events. Rubrics could be clearer.

I did not like this professor. The quizzes were online but she got crazy about attendance. She gave multiple students 0 on the in class participation even if they were in class. Not very good professionalism. All her lecture slides were posted on d2l and in class all she did was read off the slides so it was kind of pointless to go

Dr. Yelinek is a wonderful person, but her teaching style is not my forte. Attendance is overdone; she made a student come to class with covid (even with proof) for attendance points. I didn't use the textbook after like the 4th week, class can be 4.0-ed with your eyes closed. Not a lot of work, hardest part is the attendance for sure

This class is fairly easy. Classes are lectures, but all lecture notes are online. Attendance isn't mandatory, but she does do random in class assignments that are worth points. There are 5 open note, online quizzes and no exams. She also gave us a extra credit quiz at the end of the semester for up to 70 bonus points (which is a lot).

class was easy, tests were all online. Yelinek is crazy about attendance. I showed up to every lecture and completed her attendance checks on d2L. More than once she changed my grade to 0 and claimed that I wasn't in class and wouldn't change it back unless I emailed her multiple times. She is not professional AT ALL.

Don't take this class if you genuinely want to be taught the material, every week a different group has to give you a presentation where nobody actually retains or feels interested in. Also Jodi, has lots of good and bad days, and I feel like she personally took her bad days out on her class. It made me feel like I was getting group punishment.

This class was super easy and all of the tests were online. She is also very nice. The only downside is that she is a little bit crazy when it comes to attendance. Overall though this class was very interesting and I definitely enjoyed it. I would 100% take it again.
She was just very difficult to work with when I talked with her I always ended up feeling worse.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quizzes are easy as long as you take good notes, they are timed a minute a question though (not as bad as you think). Textbook is informative and helps as well. Sometimes the ends of lectures were rushed, but overall a good class and would definitely take it again.

All quizzes were online, taken at home, open note and open textbook (super duper easy). There was no final exam. Attendance is not mandatory, but there are in class assignments that are due during classtime on random days. Dr Yelinek is kind and very knowledgeable about her field. Her class is extremely easy!

I would have been more willing to honor the mandatory attendance policy if half of the lectures weren't student group projects. You can pass this class if you just show up, but class is deeply boring. Overall Dr. Yelinek is fine and has clear assignment criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was such a great course. No homework, only tests and puts online and easily can get over 100% with extra credit questions. NO FINAL. If you want, you can take the course completely online because she just assigns an "in-person" assignment randomly but you can easily complete it from home just watching from D2L in the quizzes section.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: she spreads so much misinformation in this class from claiming and showing us videos of people espousing the benefits of supplements to cure or treat bipolar disorder and yet as a sociology professor describing her own family, she says "low" or "high" functioning autism which is not accepted by the wider medical community; also very disorganized
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I think Dr. Yelinek needs to do some self-reflection. Regardless, if you do the work and go to all classes, you'll get a 4. Quite a few things contradict her syllabus regarding grading, but if you bring it to her attention, she will make amends. I've noticed she also likes to take off points for minuscule reasons.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Jodi is a suuuuuper kind person and you can tell how much she cares about her students and the topics at hand. I was not a big fan of SOC350, I felt like there were so many random assignment requirements amongst other things that made the class 10x harder than it needed to be. I wish I had taken a dif class with her, but I really like her!
As long as you show up to class and pay attention you'll be just fine. She asks questions about your experiences as it relates to the course and I encourage you to respond.

Dr Yelinek was amazing!!  She is so sweet and you can tell shew is genuinely passionate about the topics she teaches about.  The class was so easy and there was so much extra credit offered that if you did not get a 4.0 that's on you.  She said the book was mandatory but I just took notes from the slides and I was just fine.  Take this course!

honestly prof yelinek is a super sweet person outside if class, but she does not answer questions, doesn't help her students, and grades SOOO harshly with no chance to fix anything. also doesn't grade in a timely manner so you never know your grade in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The only negative I would give is grading criteria doesn't match the syllabus. Otherwise, she was very caring towards students and willing to help when needed. Class was mostly lectures and projects, homework was straightforward. She's a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Love professor Yelinek. Would 100% take any of her classes again. She really connects with the entire class. But she does not give trigger warnings for some of the lectures. Which some of them might be needed. But love love loveee her.

Was an amazing professor very caring! The extra credit quizzes and presentation helped if you missed an actual quiz. Only 6 quizzes the whole semester try not to miss them because making them up will be hard. There is a textbook but I found it free online

Dr. Yelinek is by far one of my favorite professors I have ever had. She is kind and caring towards her students and is very understanding. The grade is based on weekly page papers based on reading and lectures. There is  1 final paper and 1 film paper, and a group presentation. Overall great course, and would recommend it even for an elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Yelinek grades entirely on the 6 quizzes given in class (600 pts). This is the only thing that determines your grade. It's nice as there is no homework but you have to do well on the quizzes. There is no final and there's a large EC opportunity at end of semester. I'm taking her again next semester
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Yelinek's class is a good choice. She takes attendance every class but if you miss a class you get points taken off for weekly assignments. So, if you don't plan on showing up, take a different class. If you follow the rubric and assignment directions you will get a 4.0. She is super nice and helped me a lot with learning APA formatting.

Dr. Yelinek is a great professor and cares about her students. There are no quizzes or exams in this course. You are grades on weekly papers based on the textbook, a group presentation, film analysis and a final project or paper. I 10/10 recommend this class you will learn so much useful information.

This class was so easy. Your grade is made up of 6 Quizzes that are only 25 questions each, so no homework. The quizzes are not difficult either, and she offers a huge extra credit assignment at the end of the semester. This class is a guaranteed 4.0!! I spent 30 min max on this class a week.

Would highly recommend her if you need to take this course. Quizzes are easy A's as long as you review the material and take notes.(open note & textbook). Material itself isn't difficult either. I actually forgot to take one of the quizzes and would've lost a 6th of my grade but she opened an EC quiz that made up for the lost points.

She is an amazing professor and incredibly caring. One of the easiest classes to pass if you follow her instructions. There are weekly reviews, one presentations and a few papers. She grades very well! Take this class and you won't regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really simple class with only 6 quizzes that made up your grade. Excellent professor with solid lectures and someone who wants you to succeed! Helpful for a senior looking for some upper level electives to easily 4.0.

Professor Yelinek is a great educator and wants you to succeed. One thing about the class that I disliked was the amount of busywork this course had. Get ready for weekly assignments, group presentations, several dense papers, and a large final project. You will have to work for a good grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Yelinek's class was very straight to the point and manageable. She allowed all the quizzes to be open book/note/powerpoint. The grading was made up of 6 100 point quizzes and offered an 80 point extra credit quiz! You can tell she wants her students to earn a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I have absolutely no respect for Dr. Yelinek after taking her class. She promotes stigma against mental illness which I ultimately had to go to the dean about. Requires cameras to be on and screenshots you if you are on your phone or laying down. Told us getting covid is not an excuse to miss class. Ironic for this being a mental health class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Yelinek! She was very polite and the only grades in her class were quizzes that were every other week and if you payed attention in class they were very easy and often straight from the power points! I hope to take another class with Dr. Yelinek.

Professor Yelinek mainly read from power points for the majority of the class period, which became kind of redundant since the powerpoints were already posted on D2L for all of us to look at. Class participation wasn't mandatory, and I was able to get a 4.0 by just reading the notes on my own. The class should have been asynchronous.

I liked her a lot got over a 100% in her class. Randomly take attendance for participation pts, you never knew which day she would do it. She gave a 50 pt EC opportunity, then she even gave us another 50 pt one at the end of semester. Class is only graded on 5 noncumulative quizzes and the participation points. Doesn't believe in hard quizzes.

Professor Yelinek was super sweet, and she was very understanding if there was ever an issue. She is not a hard grader, and there were no exams or quizzes in the class. Your grade is based off of simple in class assignments and a final paper. I would recommend taking her if you want an easy 4.0.

I love professor Yelinek! If you show up and take notes and look them over before the exams, you will pass every one with an A! Her exams are easy, her lectures are clear, and she is accommodating to students. It is very test heavy but very doable. She also offered us 50 points extra credit (when most exams are worth 100). Highly recommend!

She was not interesting, read directly off her power point slides, but the quizzes were very easy and pretty common sense based. There was never homework. The extra credit offered at the beginning of the year was awesome, but she was boring. No final exam though which was nice. Easy class overall.

I could tell she truly liked what she taught. Her lectures were well organized and relevant to what was on the quizzes. She does a extra credit project to help boost your grade. If you take notes/ pay attention during class you will be fine. She is a very nice lady and makes class enjoyable.

Professor Yelinek is probably one of the best MSU professors there is! She lets you out of class ATLEAST 30 minutes early each time and there is opportunity for extra credit, and it's fairly simple. The quizzes (which are essentially exams) are quite straightforward and the study guides are very helpful. Highly reccomend this class & Prof. Yelinek!

Jodi is probably one of the best professors I've ever taken. ISS 318 talks about lifespan development and it's by far the easiest ISS i've ever took. She is very passionate in her work and her grading is very simplistic. Half the points you earn, the other half you can earn your own way. Would recommend professor!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: One of the only ISS210 profs to not do open note quizzes. Quizzes are on basically nothing from the notes or lectures. She likes to talk about things that are irrelevant to the class and gets off topic a lot. She's super nice and there's no homework though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Moreno is very sweet and kind, and open to discussing social justice issues today. She is also very funny and loves to tell stories. This class is very writing-heavy, so just be prepared. She can be a harsh grader, but she does give good feedback so that you can get a good grade on the final draft. Overall, an amazing professor personally.

Profe Moreno Mosqueda is an extremely down-to-earth person. She is very kind and not afraid to give constructive criticism. This class can be very tough, but as long as you follow her clear guidelines and expectations, this class can be very enjoyable.

Professor was very nice and kind, but could be super professor-y at times. Had clear rubrics and as long as you followed them it was good. I missed a month due to illness and for the most part she was accommodating, up until the last week of my illness. I definitely learned and thought she was funny, would take her again!

She was funny and nice to talk to, but was difficult when it came to grading. You need to be participating a lot during each class as she will take away points every lecture if not. The essays are worth 50% of your grade and the 2 tests had no study guide and we had no idea what would be on them. When I was sick I could not make up work missed

I would never take this professor ever again at MSU. Has no desire for her students, and is rude to many. Participating in class and asking questions would never get you the full attedance points. She believes study guides are a form of cheating, so be prepared to fail your exams. If you have her I suggest dropping out immediately.

Absolutely dreaded this class every week because of her. Consistently complained about her job, was impossible to reach via email and for office hours, and docked attendance points even if you participated and were paying attention. Showed no understanding for her students, lacked professionalism, and was condescending and rude multiple times.

Professor Moreno Mosqueda was the worst professor I've experienced at MSU and many other people in our class agreed. It was almost impossible to get a 4.0 in her class unless you are a native Spanish speaker. She graded so harshly and then offered no further help or feedback. She was rude at times and very inaccessible outside of class for help.

I love Profesora Moreno! She is very kind and makes her class very interesting and fun. We did a couple essays but if you put your best effort you would get a pretty good grade. She always spoke in Spanish and interacted with the students no matter their skill level! Such a great person too and very funny!

The worst prof i've ever had. Even attendance was graded absurdly harsh, being early, asking/answering questions & group participation wasn't enough to get full attendance points. Lectured forever with no visuals, anti-technology, & has ridiculously difficult exams WITH NO STUDY GUIDES. I would never ever recommend this professor, I barely learned.

Do not select this professor. There are classes that fulfill the requirement that are way easier. Midterm was 2 essay questions with no rubric to follow and is graded based of what seems to be opinion, not to mention most of the class failed it. Prof did not make it easy to work with her leaving students feeling hopeless in terms of grades.
This professor does everything possible to make an IAH difficult. She is not understanding, forgiving, or helpful when students are struggling. Avoid taking her classes at all costs.

Had zero care in the world whether her students did well or not and didn't seem to care whether or not anyone understood the material. Over half the class failed the midterm paper she assigned and rather than admit she didn't adequately teach the material she belittled us and told us how disappointed she was. If possible DO NOT take her class.
lol you better hope your mom doesn't die while you're in this class because she will give you a 0 for missing class to go to the funeral.

She never taught, she just had us pay for a $75 online Spanish learning program and called it a day. She'd grade projects, but everything else was automated by the website. When I reached out to her with a problem, she would be very rude and blunt when emailing back. Do not take this professor.

This professor has no care for her students. Since the first day of classes you could tell she had no heart to see her students succeed nor was clear with her complex curriculum and the expectations she had for all assignments and projects. She is flat out rude and does not have email etiquette or skill of respecting those "below" her. 0/5!

Overall, the class content was not difficult. Her grading was harsh and she was condescending. For a language class, we should be given room to learn from our mistakes and improve them. However, Professor Moreno is unforgiving. Did not seem like she cared.
Do not take this class, I regret it so much. The professor grades so hard and the lectures are very difficult to follow. You're better off taking any other IAH course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I've never seen a prof non-stop talk for an hour and 50 minutes like she does. Lectures are incredibly hard to follow. Unforgiving if you are sick/have any issues. Assignments are due at 5 pm twice a week which is VERY inconvenient. Grades way too hard for an IAH. I've never had a worse professor here

Worst professor I've had at my time here, hard to follow along, does not care for students issues with homework, grades unfairly in every possible aspect. You could be have the worst illness of your life and she would still expect you to turn everything in. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

Hard to follow along in class,  extremely tough grader, would not provide sympathy at all.

reviews.comment: Grades very diffcult.

The class was easy and I did fine but she didn't really do any teaching. The class was asynchronous and she just had us buy (expensive) spanish teaching programs online that did the teaching. When I did interact with her she responded quickly and also sent emails to make sure we were on track.

The class itself wasn't that hard. There was an average amount of homework but it was all pretty repetitive. Her as a person is where I grade her low. She was very uptight and condescending. Would interrupt you before you could finish your question, refused to give extra credit and was overall inflexible and stubborn. Passable, but bad attitude.

I absolutely loved Profesora Mosqueda! I was genuinely excited for my 8 am classes every Friday with her. She seems like she really cares if you are struggling with any concepts and is great at giving very helpful feedback.

She is such a great professor and makes class really easy and fun. She likes to get to know her students and makes class interesting. She teaches the class entirely in Spanish, which I find to be very helpful since I am minoring in Spanish. I would definitely take another class with her again!

I was lowkey scared of her at first because she seemed scary, but I don't regret taking her class. She will give you feedback on the smallest details that will make your work go from sloppy to a professional level.

She's tough, but she knows what it takes to become a respected professional in the creative industry. The class isn't hard, but keep her feedback in mind, she really wants you to succeed. I picked her class because I saw she had tons of creative experience compared to the other professors offering the class. You'll get a lot out of her class!

She is tough, but only because she truly wants you to succeed. She tells you what you need to hear, but not because it's personal, of course, but because she knows good design. I would take her 100 times over. Be open to constructive criticism, try, and show up. Maral is a GREAT teacher.
hard. she knows the industry but she is extremely tough and only cares if the projects are what she would have done
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Maral gives you plenty of time to complete the three projects graded in this course. As long as you show up and listen to her feedback, you will not have an issue with this class. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tough class, but I have never learned so much from anyone else. Made me into a good designer.

Maral does not care about her students, and I have learned that the hard way. Your final grade is based off of nothing but projects. Usually 4-5 and no more. She likes things her way, and not our own style. At the end of the day I need someone who's understanding that things in life can happen and life gets in the way, and she is not that someone.

You get what you give when you take Maral's class. She has a lot of experience in design, so she tends to grade things to her liking and she will be direct with how she gives feedback. As long as you follow her suggestions, which can actually be very helpful, you will do fine in the class. She gives plenty of time for each project.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She knows design well but she's just not a professor who truly cares about her student's well-being. And that's fine, but I'd rather take a class with a professor who is a bit more understanding that sometimes things happen.

reviews.comment: Maral is a very passionate professor that truly cares about her students success. You will get out of this class whatever you put in. Nah

reviews.comment: Maral is undoubtedly one of the best professors I've encountered at MSU. Maral delivers feedback in an honest manner, fostering an environment where growth and improvement are encouraged.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have had Maral for two classes. She is a tough grader, but she knows what she is talking about. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Maral is a smart woman and knows design well, however, she was not meant to be a professor. She only wants you to do your creative work the way SHE likes it. If you turn in something that wasn't made with her specific style in mind, she will change the entire thing the second you show her. I respect that, but feel we should have creative freedom.

I started taking her for ADV326 and ultimately had to drop the class so I can take it with a better professor. The assignments she gave were graded on her opinions and didn't teach us anything. The semester was based on 5 assignments for a final where we were given no direction whatsoever. Don't take this class unless you want to waste time.

Maral is my favorite professor I have had at MSU. Although she is a tough grader, if you work with her enough and respond to the feedback she gives you, you will do well. She is a design legend and I am honored to have learned so much from her. You can learn adobe software online, you can't learn Maral's design techniques anywhere but from her.

The class is based on only 5 assignments. The class is pretty useless, she shows us slides just about the project and does not teach us the software.
Work is graded on her point of view of design, if you don't have the same vision as her good luck you won't score higher than a 70.
She sets you up for failure has no regard to student success.
Avoid this prof at all cost, she grades hard and cares more about her syllabus than you. Do not recommend at all.

reviews.comment: Maral is the type of Professor no one likes. She flat out doesn't care about your success not matter what goes on in your life. Maral is amazing, I've learned so much in her class.

reviews.comment: Worst professor Ive ever had at msu. Let students in my class get away with cheating off of each other with no point deductions.

I have had Maral for 2 years. At first she didn't like me in the coding class, but this year it was different. I really enjoyed having her as a professor. reviews.comment: I have taken ADV354 over the summer (Summer I and Summer II). We are given videos and assignments that aren't even graded just to turn around and do a whole separate project. You learn a lot in this class- how to use Adobe Illustrator, InDesign & Photoshop. One assignment assigned each week (due two weeks later) and quizzes after lecture. All the quiz questions are directly from lecture notes- so GO TO CLASS! She's a very nice, approachable prof and will always answer questions/provide guidance if needed!

I disagree with the previous post. This was a good class but requires work. All the quiz answers are given during the class, no excuse to get less then a 4.0 on the quizzes. The professor was easy to talk to and always stayed after class. There was plenty of extra credit. Go to class, do the work and the extra credit. You will do fine.

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She was an amazing Russian professor and made me want to continue Russian

Professor Kumakhova brings exceptional passion and deep knowledge to Russian literature. Her enthusiasm can lead to in-depth discussions that may extend beyond the allotted class time. This course is ideal for students with a strong foundation in reading comprehension and a genuine interest in the subject.

Though the heavy workload and her strict grading proved demanding initially, this course ultimately honed my writing skills and fostered a profound appreciation for Russian literature. It has become a truly fascinating subject for me, making it one of the most valuable experiences in my academic career.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is a native speaker, so she does know what she's talking about. She does stress me out though as she can get upset during class and is prone to tangents. That being said, if you do the homework and make efforts to improve and understand then you'll be fine. But be prepared when you come to class or it will be a solid hour of anxiety.

This teacher is one of the worst for such a low level IAH course. The amount of work she expects students to do outside of class is simply unreasonable. She insults students during class. She has no clear method to grading (essays, journals) and will take points off and give reasons as to why that make no sense. Do not take this class.

reviews.comment: Only take IAH207 if you enjoy reading and discussing literature at least to some extent.  She is very intelligent and incredibly passionate.  She can be a little intimidating and there is a decent amount of work and reading involved, but she's very open to deadline changes and understanding.  Her passion is one of her most admirable qualities.

This class requires 7 books you MUST have a copy of. She will know if you don't read. Will make you redo assignments if you are missing something but you will get a good grade if you fix it. she is very fair with deadlines. Does not respond in a timely fashion to emails. about 6 required textbooks needed that you must buy and have a physical copy of. very mean to students will yell & use a synonym to call you stupid if you ask a question that she doesn't like. extreme amnt of reading she will kno if u don't read.

reviews.comment: Best professor for 101/102, as she is the only native speaker I've met in the department, and knows how to teach. This is the best way to learn the phonetics at this level. LOTS of homework, but she lets you resubmit at the end if you missed the deadline. Study and ask questions and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She will EXPECT you to retake assignments you did not do well on. Mind you, this is not to make your life hard, she does this to help you bump your grade up and to learn from your mistakes. DO ALL OF THE READINGS! She is very funny and she will help anyone who needs it. She may be tough but if you put in the work, it makes it worthwhile!

Professor Kumakhova simply grades on opinion, not on factual evidence in texts. If you don't match her opinion in an essay/journal, you will be required to have a meeting with her and rewrite your response. This made class very difficult. You are not able to interpret readings differently from her. If you do, you will fail. Would not recommend.

stories are long and hard to understand. would write 1 1/2 pages per journal, still recieve 0% and asks me to redo everything. stories, quizes, journal due before class (3x week).  3 essays + presenation. will call u out even on zoom. such a harsh grader for a subject that is a uni requirement + not something i will ever go into in the future.

She was a little hard to get used to at first, as she uses a more collegiate style of teaching language. At first, I hated her class, but then I adjusted to it and now I'm doing really well. During this adjustment period, my grade didn't suffer at all. I've learned more in my 1 semester of Russian than I did in my 4 years of high school Spanish.

A lot of her assignments were unclear. She'd tell you one thing but on feedback from assignment mention a bunch of other things. Class was pretty boring for me personally. She is nice overall but her teaching is not up to par. Wouldn't recommend for first option.

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I see a lot of negative reviews but I wanted to say that if you truly want to learn Russian and show you care she will invest time into you. She really does care about her students. Sometimes she does get upset and is strict but if you keep up on your work and show that you're attentive you will be fine. I really enjoyed her.

Grades based off of no rubric, rather how she feels. We had lots of reading and journals. Be ready to stay after class since we couldn't finish in time, and also expects you to meet outside of class for every assignment.

Literally the worst class I have taken in my life. Professor is the most unorganized person I have ever met. Grades based on opinions, changes the course materials whenever she feels like it. Very strict, so it's best to do your homework and study for the quizzes at the start of class. You'll be fine if you do what you're supposed to.

This professor is so unorganized. The grading criteria is not clear at all and she grades based off her own opinion, not the rubric. Classes are boring and hard to get through. English is not her first language and that is clear when she is grading essays.

reviews.comment: She is a good professor. Be prepared to spend hours of your time doing a lot of homework that isnt necessary.

reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

Professor Kumakova is the most demoralizing professor I've had here. Grades for assignments are more a reflection of her mood than of the quality of your work. If she is upset about something, expect her not to rest until everyone around her miserable, regardless of whether or not the thing she's upset about has anything to do with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She doesn't explain what she is doing or what will be on the tests. So you teach yourself but have mandatory lectures that don't help.
Dr. Khumokova is my favorite professor at Michigan State. She is tough, but really teaches you the language.
She's very tough but willing to teach you. But as she said when I was in her office, "I do not suffer fools." Do your work and seem interested is all she asks.

I love the woman to death amazing personality but she is not a good teacher. She brags about the soviet union and their former power and how they are better than america and the language is impossible to learn in the class setting.

I'll be honest. I did 8 semesters with this prof. My lowest scores in undergrad. However, Prof. Kumakova's insight is crystal clear and real. She doesn't bs and she doesn't paint a false pict of the language or culture. After graduation i spent 2 years in the peace corps. She is inspirational in her teaching and true to form. God bless her. E Til

Very easy to understand, she has very little accent. She's always happy to share her experiences from Russia. She follows the text, and the course is very organized. There are never any surprises on tests either. The only downside is that you're only allowed 2 absences.

Sure she's a little crazy, a maybe a bit of a flake when it comes to assignments, quizzes, etc, but if you do your work she's very sweet and definitely knows her stuff - most people who try to teach their native languages aren't very effective, but Zarema can explain complex concepts so they make sense even to us English speakers.

I really wanted to take this class, but I'll never take another class with her as instructor.  If you make one mistake, the entire class will know about it.  She's horrible.  Stay away from her.  The books are interesting, but she's evil.
