Even if you don't like his lectures, you can always not attend lectures and instead watch videos on D2L from professor Maccombs, who is also an amazing professor. Overall the class is difficult but you have many options on how you want to approach the material.

Very bad lectures that would be a waste of my time. I never learned anything from him and had to spend many hours trying to learn to succeed in this class. Not helpful at all though he makes funny jokes.

Nice guy, but his lectures move way too fast to take notes on, much less understand. We had only three 50 minute sessions a week and yet he would speed through his notes and let us out 5-10 minutes early despite the intensity and volume of the material. I found Calc III to be easier than Calc II but I would not recommend taking it with Prof. Abbas.
The professor himself is fine. Nice, explains things well, and is very approachable. However, the class itself is just hard. No other way around it.

Great guy who cares and knows what he's talking about but has so flaws in his lectures. He can be fast with his notes and has a lot of words/explanations/theorems. Other than that, I can't blame the guy, the class is hard in general. The quizzes and exams have T/F questions that would screw me over. 100% on the written part but 60% at the end.

He was such a nice professor, and would answer any questions you brought to him, but about half way through the semester, his lectures didn't make sense. He didn't explain much to us, he just re wrote his notes for us to copy down. We normally did a couple example problems in class, but he didn't explain the steps he just did them.
Horrible Handwriting, would leave lectures without understanding anything, he proceeds really fast and its hard to grasp all the topics hes teaching

He will consistently bring up thought-provoking philosophical questions such as why people so universally conform to silly naming conventions such as "u substitution" and "p-series."  He realizes not all students will need to use Calc II in life.  So, he gives them philosophical wisdom instead.  This is what sets his lectures apart Ryan's videos.

Casim is just a huge meme between me and my friends. With his little jokes about the Stone Age to the caveman method, he got funny little jokes. He lectures quite well but his handwriting is not very easy to read at all. As a professor in any other class I would take him again, but as the professor for Calc 2 again, it depends on how you learn.
Not Casim's fault, but this class was super hard. He made the lectures almost enjoyable to attend. Ask questions, do the homework, and put in the time and you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great guy, so incredibly funny. His lectures were clear and useful for WebWork. Just make sure you go to recitation and take the quizzes. The exams are not bad if you study using the old exams that they provide. 10/10 recommend this guy, he's a gem

What a guy. Abbas is a German genius mathematician with a slick accent. He's always cracking little jokes, bringing a little light to a very dull and stale topic. The class is stone cold. But that's not gonna change with a different prof. Plus lectures aren't mandatory because he posts his notes online. Go to recitation for the quizzes.

I love Abbas with all my heart! Having him as a prof is like having a genius grandpa teach you math; super approachable &clearly cares for students. Explains ideas well&can offer alternative explanations. Writes down everything he says and posts online; this can be annoying in class but makes it easy to miss class, but don't skip- he's super funny!
Loved the guy. Interesting despite the topic and always cracks jokes. Easy grader and throws a huge curve at the end of the semester.
It's not an easy class, but he definitely helps. The homework problems are very similar to those on the quizzes and tests.
I love this guy, really cool!

Funny guy, really smart.  If you're naturally good at math this class won't be too bad.  I would avoid skipping as he covers about a section a lecture.  Homework is tough, but the quizzes and exams are quite easy.

Sharp guy, expects a lot from his students--sometimes I think he confuses us with his grad students. He doesn't always work out solutions to the homework problems before he assigns them, which can turn into long and grueling homework sessions. Homework took roughly ten hours a week, often more. However, it was definitely worth being in his class.
Homework due twice a week- very hard. Tests (2 exams and a final) were easier than the homework. Quizzes once a week. Difficult class, but some interesting proofs. Funny guy
This professor was terrible.
The class was hard, but not beyond what someone in an Honors math class should be able to manage. He gave up his own time for a problem session, and was helpful with office hours. Highly recommended

Very very difficult, even for an honors course. Not impossible though: a good challenge for someone looking to do well in a math career. He explains well, but the material can be so murky that it is still takes time to sift through. Gave up his own time to give us an unofficial recitation session: I highly recommend him.
Great teacher, commited to helping students understand Calculus and do well in the class.
excellent communications ability
hes hilarious, i liked the lectures
He's a really good professor and does a lot of examples to help you understand.  I would definitely recommend him.
Abbas is the****.
I like him because I understand him when he teaches me in class.
Abbas is hilarious!!!
He's not a great prof, but he's a damn genius and he's really funny.
Don't take this class unless you want to enter hell

The lectures are hard to understand and terribly organized. The quizzes are extremely confusing, but exams are better because the TA's write them. There is no homework, only quizzes and exams. The class is unnecessarily difficult and stressful.

The entire course grade is based on quizzes and two exams. It's unrealistic what you're expected to memorize. You don't get missed quiz answers back to study. The lectures teach you nothing you'll have to do most of the learning on your own. The syllabus states 1% per absence will be deducted from your final grade. Don't take unless you have to.

Much more tolerable than co-professor. Would have had much fewer issues with this class if she had taught more of the lectures. Actually graded assignments as if we were college students, rather than individuals with Ph.D's- gave clear grading criteria. Overall a caring professor; however, course lacked a central theme which overall made difficult.

Made this class tolerable for me. Much better communicator, and much better at working through content with students, than Professor Craig. Easier grader, with much better communicated expectations on the work she graded.
Very nice, caring, and a great grader with gives amazing feedback on papers.

Being only an assistant prof. she sure does the bulk of the work for this class. She's very caring and wants you to do well. Makes things easy to understand and how they grade things(even though it is EXTREMELY hard for an intro course). It is guest prof. lectures with short exam responses. She is the reason I let alone passed this, main prof. bad
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The main professor for this class Dr. Craig is terrible. She does the majority of the work for being an assistant professor, genuinely cares about her students and their grades. super super easy to reach and always very kind and helpful.

Dr. Bennett was great in FW181! She was very easy to contact and schedule meetings with if you were confused on the content, and helped me get a great grade on my final paper and gave awesome feedback! She is one of the best teachers I've ever had!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is one of the best professors in the world. I have never seen someone who pushes you work for everything. Dr. A you are the best teacher ever and I will never forget you. The ones who were talking smack about you were obviously lazy in class and want an easy A.

Great professor, doesn't take bull.  You will work hard so if you are looking for an easy class don't take it.  But if you are looking for a class that challenges your perspective and helps you become an independent thinker than I recommend her.
AVOID AT ALL COSTS! You will spend more time working on her assignments week by week than compared to the rest of your classes combined.  She grades unfairly and displays favoritism amoung students.
Debrenna teaches a challenging course and she is quite willing to help.
Doesn't grade fairly and fosters negativity. Students don't count.

Diversity specialization is biased and outdated and doesn't take into account the needs of many select groups and populations.  Attention is given to double standard producing outcomes when important reality focused viewpoints are disregarded.
She good
Dr. A is fantastic.  I can't think of one bad thing to say. Best class/proff here at MSU. If you can, take her class. Your ideas will be challenged and you will learn so much.  AMAZING!
Dr.A is a very kind and good woman who loves her students and tries her best to relate to everyone. She is helpful and willing to work with students when needed.
Believes her lens of the world is the only one.  Seemed to single out students at times and not in a good way. Not as openminded as she believes.

Terribly structured class. He takes over 60 slides to explain a topic that our in class professors can explain in 6. I wish I could attach a photo to this review to help you visualize how crowded and confusing  the slides unnecessarily are. He uses grammar structures to explain themself, harder if you aren't familiar with concepts already.

Ausin is really funny and silly, and the TA was great. The class was confusing at times, because the organization of topics is kind of weird. Just dont let content pile up and youre fine. I never actually bought the textbook, its on internetarchive. Buy the Spanish verb tenses book from mcgraw (its like a workbook) and its genuinely a cheat code.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is the worst professor I have had here at MSU. The class itself is okay, it's graded pretty tough. However as a professor he lacks empathy and understanding for students. You only get two absences for the entire semester despite having excuses absences, doctors notes, going to competitions for clubs, etc.

Professor Ausin killed my passion for Spanish. He is difficult to work with, unaccomadating, and impersonal. Ausin allows 2 absences during a 4 month long course and if you get sick expect to lose points for that. Fortunate for Ausin is that he doesn't teach the classes so he has no worries about getting sick. Avoid at all costs.

Professor Ausin is very strict and very difficult. He is one of the least understanding and accommodating professors I've ever had. He's very impersonal and is not invested in your success in his class. His online lectures are poorly structured and hard to follow. Avoid

The professor just grades and manages the homework. It's other people teaching the material for him. This creates a disconnect between the students and professor, especially if you need help. This is a 3 credit class but feels like it should be 4. The work is really unengaging and so far the Spanish program is killing my passion for the language.

Grades INSANELY hard. Rubrics are not clear, leading to confusion on the midterm and the final. Overall a nice professor and is a good guy, just clearly does not push you to succeed in the course. Group projects are mandatory and constantly received points off when other group members did not contribute. Would not recommend this class to anyone.

Basically this course is taught by like random teachers that answer to Professor Ausin, he's not involved like whatsoever he just does the grading and posts the assignments but he's not there for the actual in person class. Lots of homework every week and very heavy lecture material.

I took Professor Ausin for online SPN310 during the summer. It was all online, and we met once a week for a short quiz over what we learned during the previous week. He's a tough grader, but if you ask him for help and explanations, he's more than willing to do it. I really enjoyed the class and thought Professor Ausin was nice.

Do not take this class to fill a humanities requirement. So much work, there are so many easier alternatives. I thought it would be interesting because it's about swearing but it was an ungodly amount of work with such harsh grading. Worst class I've taken at MSU, seriously how is he still on payroll. Who else can I complain to?! 4.0 cutoff is a 94
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I've ever had. No clear rubric so he marks you down at whim on whatever he feels didn't meet his standards. Had to correct him multiple times on assignments and quiz mistakes so he'd fix my grade. Absurd amount of reading and writing assignments weekly. Just a poorly structured class with an even worse professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This teacher was terrible, he has so much work every week. His grading is super harsh, he's so uninvolved. I was having issues with the SPN310 textbook, and he basically told me it's not his problem and refused to help. Too much detail, it's hard to grasp ideas sometimes. Strict grader, he's literally awful. Can't wait to be out of his class.

This professor is awful. Harsh grader. Reading quizzes with lots of questions with a short amount of time. There is so much group work with an online class. Essays and reflections every week that are not horrible but it is just a lot of writing. Do not take this class, save yourself the stress of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Terrible professor probably one of the worst I have had so far. Took this class without looking at his rating. Such a harsh grader for a university required class, just pick a different IAH and save yourself the trouble. Not worth it at all, does not know what he's doing and assigns a ridiculous amount of work. This class blew my 4.0.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Worst professor ever! Do not take his course, especially if you're just trying to fill a humanities requirement. He graded harshly, only handing out 100s if you went above and beyond the assignment requirements. Will take points off with no justification. Grading scale is crappy, with a 4.0 being a minimum of 94% overall. Group work was constant.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I had professor Ausin for SPN 440. It's not listed here so I wasn't able to choose it, but this professor is awful. The class was online asynchronous but with weekly check-ins. However, Prof Ausin felt so uninvolved and gave terrible feedback. Exams are all oral, and he gives only 18 minutes for 36-question quizzes. I felt set up for failure.

He only teaches in D2L through PowerPoints with audio. They're well made and interactive, but can be confusing sometimes. Any questions can be cleared up in class. There's always a preview quiz before the actual quiz, which was helpful to me. From my perspective with 4 years of Spanish experience, I thought his system worked fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: For SPN310, lectures are online PowerPoints that are prerecorded and you are given four days to view them. There are two recitations on Wednesday and Friday with a TA and quizzes each week on D2l. This class was not bad, but just a lot of work for an intro class with almost no free time. The grading scale is also very tough (4.0=94+, 3.5=88+...)

All of the content from the course was self-taught from a powerpoint. It was very confusing for someone who is not an expert in English grammar. There is a LOT of work outside of class so beware. The exams are around 70 questions in 50 minutes so it's practically impossible. Also the threshold for a 4.0 is a 94%.

He is extremely uninvolved with the class. He does online, recorded lectures that are terrible. This is my 7th year taking Spanish, I received a 4 on the AP Spanish exam, so I already know the topics being taught. In my opinion, they're taught horribly. Along with that, the tests/quizzes set you up for failure with strange, unnecessary specifics.
His recorded lectures are fine, and the synchronous portions are taught by TA's which are good. You do not need the textbook imo, and the class is okay as long as you keep up with the work.

Taking this course online is pretty much impossible because you have to teach everything to yourself. I don't even have a good understanding of English grammar, so I don't know how I'm supposed to teach myself it in Spanish. the final was ridiculously hard with 72 questions in 50 minutes. I felt set up for failure.

Professor Ausin was great! I had him for IAH231C during COVID. He is super clear on his expectations, grading process, and is fair. The class has lots of reading but I wouldn't say it's too much. The material is actually interesting. I would highly recommend this class and professor. One of the better IAH/ISS classes I have taken at MSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Ackerman tries to make class fun. If you care about your grade, show up, and put in the effort outside of class, you will pass. He will never cancel a class, even if the weather is really, really bad.

You genuinely have to put in effort if you want a good grade. If economics is not your strong suit, you might want to go to office hours and the help room to get better. The professor is really nice and helpful, but only if you ask for help. The grade range of a 4.0 is larger than the stereotypical 90-100%, but it can still be challenging.
He makes the class entertaining and interesting, I recommend for EC201/202.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: THE GOAT.🐐LeBron James in the lectures should say it all. He is also the GREATEST 3rd grade girls soccer and basketball coach to never win a game! (Please include me in your syllabus week lecture)
On the first day of class, he will talk about the similarities between himself and Lebron James. This is Ackermann teaching students that he is, in fact, the GOAT.
if you're not a business major, i highly recommend you take this class in person. very difficult concepts that are hard to grasp and the exams are very math-based, which can be a struggle.

I truly do not understand the complaints about Dr. Ackermann or his class. His lectures were entertaining and actually explained the material rather than rushing through it. The tests were very similar to the homework and practice tests, sometimes having identical questions. An 88 is an A and the lowest three homeworks and lowest test are dropped.

Ackermann is a funny and nice guy, clearly loves what he does. His lectures are good, nothing amazing, but the weekly homework assignments are lengthy. His 3 midterm exams and final exam were difficult, but doing the large amounts of practice questions definitely helped. I did bad on the final, and still ended with a 3.5.

Recorded lectures weren't great, most of the time it felt like he was phoning it in. Frequent typos and errors. Wording of questions bad on homework and worse on exams. The only reason I managed to get the grade I did was because I got tutoring twice a week and they were able to basically teach me instead. Also, no notes allowed for exams is insane

Wrong answers on practice assignments. Conflicting info between textbook/Connect/lectures. Connect hw was torture, sometimes you'd answer 100+ questions (2 hrs) for one chapter. Then go do his hw assignment & realize it's different. Tanked the final despite studying for 6 hrs for it bc the wording was confusing (also he was really noisy during it?)

Jeff is funny. The textbook that he assigns sucks though, and asks horrible questions, teaches nothing, costs more than its worth (which should be $0), and finally was broken for a good two months on Firefox. Class was overall worth it and iClicker for attendance only (not graded on correctness) is great. Cutoff for a 4.0 is an 88, not hard.

Don't listen to the negative reviews. He's genuinely a really good professor, his lectures were educational and he posts them all on D2L later. While there is a lot of weekly homework, and the tests are decently hard, he is a fair grader and lets you drop your 3 lowest homework assignments and lowest test. Also you only need a 88% for a 4.0, so...
Don't take, his videos are poor and not helpful. Use practice exams to study. Overall not a good teacher.

I took this course over the summer for a major requirement. About what you can expect from an Econ teacher, however the class wasn't the most boring thing I've ever taken, I just don't have a passion for Econ. Micro was harder than macro in my opinion. Teacher was always available outside of class when i emailed for help.
Not fair, other EC201 get cheatsheets and calculators and online courses with him don't it is so hard to understand.
It is hard to imagine that in our planetary system, there could exist a professor of economics who is both skilled and humorous to such an extent. Always the number 1 choice.
Being a tenure professor goes a long way. Your TA's do all of your work for you while you sit back and watch students struggle!

He was good teacher. He was extremely helpful if you go to office hours. Top hats are included as attendance as completion not accuracy so that was amazing. He was really easy to talk to, fun and helpful. The practice test was almost exactly like the actual test. Make sure that's your main source of study material for 201.

DON'T TAKE MACRO FIRST! THIS WAS A MISTAKE! Ackermann always made the class fun and interesting, making me want to come to class every day. But man, he could NOT teach. He hardly goes over the content, often going on side tangents about family or the news. Be prepared to teach yourself and get yelled at if you email him if you're confused
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very outgoing personality. His classes in-person vs online are basically the same (i took in-person but i have a friend who took it online), i would say his class in-person was easier because participation grade is easy credit (just show up for iclickers). I probably studied a combined 3 hours outside of lecture for the exams and still got 4.0.

His class wasn't difficult per se. However, Professor Ackermann fought my RCPD coordinator on midterm extensions. I had life saving surgery, and only received a two-day extension for the first midterm. The work is definitely manageable, but his schedule is incredibly strict. Also, in-person exams for an online course are brutal. (EC 201 & 202)

This class was extremely difficult. The professor is nice, but doesn't teach well, and I felt like I had to teach myself everything for the exams. The exams were very hard, and there were not many assignments to help balance your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: With little to no choice for an economics class, you will most likely get stuck with Ackermann. If this happens, I hope you are good at teaching yourself the entirety of microeconomics. Even with the video lectures, much is up to interpretation during the exams when you have to study eight different units for a single exam. Would not take again.

not a lot of homework, you watch lecture videos then have a few assignments each week. 4 exams and one is dropped. chill class but it's hard because you basically teach yourself. I've heard he isn't easy to go to for help though I never did. just stay on top of everything since there isn't much to be graded on or turn your grade around.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ackermann is a hilarious guy and tries to keep up with the trends. Although his class is incredibly hard, you can't hate the guy because he is so funny and caring.

Honestly it's a whatever class, I can't claim bias or anything, but like I showed up, 3rd row to front, quiet, attentively. But its like every interaction is lol why do you like hate me. Like I just take it personal sometimes and couldn't help but feel like rip me. Like idk I think he's rude and bald sorry.

Prof. Ackermann was great! I highly recommend taking his classes; he is super chill & funny and teaches great. 4 exams, including the final, with one drop(all MCQ). Not very homework heavy and he usually extends the deadlines. Good Luck!
I found success in this class by completing the homework and attending help rooms. The resources are there for success, highly recommend taking advantage of them!

Typical tenure professor -- recycles the same video lectures, wants you emailing his TA instead of him, etc. Beware that he has a history of changing course cutoffs at the END of the course to make his teaching skills seem more impactful.

i love ackermann he's so silly. i have him online and even though online classes aren't usually ideal for me, i would rather have him online than a different professor in person. the lectures actually make sense, and he provides good resources like fill in the blank notes, along with accessible office hours. everybody loves this man for a reason!

Great guy, very well spoken, lectures are clear and concise. Grading criteria and homework are very simple and clear. If you go to his office hours every so often he is a lot of help. Office hours and practice problems in his classes are the key to an easy 4.0!

One of my favorite professors, was very funny and made lectures fun. Online questions were given during class so make sure to show up for easy points. Homework was pretty easy as long as you had the notes. Exams were easy as long as you actually did the notes and homework. Homework questions were very similar to exam questions.

Ackermann is a very funny, smart guy. I took him online but it seems he knows how to engage his students with his examples and in class questions. Warning: Do Not Buy Textbook. There is no reading for the class and it is very expensive. There's also a good shot that his already generous online grading curve may be lowered again, but still study up.

His online course was not my favorite, so I would suggest taking him in person since I've heard great things about him. The online course just lacked a personal connection which made it easier to get boring. He dropped 3/4 homework and even an exam so that helped my grade since the material can be hard to grasp over videos/slides.

For an online class it was fine. I already took AP Macro in hs but didn't get the credit so I had to take it again. I wouldn't take this class until you take EC201 since most of the first and second units are based off that content as review. Exams were ok. You get an exam drop out of the three exams plus the final so I skipped out on the final.
I didn't like this class, would not recommend it

I liked the class however I will never take an online Econ class ever again, I did not learn anything and I still got a 4.0. Definitely recommend in person lectures if you Wanna learn about your major.

Professor Ackermann was hand-down the funniest professor I've ever had. My top highlight was when he asked an open-ended negative externalities question about the worth thing our roommate has ever done. After submitting my response, my roommate chased me out of class, which ultimately resulted in me being able to finally switch roommates.
It was a good class but the exams were harder, though.

Was entertaining and made lectures more fun. Uses TopHat during class so make sure to show up for easy points. The exams were difficult, but he has a lot of materials including the homework that can help you study for them, and a lot of the practice questions are similar to the actual exam.

His class is test-heavy, and the tests are hard. The average test score is never more than 75%. He is good when he does his lectures, but he is not easy to work with, and, most of the time, won't help you if you need any help. unfortunate for sure.

Ackerman was a funny guy who made lectures pretty fun to be at. He dumbs down economics and makes it easy for non-econ people. tophat is required and so is macmillon achieve. Homework wasnt hard but tests have majority of the weight for your final grade.

Enthusiastic about econ, teaches concepts well and makes them fun. Fill in the blank notes are provided too. Homework took about 20 minutes per week, and that is the only work i did for this class besides attending classes and studying. Exams were a little difficult, but very manageable. You also get drops which helps a ton.

The way he teaches the material is fine, not particularly outstanding. Video lectures were simply old zoom recordings. Worst part is how inconsist the video and sound quality of lectures is. Few were high quality, some were ok, many terrible.

For an A:
1. Ignore Lectures
2. Watch Jacob Clifford Economics
3. Go by each section of the textbook

I had Ackerman for EC 202 online last semester and EC 201 in person this semester. I recommend taking it in person and attending lectures if you struggle with time management in online courses. To succeed on exams you must understand the content you are learning and it is almost impossible to do well by cramming since the study guide is different.

Ackermann is a good prof who knows what he's talking about but you need to be able to learn on your own to be successful in the class. You can't just wing exams but go to the helprooms they're more helpful than anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You can drop 1/4 exams. Study hard and you can get the grade you want. A couple of homework assignments each week and a few hours of video lectures. You can drop 3 homework assignments. Prof was nice and lectures made sense.
Overall a hard class, but help room, lecture videos, and textbook work can help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ackerman is a really cool guy, he cares about his students and wants his students to succeed. He tries to have interesting lectures to keep you entertained and teaches in a very comprehensive way. I am planning on taking his 202 class because of how well he taught the curriculum.

Ackermann acts nice in lecture, but is pretty rude if you try and go to him for help. He explains things in a way that feels belittling, and. I never felt comfortable asking him a question. For homeworks and exams, he writes the questions, and they are not easy. It is hard to study for exams outside of the stuff he gives you. Beware of the tutors

I'm not sure if the course work was just hard to grasp or if it was just hard to learn.There are recorded lectures and then homework assignment(s) due every Wednesday. Exams are pretty similar to the HW. You are only graded on homework and exams.The homeworks are basically quizzes bc you only get one attempt and some of the questions are confusing.
Great professor. Homework and exams are not bad. You can tell he cares a lot about the course.

Good professor. Posts slides online, and multiple prep materials for each exam (questions on prep were extremely similar to exams). Any difficulties I had were from the content, and not the professor. Would recommend for sure.

Terrible. Expect one-word, vague, and unhelpful responses to questions. He is immature, rude, and does not respect his students. It's an unpleasant experience to attend his in-person lectures and encounter him face to face. He cares more about inflating his ego than helping students learn; I recommend taking EC 202 online if he is your professor.

I think that he is a good professor it was just hard to focus on the course since I took it online. The practice problems just weren't like the tests. I also took macro before micro so I don't know if that made a difference. Overall I think he is a good professor you just need to watch the lectures, spread the coursework out, and study.

This class is HARD. I needed it as a prerequisite for my minor and I wish I didn't. It brought down my GPA because you are only graded on quizzes and tests and the tests are extremely difficult compared to the quizzes. Some questions are easy give aways, but then random topics get tossed in and make you fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I took asynchronous EC 202, and I enjoyed it more than in-person, and will be doing 201 online as well. I found the online version very helpful in that you can work at your own pace, have 1 assignment due at the same time every week, and take the tests from your room. The policies are generous and fair, and expectations are laid out.

His lectures were really awesome, he explains problems is very helpful. The textbook is also really great, it follows the lecture almost 1:1 and it has you fill in some information. There are a ton of resources like practice problems with explanations and videos. If you show up, do the practice problems, and review what you missed you will pass.

Do not take this class unless it is your only option. Extremely difficult with no help from either the Prof or TA. I got nothing from this class and it was honestly a waste of time and money. He adjusted the schedule due to the events at MSU but still didn't do as much as other professors.

Very difficult if you aren't interested in economics. Lots of regularly scheduled homework but manageable. There's a workbook that he recommends you buy but I handwrote notes and managed a 3.0. Hardest part of class is motivating yourself to go to a lecture that he makes feel like a high school environment.

reviews.comment: Last economics class I had a lot of trouble getting ahold of the TA. So when a problem arose in this class and it was about an assignment due in a day, I decided to reach out to Jeff directly so I could turn it in on time instead of waiting days for a TA. Jeff responded with a paragraph telling me to contact the TA instead of him with no answer.

You can tell he's passionate, but doesn't do a great job at explaining and tries to be in college again... WELL anyways you probably can't avoid him... so do the homework and try to understand those, as it's the same type of questions on exams. Oh you can also drop one (if you do well enough on the first three). but try to go to class.

Jeff is an awesome professor, but because I did the course online I didn't really have the chance to connect with him. The coursework is honestly kind of difficult, even with the lectures and the homework assignments. Because you can't really ask questions with classmates or the professor, you really struggle to get the concepts.

Professor Ackermann is a seemingly funny and nice guy, but I'd never take his class again. Nobody knows what he's talking about. The clicker questions show that based on the fact that the answers are always all over the place. Often overcomplicates the material to the max, both in class and on exams. I hope he shows this rating to his lectures

This is the only review you really need. The homework and tophat during class take up 40% of your grade. you can drop one test. tests are identical to the homework so review those. funny but could be a little better at explaining. Would recommend. Hard to fail this clas. get 100 on everything youll 4.0 with a E on Exam 3 and can skip the last exam
Do not take Ackermann online if you want to understand the content and actually learn anything.

reviews.comment:
Lectures were fun and he uses TopHat to track attendance
Homework assignments are easy as long as you pay a bit of attention in class 
Tests are just like the homework, if you can review your homework you are almost guaranteed a good grade
Talks a lot in lectures, gets off topic really fast. Do the homework if you want to do well. Exams are heavy, make sure you do well on the first two so you can drop the final exam.

I did ECO 201 online, and at the beginning of the semester Ackermann threw all his notes and powerpoints on D2L, and that was the end of his teaching for the semester. You will be required to learn it all on your own with no lectures or Zoom meetings. Hands down worst professor I have ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The exams were lockdown and the questions were all worded funky. He offered office hours but it was hard to get questoins answered. Might like it more in person

Professor Ackermann is a funny guy but when it comes down to success in this class I think he falls a little short. There are 3 30-question tests, two of which count towards your final grade weighted at 70%. If you're a bad test taker I strongly recommend staying away. He makes lectures somewhat relatable to things that apply in today's world.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Is not very available outside of class, and when you do meet with him he rushes you out of his office. When he describes concepts to you, he just pulls up the slide show.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class overall sucked, the exams were nothing like the practice sheets or the lectures, this teacher is hard to reach, because if you have a question, they will just email back look at the syllabus. Homework is 100% as long as you do it. There is still a good chance you will pass, but not with a great score.

Professor Ackermann is a passionate professor that cares about his job and students. However, he oversimplifies and under-explains material. I felt that I was always lacking the "why." Furthermore, his meta-level approach to economics undercuts the actualities of the world around us.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:

GREAT PROF!

reviews.comment: His class was relatively okay, it was lecture heavy and we had top hat in class participation points but it was just for completion, we had problem sets for each chapter but they arent terrible. 3 exams, and he drops the lowest one, funny prof which made his 9am not terrible

This is the best micro professor at MSU, no doubt about it. Tests are easy if you take the problem sets seriously and do the practice exam. Lectures were engaging and extremely concise, almost zero bloat in the course. Homework outside class was minimal, no more than an hour a week on non-exam weeks.
if you can take econ with any prof choose Ackerman! he explains difficult concepts in such an easy way his lectures are amazing never zoned out the entire semester

Exceptionally nice person, and genuinely tried to get to know the students who made the effort to show up, despite that it was a huge lecture hall. Course wasn't super super easy (he did not pull his punches on the exams) but if you show up to the lectures and take notes you'll be just fine.
good guy, would recommend
loved him!!! very difficult exams, but fair
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

He says the textbook is needed but you really just need access to the online homework. The course is pretty straightforward and as long as you do some practice problems before the exams they end up being pretty easy.
Great professor! Material is not easy but he is a good teacher. Do the practice problems and go to class and you'll do well.

I took an asynchronous class with Ackermann and he was sometimes difficult to communicate with. The circumstances definitely didn't help, but sometimes it didn't seem like he prioritized his online students. The class itself is very homework heavy and is partially graded on correctness. Exams are pretty standard.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Ackermann is a good guy, EC201 and 202 aren't hard and he's really upfront with what you need to know for homework/tests so as long as you keep up with the homework you'll do fine in the class. He makes an effort to be fun and relatable so going to lecture is a good plan too, if you're able.
Never watched any lecture videos and I did fine. Do the online exercises and google what you don't know. Lowest exam is dropped, which is a big bonus.

For all the classes taken at MSU, both Ec 201 and 202 were the best classes I have ever taken. There are a ton of resources that are given within the class and if you put in the effort it will pay off. You'll learn a lot and have a lot of fun doing it. The goodbye song was the best by far and I was always excited to come to class.

He never got back to emails. Very unorganized. There were 3 exams and a final, lowest exam grade drops so if you are ok with your grade before the final, you dont have to take the final. Lectures are not easy to understand.

One of my favorite professors this semester. He may have had heavy lectures, but they were easy to follow. He also gave quite a big amount of hw, but it was manageable. Plus, he understood all our circumstances and a month into the semester, he dropped more assignments, and let us bring cheat sheets into exams. Gives good review packets for exams.

Jeff is a gem. Econ can be very boring but he tries his best, even in the lecture I felt like he cared for me and my grade. He is very good at explaining things, so if you are confused GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS. I wouldn't choose another prof over him.

Some love him, some hate him. I think he has a good personality to match the entry-level content. If his lectures confuse you, look back at the textbook definitions and you'll probably be fine. He stays after class for a few minutes so it is easy to ask questions from the hw and get a deeper explanation.

Easy 4.0 class. Professor Ackermann's lectures were simple and easy to understand. Show up to class because he uses iClicker questions for attendance. Lots of homework but he gives you plenty of time to do it. I would definitely take him again.

Professor Ackermann is a really good choice for EC 201 compared to any other economics teacher at MSU from what I have heard. He makes his lectures very interesting and provides you the right resources to succeed on exams. He posts practice problems that are very reflective of the exams. Homework can be a bit too much but its still manageable.

The midterms will hit hard but it's a manageable grading scale and he was very generous with giving extra credit opportunities at the end of the semester as long as you have put in the work prior in the semester.

Professor Ackermann is a really fun professor, especially for a subject that can be boring. He does give out lots of homework at some points, but it's not very hard and is easy to get done. He's very friendly and wants everyone to pass, so I would absolutely take any of his classes if you can!
A great professor. Keeps class interesting and engaging. Never asks too much and anyone can do well.

Professor Ackermann was one of my only professors that was able to make online learning really interesting. He was always available to help outside of class, but do keep in mind that there are 2000+ students just in macro, and he also teaches micro. If you need to take an econ class be sure to have Ackermann as a professor!

I liked Econ with Prof. Ackermann. I think he explains concepts in a good way and cares about his students. He uses tophat to ensure you're attending class, but they're participation- based so it's a good way to get some free points. I thought the final was a bit difficult, but overall I enjoyed class and would take another class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Ackermann is a really funny and caring professor. He tries his hardest to make his lectures interesting and funny and likes to interact with the class (even online classes). That being said, he gets off topic quite often, making it difficult to follow the lecture. He also does not go into much detail on the topic covered in class. Teach yourself!

Awesome guy. Funny, accessible outside of class, and really wants you to succeed. For a class of 400+ students you really feel like you know him well. Microecon is never fun but so long as you put in the time and use the many resources he makes available, you're alright. He explains tough concepts well and can adjust accordingly. Great professor.

Prof. Ackermann is a good guy but a bad teacher. 2 tests count for 70% of your overall grade. He wants to do his best, but he just isn't a very effective teacher. You have to study his graphs and equations if you want to do good on tests.
He wants everyone to succeed! Great professor, I enjoyed his class because lectures did not feel like classic boring lectures.

Great guy. Down to earth, friendly, very positive and upbeat. Makes lectures fun and engaging. Ties in current events and news while staying apolitical, makes interesting TopHat polls. People complaining about the difficulty are the ones skipping or on their phones. Show up, pay attention, do the work, and you will do well

Professor Ackermann is a nice guy, but very unprofessional. He deviates from lecture way too much and doesn't clearly explain what he's teaching. I recommend reviewing the TopHat questions more than the Connect ones. Also, get a tutor and visit the TA's office hours for real help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I really like him as a person. Tries to be different than other econ profs for 202 because he gives more credit for participation and homework. If you're 1% away from a higher grade, he isn't going to round it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: We can drop one test but honestly his tests aren't like his review guides and its ridiculous. He's a cool teacher but there is so much he could do to improve on teaching including examples, gibing hw that actually helps us learn, improve how he explains.

Class is hard but also a joke. For Fall 2019 the curve on the class was massive because of how bad students were doing. biggest piece of advice for this class is to keep up with practicing the concepts because everything builds on each other and it can get very confusing very quickly. reviews.comment: good teacher.

Dr. Johnson genuinely cared about his students; he would often take time out of class or an assignment to ask us how we were doing. I learned a lot in this class. Great material, a lot of reading, inspirational. His opinions are malleable. He cares about his students and gives us resources to de-stress. highly recommend

Professor Adebiyi really cares about the material he teaches and his passion is noticeable. Participation is very important. LOVE Gana(his nickname). His lectures are filled with passion, and you can tell he cares about these issues. He also WANTS you to get a good grade. He gives you multiple chances on exams, and lots of times to complete assignments (which are also so easy) He's great, Easy A.

He goes off on rants constantly and it is never clear on what he is lecturing about. Hates when people disagree with him. Horrible, avoid if you can.

He was the worst professor I have ever had. If you can avoid this class then save yourself!! The worst grading scale I have ever seen, he absolutely adores group projects with basically no direction or rubric given (it's almost 50% of your grade). Absolutely awful professor, one of the worst I have ever taken. Her lectures online are terrible and they are very unprofessional, she is constantly making mistakes and going on tangents. Horrible teacher, if you end up taking her out by default then use khan academy. They're 100x better at explaining than she ever will.

Not the best teacher, but she gives you all the materials to make yourself succeed if you try.

She was one of my favorite professors by far! She was very straightforward and gave students many chances to meet with her if they needed help. There were no surprises on the exams. As long as you are good at studying she is a great professor to take!

She was a terrible teacher. She only taught from the course pack, which only had fill in the blank sections she'd go over. Comprehension checks helped some, however, the class was all tests (5) and no homework or quizzes. Don't take her if you don't have to, you'd probably do better elsewhere.
Posts lectures online, don't need to go to class to ace the exams which are easy if you go through the notes and the sets of study questions she gives you

This was easily one of my favorite classes because Dr. Denison made the material interesting. Yes, she can be difficult to listen to for 2 hours, but it's easy to see how much she enjoys teaching. Her lectures are posted as videos online so it is basically an online course, but her voice is very hard to listen to for long
Great professor, very enthusiastic and a good teacher. Covers material well. Exams are easy as long as you study the material. Questions are taken almost exactly from study material.

Dr. Denison is one of my favorite instructors so far. She teaches the written objectives and tests on the objectives. If she seems redundant on certain issues, there is a good reason. Highly recommended instructor.
Excellent instructor. Very knowledgeable. Clearly lays out what you need to know and test on the lecture material covered. No surprises.
Very straightforwards class.  No surprises on the tests.

The best professor I've ever had. If you went to class, paid attention, and did the work, the tests reflected the amount of work you put in to learn the material. I was always excited to go to class and wish my other professors were as passionate about their subjects as Denison is about Physiology. If you work hard, it's an easy A!

Dr Denison, Teaches with expectations of someone majoring in Physiology. Her tests are nearly impossible. Grading system is 90% tests and 10 % homework. If your not a good tester you will fail. Her test are very hard. Good luck

This professor genuinely wants his students to succeed. His passion for the material makes lectures engaging, and I found his class to be one of my favorites. I would absolutely recommend this professor to others.

Easily one of my favorite professors at msu. You can tell he really cares about his students and will do everything in his power to help us. Rubrics and study guides are straight forward. Dr. McKim was a wonderful professor. You can tell that he's really passionate about his students and wants all of us to succeed. I would definitely take him in another class, and I recommend others take his class.

An absolutely amazing professor, passionate about what he does and talks to you like peers, rather than students. Such a manageable workload, all exams are open notes. Extremely understanding and easy to reach. Could not recommend more.
This professor was amazing, I absolutely loved his lectures. From this class you learn a lot about communication and how to be a good leader.

Professor McKim is one of the best CSUS professors I have had.  He truly cares about the students and his lectures are incredibly engaging and fun.  I looked forward to going to class and I wish I could take his class again.  There is not a lot of homework and the course is very manageable.

Professor McKim has been one of the best professors I have had at this school. He is so caring and kind to his students. His lectures are fun and engaging and he wants everyone to succeed. I would have him as a professor a million times again.

Literally the best prof I've ever had at MSU, and I'm not even a community sustainability major. He cares for his students, their success, and has the most engaging lectures I've ever had in school. I wish I could take again for him

I LOVED HAVING CLASS WITH THIS MAN!!! He literally made working out fun twice a week, SUCH a nice guy, I have no idea what all these ratings are, literally the kindest guy. He is very kind and supportive, always respecting the boundaries between student and teacher while still looking out for his students' well-being and safety. He is 1st in the world in taekwondo
I absolutely loved this class and Southwick is a great instructor. The class is one that you have to work at, but it's worth it, and he makes it fun. Highly recommended.

I can't believe this is even a for-credit class.  It's more like a social event for instructors, in which they either don't show for class, or, give instruction to lower level belts who are inadequate instructors and simply don't care.
Great Guy!!!

Ron is an excellant instructor, and overall nice guy.  He makes sure everyone understands, and is very considerate of people's different levels of physical ability.  I really enjoyed learning taekwondo with Ron, and will continue in the future.
The best out there!

very funny, very difficult, and very imformative

Ron is a great guy. He's funny, he's engaging in his lectures, and is clearly passionate about his teaching career. However, his exam's are near impossible. Tamborini is one of the sweetest and most caring professors I've ever had. He is knowledgable and passionate about mass communication and his lectures are packed but entertaining. He does talk a lot but the content is interesting and makes it better. LOVES his wife, HATES UMich, and always cracks dad jokes with us.

My fav professor by FAR. sweetest man you will ever meet and an amazing, clear, professor. If you need to take this class and its your only option, do it, but if you have other options, do that.

Worst professor I have ever had. So lecture heavy he doenst post the slides which are from the 1900s btw talks like an ice age character and goes through them so quick without enough time to write everything down. No homework basically your entire grade is based off of exams with the exception of the random in class participation papers. stay away.

Also BEWARE of pop quiz writing exerts at the end of classes to count towards your attendance grade.

He is very nice but he does give out random in class papers throughout the semester and he will have you do his research projects as apart of your grade but there options to get out of it. Also attendance isn't mandatory but the lectures aren't posted at a later time

Hands down one of the most caring professors at MSU. Attendance is taken through random small writing assignments. His slides are not on D2L so attending lecture is important. Tamborini is cool. Simple lectures that are helpful (he tells you what will be on the exam). Just take notes and you'll be set. reviews.comment: Professor Tamborini is really pleasant, and his lectures were very clear and didn't have any useless information. The assignments were really reasonable, and the exams were really doable if you attended lectures and took good notes. I would absolutely take more classes from him.

you HAVE to attend class. attendance isnt graded, but you will find everything very difficult if you skip. the three exams count for 75% of the grade. grading was very lenient. there is a stats section in the final third of the class, beware. had to teach myself all of that.

Very detailed in his lectures.  Explains the why's behind the formulas which helped me learn efficiently.  This is a study-intensive course. Tony Mandarich

Great professor. Very sarcastically funny and helpful when asking questions. I absolutely loved COM 275 with him!

Ron is a very good professor, but if you do not bother to do any work and don't study then you will have a hard time in his classes.

ALEKS is absolutely the worst program, and the professor made the exams so much harder than anything we had to do on ALEKS. I loathed this class and despise Ron Powers

This was the worst course I ever took.  The software, ALEKS, was worse than myspace!  Ron Powers was never available and put all the work onto his TAs.  He made the last few tests really hard to purposely lower our grades.

He has got to be the worst professor ever. He goes extremely fast and doesn't even know what he is talking about himself most of the time. Don't bother asking for help because he will make you feel so small. Most definitely the most rude person.
Rude! I have never met a professor in my four years as rude as this man.  He is unavailable during office hours, and belittles you when you ask for assistance.
It is much easier to just go with the book than try to follow his lectures. And, a great deal of the time, he seems to say "told you so" rather than help you before there is a problem.

I dont know how this man ever got a job as a trig professor because he does not know anything about it. I had to substitute class with a tutoring sessiona and things went better but if you have to rely on his teaching good luck because you will need it

I'm the worst person ever at math, so the class was pretty difficult for me. But, I think that Powers is a pretty good Prof- he is very helpful and he sorta looks like Elton John. Not the worst, not the best.

He needs to actually retire already. He could be my grandpa and it seems like he enjoys teaching but his class was miserable. Hated all my papers no matter how much work I put into them. Forced unnecessary class participation. Not fun to chat with at all. Way too much reading, and the homework had almost no connection to writing sometimes. not good
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor is the best teacher here at James Madison. As one of the founders, he is extremely passionate about teaching, especially freshman, which is hard to come by. Take his course if you want to become a better writer. My papers only improved. I appreciate all the time and effort he put into the course to help the students get the most out it.

Professor Dorr is an eccentric old man that is very passionate about writing which makes the class enjoyable. However, it is very hard to do well in the class due to his extreme pickiness when grading papers. He will humiliate you participating in class but it is worth it. Unless you have PERFECT grammar, don't expect more than a 3.5 in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Great professor, very insightful and wise however he is a VERY tough grader on papers. Make sure you go to office hours and participate in class discussions, although you dont get marked for absences, it will seriously hurt you if you don't show up.

Although once a great professor, in recent years Dorr has been overcome with sentimentality. Inappropriate morality lessons and Bible quotes in class, scattered dry discussion and overall not a lot of progress. Grades based on level brown-nosing done in class, not quality of writing. Overall a major disappointment.

One of the better English professors at James Madison if you are looking to better your writing. He grades tough, and takes no B.S. He expects you to attend most classes and if you do not he will call you out on it. Also make sure you have the readings done because he does active discussions.

Probably one of the hardest profs I've ever had, but he's taught me so much about writing. He's amazingly smart and his classes often run over because we have such good discussions. He grades really tough, but it's worth taking the class.

i knew i would like him. and then i did. it was great. serious, smart, passionate about his work. everything you could hope for. hard grader, which angered those used to grade inflation. earning a b? who has ever heard of such a thing!
No Comments
JMC lost one of the best profs ever with Dorr's retirement. Perhaps, though, he will yet live out his dream of being reincarnated as a Hutterite woman...
No Comments
No Comments
Although Dorr certainly is one smart cookie, his class is only benefical to those who go to office hours regualarly, which I didn't.
very hard, but an amazing prof

Prof. Madrigal is a good professor, it's just he pushes you to be a better writer. He's very relaxed with due dates and often gives us more time to turn writing assignments in. He usually holds office hours after class if you want him to peer review/edit your paper. He often gives really good feedback which has helped me become a better writer.

Took over a class originally taught by another teacher- so not much to say about his class layout. He's extremely socially awkward and expect to cringe at least 5 times every class. Gives horrible feedback (copy & paste on multiple docs) and talks about nothing all the time. Not a hard class just horribly unenjoyable

Hands down one of the best professors I have had so far. The lectures teach you a lot about writing at the college level if you pay attention and participate. Will help you to succeed indefinitely whether it's in class or outside of class in his office hours. Professor Madrigal is, in my opinion, a gifted writer and teacher.

Pros: Cool guy, very relaxed, and works with you whenever you need help and tell him. This man straight up does not teach, he just talks about random things during lectures. So easy. And I got no less than an 88 on all of my papers. Cons: He doesnt give feedback when grading, just good grades. Relies heavily on peer review. Such boring lectures.

This prof is an easy 4.0. Even though he talks in circles sometimes and the lecture seems pointless sometimes, you have to go. You can just sit on your laptop all lecture, (got a lot of outside hw done). Initially every assignment is confusing, but he is good at explaining what he's looking for, so they're all super doable. Easy 4.0 & honors credit
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Boring lecture but learned a lot and not too difficult. Fair grader and only textbook needed was like 10$. Papers weren't difficult and not many to do.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Enjoys writing, but does not share very many tips on account of how to improve your own work. Fairly easy to do well in here, but the content of the class is not interesting. The professor himself is very genuine and friendly. I would recommend him to others.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Madrigal is very intelligent and knows how to write very well. He gives you a very long time to do each project and is not too strict about due dates but do not take advantage of that. Sometimes he will say things that do not exactly make sense and use big words but as long as you write how he speaks and writes, you will be great.
He is a grade C intellectual, and too unintelligent to follow basic argument. A very nice man, and not a brutal grader, but really should not be a doctor.

The class is two hours long and they are so boring. He rambles about nothing the whole class and then assigns a paper. He's a pretty easy grader and he's easy to talk to. He's really lenient, if you ask for an extended deadline, he'll give it to you. He checks attendance.

The class is easy, but he talks in circles. The lectures are pointless, so you can just do homework for other classes. He is a huge pushover and will push back assignments if you ask. Overall, a very easy class, and a pretty respectable prof.

MC 111 with Professor Ahlquist is amazing! The class focuses on writing about conservation and the environment. His passion makes discussions engaging, and he values participation, so speak up! If you care about the topic, you'll love it. His feedback is thoughtful, pushing you to grow as a writer. Highly recommend for anyone interested!

Ahlquist is an amazing person and very, very nice professor. He is very into expanding native rights, and is generally against the use of technology to address social issues like climate change. if you disagree with him on both those, you should think twice. As someone who disagrees with him on those though, he is still a great professor

I'm so glad I took this class. It was my favorite in my first semester of JMC. He really did a lot of work to make his classroom a community and a safe space for all his students. Discussion matters, and participation matters, but the topics are so interesting that it was easy! Lots of reading, but it's mainly online articles. HAVE to read them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: I had him for MC111 this Fall semester. Super smart and caring, will help you throughout the course. It's a hard transition going into JMC, but he brightens the whole atmosphere. He creates a good environment where you can have fun, insert your opinion, ask questions, and learn. I highly recommend him for any course you choose to take.

Professor Ahlquist is the best professor I have ever met. I took MC111 with him last semester, he has been such an inspiring and caring teacher. I would not say this class is easy, BUT, if you really put in effort, you are ready to get a good grade. Make sure to go to his office hours for extra comments! recommend this class to all JMC people!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took MC111 with Ahlquist and definitely came away a better writer! He is very understanding when it comes to personal issues and is clear with his expectations for class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors! The content and discussions are very engaging. You are graded on participating and are allowed limited absences. There are a few small writing assignments and two papers. He has high writing expectations and does not grade easy. Overall, he cares a lot about his students and will be willing to help you.

Professor Ahlquist has a way of brightening the classroom, whether in-person or online. Each day he was equal parts personable and intelligent, his anecdotes about each reading made the mountains of text legible and worth tackling each class. By the end, you'll walk out with more than a polished writing style; you'll find a friend in Ahlquist.

Professor Ahlquist is my favorite professor by far! One of the most caring and genuine people in the world. He sparks an interest for any topic we're discussing and makes you excited to come to class. He is all about establishing connections and making sure that every student feels welcomed and comfortable with him and fellow classmates. Love him!

Professor Ahlquist is the best Professor I have ever had. He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He makes learning easy, not like an easy A (you have to work very hard) but in the way where he ignites a spark within you that you didnt know existed. His feedback is very helpful and he is always available to help.
I love Prof Ahlquist! He is an amazing guy! he's very passionate about his field of study and students! I Will take in again sometime in the future,
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This was my second time having Professor Ahmed and once again, I enjoyed him very much. Hes such a kind and generous professor with so much love for his students and his work. I really appreciate him and I hope to have more classes with him in the future. Hes an undeniable asset to the Department of Romance & Classical Studies.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Ahmed is a wonderful professor. He puts his heart and soul in his teaching and is extremely passionate about the French language. He also seems to be particularly interested in classic French literature. He is so kind, caring, flexibl. I wish that more college professors were like him. You're bery fortunate to have him.

He is insanely helpful and gives great feedback and you can definitely tell he wants you to succeed. It is a hard class for those French does not come easily to, so you'll have to put in effort. Manageable homework, short readings. Lots of quizzes/exams and a few papers. Participation is very important. You'll gain a great knowledge base in this.

Its an online course so you have to participate online. When not understanding the professor is easy to email and responds quickly. His lectures were good and the reading posted was a lot, but the course was easy to manage. The final exam was easy, I only used to DSM and the clinical cases books.

This guy is a great teacher, engaging, reasonable and empathetic.  Brian genuinely cares about the students and is sincere, but expects you to work.  He makes a difficult topic look easy.  I really may not have made it with a different professor.  Highly recommend!
He is not good at giving clear directions in class.  Read and follow the course syllabus--he treats it like a contract!

Dr. Ahmedani is a great research methods instructor. This is generally a really hard course but he made it quite a bit easier. Now having said that, it's still alot of work. Just isnt as bad as it could be. Just be warned, DO NOT CHEAT. He is vigilant and will bust you (at least thats what he says).

This professor teaches a very difficult research methods class.  The class itself is a lot of work, but Prof. Ahmedani has a great deal of experience and shares this with the class, which livens things up.  He is very funny and jokes a lot.  He's often willing to help students.  He's also (easily) the hottest professor I've ever had in college.

VERY hard subject. While it gets easier to comprehend the various topics and understand the terminology towards the end, there isn't often enough time to write everything down during the test that they are looking for. She can also be a little nit-picky on the tests when it's hard to understand what the question is asking for.

Awesome teacher! Funny and interesting--often supplements her powerpoints with videos and fun facts. Only teaches practical things you will need to know. Involves the class during her lectures with discussion and questions. A massive amount of info to learn in this class but she helps make it enjoyable and easier to remember.

She was the perfect anatomy lab professor. Provided lots of visuals and hands-on specimens. Tried to make everything as clear as possible and genuinely wanted us to succeed. As long as you study her lectures and your notes, you will do great on the tests. Only problem was that there were only 2 tests so the grade weight on each was very high.

I've never hated my life more than when I took this class. I stopped going to lectures half way through semester because it was a waste of time since my math skills were actually regressing when he taught; Instead, I taught myself the topics through Youtube videos. I paid for this class yet I'm the one teaching. Don't take if you want to live.

I've never cried or called my mom for anything this much before this. I stopped going to lectures because I learned more from someone else teaching me than the professor. I was starting to think that I was the issue but I shouldn't have to pray that I get hit by a CATA bus on the way to my exams. If you're not religious, find one & start praying.
Took confusing notes and gave us practice quizzes that had many things not on the exams. Takes attendance each class. Taught very slow though which made it easier to understand.

His handwriting is extremely sloppy, students have ask what he wrote on the slide. Lectures are confusing, on top of his extremely thick accent. Very unorganized, answers questions incorrectly, and doesn't understand the questions students ask him. He often gives no help for the question that was asked by the student due to misunderstanding them.

Could not be more confusing. Horrible hand writing, extremely thick accent, constantly gives the wrong answer and then has to be corrected by students, super unclear communication. No real explanation ever, simply fills in the notes and then tests you on said notes the NEXT class. Don't take this class unless it is literally your only option.

So confusing and disorienting. Professor has messy writing and a very thick accent. Does not keep a cohesive schedule whatsoever. You walk in class, take notes, and take a test on the notes you took the class BEFORE. No time to study whatsoever.Even told me and my entire class we had a big exam the NIGHT BEFORE. 0 out of 1,000. Could not be worse.

MSU did nothing to retain him. He's the most loved professor I met at MSU--and I'm a senior. See Shastri fosters classroom communities with real care. Not easy to take over, I get it, but the profs taking over did try. Its the management's fault. They don't care we lost a gem of a prof

Such a nice and amazing person. He really cares bout his students and fosters and kind and nurturing environment. As long as you show up, participate, and do the work, you will have a wonderful time and grow so much as a writer.

He's really sweet! His grading for his Creative Fiction Writing class is just making sure you complete assignments on time, and making sure you participate in class. The class's workload is probably 3/5, so not too much or too little. He's also an enthusiastic professor, and willing to work with you to meet your needs.

Shastri is so sweet. Big fan of him. Intro to Creative Writing was very much that, an introduction where you explore different forms of creative writing. His grading scale is pretty clear and as long as you actively participate and give feedback during class, you should be fine. Feedback has a focus on positive aspects as it is an intro class.

Don't go near him if you're gonna take this course. Daily 30-50 pg readings that will be on the final. Pop quizzes with a 10 min time limit. Doesnt let you see your grade until you have taken the final, meaning you have to email him to see your grade. Lectures are only pictures, so notes are based on what he's saying or notes on the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a genius and very passionate about what he teaches. Not a tough grader, but you're going to have to do some research and reading. The material is pretty interesting so it's not too bad. One of my favorite professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof is very passionate, but grade is entirely based on weekly essays, participation, and a 8-10 page final that is 40% of your grade. If you miss lecture you miss all of the material, but all the essays are based on the 30+ page articles you have to read 2x a week. Class is very interesting, but very stressful and difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr Cornelius is fun, but his class is very hard. If you see him teaching this class and Jack the Ripper & Victorian England, this class is not about that. This class is on African Traditional Religion and Warfare & the final is 40% of your grade. The concepts are very abstract and hard to grasp. Fun teacher, but try your luck elsewhere
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Mr. Cornelius was the absolute BEST TA I have ever had. He is very inspirational, energetic, and cares about all of his students. I can not recommend any class/section with him enough. You will not regret it at all.

Literally an awful professor. Never knew the answers to any question I asked. The assignments were so confusing because he never explained them. He also didn't know how to work the online D2L system. 0/10 DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASSES.
He was very bad and didn't know how to use D2L to put assignments in. Never responds to emails and doesn't have office hours. Good luck if you get stuck with him.
Doesn't know how to work D2L. Won't email you back at all. Sucks at communicating about literally anything.

ASIANLAN426 (Advanced Spoken Japanese), Imamura is the only teacher of the class and it is organized very poorly. The homework has an insane amount of typos and when it comes to preparing speeches, there are no examples and explanations are not clear. Her "feedback" is extremely blunt and rude, and sometimes just downright hurtful.

Imamura sensei is a wonderful teacher! She really cares about how you're doing in class and helps you as much as she can. Even though the class is a lot of work, if you're able to attend everyday and keep up with the content, it will be pretty easy.

Imamura Sensei was a great professor, definitely recommend taking her class! She rly cares abt her students. You have hw and class every day, so make sure that your other classes aren't too time-consuming- languages requires consistency and time. However, it was such a rewarding & fun class, I also loved getting to know my classmates.

She does give a lot of homework, but that's expected of a class with a language as difficult as Japanese. If you do have mistakes, she will ask you to resubmit a new corrected version of the assignment, but it's all for your own benefit. She's a great teacher and everyone in the class really seemed to enjoy having her as a teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Overall great teacher that does everything you can ask for from a uni level language professor. Very clear with her expectation and grading, takes her time and fully explains everything very well. Clear deadlines, goals, and instructions the entire course. 100% would recommend

GEO221 online. He was great! Very responsive outside of class (online course) via email, and the labs were very easy to follow. Some may say there's a lot of labs/assignments (I personally didn't think so), but there's no exams, and as long as you set a decent amount of time between beginning the assignment and the deadline, you'll be alright.
His class is a lot of work, but he makes the instructions very clear and you will receive a good grade as long as you follow them. Not a difficult grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Inaccessible in terms of help and assigns loads of assignments.

He is super sweet and checks in with us to make sure we are all okay and to remind us of due dates in our GroupMe. There are about four papers that we had to do (not very long), and there is about 20 pages of reading per week with a weekly quiz. Overall, a great professor who cares about his students and the information at hand.
Honor section is more difficult compared to other sections.
You have to study lectures before class. Useful material.
dont take.
Would give a 0 if possible. Avoid this TA if you can help it.
