literally the worst teacher I've ever had. the dude has existential crises in class and doesn't teach anything helpful, and didn't even know when our midterm was. there's maybe two people in the class that actually know what's going on. DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH HIM.

This class is 60% exams, and there is no homework, your entire grade is based on your exams, attendance, and class participation. The class uses tophat, and participation is graded on accuracy. So basically, you need to do well on the exams. The exams are really hard, poorly worded, answers have like 6 options. For example: A, B, C, D, A+C, B+D.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is hard but manageable. Professor Johnson is very nice and helpful. I went to his office hours once, and he helped walk me through what I didn't know and told me what would be on the exam. The book was also not necessary, but helpful. I don't think attendance is mandatory, but if you skipped the lecture, you would probably fall behind.
Really interesting class very science heavy and the tests have a lot of small details that made it very hard to do well on them but I thought it was very interesting.

If you went to class and reviewed the lectures and asked questions you will do well. His lectures were very interesting and he was very thorough with the harder to understand concepts. Overall, it was a great class and I recommend.

Required lecture attendance, graded TopHat (accuracy), and some homework assignments. 4 midterms and the final, lowest score is dropped, so you could skip final. The instructor sometimes explains concepts in a confusing way and occasionally goes off on tangents, but he is very kind and always willing to answer questions. I wouldn't buy textbook.

Previous reviews on this class scared me. While this class was somewhat hard, the prof truly cares about his students succeeding, & lectures are very interesting. You will need to genuinely study for his exams in advance and 10% of the questions are based on niche things he mentions once, the rest is straightforward imo as long as you study well.

I struggled a little with some of the concepts in the class and had to study for this more than I was used to. The lectures are information heavy but he is a good teacher and you definitely want to come to class otherwise you're screwed. Drops lowest exam so you can skip the final and gives extra credit if needed based on test scores.

class is very interesting but its a lot of material covered in a short amount of time. tests are more difficult and almost feels like no amount of studying could get you an 100, but workload is very manageable. dont buy the textbook, you can study without it. very good class but VERY science focused.

Personally, I didn't like the course material but Dr. Johnson was super helpful and knowledgeable. The tests are tricky, but you do get to drop the lowest score which is always nice. He's clearly passionate about his work and his job, which I liked.

DON'T BUY THE TEXTBOOK. It's not needed ever- the prof is super passionate about what he's teaching, and you'll learn a lot by listening, asking questions, and being in class (required!!). Study for the tests by doing the Learn mode- there's a few on quizlet and knowt! Chem and bio background is good to have but not required.

I with a 4.0 and didn't need to take the final. There are 4 midterms throughout semester so it feels like a lot of content but the study guides are very helpful and there are a few options for extra credit. Attendance is mandatory so make sure you attend lectures. There is barely any homework and he gives you a lot of time to do it.
Attendance knocked my grade down pretty bad, but overall good course. Just make sure you go to lecture.

There are 5 exams for this class, so it definitely involves a lot of studying. I will say I did find his exams to be pretty difficult. He does genuinely want the class to succeed, though, so putting in the work is worth it. You can drop one exam, and he did give extra credit opportunities at the very end of the semester.

He offers a lot of extra credit which boosts the grade a lot, but the tests are very tricky and you have to know the material inside and out to do well. Also, attend the study sessions, they are the thing that helps the most with the tests.

he wasn't a bad professor per se, but it's super lectures and tests heavy. there are four exams, and he would send out study guides, but i swear the tests were so different from the study guide (i might also just be a terrible test taker so idk). it's a boring class tbh and i wouldn't recommend it if u can take something else

This has been one of my most challenging classes thus far. However, I would like to emphasize that Prof Johnson is a really fantastic guy and professor. His exams are incredibly difficult, but he has given us extra opportunities to boost our grades if we are struggling. This class is fascinating and I recommend it if you're up for a challenge!

He recommends to buy a textbook, but you don't really need it unless you want to make anotations to make studying easier. He is very passionate with lectures and encourages to ask questions. Overall very helpful and prepares you for up and coming exams

Professor Johnson is an amazing and understanding guy. Exams are very hard, however. If you miss any lectures you're out of luck, there is no free absences, and it is 5 points per class. Don't buy the book. Gave us another extra credit opportunity because of low class average which was nice. Do not recommend for first semester freshmen.

The class is very interesting, but his exams were very difficult. 60% of your grade comes from exams, and there is a cumulative final. His exams are worded poorly, and made it difficult to do well even if you know the material. Great class, but poorly taught.

The exams for PSY 209 were VERY hard, and there was a total of 5, but you got to drop one, so that was nice. This class is very lecture-heavy, so make sure you are ready to take a lot of notes. The syllabus says that the textbook is required, but I did not use it once, so I don't think you need it.

This class was somewhat difficult, the tests kind of felt like they were to set you up for failure. Professor Johnson was really nice and his lectures were good as long as you actually pay attention. Make sure you really know the specfics

Certified yapper who talks nonsense for half the class. Wording was always so confusing on his exams. His TA was not helpful whatsoever. Not a very fun class at all, not a very good teacher, and really likes to test his students...

well he's a yapper, he talks and rambles a lot in class, his first exam in this class didn't go too well so he adjusted the syllabus so one of 5 exams (yes 5), gets dropped, they are also in-person on paper now, no longer online like previous years.

Professor Johnson is a really good psych teacher, but will go on tangents a lot. Its basically like AP psychology just a little more in depth on the biological parts. Although the book is "required", you can get away without reading it. Tests were all online which was really helpful, but attendance to lectures counts for points.

Class is science-heavy (it's in the name) so it would be good to have some general knowledge. All assignments and exams are online + he cancels lectures on exam days. Grading was decent, sometimes he was not clear on what he was looking for on assignments. Overall, he's a good professor but sometimes gets off-topic in classes.

Gives amazing lectures, but I def recommend downloading the slides before class & just writing what he says directly on the slide; it's so much easier and a lot of what he discusses are on the exams. If you do that (and pay attention obv), you're golden! 4 exams, 1 final, 7 activities (short answer to smt he discussed in class, very easy) 1 is EC.

He was a great lecturer. Really passionate about the subject and VERY happy to answer any question. The class was basically a neuroscience class, so be aware of that, but if you have a general bio background you should be alright. Test heavy, but they are on D2L so not a ton of pressure. Highly recommend for neuro majors

He is a nice guy, but it takes forever to get through lectures, and sometimes we have to rush through them towards the end to fit them in our unit exams. 5 exams and attendance is required. He cares about students' questions to materials and is open to new ideas.

I really enjoyed this class. He is easygoing and super smart. He has an answer to basically any question you ask regarding the material. This class was pretty simple if you enjoy psychology and neuroscience. None of the topics were too complicated and all of the assignments were easy. He isn't a hard grader and exams weren't the most difficult.
Professor Johnson was amazing you could tell he loved what he was lecturing on and was very knowledgeable on the topics. Loved his class.

Johnson is unnecessarily difficult. Definitely some of the hardest exams Ive taken. His wording on the exams is confusing as well. He should be teaching a 300-400 level class. He is super strict while grading. Johnson will find ways to stress you out. Also, he puts an exam a week before the final exam so thats cool.

Such a nice guy answers all the questions in the lectures. Some days can seem rushed, especially before exams. Exams are heavily based on the sides, but he posts the afterwards on d2l, but he gives so much more information on class. The book is helpful, but if you don't have a good background in chemistry and biology, good luck.

PSY 333 With Professor Johnson was an interesting class, that I enjoyed for the most part. Beware- his exams are some of the most challenging exams I have ever taken. He words questions in a very confusing way and uses medical terminology that he hasn't taught us. He was pretty flexible with exam and due dates and would always answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extra Credit is only announced in class, and you're told specifically what to do. Lectures are very interesting, looked forward to class every other morning. Didn't use the book as much as I thought I would, so I don't think it's really mandatory, but it helps if you're having trouble. He's so nice, makes dad jokes, and takes any and all questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Graded on 3/4 exams and 6 random in class assignments. No extra credit. Super nice guy and very interesting lectures but graded on so little. I personally didnt do the best in the class bc I didnt study as much as I should have.

It was such a fun class! I didnt read the book at all pretty much and still got a 4.0. However, he does test on really hard topics so if you dont have background knowledge about biology, you should read the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took PSY 209 in the fall, and Dr. Johnson taught me a lot. He brought his dog, Mitch, to class once. Sometimes came late to class and seemed frazzled. Come to class because he gives sparse powerpoints and elaborates on the concepts. You get to drop your lowest exam. His graduate assistant, Ben Fry was at times more helpful than him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is really hard. Especially for a lower class. He does random participation points (6 ) and there only worth like 2% of your overall grade. And he grades harshly on those too. The exams are hard as heck, there based off of the book, the slides, and what he says in class, he does drop one in the end. The final exam was the worst exam ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: His exams (psy209) are SO difficult and 1/6 of the questions are over things that he doesnt teach or even mention. Your grade is 925 points for exams and 60 for participating. You get to drop an exam at the end. Definitely a class you want to have good chem and bio background in. 209 being a low number is deceiving. Extremely difficult class

Listen. I really wanted to like this class. But this guy. He is nice and answers lots of questions but the lecture material sucks. Not much cooler than your run of the mill psych 101 class, just harder. All your graded on is test and random pop quizzes. Do not recommend

Lectures fairly fast paced through out the whole class period, but freely answers any questions through out. No need to get the book, all exams are lecture based. Definitely my favorite most interesting class, would recommend to any Psych or Neuroscience major!
reviews.rating_tags: LECTURE HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Johnson's lectures were definitely interesting. He does talk fast, but he answers any questions and clarifies anything that his students need. He drops one exam, and if you study the powerpoints and go to class you should do well on them. Overall a good professor.

One of the toughest courses I have ever taken.. just took this class to fulfill a B.S. in Psych requirement & it was not easy. Your grade is solely based off of 5 exams (one gets dropped in the end) & 5 in class assignments (have to attend lecture because you don't know when he will assign one). Tests for me were very difficult.

Dr. Johnson's lectures are great but move a bit fast. He posts the lectures online though so not a big deal. If you study the powerpoints you'll do fine on the tests. There are random class assignments sometimes that are easy but it means that you have to go to class in case theres an assignment. He ended up dropping the lowest test grade too

If you go to class and put in the effort to study, you'll be fine in this class. He asks some questions on exams that aren't in the notes & will just be things he said out loud in class. This is an interesting class and Dr. Johnson talks kind of fast but is always happy to answer any questions anybody has. It's really about the effort you put in.

I think the professor talks too fast, his power points have 2 words per slide on them, his exam review study guides are ridiculously long, and its unclear what specifically he is asking.  The professor does let you drop one of the 5 exams, including the final which is nice.  But you never know when there will be an in class quiz/discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Alexandria is an awesome dance professor! She cares so much for her students and makes class like a fun workout! Totally recommend! I will keep taking her classes!

Alexandra is a kind person who is very passionate. But from a dancer perspective I feel I didn't learn much from what I thought the class was going to be. Along with that many things we did in class and talked about made me uncomfortable. If you are a dancer and wanting to dance I don't recommend

I love Alexandria! I am not a dancer by nature but I had a great time in her class. She really cares about your progress and is super understanding. I think I've really improved because of her. I would highly recommend her class

Professor Alan is an all-around good guy, and I genuinely enjoyed waking up and going to his class. While the tests can be challenging sometimes, if you do the proper studying beforehand, then you should be well prepared. Always in a good mood and made learning interesting, relevant, and fun. Would highly recommend him to anyone.
Best professor I have had at MSU so far

Very nice and chill but the class is literally three exams that are mostly on the insane amount of readings he gives you. If these were assignments it might have been easier but if you do bad on one test you're cooked.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's okay, seems like a good guy, but the way he teaches is just droning on and on, as well as going off topic often. This class is graded mostly by exams (75%), which makes it especially irritating when he doesn't fully cover some topics in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy, but his lectures often bored me but it would be amazing for someone really interested in geography, he knows what he's talking about. Grade is based on 3 exams and attendance, and 10 extra points if you visit his office hours. No textbook required and attendance is mandatory.

There are 3 tests throughout the course which are the only assignments in the class. The class is super lecture heavy, but the professor goes off on tangents that aren't relevant a lot so it's important you pay attention because his slides also don't give you a lot of information. He's a great person though and super nice and do the class readings!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Love this professor as a person, however his class is literally graded on 3 exams and attendance. His exams aren't overly difficult but if you make one too many mistakes it can easily jeopardize your grade.

By far my favorite teacher at MSU! He is so excited to teach each class, which makes it enjoyable. The only issue I have with him is that there is no study guide, and the grade is based on 3 tests. This caused me to get a lower grade than I wanted because the exams were so random. I learned a lot and genuinely loved coming to that class every day.

Very very hard course for an ISS 200 level. He's an interactive and nice Prof. I would save yourself the trouble and take a different course. Way too hard to be a 200 level. You have zero assignments, class is based off 3 exams (including the final.) The exams can be tricky and require lots of studying. You must attend every class! No curve either!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: by far my favorite professor. I was really sad to hear he is retiring, but it is well deserved. He has been at it for a long time. He really did make learning more enjoyable. Thank you, Dr. A.
He was a good professor just talked a lot and if you aren't interested in his subject you won't like his class. He can be fun and I like him as a person just wasn't a huge fan of his class

Alan is bound to be one of your favorite professors during your time at MSU. He is full of life stories and makes the lectures fun. As for the way he has his course set up, your grade is based off of 3 exams so if you mess up on one of the exams, your grade is going to be iffy.

Dr. Arbogast is such a dad, in the best way possible. Content of the lectures were boring (if you're not into geography) but Dr. Arbogast made it 10x better. You're only graded on 3 exams and then attendance, but they're all easy as long as you take notes. Overall, Dr. Arbogast is a silly guy and his class is pretty easy.

I really enjoyed his class. He was very engaging and didn't take the GenEd too seriously, like I think many other professors who teach them do. He seemed to really care about his students and gave credit just for coming to talk with him at office hours. I also felt like the things he taught were actually worth learning.

There are many other easy ISS classes, good guy. Only three exams, no assignments. So if you do poorly on one, you fail. He does not know how to teach because he yaps the whole two hours. People leave in the middle of his lecture because he goes off topic.I had to teach myself everything, and his lecture slides are only pictures.TAKE A EASIER CLASS

Super nice guy and loves what he does. The course is basically geo and the concept are hard to connect as the course bounces all over. Only 3 exams so it everything he says matter. Lots of relevant content but class seemed to drag on quite a bit
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Arbogast is a girl dad to the core. He made the course so much fun and while blunt at times he was incredibly kind. He was very understanding about my test anxiety, and was overall very supportive. His class is lecture heavy and his slides are mainly pictures. So every word counts as anything he says is fair game for exams! 10/10 class!

only 3 exams. class was hard to connect but lots of real life examples that were relevant. be sure to do the outside reading as they are on the exams. you can tell he loves to teach but class can at times drag on

I loved this class and I loved Dr Arbogast! He made lectures super engaging, and he's really funny! You can also tell that he loves what he's teaching! The tests can be kind of tricky but overall not too bad! Just make sure you do the homework and show up to class for the points! If you have the chance to take a class with him I highly recommend!

He is a great guy but the class is doing to much to be a uni req. only three exams but they make up the entire grade so if you do poorly on one you are screwed. Also wasnt aware that it would be turned into a geo course when it was just labled as Big ideas iss.

Dr. Arbogast was pretty laid back, and easy to follow! His lectures were very straight forward and he used a lot of real world examples to reinforce the content he was teaching. Pretty easy as long as you show up to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This man is an absolute diva. I love him, he said the funniest things, I was always giggling. I highly recommend him he's a king and he's amazing.

This man is incredible. Never stops talking about his wife or his daughters, we love a girl dad. He gives his lectures with a good mix of actual knowledge and his personal life experiences. If you don't appreciate a woke professor, he's probably not for you, but I appreciated it. Love you Alan, keep up the good work king!

ISS205 is mainly a prerequisite, and the median grade across every professor for this course is a 4. However, he attempts to be different and unique by making this class harder than every other ISS. He believes a small percentage deserves a 4 even if everyone does well. This makes it completely unfair for his students compared to other professors

Arbogast was my favorite professor this semester! His lectures were really interesting, and he gave out study guides before each exam which were very helpful. He's very easy to talk to and understanding. If you attend lecture + pay attention and do the readings, an A is very possible.
Love this class! His lectures are engaging and really interesting to listen to

ISS 205 is mainly a prerequisite that students take, he makes it way to difficult and it is definitely not Big Ideas in Social Science. It should just be called current events and geography. He brings up current events and then gives his very liberal opinion on it attempting to brainwash other students.
Alan Arbogast is the man.

Really like the guy and his lectures, but I feel like he should make the lecture material actually available to the students instead of penalizing them for not retaining every word of what he says. His slides are basically just pictures, and are hard to make sense of after the class. His exams were fairly tough, but easy enough to get atleast an 80
He has good energy when giving lectures but the class just seems off. Should have just called it geology. He also loves brining up current events and giving his very liberal opinion on the situation.

I enjoyed this class a lot, especially gaining more knowledge about Michigan history as well as what is going on in other countries. I know that I would sometimes come late, but that didn't affect my learning, but I found that the exams were tough even though I would study in advance. Overall, great class and had a great semester with you!

Professor Arbogast is THE best professor I will ever have. His exams are hard and very outside-of-class video-heavy, but his lectures are entertaining if you interact. His wife is a mental health therapist, and it shows. A girl dad who loves what he's doing and is passionate about what he is teaching: if you can take a class with him, YOU MUST.

Professor Arbogast was really good at making class interesting and keeping the energy up.  He was a really fair grader, and would correct test answers if they were confusing and a lot of us got them wrong, blaming himself instead of students.

There's a decent amount of reading involved, but honestly you could probably get yourself to a 3.0 just by showing up and paying attention in class. Dr. A knows his stuff and is more than willing to answer questions for as long as necessary for the class's understanding. Great dude who really cares about his students!

Dr. A is one of the best professors i have had. He really cares about his students and his lectures are very engaging. Its easy to get an A in his class if you just listen in class and watch the videos or articles he posts for before class. He used top hat in my class and had 5 pop quizzes and took attendance but it wasn't daily.

Amazing professor, and definitely cares about his students. Grades very clear - 5 of 6 quizzes, 10 of 12 attendance dates. Very much girl-dad energy. Makes class fun, and enjoys what he's teaching. Would absolutely take again.

I took 206 online. There were no video lectures like in my other online classes. The lectures were made up of pages of reading. There was also a textbook to read from. Very reading heavy. Grade is made up of 14 quizzes (16 quizzes but 2 are dropped), 3 papers (pretty easy), and a final exam. The quizzes were tricky but open note and timed.

Online class taught entirely by the TA. Never communicated with Arbogast at all. Class was fairly easy. A few HW assignments and the exams were easy IF you read his notes. I briefly skimmed the notes, then copied and pasted all of his notes into a word document and used the search tool to look for relevant words. I 3.5 the class.
LOVE HIM! Very interesting, very enthusiastic, a bit difficult but totally worth it.
Great Teaching Style and Clarity. Course is relevant to current events and a must for anyone interested in understanding the interconnectedness of our planet.

I had him in sp. '96 and still remember how great he was. The class was very interesting.   I almost switched majors because of him and his class.  Also, very helpful during office hours.  Would highly, highly recommend.  (I only knew the course # because I kept the book (5th ed.) and the info is on the SBS sticker - that's how much I liked it!)
great teacher!
Very interesting! His tests are tricky but class is great.

This class is so easy. One assignment a week. Attendance is mandatory but it's only worth five points of your overall grade so you're fine if you don't go. Exams and quizzes use lockdown browser but she moved every one to taking it remote so it didn't matter. Easy ISS to 4.0.

Her class is not difficult in the slightest, with quizzes and exams being open-note.

Assignments are straightforward. 

She has a midterm which covers the first textbook and a final that covers the second; her final is not cumulative.

Unfortunately, her lectures are not all that interesting. I often found myself confused in certain sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bryant has been my favorite professor at MSU so far. I took her class to meet a school requirement but found myself actually interested in her lectures and the material. The textbook is free and though attendance is mandatory, she is very understanding. She wants you to do well!

Super nice professor who cares about the material she's teaching and cares about students. Very straight forward and easy class. Every quiz question was bar for bar from the combined lecture notes SHE would provide and let you print and take to the quiz. Not possible to fail. Also canceled class or finished early many times. 10/10

She is one of my favorite professors at MSU. She genuinely is passionate about the material she teaches and that reflects in her lectures. She also cares about her students and wants them to succeed. The quizzes and exams are open note, so you can actually focus on learning the material during class rather than memorizing. Take this class!!
TAKE THIS CLASS FOR UR ISS REQUIREMENT. SHES SO CUTE I LOVE HER AND CLASS WAS SO EASY AND SHE IS VERY CHILL AND TEXTBOOK IS FREE!
Amazing professor and very passionate about teaching. She somehow made every lecture interesting. 100% would take again
super sweet!! i loved the class its easy and workload is not heavy at all. exams are open note lock down browser. hws super easy. book is free!
Dr. Bryant is the best professor at MSU. Even though the class was just a general requirement, I was interested in learning.
dr bryant is so caring i would highly recommend
Dr. Bryant is one of the best professors I've had at MSU. She is very caring and compassionate. She let us use open notes on all of our quizzes.
Good professor, open note quizzes and tests makes things very easy. She posts all lecture notes and slides, doesn't stray much from the notes on quizzes and tests.

I had her for iss 210 and this class was very good. As long as you do the discussion posts and do good on the tests you will get a good grade. The tests were open note and you can print out the lecture notes she made and the tests were very self explanatory. I would 100% take this class again

Professor Bryant is admirably kind, charismatic, and understanding of student circumstances. She is very passionate about social issues and the content her class teaches. Her effort to maintain unbiassed perspectives while being educational about the topics she lectures about is evident and appreciated.

She was an extremely easy class but it was definitely the most pointless class and the biggest waste of time. Her lectures just go over the readings basically word for word so you really only need to do one or the other but she makes attendance mandatory for some reason. Easy class but such a waste. She also gives short notice for canceled class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Bryant was such an amazing professor, the work load was very light in this class. We had weekly discussion posts, a few quizzes, and exams. But for all the quizzes and exams she allowed you to use notes and she had lecture notes available on d2l that had the exact answers to the test. Attendance was taken but not graded.
Probably the best professor I've had by far, the class was enjoyable and I learned so much.. She is great with grading and I have never dreaded doing her work. 10/10
Easy class, easy grade. Would definitely take her class again!
Very easy class, I highly recommend taking it.

She's such a sweetheart! During her first lecture, she said something under the lines of wanting all of us to get A's (which she said was 100% possible) and she hoped to be able to interact with all of us. Her feedback to our online papers/responses shows she cares about our performance, and her lectures are easy to navigate.

Super sweet professor who actually cares about students. She's really understanding and literally designs the class so you can get an A. It's so easy, everything is open note, and you don't even need to read any of the books to pass. 10/10 recommend as an easy ISS if you need one to take.

By far one of my favorite professors so far. She cares more about you asking questions than the grade you receive. Class is super easy, and every quiz and exam is open note. She is an amazing professor, and this class challenged me to question my views!

Very easy class, every exam and quiz was open notes provided by her. Attendance isn't mandatory but her lectures are pretty interesting and really easy to reach outside of class. I would def recommend for anyone.
Dr. Amber Bryant clearly understands students and does everything possible to help them succeed in her class.

Absolutely LOVE Dr. Bryant. clear, easy-to-follow lectures. The only downside I could see is the pace can be a little fast for notetaking but the tests and quizzes and exams are NOT cumulative! So you have lots of little breaks.

Dr. Bryant was a very good professor. She is very understanding of students and truly wants to see them succeed in her class. Tests we all open-note, so as long as you prepared yourself well, you could pass. Overall 10/10.

The first half of this class is super easy, she sends you a notes packet to print out and you can use it on the exam and the exam is word-for-word from the notes. The second half requires you to do the reading, but the exams are taken at home so... The lectures are a little boring but Dr Bryant is very sweet and friendly.

Professor Bryant is the best. She is kind and lectures are actually pretty interesting. Attendance isn't mandatory to get a good grade and there is minimal work in the class. Open note on every quiz and exam, so the easiest 4.0 ever. I actually learned a lot in this class as well, so I highly recommend taking this class with professor Bryant.
I really really enjoyed her as a teacher!!! I would recommend everyone to take her class. You can tell she really loves what she is doing.

TAKE THIS CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSER. The best and most understanding professor I've ever had. Everything is open note and there are only weekly discussion posts. Lectures aren't required, but I would go because the class is so interesting and gives a different perspective. Definitely would take it if you want a 4.0.

Dr. Bryant is an amazing professor, she is very kind and likes to have fun in class. The class is made up of 4 quizzes, a midterm, a final, and discussion posts every week. All of the tests are open note and she gives you her lectures notes, where she pulls the quiz questions from. This is a very easy class and also very interesting.

Dr. Bryant is an amazing and understanding person. Her lectures are very beneficial and prepare you well for quizzes. The class's only reading is really only required during the second half of the semester and its relatively short, but MSU should really have more professors like her.

Amber Bryant is one of the sweetest professors I have had at MSU. She is super understanding and wants you to succeed in her class. There is extra credit. Open notes quizzes. If you pay attention in class then you will get a 4.0
Very laid back and cool.

Dr. Bryant is a great professor. The lesson plan is clear; you have similar weekly assignments, which helps create a schedule. As long as you show up to class, pay attention, and do the work, you will get a 3.5. She and her TA are available out of class in case of any problems. I would definitely go out of my way to take one of her courses again.

She was chill and even told us that she understands that we are all in different situations and it's okay if we can pass the class without going. Loved her, tests are open note and online, and she posts the combined lecture notes so you can just go off of those

Dr. Bryant is a great professor, is caring and always willing to listen; allowed me to turn in late assignments as well which not all profs do. Simple class, show up twice a week and take notes/pay attention and you will bare minimum 3.5 this class. Would highly recommend as it is straight forward, no trick questions or pop quizzes. Take this class

This professor really cares and wants to see her students succeed. Her lectures were interesting and she made sure to incorporate a variety of teaching methods to keep students engaged. She also provided many opportunities for extra credit and resources such as lecture notes to help students learn.

Bryant is super nice and the class was very easy. Everything is open note so you just have to print out the slide shows and guided notes. I recommend lectures as it makes the quizzes easier to take, but all the notes are available so it's fine to miss a lecture. Pretty boring, but I did learn some interesting and useful things about education!
Lots of discussion posts, quizzes and readings. Some info on slides was confusing. She was a very good teacher though and I would taker her class again. Just show up to class and you'll be fine!

best professor by far, if you attend the lectures and go through the notes you will 100% pass the class. She also is very kind and passionate about what she teaches. I loved her energy. The quizzes, tests, midterm, and final were open notes! please please take her class i am so glad i had Bryant as my prof. she has a very kind soul.
This course was really easy with not many homework assignments at all but the lectures were very boring and not engaging but an easy A. We also got to leave class early most days so that's a plus.

A great lecturer. She makes the class very simple and interesting. Often the tests are open notes. She is very willing to work with you to get you to the grade you want. She provides a lot of extra credit opportunities. She wants what is best for her students.
I enjoyed this class and Dr. Bryant was a great professor, you could tell that she is very passionate about her job which makes learning just as enjoyable.
My favorite professor so far she was easy and helped me get a 4.0 highly recommended
My favorite teacher EVER. She was so understanding and would give me extensions whenever I asked. So many opportunities for extra credit too!

professor bryant is a pretty good professor and seems very knowledge on the topics taught during class. i enjoyed having her as my professor and would definitely recommend her for as a great ISS prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Eh

Very good down to earth, relatable professor, that is also a good teacher, workload was good and the quizzes and tests I felt very prepared for ( and most of them were open note). Class wasn't any harder than it needed to be and having her as a professor was fun, and I would definitely like to have her as a professor again.

Dr. Bryant's class was very nice. All of her tests and quizzes (including midterm and final exam) were open note. As long as you take notes, you are almost guaranteed an A. There's one discussion post per week and she also offers 3-4 extra credit assignments. She's a very sweet lady.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: All her quizzes, the midterm, and the final are open notes. Make sure you know how to use your notes and can find things easily. Textbooks are required but you can make do without reading them.
Loved her and would definitely take her class again! All quizzes and tests are open note, and she gives you both lecture notes and guided notes for all, if not most, of them. Class was pretty easy!

Dr. Bryant is amazingggg! Not only is she a great teacher but she is very kind and understanding. The class is not bad at all you have two textbooks that you cover throughout the semester. Each week you have discussion posts, and most tests are open note. 10000000% reccomend.

Super lecture heavy, but if you didn't go most of the time you wouldn't understand what was happening. She is kind and when she isn't just reading off the slides and gets us to participate it's a fun class and she's a great teacher. Also all exams and tests are open note.
So kind and accommodating! You can tell she is passionate about what she teaches. She keeps lectures interesting and fun. Only a discussion post a week and a few quizzes. Definitely recommend.

The class was based off two textbooks where you would read 50-75 pages a week. Lectures would primarily go over what you read/learned about within this reading. If you show up to class/read you are basically guranteed a 4.0. She gave a decent amount of easy extra credit as well.

She is absolutely amazing! She gives clear expectations, tells you how you will succeed in the class, gives phenomenal feedback, and answers any questions we have. Attendance is not mandatory, but it is helpful to be in class to hear what she says that aren't in the slides. Overall best professor I've had this semester!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Bryant is very kind and caring and wants to help you succeed. Quizzes and tests are open note, and homework is usually a discussion board due once a week. I find the material very interesting, and I would definitely take one of her classes again!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is amazing, she is so kind and will answer all your questions, she give you information that you probably never knew you needed. Her quizzes and tests are easy (open note) and she shares her lecture notes. If you go to class and pay attention then you will pass, a lot of people don't read the textbooks but I did and they helped me a lot.

This professor is extremely easygoing. Lots of lectures but they are interesting and engaging. Minimal assignments and open note tests, midterm, and final. If you pay attention to lectures and copy notes you won't need to worry about reading the textbooks.

She is an amazing professor who cares about her students and the information that she teaches. She makes the content interesting through her lectures. If you just show up for class you should be able to pass no problem. Open-note tests, mid-term, and final.
Overall a great teacher, she loves feedback from students.
She really cares about her students and is such a sweet person. A lot of reading but it is easy to keep up with and tests and quizzes are open note.
Allowed to drop grades. Open-note quizzes. Takes the time to help individual students.
Good professor, teaches well.
Easy class, just do the discussion posts and check the lecture notes for the quizzes.
All exams and quizzes are open notes, so definitely an easy A class as long as you take good notes. She made the lectures as fun and as interesting as possible.

She is awesome! Quizzes are online, open notes. She posts all of her lecture notes in case you want to look through. No projects, just quizzes and worksheets. Content is interesting and she is easy to listen to.
Super nice and understanding, take good notes and show up when you can because it will help you.

This class was easily my favorite class of my first ever college semester. Professor Bryant really did a wonderful job easing us students into the college curriculum and managed to make the class engaging and productive.
She was really easy and laid back. A couple books read but open note quizzes and exams, fairly easy class and fun.
Lecture heavy, but a great class to take! She is very straightforward with information and the level of difficulty is more on the easier side. Extremely respectable and understanding.

I really enjoyed this class with Dr. Bryant! She was very very sweet, you can tell she deeply cares about her students and those around her. Her classes are mostly lecture based on 2 different textbooks. She makes the class more interesting by including documentaries/movie days, and she gives out extra credit quite often. Quizzes are open book too!

Very easy class if you show up to her lectures and keep up with readings. Quizzes are not difficult and she gives you good lecture notes. Not many assignments a week only discussion posts that are very easy to answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bryant was a great professor! While some lectures were heavy with material she often used tools to make them more engaging, such as google polls or other ways to get class opinions on the content. Lecture notes are also posted weekly for important ideas and to help on open note quizzes which personally helped me better understand the readings.

I would definitely recommend anyone to take this class, it was really informative and laid back as far as workload. I feel like I really gained a lot from this class but also didn't have to worry about it.

Easy A, some interesting lectures, great person, very caring, I learned a lot in the course and did not struggle with grades. Although the lectures sometimes feels like she is just reading off a sheet of paper rather than being an expert on some of the subjects.

Although the course is lecture heavy, she finds a way to teach the lecture in a chill and conversational type manner. She gives you her own lecture notes before a quiz which are super helpful and she lets you print them out and have them during a quiz. Overall I would highly recommend taking her course because she is very down to earth.
she was a very good professer made the material intresting and lectures while being a little dull she would add non graded inclass activities that made it easier to understand and more enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bryant is a passionate professor, you can tell she cares about what she's teaching. Attendance is not mandatory, and for the most part, everything covered in lectures is posted online. Exams/Quizzes are all open notes, which are also posted online. Overall, the class was very easy and I would recommend it!
Great professor, just take notes on the lectures and all quizzes will be easy. She is very straight forward and understanding. She wants her students to succeed and puts them first.

Very caring and passionate professor. She would help you out if you reach out to her personally. Coming to class is not mandatory as everything is on the lecture notes. All exams are open notes and just print out the notes she gave you and earn your easy A.

Overall very easy class. You will do well if you read the notes, which are posted. Going to class can be helpful since she goes over her lecture notes a little more thoroughly but it is not mandatory. Quizzes and exams are all open note and you will do well if you print out any resources given. Professor Bryant is very likeable in general.

Easiest ISS you can take at MSU. She lectures from a note paper that she posts online. The tests are open notes so you can print off the lecture notes and take the quiz. The answers are almost word for word what is in these notes. She tells you to read the book however it is not necessary bc she talks about everything that is important in the book.

Prof reads off of a script for all her lectures that obviously aren't written by her. Class is quite easy - only major homework is discussion posts and she posts all the lecture notes on D2L so going to every lecture is unnecessary. Don't bother buying the books unless you can find them for free. Overall pretty easy A which is nice for a gen ed.

I had Professor Stanton for the 2025 Fall Semester PR 225 Writing class. I thought I took a lot away about the basics of writing in the PR world and found it to be a very helpful introductory course. Professor Stanton gave great feedback, cared about how her students did, and was not a harsh grader. I would definitely recommend taking this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I had Professor Stanton for the 2025 Fall Semester PR 225 Writing class. I took a lot away from the class and was a really good introduction to writing in the PR world. Professor Stanton gave great feedback throughout the semester, was not a harsh grader, and showed a lot of care for her students work.

The class required a lot of writing assignments, and she was slow getting our assignments back to us. But she really cared about the class and about helping us build a PR writing portfolio. She wanted us to participate. We did a lot of partner exercises in class that made the class more interesting. I liked that she walked around the room so much.

Don't be discouraged from her class. She's attentive and engages, so anticipate her walking around n asking questions. Workload is manageable. She goes out her way to help best she can. Stay after class if u have questions; she addresses them transparently and guides u step by step. There's a textbook & subscription, but u can pass w/o if u engage.

Great professor! She's very transparent, approachable & sets clear expectations while still being supportive. She encourages participation, stays after class to help & ensures everyone feels heard. I loved how she taught us to use AI ethically and modeled project expectations. You will get from this course what you put into it, so show up & engage.

Lectures were long, not really her fault,(6pm-9pm) class. Feedback takes a while to get back. I thought she did her best. You could tell she cared about preparing us for the workforce and reflected that through the assignment she gave us (you build a portfolio throughout the semester. Final is improving the work you already did from her feedback.

Just don't take her courses. Waste of time literally. Got quite an attitude with me multiple times when I would ask questions. Rambles about NOTHING. Uses chatgpt to grade and give feedback. My group never showed up and she didn't care. Just doesn't care about her students honestly. Hope she does some reflection after this semester.

Lectures are impossible to follow- class material is unclear in how it correlates to assignments (and there are a lot of them). Assignments are time consuming, and feedback is fully AI generated. Also spoke condescendingly to students often. Nice enough, just extremely frustrating to work with.

Lectures are extremely boring and hard to follow. Used the required textbook one time at the beginning of the semester. She also requires you to get chat gtp premium and i think she uses AI to grade. Sweet lady that definitely means well, but so so disorganized and scattered.

I'm still thinking about this class a year later. The way we were "teamed up" was so chaotic. She separated us vaguely by interest, then just threw us into a group of like 12 ppl to try and find 2-3 ppl to spend the next 10 weeks working with. My group was awful & her grading was merciless. One of two classes I didn't get a 4.0 in my entire career.
Graded us with chatgpt because most of her rubrics were wrong so that was nice. her feedback didn't even follow our assignment sometimes.

Makes grading so difficult for a beginner-level course on grant writing. I have never done grant writing before and have never been graded so hard for something I have never done before. Be prepared to have unfair grading, a lack of care from her, and overall one of the worst experiences in a classroom. She also has an unfair grading scale as well

Such an awesome prof. Very kind and resourceful. I took this class without knowing anything about grant writing, but her lectures were great, and she gave very helpful feedback on assignments, so this wasn't an issue at all. If you have to take an upper-level writing course and this is an option, I'd 10/10 recommend you choose to take one with her.

The class moves fast and covers a lot of material. There are weekly quizzes and exams that make up most of your grade. Because of this, you have to study a lot outside of class. Overall, she is kind and helpful, but if you are not strong in algebra, you may need extra help like a tutor to keep up.

such a difficult professor, so much to do on webwork but she says its not important. You only learn in lecture (not recitation), so if you miss the lecture or part of the lecture you're done for. She won't answer questions that she answered in class already, which made it feel like you couldn't email her with questions, also won't reteach concepts.

If you're good at math do other students a favor and take her lecture (people not good at math will struggle with her teaching style so let them take a better prof.) Lectures are too short for the amount of chatting she does. I retaught myself content after class. She's sweet and wants to help you when 1-on-1 but she should teach a smaller class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
She's a sweet lady, but I think she should retire soon.

She makes mistakes during lectures that students often have to call out. There's a quiz or midterm exam during recitation, with the quiz being 20 minutes and the midterms being a full period.

You'll do great if you're good with math, but I suggest taking a different class if you struggle.

I don't like the structure of MTH 103, Professor Allen is nice but expects far more than you would think for a class of 400-500 people. A lot of my lectures, the first 20 minutes would be spent yelling at various students and complaints about the students.

The structure of this class is awful, but it will be the same regardless of your prof, so no hate to prof Allen. Just SO much hw, quiz/exam EVERY week, 2 50 min 500 person lectures so there is no time to ask questions. If you want to succeed, go to every class, office hours, and watch videos. There is a reason why so many people fail this class.

She makes so many flaws in her lectures and teaches at a really fast pace. She also stops the whole lecture if she hears one person talking and wastes time when lectures are only 1 hour. Lots of webwork problems that don't give any good feedback if you're wrong. Some exams also don't resemble the study guide so know every single bit of material.

Only graded on homework, quizzes, tests, no extra credit
Office hours help alot sicne she is normally slow during lectures 
Quizzes and tests are decently hard I'd study vocab such as "what makes a polynomial a polynomial, etc"
Literaly algebra 2 just in college 
Webwork (hw) is due every week 
Go to the MLC or office hours for help
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's a very sweet lady. The lessons are so easy if you print out the notes and go to class. She makes a lot of mistakes during the lecture, so it can get a little confusing at times, but overall, she's decent.

Her lectures are full of flaws and she prefers to rush through content instead of teaching it. 
The grading for this course is also awful. Work has to be exact in a way that feels like walking a child. 
If you can take another, please do.

I want warn you that this class will be difficult, that is not say you cannot pass it but you are going to have to WORK FOR IT. This is NOT a class where you can no show lectures, not go to extra review sessions, and skip office hours. Without office hours I would have failed this class! She is extremely devoted to helping you learn!! Just try!!

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!! If you are already struggling with math, taking this class will push you back even farther from where you started. Sue Allen is not consistent with teaching in her lectures, and everything earned must be studied outside of class. The workload is excessive, and the professor doesn't know how to properly teach.

Don't take this if you struggle with math in the first place. She made a mistake at least 2 times every lecture and students would have to correct her. She spends way too much time bashing the students for grades instead of teaching, and her teaching style is horrendous. Her class made me feel like I was in high school again.

Prof Allen is not great at teaching. She will rush through lectures and just do the work without explaining how she got her answers. Talks multiple times about how if you get the answer but not her way you will not receive credit. Be ready to have to teach yourself. Do Not Take

DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE IF YOU WANT A GOOD GPA AND TO NOT HAVE TO RETAKE AGAIN!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!  you can put in 20 hours of studying and still will get bad grades, does not know how to teach and I end up watching lecture videos online. take it with a different prof.
Can not teach. She will do the work without any explanation with it. She is easily agitated and will stop lectures to walk up to and yell at students. If you can do not take.

Terrible. If you can get out of having her as a prof, I would. She does not teach the material, and quite literally tells you, "You should have learned this in High School." instead of helping. If you do poorly on weekly quizzes and exams, you will not pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Susan Allen cannot teach math. I spent most my time in the MLC (Math Learning Center) where they actually helped. She rushes lectures and goes way too fast. There was also times when she made her own mathematical errors, and other students in the lecture hall corrected her. She has a sweet personality, but is not a good professor!
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mrs Allen is so sweet, the content is difficult but she really cares about students success, She hosts extra office hours and review sessions to help with any difficult content. The lectures are fast paced but there is a lot of content to get through, I would highly recommend taking 103 with Mrs Allen.
She's good, she just doesn't explain her answers, rather just gives them to you. She moves on very quickly in lectures

Poor teaching style. Talks too much before class then rushes at the end, overall not organized in the slightest (which I need in a professor) her explanations are not cohesive/helpful. Treated class like high school, she's very funny but not a good math professor fit, she should be a highschool history teacher! If you're bad at math don't take her.

I didn't enjoy professor Allen's teaching style. She treated the class like a highschool class, and showed us the same sort of respect as highschoolers. She tends to start talking way before class started and usually ended class late. She was also sensitive about people leaving early. She was fine, but I didn't love her teaching style or anything.

Shes a very sweet older lady.She often treats her class like grandchildren. She will often open up more office hours, exam study sessions, extra practice before exams, etc. She is there for you if you need help and genuinely wants all her students to do well. She can sometimes make mistakes but she fixes them quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Sue Allen is a caring, light-hearted professor.  She wants the best for her students and is very personable. She loves to joke around, but often gets off task during the short 50-minute lectures. I struggled with her lack of organization during lectures. She tends to over-explain the easy stuff, not focusing enough on the difficult content.

Sue Allen is an amazing math professor. I've always struggled with math, but she explains it clearly, making it enjoyable. The class is tough but manageable with effort. By attending office hours, doing practice problems, and learning from mistakes, I improved significantly. She genuinely cares and goes the extra mile to help her students succeed.
Please Please do not make the same mistake that so many people in that class went through, spare yourself and do not take this class with her

Dr. Allen was not a horrible professor, however if you are taking math 103, DO EVERYTHING YOU CAN to take one of the other professors. Dr. Allen messed up in class very frequently and did not explain things in an easy to understand manner. From what I heard, the other professors had much higher grade averages and were more well liked.

I was one of the few people I knew who passed this course, and I earned a 3.5. I think Mrs. Allen was one of the best professors you can get for MTH 103. Your grade in this class is based on how much effort you put in. Any good advisor will have you take CEM 141 and this class separately. You get to drop 2 quizzes and 1 exam, which was generous.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Was kind and helpful. Made mistakes during lecture but fixed them quickly. Make sure you attend lecture or else you will probably fail the class. There is a quiz every week. Homework was easy but there was a lot of it.

She is just too old to be teaching still, constantly making mistakes which makes it hard to follow the lecture. She is always confused and gets upset/hurt pretty easily about not coming to class or leaving early. You have a test or quiz every recitation, but if you do the reviews and go to the mth help room not her office hours it wasn't very hard

Allen is a very sweet lady, and cares about her students.If you want to pass, go to the lectures!! She often holds review sessions before exams. She's definitely too old to be teaching still and is sometimes hard to hear in class and makes mistakes. This IS a harder class, but you have all the recourses to get a 3.5 or 4.0.

Allen is an alright professor, although she often makes mistakes in lectures. I think the issue is less with her, and the MTH103 class as a whole. It goes by way too fast and can be very difficult to learn with the notes provided. Be prepared to use a LOT of outside resources, and consider taking MTH103A instead (because I really wish I did).

Super sweet, often hosts study sessions before exams and occasionally before quizzes. Easy to reach out to. Provides a schedule for the week every Sunday night or Monday morning via email as well as on D2L. Follows her syllabus. Allows two quiz drops and one exam drop. Lectures are effective and easy to understand as well as posting online lectures

Sue Allen is such a kind proffessor and is very helpful if you reach out for help. Test and Quizzes were very hard for me at the beginning but that's because I wasn't asking for help. After going to office hours and attending the MLC my grades started to go up. You have all the resources you need to be successful in this class
really hard:(
Truly just not a great prfessor, not understanding and I would advise everyone to find a different proffesor
She is a genuinely good professor who actually cares. You honestly have all the resources to get a 4.0.

Professor Allen is a caring instructor who genuinely wants students to succeed. While she occasionally makes minor mistakes during lectures, her notes are clear and the quizzes/exams align well with the material. Utilizing resources like unstuck AI and going to office hours can really help overcome the course's challenges.

I personally dont agree on what majority people here says. I find that she is amazing! Go to office hours, she would guide you through the course. Honestly its just a skill issue if you're struggling.
I didn't struggle but I know a lot of people that did, just make sure to stay on top of your work and be well prepared for the weekly quizzes

Quiz every week or exam. No extra credit opportunity. Allen makes many mistakes every lecture which makes it hard to follow and learn. Many students have had to shout out and correct her multiple times about mistakes she's made during note taking. Would not recommend her if you are taking this course and aren't good at learning by yourself.

If you struggle with math like me you are going to find this class difficult. Allen does the best she can but with the sheer amount of content you have to learn in such a short span of time you can get very easily overwhelmed. She has office hours though which I recommend taking advantage of. Overall MTH103 is gonna be hard no matter the professor.

Sue is a great person and she cares about her students and math. However, she frequently makes mistakes during lectures which is confusing. She will often get off topic and we lose a lot of lecture time because of this. She also hands out a lot of difficult homework that is extremely time-consuming. There is a quiz or exam every week.

Professor Allen is very sweet. She does make mistakes in her lectures often but catches them quickly. I found it most helpful to watch the recorded lectures when studying and rewrite my notes. My ULA had a heavy accent which made it hard to understand sometimes. I felt like I taught myself a lot in this class. Watch the video review before exams

Sue really does care about her students and it helps to make your face known. Go to office hours and get to know her. She is the sweetest and wants to see people succeed. I didn't even do well in the class, math is not my strong suit, but she really tried to help me understand and is overall so nice. Don't listen to people. I 10/10 recommend her.

This class wasn't very difficult for me as long as you keep up with the notes and webwork assigned. There is usually a quiz every Friday for this course. Prof Allen is super sweet and takes her time but does occasionally mess up but is usually able to catch it. I will say is that she isn't usually to fit in all of the content in the time she has.

Professor Allen is so caring and wants all of her students to succeed. The notes were very easy to follow and the quizzes and exams were very similar to the notes in the lecture. The homework on the other hand is a bit harder than what you learn in the lecture so don't get discouraged if you can't get the correct answer to every question.

Professor Allen really cares about her students! She sometimes makes mistakes during her lectures but it didn't really bother me. She held review sessions outside of class to help with quizzes and exams. She really is the sweetest person and was a great start for my college journey ! To pass you'll NEED to take notes and understand the homework!

Shes too old to be teaching, cant get through one lecture without her messing up and having to go back and correct her own work, sweet lady, but needs to retire. Go to lectures, do webwork, go to math learning center, and use the practice exam to study for exams. Sometimes she passes an attendance sheet around, but again is too old to remember.

Sue Allen loves her students, and genuinely cares for their success in this class. I couldn't of asked for a better professor to kick off my start to college. Yes there's a lot of homework, but if you want to pass that's mandatory. Loved this class even though I might not be the best at math. She provides plenty of help to prepare for exams.
Dont take math 103 in general it is a GPA killer.

Key to passing the class is going to lecture. Prof is very nice and has lots of office hours and tries to help. It can be a bit frustrating when she often makes mistakes during lecture. I think she's a nice person, but should retire soon. HW is harder than actual tests/quizzes. Do the work and you'll be fine.

Sue seems like a nice person, but she needs to stop teaching. She doesn't make sense, makes tons of mistakes, coughs every 5 seconds, and gives insane amounts of homework. My roommate and I ended up watching lectures from another Prof just to understand what we were doing. I really don't recommend taking MTH103 with Sue if you can help it.

I loved her, very much sweet grandma vibes. Provided lots of help with many office hours and an exam review session per unit. There was a decent amount of homework but thats expected in a math course. Do your homework, pay attention, and study, and youll be fine

Professor Allen is amazing for MTH103! Right from the start she was very caring and wanted all of her students to pass this class. She has office hours 3 times a week and will answer any question you have for her. She truly cares about her students! YOU JUST HAVE TO PARTICIPATE! How to pass? 1. Do homework. 2. Print notes 3. Go to class. Got a 4.0

Professor Allen is a good teacher, but this class is very test/quiz heavy. You have a quiz almost every week and the grading is very nit-picky. Its very hard to stay confident in this class. The homework assignments are not bad at all. The professor is very sweet and has a kind soul. Ask for help if you need it.

she constantly messes up in each lecture which makes it extremely difficult to follow along. she also gives a quiz every week and the homework is heavy and usually way harder than what is taught in the lectures.

I retook this class as a sophomore after getting a 2.5 the first time. Allen is an amazing professor that treats you like family! I spent a lot of time in the MLC to quickly finish the homework. To succeed you need to attend class, STUDY, and pay attention when she says something could be on a quiz or exam. Very straightforward class, loved her!!

Mth103 as a whole is a disaster at MSU, so I wouldn't put all of the blame on the professors. Professor Allen tries her best to teach this content however, the time constraints of this class make it difficult to thoroughly develop an understanding. GO TO OFFICE HOURS, she is willing to reexplain content that you might be struggling with. LOTS of HW

The lectures were long and unengaging, Professor Allen would often make mistakes and erase or correct the notes that she was teaching us. The class used iClicker, so attendance was mandatory and graded. I did not enjoy this class at all, content was barely taught but was expected to be known. One of the worst classes I have taken.
Hard professor to understand. There are better and easier professors to understand. The homework was heavy and not easy to understand. She was also very short with you.

Really important to participate in class! Prof. Allen is such a sweetheart and is SUPER passionate about the content she teaches. Her students are mostly freshmen (I am a junior) and they don't realize that professors can make errors sometimes. She's super helpful with questions! I'm someone who NEVER understood math until she taught it to me!

I would avoid this class. Sue Allen is a nice professor, but she constantly messes up in lectures and her students have to correct her, making the whole lecture 10x more confusing. The homework (webwork) wasn't related and was much harder than what we learned in class. Used photo math for the majority of the semester. Practice exams were the exams
Took MTH 103. Too fast, did not explain a lot of things thoroughly. Came in with a basic knowledge of algebra, but wanted to take it again to review before going into 124. Did not help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: old school in my opinion, nice lady, not so great teacher, very fast pace

Professor Allen was kind of all over the place. She was very sweet and I really like her as a person, but not as a teacher. There were quizzes basically every Friday, and I always had to watch the recorded lessons from the other professor because she either never finished the notes in class, or didn't really explain anything thoroughly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Almost never paid attention to classes but managed my way through by watching the online lectures that is provided for everyone, really recommend them if you're slow with math like me. She replied to emails and had a very clear criteria that included the ability to drop 2 out of 7 categories including exams. Webwork doesn't help so dont rely on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lots of homework, as well this teacher would always go ahead of what the quizzes would be on , taking this class just piles more and more stress like never before, students would always have to correct the professor as well, this class was required for me and I would never take it again.

Sue Allen is a super nice professor!  However, I probably would not take one of her classes again.  She would constantly make mistakes on the notes and a student would have to raise their hand and correct her.  She is a bit dull but I don't think that is her fault because the class is super hard to make fun and engaging.
make sure to go to office hours and it is more helpful than the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is a lot harder than what you would expect for a college algebra. Lots of homework and quizzes pretty much every Friday which gets really overwhelming. Also, I had a university approved absence form and she was my only prof who would not give me an excused absence, even though the university approved it

Ahhhhh, this might've been the worst class i've ever taken. Be prepared future students. If you're not already good at math, you will not get any better while taking this class. If you don't want to tank your gpa because of one class.. get a private tutor. Everybody knows at MSU that the math department is a travesty, i just became another victim.

If you are taking MTH 103, Sue Allen is the go-to professor. Out of all the math professors, Sue Allen is the nicest, most considerate, easiest, and most helpful. She helps you prepare for quizzes and exams better. She will go out of her way to help students. You have to pay attention and not talk to people around you because she'll call you out.

Professor Allen is such a sweet lady and she definitely cares about the well-being of her students. But this class was really hard for an algebra class. Students are given quizzes every single Friday before even having the chance to actually learn the material. Be prepared to spend hours of your free time trying to pass this class.

Professor Allen is a nice professor who is available outside of class for help during her office hour and holds review sessions. However, students are given quizzes every single Friday before they're able to even digest the information that is blown through in class. Additionally, the exam reviews are never representative of the actual exam.

For an algebra class it was surprisingly difficult. The lecture do not do much teaching, rather they are just the professor quickly rushing through a page of notes. There is lots of online homework, and quizzes and or exams very often. This class requires an unnecessary amount of additional learning outside of class.

This was a tough class but don't be scared by the other reviews. I went to MLC like once-twice a week and attended office hours before her exams and am passing with a 4.0. You will need to print out the notes and iclicker into class but you can drop two categories that go to your grade which can be exams! Webwork is very hard for no reason though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Absolutely horrible. Never explains anything thoroughly, but has many opportunities for hep like office hours. Rambles in her lectures so much that sometimes you have to watch the rest of the lecture through video. If I had to take this class again, I would take it with Shannon Griffen.

There is no leniency whatsoever for attendance but the lectures are pointless. Everything is on webwork, w/ 4 exams and a quiz almost every week. She's so boring, it's so bad and I've fallen asleep in this class more than I've learned in it. Assignments are due at 7 am which is the weirdest thing I've ever heard of. You have to pay to do homework.

The worst professor I have ever had forgets what she is doing every 5 minutes attendance is mandatory even though you're listening to a brick wall give information thinks students fail assessments because they don't go to office hours even though most peers I know end up back at their dorms and watch a different professor teach it via lecture video

She is an elderly woman who needs to retire. Makes a lot of mistakes during lecture, such as writes and solves problems incorrectly, and forgets to turn on her microphone until reminded by a student. Does not allow more than four unexcused absences or she will automatically fail you and all lectures/recitations take attendance.

hardest math class ever with short confusing lectures. webwork did not help learn material, exams are difficult. failed first 2 exams even with 100% on all assignments and attending MLC, ended up failing the class because i couldn't get 100% on the others. math department at msu needs work.

Honestly, she isn't the worst professor I've had, but the Math Department at MSU is lacking. Classes last too short to absorb any useful information, and by the time you're done you walk out knowing nothing. It's not difficult if you're able to go over the information yourself, (and make corrections to stuff she did wrong,) but it wastes time.

-SUCH A HARD CLASS 
-attendance taken via iclicker 
-if you don't go to class you miss so much
-webwork is horrible
-does not explain how you get to an answer or why it works the way it does

Just show up to lectures and do your webwork and its a fairly easy class.
-She's a pretty easy teacher but an easy class
Easy class, pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor was very nice and thorough, however, you have to pay to access the homework and pay to print out the notes because it's basically required if you want to pass the class. And attend MLC. The online program, webwork, is often different/harder material than covered in class. Overall very angering, but the material isn't hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was unusually difficult. This class is a pre-rec for stats and stats is 10000x easier. The lectures move super quickly and are not easy to understand. All of the concepts should be easy but they are way overexplanined and overcomplicated. Not to mention there are tests every single friday. If you can test out of this class DO IT.

I hope to never have to take her again. Her exams were never like the study guides or homework we had every week. I went to office hours and she wasn't helpful whatsoever. I wouldn't recommend her at all.
She is very kind and always wants to help students. She loves to get questions and feedback about her lectures. Just go to lecture and do the homework and you'll be fine!
She wants you to do well, you just have to put in time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Allen was very kind and seemed willing to help me if I needed it, but her lectures consist of her quickly filling out notes, with very little explaining. I am a step by step learner with math, and Sue pretty regularly neglected to clearly explain what she was doing. Anyone can read over completed math notes. I needed someone to TEACH me

Professor Allen was nice but since the lectures are so big it's not easy at all to build any connections. I think she taught well during the lectures. You don't have to go to the lectures but the class will be a lot harder so you should go. If you don't study or work hard, you'll barely pass or even fail so you really have to put the work in.
She works really well with student-athletes. Is always available and helpful in office hours. Super calm and kind!

Prof Allen really cares about her students and she stays after almost every lecture to help students who have questions. However, if you do not put in the effort to actually learn the material then the homework will be very difficult to complete. All lectures are recorded, so attendance isn't necessarily mandatory but is heavily encouraged.

MTH103 is a large class at MSU so it is hard for Professor Allen to make connections with the students unless they reach out to her. With hard work and studying you CAN 4.0 this class. I attended the math learning center and focused on the first 3 exams so I did not have to take the cumulative final.
