Professor Arch is fantastic! His lectures are interesting and he often gives quiz answers in the lectures. He gives a quiz oer the reading/ film in every class, but the quizzes are easy enough (if you did the reading) Sometimes the reading is super long or dense, but other then that his class is easy and enjoyable!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Arch is a great lecturer and generally cares about his students. He is easily accessible via email, and responds quickly. This class was material heavy, but very interesting and easy to engage in over all. I would go out of my way to take another class with Dr. Arch. Read the books and go to majority of classes, and you will be fine.

Professor Arch made IAH 207 a very interesting course. While it is sort of a heavier workload (because there are multiple books, films, and short stories to read and view along with a few writing assignments), all of the work was generally pretty interesting and Professor Arch did a good job of making sure everyone was on track and engaged.

I enjoyed this class a lot. Honestly i missed quite a few classes because it was at 8:30 but he gave good opportunities to improve on assignments and gave good feedback on what to improve. He guided discussions well and cared more about how much you participated and improved on assignments than how often you came to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: loved hearing the man speak, he had very interesting opinions and made an effort to choose literature from authors with a variety of backgrounds.

Had Dr Arch for Gothic lit, one of the best and most interesting to listen to professors I've had at MSU thus far. Lectures are always engaging and he does well to analyze texts and films. Highly recommend.

Honestly, you would've loved this course if gothic literature interested you. He was a good professor, I just personally struggled getting through the readings for this course, which ultimately affected my grade. Just boring if you don't like this kind of stuff. You literally have to read the material or you will not do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great professor! If you read the required text and watch the required films, you will do awesome in this course! I went to lecture about three times and received a 4.0! I would recommend him to anyone. The class is interesting and easy.

Professor Arch was an excellent professor.  The class was very well-structured and he gave outstanding lectures.  It's clear that he's very passionate about what he teaches, and that passion helped keep me invested in the course.  No complaints from me.

His lectures are extremely interesting and so is the class. The books, stories and films that were assigned were very interesting. I also loved the way he had us analyze stills of films/paintings. He was very well rounded in his teaching and made the class enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: I loved this class! I never felt like there was an abundance of reading. You read short stories and novels. You also watch films. Weekly quizzes are multiple choice and questions are easy if you did the reading. Participation isn't required, but he usually gives away quiz answers in class. There are a few writing assignments. You want the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class was gothic lit and it was so fun. Lots of reading but also movies in the middle of the semester. Quiz once a week and packback once a week and an essay every 3 weeks. Not hard at all just read the material. Ended out with a 4.0 very fun class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Arch was a really great professor! That isnt to say that his classes are an easy A, if youre going to take one be ready to put in an honest effort. But hes thoughtful and his lectures are interesting and easy to follow. If you dont mind a little reading, I would recommend taking his course.
He was amazing at keeping me engaged in the assigned works and very responsive to questions. The quizzes and tests weren't that difficult if you read the text. It was an easy 4.0.

Loved having Arch. Hes an interesting guy, fun to listen to. This class isnt an easy A, you do need to show up for recitation and attend lecture to do well on quizzes. Its mainly participation based since the questions are so easy. Even if you dont read the stories, he usually covers it in lecture. Its college, you get what you put into it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Grading scale is ridiculous for a required english for no-english majors class. TA was terrible and never emailed me back when I asked about my assignments and attendance. Participation is not a reflection of ones understanding of material, but in this class they think it is!
Too much work for a required low-level english class. Never had as many assignments in my two years in college as I had in this class. No one cares about the gothic and he is pretentious.

In this class there were 6 novels we were supposed to read. I read at least one of them, most of the short stories are easy to get through, especially compared to the novels. A few horror movies were assigned, I only watched the action/thriller one. Overall easy class to get an A-/B+ if you stay on top of your stuff and show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I spent so much money on books I did not  even read. The assignments were easy to do. Just turn in everything on time and show up to recitation and easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Arch really loves what he teaches and it makes the lectures more entertaining to listen to! Hes very adapting to technical issues and is an all around nice professor. I didnt have much interest in his course at the start, but he made the class enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My class got switched last minute to the gothic arts and I am so happy for that. I loved his class the whole semester. There was a lot of books and short stories that were all so interesting and fun to learn about. My TA was terrible but I still had a great time. The only down side was my class was at 8:30 across campus. He was great overall!!!
Grading scale is totally messed up.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Poor organization in classes, TAs even seem confused. His lectures are tangential. They abandon course material and force a political agenda.

I really enjoyed his IAH about gothic literature. I feel like I learned a lot without stressing a lot. Highly recommend the class and the professor. Easily the most entertaining lectures of the semester for me. Always engaged my attention. I know you don't want to, but read the books. It's just better for everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof Arch is an amazing professor who genuinely loves what he is teaching; he is a funny and cool guy. Recommend reading the texts assigned because they will pop up on exams and quizzes. The readings are also helpful for the writing assignments. 2 small writing exercises and 2 formal essays. Posts PowerPoints from lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Lectures seem a bit long, but you'll get used to it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Arch is an over all cool guy. He cares about his students & is passionate about what he is teaching. Goes deep into gothic lit & has insightful ideas on concepts. I learned some cool things. Recommend reading because certain exam questions aren't covered in lecture. Pop quizzes & essays - not bad at all though! Take him for IAH!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. Arch is an amazing professor. His lectures are always insightful and he will specifically tell you information that will be on tests so attendance is highly suggested. He's hilarious and it's always a delight to go to his class. I would recommend this class to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took this class because I needed it to graduate and I thought I was going to hate it but Arch is one of the best profs Ive ever had. Very interested in the subject and makes lecture interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Doesn't require you attend the lectures, but the content in them is ALWAYS on the test. He even straight up says some things which appear on the test. Talks largely about his theories on literature and is rather open-minded and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Arch is an amazing professor! We have lecture twice a week and recitation once a week (easy points). There are few writing assignments, which are moderately challenging. Pay attention during lecture and actually DO YOUR READING and you will blow through exams in 5-10 minutes, no joke. I love his exams because they are NOT designed to trick you.

If you wanna write papers with no guideline and be marked down by the TA's for not having good structured  formats then please by all means take Arch. He's test are easy if not ridiculous. There isn't really a right answer on the test more like his answer and the majority answer. The questions at times are pointless. Funny guy and an ok class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I would not recommend this teacher to anyone. He doesn't help you at all and you're better off not going to his lectures. He treats you like a child and is disrespectful.

His lectures are super boring and he expects you to read 8 different books. Don't take this class if you expect an easy 4.0. His exams are not too hard but the grading scale on the papers you have to write is Ridiculous. 95% is a 4.0? that is stupid for a class that is mandatory to take that is not most peoples majors

Dr. Arch expects your to come to class, pay attention, and think critically about the topics discussed. If you pay attention and participate in class discussion you'll do fine. You have to write a few papers, but he's very fair with his grading. He's pretty funny too. He's older, but hot in that older guy way. I'd have a beer with him any day.

pretty cool prof... the class was really hard and he expects a lot of you, but he's pretty friendly and will help you out if  you asks =]he's also reallyyy funny, if a little bit boring =P overall 7 outta 10

Good professor! I enjoyed the texts we read and felt that he lectured on them very well! Attend the lectures, read the material, and do the assignments and you should be good to go! (oh, and since I know you look at these now HI PROFESSOR ARCH!!!) He reads this stuff...

By far the worst professor i had in 4 years at MSU. He assigned a project with NO guidelines...and no help. He failed 12 seniors, and pretty much said it was our fault for not coming to him for help, and when we had..he as vague. He caused a student to go on anti depressents. HORRIBLE.

my favorite professor not teaching in my major.  i was in a lecture with 300 other students, and he was still able to make the class really interesting and engaging to all those different personalities.  a really intelligent, funny, and clever guy.  he'll deffinately keep your attention in class. i learned a lot that i can relate to real life.
Great prof, enjoyed the class a great deal
Highly eloquent and definitely pretty cute for his age. He's not an easy class by any means though, you'll have to read and work. It's worth it though. He;s pretty intuitive about his students.

He really knows his stuff-  subject matter may not be very interesting but he tries to make it fun.  Take him-  he's great.  Also-  when he grades he makes comments so you know what he expects for next time
It's an interesting class, hands down.  And Professor Arch is excellent at explaining the reading and making everything clear.  Take good notes, read (some of) the books, and you'll do fine!
One of my favorite profs to date. The only class of the semester I actually enjoyed going to! Would highly recomend any of his classes.
I took this class with Steve Arch years ago.  It was a Faulkner class.  I think it still is one of the best classes I have ever taken.
Definitely a wonderful asset to the English department.  I learned so much from his class.  Highly intelligent and good sense of humor.  I highly recommend him.
He's sorta lame and difinately not hot
I took Arch for my first English class on my way to a Major seven years. Excellent professor. Never did manage to have him again though.
This prof is hard, but you will learn a lot. He is truly an asset to the Department. Excellent speaking style. THIS GUY IS HOT, even though he is old.

I took every course Dr. Athanason taught during my years at MSU. He was an extraordinarily gifted teacher and scholar. Today, I hold my own PhD in English and American Literature and teach at a major university. As a tribute to Arthur, I teach at least one of the plays I studied with him every semester - Joseph Pizzo, PhD, MSEd

I took every course Dr. Athanason taught during my years at MSU. He was an extraordinarily gifted teacher and scholar. Today, I hold my own PhD in English and American Literature and teach at a major university. As a tribute to Arthur, I teach at least one of the plays I studied with him every semester - Joseph Pizzo, PhD, MSEd

In 96/97 I had him for a undergraduate course on contemporary drama and a graduate seminar on Tennessee Williams and William Inge. I remember finishing a 20 minute speech in the seminar and Athanason asking, "Now what was it really about?"  Uh!  -- He was a one of a kind teacher and he will be missed.  Great guy.

I was heartbroken to see Prof. Athanason had passed away; he was an absolute revelation as an instructor and gave me one of the best academic experiences of my four-year MSU career.  He will be missed and I am sorry for future students who will not benefit from his teaching.

Sorry to hear that he passed away.  took him in the fall of 1999.  At the time, he seemed vague.  My grades in the class were poor and I thought he was a mean old man.  As the class progresed my work got better and it seemed I was better able to grasp the course material. A lot of difficult questions he asked but looking back the class was worth it

He said, during office hours, that when you are standing in a mob full of people, it is impossible to find the others that are willing to step away from the crowd. It is only when you have the courage to step away from that that you are able to locate the others who have also done so. He was a brilliant man and I try to live that wisdom every day.

Arthur Athanason died on September 5, 2005. I studied with him during the first years he was at Michigan State. He was the greatest of all my professors and my first literary mentor. The world has lost a great man. Susan Dormady Eisenberg

While I graduated several years ago, I came across this site and wanted to add my 2 cents on what a great professer he was/is.  While I the course was difficult and he was very demanding, it was one of the best experiences I had in my 5-plus years of undergraduate education.

Wonderful professor. First I thought he was harsh and obtuse, then I thought he was arrogant, then I thought he was crazy and finally I thought he was brilliant. I think he might be all of these things. I learned so much about how to approach theatre and literature in general. TAKE HIS CLASSES!!
brilliant professor, sell your first born to have one of his classes

Dr. Athanason cares more about what we learn in his classes and from literature than most teachers ever dream of. He isn't afraid to challenge students to think for themselves and he expects a lot out of you. I grew so much with his guidance.

I took this class in the early 90s. It's one of the few memorable experiences from MSU's teaching staff. He made me look at literature differently, with respect for the creator even if I didn't like it. Great professor.
This teacher was a frustrated thespian.  He should retire and let new teachers take his place. No one should have to endure him acting out scenes from plays ever again.
He's hard, he's passionate, a little over the top sometimes, but he knew what he was talking about

As an MSU graduate, I remember most those profs who made class come to life-Anthanason is one of the great!  As stated, he is a TOUGH grader who makes you work, but you will learn an immense amout about literature from the insightful questions he poses.
Tough grader, but just an EXCELLENT teacher all around!  Brings literature to life. Incredibly intelligent and a very personable and caring professor and person.

I took this course back in the mid 1970s and it was a life-changing experience.  Not a lecturer but a guide, he asks remarkable difficult questions that have no right or wrong answers and asks you to learn by answering them concisely. Outstanding!

First English courses with him, I was a freshman, took time to appreciate the total value of lectures (and sometimes didn't grasp them) until I was older - you will not forget this great instructor! My class was 1978-79!
Excellent lecturer.  Passionate and intelligent, tough grader.  Recommended!

Truly cares for students and is not boring whatsoever. She is a delight to have as a professor and makes learning biology fun and interesting. Her lab consists of lots of teamwork effort. Make sure to pick a good group that you can rely on. She is very understandable and wants the best for every student!
Dr. Balcer is a great teacher and is very understanding of students. She is always willing to exempt you from class or give you an extension on an assignment. She also just made lab really fun.

Lectures were kind of slow and didn't always add additional information to the pre-class videos. Exams were on the harder side and it was sometimes hard to tell how detailed answers were expected to be. Group work heavy.  Possible to 4.0 if you submit all assignments and extra credit.

Balcer genuinely loves what she is doing and tries her best to teach that caters to everyone. It is a flipped classroom and tests can be way harder than you think. But the extra credit helps immensely.

Dr. Balcer is a great professor! She is a recent PhD grad so she understands what it is like to be a student and is happy to help work with you. You'll be in an assigned group the whole semester and there is a self-conducted research project at the end. She is super nice and gives lots of feedback when asked! Would definitely recommend her.

There was a lot to read, as I was in the section about creativity. Weekly notecards are due, about the articles. She is pretty unclear at first but eventually posted what she was looking for in the notecards and I was getting 4/4s every time. In class there was lots of group work and discussions, that honestly were pretty boring. Easy 4.0.

she will not respond to emails but she is a nice lady and cares about your success she does take a while to grade things and did not give feedback when points were marked off going to class was only important when it involved assignments (index cards)or projects, besides that it was pointless it was a okay class but i would not take it again

I once heard someone say, "This class takes 6 years off my life," and I've never heard a truer statement. She is so unorganized, I don't think she understands half of the things she says, and a lot of her takes were ridiculous. Her grading never makes sense, and when you ask her about it, she won't give you a clear answer as to why
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Only in person once a week, the rest you are online. Grades are very easy, I had her for IAH206.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class was asynchronous yet we still had group projects even though we didn't have zoom meetings. She would take off points on every assignment without saying why. Didn't respond to any of my emails the entire semester, even when my group mate wasn't doing the work and we had to do it for them. Don't take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I didn't know what to expect, considering I chose this course kind of last minute, but I truly enjoyed having her as a professor. Although she may come off as a tough grader, she is very understanding, just to-the-point. Just try your best to get to know her and how YOU learn as a student, and try not to fall behind on the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a very nice and great professor overall. Although, gives a crazy amount of work for a pre-requisite. Constantly having to do something its literally just an unnecessary amount of work and is a bit of a tough grader. She's helpful and nice though.

Overall she teaches through discussions within the classes about material she provides, as well as projects and papers. She actively works with the students to create projects that will benefit us. Overall, she is a caring professor who will talk during office hours or after class about any deep discussion or questions about the topic.

I found the class discussions very interesting. Dr. Atabay really changed my perspective and I think she is a very intelligent person. I had many great conversations with her in her office hours and she truly cares about your feelings and life outside of school. The class itself does require quite a bit of reading but it does spark for good convo.

Dr. Atabay was probably one of my favorite professors. She is incredibly intelligent and carries herself in that way as well. I've had discussions with her about the material that she teaches and I found them extremely valuable.

the amount of work this class requires every week should be criminal. Most of the people taking this class are full-time students, and a good amount of those people have jobs. Personally, I work 30 Ish hours a week and have the load of a full-time student. This class essentially requires about 10-15 hours a week. there are 10+ reading per-week.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I liked Dr. Atabay a lot. She said, "Remember it's my job to expose you to as many perspectives as possible. So you might think you're agreeing or disagreeing with me, but you're not." I think that sums her up really well. If you're willing to work hard and keep an open mind, you'll learn a lot from her, even if she sucks at responding to emails.
Class wasn't horrible, but only a few assignments. Make sure to work with your group to do well as there is a lot of group work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While this class is not too difficult, I found it poorly organized. I emailed the professor several times over the semester, and she did not ever respond back to me. I had to go to office hours just to clarify things that I had sent over email. The class is long and can get boring, and there is a lot of group work. I appreciate the lack of exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took the asynchronous class due to my busy nursing schedule. This class is okay if you just keep your head down and turn in your work on time. There are no lectures. Just readings that you have to analyze throughout the semester. Make sure to follow the rubric, but she will take random points off for things that weren't in the rubric.

Dr. Atabay is passionate about teaching others about the middle east. this class could have been really interesting but I did not care for the professor to much. My classmates and I always seemed to be confused on what we were doing because instructions were very broad. there are quite a few discussion papers that require a lot of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Atabay was really invested in the material covered in the course, she really loves speaking about the Middle East and stereotypes related. I will say, I thought this class was going to go over culture and politics within the Middle East, but it kind of seemed like I should've had a background on it to participate. Prof was great though, kind.

In my experience I would find another IAH to take or a different professor. Dr. Atabay was only focused on reading and writing papers. She NEVER responds to emails. You can only miss two classes the whole semester before being advised to take it again. DON'T TAKE HER CLASS!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class was a lot more difficult than it should have been. We were expected to spend 12 hours a week outside of the class doing work. She is very picky about every little detail when grading writing assignments which are the only kind of assignments she gives by the way. I thought the topic would be interesting but she made it so boring!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is not worth taking for IAH credit THERE ARE SO MANY BETTER OPTIONS!!! She expects you to read an insane amount each week and there are 3 group presentations throughout the semester. She has never answered my emails and grades very hard. Pick another class! Attendance isn't necessarily mandatory but you can't miss every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I thought this class was going to be an overview of the Middle East (history and culture), but we focused on very specific topics and learned very little about the Middle East in general. The first 10 weeks of class are very essay and reading heavy, and then the last few weeks are more focused on group projects. Class discussions are also important
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I ended the class with a low 3.5 but Dr. Atabay curved it to an A!:) However, this class is essay heavy and she is a hard grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: WORST PROFESSOR !!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: All of your school work will be based on tough books and films. At least 30 pages per week. You MUST attend class. You only get four hours of absences and she uses participation as a major part of your grading. If you want a 4.0, attendance & active discussion is necessary. Her assignments are very subjective, 2 essays and 3 group projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is more than a good one;)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Pros: Willing to help you and won't punish you for being bad at the skills required for the class. She will actually try and help you understand what you need to work on to help you in the future. cons: The workload is extremely heavy. Lots of reading and writing. Finnish reading early. Start your work soon as you know the assignment.
Teacher answers all questions you have and really cares that a student does well.
She is way too demanding. I would NOT recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: She is an awesome professor, and very willing to help her students. I got a bad grade on one of my papers, and she let me re-write it at the end of the semester, even when she had a lot of things to grade. She really puts her students first, and the class was very alive and interesting.
She is a nice teacher but demanded a lot from her students.

Terrible. Too much work. She acts like its the only class we have and I just had a presentation to give today, I have two papers due within the next two weeks, and I have to read a whole book in that time too. The course information is interesting, but she is way too time consuming. I know it's 4 credits but I've never had a teacher give this much.
Learned a lot! She was friendly and very good at sparking conversation.
Excellent professor, and a wonderful kind person.
Love her! She's amazing and really goes out of her way to help students.

Madame Wolfgang is one of the kindest people I have ever met! Michigan State really is lucky to have her as a French professor. She is extremely accommodating and understanding and really makes an effort to know the entire class. Course expectations are very straightforward.

I love Professor Wolfgang! I really enjoyed seeing her each week; she made French oral expression tolerable and fun. She encouraged a community within our classroom, and created a safe and welcoming environment for everyone. She was also so generous and accommodating to us -- especially in stressful times during the course. A truly great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Very nice, caring, and accommodating. Encourages lots of participation for grade which can be nerve-wracking. Fair amount of reading and homework. Attendance is  required. Can be a little picky with grading homework. Easy exams, sometimes take home. Offers opportunities to drop absences. Will accept homework if not in class the day it's due.

I took his 111 a couple years ago, and I remember everyone being really scared of him, a couple people crying on different occasions, he said all our reading journals were "stolen", which is what he says every year. Despite all that, I actually learned a lot from him. I use the theories we read in almost every paper I write to this day. Cool guy.

I took Prof. Jacksons writing and research class that dealt with Black popular culture. Actually we could choose almost any research topic so long as it had something to do with social justice and race. I was overwhelmed by the different parts of the research paper but the individual and small group meetings helped a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Excellent professor. Lots of reading but much of it was interesting. Great class discussions about race, class, and social justice. I was overwhelmed by some of the assignments, especially the first paper about "American-ness." The small group work and one-on-one meetings with Austin were very useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I got a 3.5 in his 111. Frequently 15-20 minutes late to class. Didn't return papers until the last day of class. Very opinionated, to a fault. His assignments were very wordy and poorly worded. Have told my friends not to take his classes. The ones who didn't listen paid for it. I learned nothing about writing from his class... Don't take it

I recieved a 4.0, but the course was stressful and impossible to enjoy. Jackson never gave me feedback on my first essay, lost every single student's journal, and never even looked at my final paper that was 12 pages and took forever to write. He was late often. I loved the course's topic, but connot recommend it. Worst professor I have had
Straight up loved this class!  Because Austin was so into to material, it made it easier to focus.  Probably my favorite class I've ever taken.

If you read an autobiography read it as if you were of the same race and gender as the author. If you are reading history think about how it felt to be the person affected. These classes aren't about you. They are about the texts and real world applications. Talk to him when you do not understand he made me a better writer.

Austin is an amazing professor, and he really opened my eyes to a lot of stuff. If you're not comfortable talking about race, you will be by the end. He's a little intimidating in class, but outside of class he's really sweet - he admins like 5,000 student organizations. His essay prompts are really elaborate and confusing, though. Overall, great!
The best of the best. Very good teacher. Very helpful, grades fairly, keeps you engaged. Be sure to discuss, participation is graded.

By the way, to those poor sports writing here, I am a hardcore conservative, and I love Austin. In fact, it seems they are rather close-minded themselves - he's incredibly open to other opinions. As he said this term, the conservatives do the best - it's true. If you actually understand what you're arguing, not just propagandizing, he's great.

This man is an inspiration. Everyone's had those teachers in high school or profs in college who really changes the way they think, not just their short-term memory. Austin Jackson is one of those men. Some stupid people complain that he's biased, etc...no! the information is radical, and most students just want to spit out what they heard before.

This professor is not at all professional.  He should not be teaching at all.  He is biased, grades unfairly, is late to class often, doesn't maintain office hours, and treats students not on equal terms.

Austin is very opinionated, and if you agree with him in class and in your papers, it is very easy to get a 4.0.  Although I resented him a lot in the class because he wasn't open to other opinions (and I am a liberal!), I realized after the class was over that I really did learn a lot and it made me think differently about racism, ect.

if you are conservative DONT TAKE THIS CLASS. if you want to talk about racism and slavery and how white people are terrible and malcom X is the greatest then take it. He doesn't give back papers till the last day of class, doesn't help your writing skills AT ALL.

Agreeing with the person before me, if you want to vent about bush and racism, take this class... If you are not and value your GPA, dont take it because if you dont say what he wants to hear, your grades will be bad. Also, his directions are confusing as hell.. and his emails are even more confusings... if you take this, good luck...

If you are a Bush-bashing, left-winged, liberal looking to vent your opinions on racism to the world, this class is for you! If not? Run for the hills!  Austin looks for people to agree with him, and if you don't, it's impossible to get a good grade. He took 3 months to grade one paper! I learned nothing about writing in this class. What a joke!
the most ridiculous teacher i have ever had.  he tries to put WAY too much into one semester.  the course was very repetative, and likes if you have strong opinions

This class started out alright and he's got a good personality, but he doesnt really teach how to write, and even though he says he wants other opions, he really doesnt. If you write in your papers what he wants to hear he'll give you a 100%.His paper topics never make sence. Theory (institutional racism) of class gets old fast. easy 4.0 though.

I just dont like him much... Is that a bad thing? I did like him, really.. and then halfway through.. his liberalness got to me and the class changed from Evo. Of American Thought to Evolution of his liberal thoughts on racism and discrimination.

One of the best professors I have ever had and would definitely take a bullet for this man. 
He genuinely cares about his students and their success; often, he makes himself accessible to students after lectures to answer any additional questions. Outside of that, he is super laid-back and chill in both his teaching style and grading.
Very easy-going professor who sometimes even stays after class to make sure that you really understand the material.

A difficult course made enjoyable. By far the best professor I've ever had. Has an obvious passion and can teach difficult material in a way that makes sense. I personally never was stressed on a deadline. He is incredibly lenient and extends assignments based on factors many professors don't even consider. Cares about students.
I really enjoyed Ayman's lectures and I learned a lot in his class, I recommend him as a professor.

Inarguably one of the best professors I've had. I went into class looking to fulfill a language requirement and have left with an Arabic minor. I'm beyond excited to next semester! There's a lot of homework, but he's very good on grading. He makes the textbooks and curriculum, so he knows his shit. Overall, a great professor!

Absolutely amazing professor. Makes learning a tough language accessible and fun. The textbook that is used in the beginning of the course can be found online for free. Lots of homework in the beginning but drops off @ end. Probably my favorite professor I've ever had at MSU and I wish I could take more courses with him. Very funny and caring guy!

Professor Mohamed is honestly the best professor I have had at MSU. He truly cares about his students, and he works so hard to make sure you learn. He's incredibly understanding and truly wants you to do well. He's so good at making you more confident in your skills, although he will really push you. Every single one of us loves him.

Dr. Mohamed is truly my favorite professor!! Despite the circumstances, I never felt more connected with the professor and students than in this class! I can tell he is passionate about teaching the Arabic language and cares so much about his students!

Professor Ayman is my favorite professor!! He is incredibly sweet and caring towards each of his students and is very understanding. Although the material can get difficult sometimes, he is always willing to help both inside and outside of class. The class was taught extremely well even being online and it is definitely my most enjoyable class:))

This man is my favorite professor that I've had so far, he genuinely cares about your language acquisition and tries to make every class useful. I knew almost nothing of Arabic when I first started and he has helped me to be able to read and converse in simple ways. He's the best!!!
Best professor ever!!! He really cares about students and hes such a nice person. He is always available both inside and outside the classroom. I really enjoyed class with him.

This man has a HEART OF GOLD. The actual subject is difficult but Dr. Mohamed is a phenomenal teacher. He definitely cares about everyone and wants you to do well. He is easily one of my all time favorite teachers. To do well in this class, you NEED to show up, and do the textbook reading and listening. Get ready to speak a LOT in class.

Ayman is amazing, 11/10 prof. He is super understanding that the language is hard and genuinely wants his students to succeed. He also did a really good job of proctoring an online class in a way that felt personal. Homework is necessary for learning the material but it's not overly difficult!!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Learning Arabic is super difficult and Professor Mohamed puts in a lot of time to making sure you understand the material. He's a very lenient grader as long as it's clear you're making an effort and is very helpful. Definitely one of the best professors I've had at MSU.

This man is the light of my life. He cares about everyone in his classes so much and is very flexible on due dates if you talk to him. He will grade you easier if you participate in class and turn in all your homework. Once he gave me credit for a conversation hour when I played Arabic hangman for an hour instead. He's a saint.

Yo, this man is the best. He is a gentle grader, because Arabic is hard af, but if you dont know anything, dont expect to pass. Hes funny, but v quiet, but its good. Hes the best ever, and I dont know a single person who has taken his class and wouldnt take a bullet for him

SWEETEST MAN ALIVE!! He is so cute (such a dad) and teaches Arabic so well. He grades pretty leniently because he knows how tough the language is but he also makes sure we learn our stuff. He's very quiet (kind of mysterious) and doesn't talk much but I would take a bullet for this man.
Honestly the best TA I have ever had. She made going to class worth it and I enjoyed every lecture. Professor A puts effort into being engaging and she is very funny.
Amazing Professor. She is super kind and down to earth. All you need to do is show up and participate in the discussion and you'll do just fine! Probably the best TA I have had so far.

While I do genuinely believe that she is well-intentioned, Professor A is condescending and passive-aggressive towards her students. 
Her recitations are easy, and I think that she does care about her students' success, which is awesome. She just really needs to work on speaking to people in a kinder way if she wants to make it as a teacher.
Professor Ismail was amazing!! I would recommend her to anyone in the university. She was constantly kind and funny. 100% would take again.
She makes classes really fun, she's very honest and down to earth, and as long as you put effort into class you'll do good.

Dr. Thompson (as she prefers to be called) was so sweet and I loved listening to her lectures. The course was relatively easy and even if you didn't go to class, you could just read the book and 4.0. I would recommend everyone take psychology of women with Dr. Thompson! It opened my mind so much and she gave such great insight.

I LOVED psy 101 and Dr. Aymor. If you do all of the assignments, required research hours, and understand the content to succeed on the closed note exams, you will 4.0 the class. This class is effort based. What you put in is what you will get out. If you go to class and take notes and study you will be fine. The workload was not bad at all.

If you're thinking about taking a class with Professor Aymor, do it! She's hands down one of the best professors at Michigan State, and it's clear that she genuinely cares about her students. If you're communicative with her, she's more than willing to make accommodations for you. In addition, the content that she teaches is incredibly interesting!

I had Dr. Thompson for PSY101, and while I wasn't a fan of some of the content, I really liked her as a professor! She made accommodations for students who did not want to do in-person recitations, and she had clear expectations. Also the final exam was optional, which was pretty cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easy class, but not the most interesting. You get a 3% boost in your total grade for perfect attendance, there's plenty of extra credit, and exams are based off of practice problems (at least 50% the same). Cheat sheet & calculator for all exams. I didn't learn anything new from 3 months of statistics from high school algebra 2.

While she is a very friendly person, she is a terrible teacher. I don't know how the university would allow her to teach. She is very difficult to understand because she has a strong accent. On top of that, she does not know how to explain concepts at all.

Prof Alin is a very very nice lady and she loves what she does. She comes into class smiling and will ask everyone how their day has been. She is Turkish and has a very strong accent. She tends to take the old fashioned or longer route to solving problems and doesnt  know how to use a calculator. Shes always there to help. She gives random EC.

This class is TA heavy. However, Prof Az. is a cool guy! You can pretty much walk into his office to talk whenever. He is a friendly guy. He is super accommodating if you want to switch around your section/TA, or if you have issues within your lab group. Noting but smiles from him!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Like alot of reviews say, the class is heavily TA graded. Your sections TA grades all but two labs, so if you have a chill TA the class is pretty easy, despite how disorganized and vague some of the labs are. Azadnia only grades the green chem project at the end of the semester, and gives mostly everyone a 100. He also responds to quick to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His TAs teach the material better than him, but you need to go to lectures to "know what you don't know" in order to get help from TAs. The TAs will also give you hints before quizzes. Don't get textbook. Do the labs, they are free points and easy. If you aren't understanding materials, recitation and office hours with TA will get you a good grade.
Flew through the lectures and the material kind of jumped around. He got frustrated when students weren't comprehending the material.

Really easy to talk to and was very understanding about timing and difficulties. Let me do a whole experiment the last two days of open lab. Quick replying to emails. Not very hands-on and you'll definitely work with your TA more than the instructor (as is normal).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I have not had a good experience with Dr. Azadnia regarding accommodating my disabilities. He is also difficult to communicate with via email (e.g., long response times, unclear responses).

Overall a great professor. He has weekly labs due which are not difficult, just time consuming due every Sunday. The TAs grade your labs, but most of them are easy graders and dont knock off too many unnecessary points. His lectures are very clear and he guides you on how to do the labs. Do you work, and you should receive an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. A is very clear about his expectations. I took the course online so I didn't really gain any knowledge from it but that wasn't his fault. He was not very in touch with the students as the TA's do all of the grading, but he was kind enough to invite us to study in the lab with him in the future because he felt bad we aren't learning properly.

Cool prof overall, but I don't want to say anything about grading because it really depends on your TA). Azadnia got back to emails in a timely manner, wasn't rude or condescending when answering questions, and told us what we needed in each section of our lab reports to get full credit.

He is one of the laziest professors I've ever had. He delegated most work to TA's that were obviously unprepared, and on top of that basically said to not ask him for points back on mis-graded assignments or he will go back and grade the whole thing and give you a worse grade 9 times out of 10. His laziness and unpreparedness is why he sucks.

Professor Azadnia is very friendly when you deal with him 1-on-1, but his lectures are super busy and hard to follow. I took this lab online during COVID and it honestly felt like the biggest waste of money and time. It was just copying down the lab from the lab manual and turning it in. This class would be much better in person.

He is funny and provided a lot of extra credit, although when we went online he canceled the final and replaced it with the extra credit assignment. The TA is who grades your assignment so your fate is ultimately in their hands, not a bad lab though. I never went to recitation and ended up being fine, but if you need help understanding, go I guess

The class is really led by TAs since it is a lab, so make sure you know what your TA expects. Some of them are better than others. Dr. Azadnia lectures during the recitation time, and this is helpful for the labs & learning about extra credit opportunities. This class is straightforward but will require some effort if labs aren't your thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Go to recitation every week because the final is all random/difficult things he says during recitation (it usually is shorter than 50 mins). Just work with your team and ask TAs for help if you ever need help. A couple of graded labs (accuracy) but most are not based on accuracy. Do the extra credit at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Azadnia is a good professor. He really sets the class up so his students will do well. A 50% is a 2.0 so he really wants his students to pass. There are a ton of points in this class and you get to drop an exam making it EASY TO 4.0. Just study a lot for the first two exams and you will be fine. Also go to the help room it does help!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I would never take another class with him again. Continuously lectured for 5 minutes past the scheduled time, made important announcements well after class had ended. Taught though examples which is not effective in chemistry since there are endless possible reactions. Rushed through all the material. Not an effective professor and inadequate.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very nice and interesting guy. Took CEM 355 and CEM 356 with him. He is always in his office ready to help if you need assistance with lab projects. But overall, try and get a good TA and you won't have to worry about orgo lab classes

Several labs are graded by the purity of the product you synthesize in lab, so get a good TA while you can, or switch to a good one immediately. No need to go to Thursday lecture, the slides are always posted. Pretty easy labs, but pay attention in CEM 252, a lot of those reactions make up the labs in CEM 255.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you struggle with big university-style lectures like me, the summer course-though more challenging-is a great way to get some personal attention. His analogies were sometimes confusing but usually hilarious and made the content easier to remember. He really cares about his students!

I took it over the summer and i would strongly recommend it. He made sure everyone was understanding the material and since it was a smaller class size he could go around and actually help you during class.
Took Org 2 over the summer with him. Spent every day after class getting stuff clarified. He was awesome and patient and speaks a mean Farsi.

Best supply chain professor. Super engaging, fair, and although the course isn't super hard, I feel like I learned a lot. His D2L is so much more organized than other SCM professors I've had who tend to be bad. GOAT Barker

This guy is the GOAT. His D2L is probably the most useful I've seen for any supply chain class and because of that it's not too difficult to do the homework or study. Dude is also hilarious and cares about you far more than the average prof.
GOAT Barker. Bro would be the next transformers.

Super funny and enthusiastic professor, which is hard to do for a logistics class. Course was organized well and there's 3 exams + optional final. Only 3 assignments and 3 quizzes. Attendance is part of the grade. He was always available for questions and extra help and his exams were somewhat difficult but fair. Take 373 with him!

Professor Barker is the BEST PROFESSOR I'VE EVER HAD!!! Truly a hilarious dude and you can tell he cares about every single person in his class. I wish I could take his class over and over again. The lectures are very entertaining and he uses a lot of jokes. Take his class, you won't regret it. The best prof I've had in all my 4 years of college.

I did not interact much with him due to this being an online course, but IAH 241A was a very easy 4.0 due to the way he structured it! It was online asynchronous and I could usually finish the entire unit within a day, maybe two if the writing assignment was longer. All in all an easy class with a professor who was pretty lenient.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Took IAH 241A with prof Bartig, great class with interesting material. Hes was really helpful when help was needed!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Bazgir made the class way too easy with the amount of extra credit he handed out. But it's hard to learn from him since he just gives the answers to everything rather than actually teaching. Also skipped spectroscopy completely last semester (just emailed everyone and said "study it on your own").

No feedback on exams (makes it impossible to tell what did you get wrong since you can't even access the blank exam afterwards). Posts some video lectures the day before the exam. Midterm 2 is a cumulative exam which makes no sense. Lots of extra credit so people tend to like him.

The best chemistry professor I have had in my 4 years here. Lecture isn't required but I would recommend still going because he explains things in ways that make it so much easier to understand. Quizzes and exams are open note/you get a cheat sheet and it's basically impossible to fail this class.

Bazgir is an amazing professor, and is truly the only reason I did so well in Orgo. With every lecture, he made them entertaining and engaged with the class, always making sure that you understand the material before moving on. If you have the chance, take Ayoob Bazgir!
Very interesting class. Professor is chill and relaxed, and content material is very easy. Would definitely recommend!
Great professor! explains organic chemistry in a simple way that allows everyone to understand! gives a lot of extra credit!

He makes chemistry so easy with his comparisons to real-world analysis. He truly wants all his students to see how complex concepts can be broken down in simple ways. He allows students to engage during lectures free of shame. He makes funny jokes and does call-and-responses so we all stay engaged. 10% EC boost to your grade. Everyone loves him

I would go to war for him
- gives a lot of extra credit
- extra tries on the hw if you ask
- he will help on quizzes and tests
- he wants you to pass

Great prof, lots of opportunities for extra credits, I got a OK Exams and quizzes but bcs I did all the hws and extra credits, which you got tons of time for btw, and I got a 4.0. If you miss his lectures, the video lecture are still great and they are not too long. Most lectures he also lets you leave early which is great. great prof, good man.

Professor Bazgir is very knowledgeable and offers many resources to for you to succeed in his class. Although I would still recommend studying with peers outside of class often. His grading is forgiving, since he allows retakes for many quizzes and takes your highest grade out of the two attempts.

Dr. Bazgir is an excellent professor. His lectures are very engaging and full of examples to help solidify content understanding. Apart from his office hours, he is also always happy to accommodate if you have questions or want to meet in-person. Lots of opportunities for extra credit. Overall, a great experience.

He is very kind and curves grades/gives extra credit based off of the class's needs. I had around a 75% in the class but ended up with a 100% because of how much extra credit he gave out. His lectures are engaging and he provides the lectures online as well. The subject itself is hard but Dr. Bazgir helped me understand a lot about orgo chem.

I was super scared to take orgo, but Ayoob made it so easy. He explains everything clearly and reviews past content at the beginning of lectures. 8am lectures with attendance not required, but I still went.  Activ takes a while to get the hang of, but there's also 10% (or more) extra credit offered. Needed 24% on the final to 4.0. Highly recommend!
Incredible

He explained things really well and made it so easy to be able to learn from. If you miss a lecture he has them all recorded and posted on D2L so you don't miss anything. He gives so much practice and help, especially with recitations as well. You also get extra credit options! Super helpful professor and good at teaching.

He's the goat, lecture is worth going to even though the slides are posted. There are so many resources available to practice and the class is structured to be very forgiving with make up quizzes and EC, will be taking him again for Orgo 2

Prof. Bazgir is a great professor and clearly wants his students to succeed. While his accent at times makes it difficult to understand lectures, he is always happy to take questions during lecture and even helps during quizzes. I am not a good chemistry student so the multiple extra credit opportunities and easy homework was a grade-saver.

Prof. Bazgir is a great professor and clearly knows the material and wants to see his students succeed. The homework and extra credit assignments saved my grades. I am not a good chemistry student and I was very surprised at the amount of care Bazgir puts into answering students' questions, even during quizzes or after exams.
Lecture can be a bit fast but he posts video lectures online so you can go over it. Overall if you try somewhat the class is very manageable.
Very good lectures and professor. If you attend class and try to understand, you will do good.

He is very lecture heavy, go to the lectures and make sure you understand, as while he moves on quickly, he will go over it as many times as you need during class if you have questions. He also has recorded lectures available, but I don't find them to be as helpful as going to class. He is always very engaging and truly wants you to succeed!
Best teacher to take for orgo makes the class feel like a breeze and teaches it perfectly also makes it very clear what will be on the exam and gives you materials for it.

Dr Bazgir is the best professor at MSU, hands down! He gives his class amiable opportunities to succeed by offering a ton of extra credit and quiz retakes. Even if Dr. Bazgir gave us 0 extra credit and no quiz retakes, it would still be easy to 4.0 the class due to the engaging way he teaches the class. It is semi-impossible to do bad in his class.

one of the best teachers i have had at MSU. I had Dr. Bazgir for both Orgo1 and orgo 2 and struggled a lot in the beginning but he was always very patient and didnt mind re-explaining things 30 different times lol. i am not the best in chem but i remember so much from his classes ! if you put in the work, his classes are an easy 4.0 and he gives ec
Amazing teacher for orgo. His lectures and slides makes organic chemistry much easier to understand. Would highly recommend taking him if you can.

Ayoob is a great professor and his lectures are always interesting; I always came even though attendance wasn't mandatory. There is lots of extra credit, making it fairly easy to 4.0 if you don't do well on exams. He always reviews content at the beginning of lecture before starting new material which I found very helpful.

Ayoob is hands down the best professor at MSU. 4.0'd both Orgo I and II because of him. He offers tons of extra credit, gives engaging and fun lectures, and truly wants you to do well. You have to put the effort forth, but you will do well if you do. I wouldn't take orgo with anyone else!

AYOOB IS MY MAN. I 4.0d easily in orgo 1&2 bc of this blessing of a man. He's my favorite professor I've ever had. Very loved by his students. Offers so much extra credit I had to get a 20% on the final to 4.0. Lectures are funny and engaging. Requires effort but that is normal, the bad reviewers are the people who expect to 4.0 without any effort.

Prof. Bazgir was one of the best professors I've had here. He made orgo 2 so easy with all of the extra credit he offered and his great lectures. I took orgo 1 online and was nervous about taking 2 in person but it was the best choice I could've made.

I LOVE AYOOB!!! SO much EC offered because he simply wants you to do well in this course. Lectures are posted online so if you miss a class you can get caught up (or never go to class if you want to). Always posts practices before the exams as well as videos. Learn the different reactions and you should do great!

I had Dr. Bazgir for orgo 1 and 2. I absolutely would recommend him to anyone! He taught the material is a very straightforward manner, reviewed content during the lecture before the exam, answered all my questions during office hours, and offered tons of extra credit. He absolutely wants his students to succeed. 10/10 recommend!!

Take Ayoob for orgo, and nobody else. his 8am lectures both semesters are the only 8am classes I've ever taken, only because I actually loved the class. Orgo is notoriously a weeder class but NOT Ayoobs class. You will learn the material so well and enjoy it. This might be a hot take but general chem was harder than his classes. Take his class!
Great lectures, lots of in-class examples on the chalkboard, much extra credit, great at explaining complex concepts simply, and overall a chill dude.

He genuinely wants his students to succeed. He gives so many opportunities for extra credit and ways to boost your grade. If you don't understand a topic talk to him and he will take the time to explain until it makes sense.

Bazgir is a great Prof. If you can get him for organic chem, do it. Helped me 4.0, available outside of class and always willing to re-explain concepts. Made material feel easy. Straight forward with concepts so they were easy to get. Lots of extra credit and online assessments.

This guy is one of the best professors I've ever had. Breaks down Orgo very well and provides plenty of resources to learn inside and outside of class. Very funny and plenty of extra credit opportunities which make the class lower stress. Genuinely sad that the class is over. The Persian Prince is the professor to take Orgo I and II with.

WORTH TAKING THE 8AM FOR! He offers lots of extra credit as the class is only a few hw grades, 4 quizzes, the 2 midterms and final. His class is all lectures (with slides posted) and he posts recorded lectures online. He is very funny and tries to keep the students engaged during class. I would highly recommend, ONE OF THE BEST PROFS AT MSU.

WORTH TAKING THE 8AM FOR! Ayoob loves to teach and is very funny during lectures, but he also posts them online so you don't even need to go. There is SO MUCH EXTRA CREDIT, no one should pass with less than a 4.0 imo. He wants everyone to do good and he makes it very easy to; I would highly recommend him for Orgo 1 and 2. He is a great caring prof!
Organic chemistry goat. TAKE HIM IF YOU NEED TO TAKE ORGO.

Beware of his accent for some people that can be a game changer. He likes to move on from information fast without much context other than writing it on the board only to erase it 2 minutes later. If the material was taught different with more consideration for the students I feel like I would've done better.

reviews.comment:
This professor truly wants everyone to succeed. Homework is what you see on quizzes, quizzes are almost exactly what you see on the exams. overall a really good professor. Do the homework, learn how to do it the other ways (where the answer becomes the question). Learn that, you'll be just fine. 
(for reference, I failed CEM 141)
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is literally the GOAT, make sure you take him for orgo!

You are making a mistake by taking any other orgo prof. This guy made orgo genuinely an enjoyable class. He is super funny, makes things really easy to understand (his accent is thick but easy to understand after a lecture or two), super accessible and you cant get any bettwe grading in any other class. 4.0 is extremely achievable. TAKE HIS CLASS!

One of the best professors I've ever had. Funny, but watch out for small details on quizzes and exams! Neither class nor recitation is mandatory (and he posts shortened lectures online), but I highly recommend going. Recitations are also bonus points for attending. All my extra credit meant I only needed 45% on the final instead of 87% for a 4.0!

Dr. Bazgir is a fantastic professor and extremely likable. Makes lectures extremely enjoyable and understandable. Orgo is hard no matter what professor you have but he tries his hardest to make sure everyone understands the content. Very easy to 4.0 as well since he gives out so much extra credit.

There aren't many grades that he puts in, just tests and quizzes. However, he hands out extra credit like it's candy. He also records lectures, which is helpful when you don't want to drag yourself to the 8 a.m. lecture. Overall, he is good at teaching the concepts.

Great Professor. He makes the class lighthearted and fun, and gives a LOT of extra credit, making a difficult subject more manageable. His accent is a bit thick, so it may be a challenge if you struggle with that, but it's honestly easy to get used to. Definitely taking him again for orgo 2!
THIS MAN IS A HERO! Please take him when you take organic chemistry, you will be glad you did!

I enjoyed your lectures a lot, it was easy and understandable to follow along. I know that I skipped one of the lectures, but I'm glad you posted it online, if we couldn't make it to class, because personally for me I would get stressed out if I didn't know what we are covering. I utilized the office hours you held (thanks to one of my friends)!

The Michael Jordan of Organic Chemistry at MSU. Dr. Bazgir is an amazing guy, hilarious lecturer, constantly available outside class and makes Organic digestible and understandable. The only knock on him is that he gave out so much extra credit it almost led me not to learn the material, but if you study out of class it's just more of a boost.

Professor Bazgir is by far the best prof I have ever had. Orgo is hard, but he makes it as easy and understandable, and as a plus, he is hilarious. He offers plenty of extra credit and wants you to do well - always available outside of class. Looking forward to 252 with him, I would only take this class with him if at all possible.

My glorious Persian king, my all-time goat, I cannot stress how much I recommend taking 251 with Dr. Bazgir. As other reviews have mentioned, he provides plenty of extra credit in his class. Additionally, he is super accessible outside of lectures and generally responds to emails within an hour or less in my experience.

My persian prince. He is literally the best orgo professor you can have. Do not listen to the 1/5 person, clearly they did not gaf about their grades because if they actually took the time to listen they wouldn't even need the extra credit. He lets you leave for the quizzes and their online. ASK HIM QUESTIONS ON EXAMS!!

Dr. Bazgir is a really good professor and his lectures are really concise and easy to follow. He gives out lots of extra credit (+1 for every recitation attended, +50 for practice problems) and is very easy to reach outside of class despite having hundreds of students. Highly recommend taking this class, he makes Orgo easy and understandable.

Dr. Bazgir is a really funny professor, and he takes time to explain everything in depth. His accent is a little heavy, however, it's understandable enough to get a great grade in the class. He provided so much extra credit during the class time that it literally could've "erased" a bombed midterm from your grades.
Best professor at MSU. Truly loves his job and is freaking hilarious. Makes Orgo easy. So much extra credit and exams are easy. GOAT.

Honestly, best prof I've had here, I'm even taking him again next semester for 252. Posts all lectures online so you don't technically have to go to class, and offers a ton of EC. He is very funny in lecture and is always available to help. Homework is graded on accuracy, but you have 3-6 attempts/question depending on the assignment.

BEST PROF EVER. love this man. I was so scared for organic chemistry but he makes it so easy. I genuinely understand everything from his lectures and the homework was not bad at all. 20 questions for each chapter and there is 50 points EC. He's also hilarious and made me laugh in my 8 am lecture. Don't take this class unless he is your professor.

This is the best professor at msu. Organic is such a hard class, but this professor is funny and so smart. He has an accent, but you get used to it very fast. The material is hard but there is so much extra credit that makes a huge difference in your grade. I cannot explain how good of a professor he is and can't wait to take him again. #Ayoobontop

Bazgir is very knowledgeable and he is just a great professor. Some people complain about his accent, but it's actually pretty easy to understand him. Just show up to lecture and you can easily get a 3.5 or above since he gives out lots of extra credit. Not too much homework, just 4 quizzes and a few tests. He also has a good sense of humor. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor ever
He gave a lot of extra credit and had very good detailed lectures, he also was helpful and accomodating.

Ayoob is the best. Chemistry really isn't my forte and I was scared out of my wits about taking orgo, but Ayoob really makes it easy to understand. He really wants you to succeed in his class. Gives out extra credit no problem. Makes sure to poll the class for questions, if any, after he explains a part of the topic being covered. He's also funny.
Chemistry is hard but Bazgir will go out of his way to help! He is absolutely the best prof!

Professor Bazgir is great! Recorded lectures, lecture slides, practice problems, & exam reviews are all on D2L. The grade is 4 quizzes, 2 midterms, final exam, & Aktiv homework. He is very accommodating to students & offers many extra credit opportunities. Although there is a lot of difficult material in orgo, he does not try to "trick" students.

Very easy professor but leads me to not remember the material or even learn it. Gave around 11% of the total grade as extra credit for CEM 252 and rounded by CEM 251 grade by like 5% with a lot of extra credit on top of that.

Professor Bazgir is your best bet at understanding organic chemistry. A professor can only lead you so far, but Bazgir is understanding and is always willing to reexplain topics and gives good examples during office hours. Orgo is difficult, especially as a first-gen student where you lack a lot of connections and experience. In short; TAKE HIM.

Had him for two semesters and I think he is a gift to chemistry. Makes lectures available online, in case if you want to sleep in (I have the 8m). Funny guy who makes me want to come to lecture and learn. 100/10.

I love Professor Bazgir! I was intimidated taking Orgo 1 at first but he takes the time to answer questions, re-explain topics, gives many examples, and gives many practice problems. I have also heard his office hours were very helpful which I regret not taking advantage of. I am taking him again for Orgo 2!

I loved Prof. Bazgir. His lectures were well organized and his quizzes accurately tested the material. Prof. is caring and easy to communicate with. He responds to emails quickly and is understanding.

I took CEM 251 with him and am not in 252 with him as well. He covers what we need to know and does so in a concise manner. He (and his TA's) is/are accessible outside of class to help students. Go to office hours if you need it and you will be able to succeed. One of my favorite classes and had great instruction!
This professor really does care about getting us through the class. Lots of opportunities for extra credit which was great. Overall very nice and caring.

Professor Bazgir was good. You can tell that he cares greatly for his students and genuinely wants you to succeed. However, orgo itself is difficult so go to class!! He does have a thick accent, but if you pay attention, you can understand what is going on. I'd also reccommend that you buy the orgo for dummies book; it pairs well with this class.

Did it in-person. If possible, do it online (all their assessments are online).Our quizzes were accessible online but the midterm and final were in person. Based off of the original syllabus few people were on track to 4.0, but last 2 weeks he decided to: drop 2 instead of 1 quiz, give retakes, 20 extra credit hw, 10 point final curve + cheat sheet

I personally loved ayyob. he was incredibly kind, if you send him an email he responds quickly. he allowed me to make up a quiz i missed and clearly wants students to succeed. orgo 1 is a lot of content and fast paced, and ayoob has a thick accent and is not tech savvy at all. offers extra credit and is overall a great guy

reviews.comment: lots of extra credit opportunities that arent listed in the syllabus. gives great feedback for honours projects
