reviews.comment: He honestly isn't a terrible professor. Content moves very quickly, and there's a lot to cover in a short period of time, but when he isn't rushing, he does break things down in a way that is mostly understandable. I did have to YouTube a lot of the content to truly understand it though. He did offer extra credit to help grading.

Lectures are boring and a bit of a struggle to focus with just going from slides to slides. He was very kind to his students and understanding and gave retakes and extra credit he does not want his students to fail. Although his accent can be difficult from time to time and unclear what he is teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I would recommend not taking organic chemistry with Ayoob. This class caused so much stress for no reason as the language barrier and thick accent meant that I could not fully follow his lectures. Additionally he would state things such as "just don't fail" or post a pdf with every student's midterm score.

This class was hard but Dr. Bazgir was a good professor who wanted everyone to succeed. He records his lectures and posts it with the slides, he offered a lot of extra credit, offers retakes, and drops a lot of grades. The lecture slides can be a little confusing and there is not a lot of practice so I recommend reading the textbook.

Dr. Bazgir is very knowledgeable, but can be hard to approach. Few things are graded; chapter HWs (8), 4 out of 6 quizzes, midterm, and final. Extra credit was given towards the end of the course to boost grades. He can be hard to understand at times, but usually repeats himself in lecture. Lots of studying on your own, not much to practice with.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ayoooooooooooooooooob!!!!!!! Great slides, he also posts online lectures and gives extra credit.
Professor Bazgir is a great guy, and very responsive. Lectures are good and answer questions you are confused about. drops 2 lowest quizzes, homework is worth points

I give all the props to Dr. Bazgir as he tried to make the class understandable, however I found myself constantly lost with nowhere to turn to. He was nice at rescheduling a few quizzes that took place during a test for another class. However, the homework is not like the tests and the midterm + final is worth 55% of your final grade.

Dr. Bazgir is definitely a knowledgeable professor. He responds back to emails relatively quickly and his helpful answering questions. Lectures are extremely long and heavy and his slides/notes are quite disorganized. His explanations are also quite short and he moves through notes very quickly. Dedicate lots of time to this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hes my sweet prince. Made Orgo the easiest class ever, IDEK how. If you have to take orgo, take it with Ayoob or don't take it all. WE LOVE AYOOB!!!!!!!!!!!

Dr. Bazgir is an amazing professor. He is extremely kind, caring and fair. He gives out a ton of extra credit to help relieve the stress of the class. He explains the concepts very well in lecture, but also has super helpful Office hours where he will help with anything. The lectures are not mandatory, but I highly recommend going!!

Whenever i emailed him about a quiz question i didn't understand why i got wrong, he emailed me back almost always within an hour, with an explanation and images to help me. He was very good in lecture and would even demonstrate stereochemistry to us with molecules. he even would say funny things during class and even get the class to laugh at 8am

Dr. Bazgir breaks down confusing topics into more understandable material. However, good luck if you have any questions because he does not understand how to answer them. Exams are heavily weighted and there's only 2 of them!! Get ready to put time into this class.

Super clear and concise teaching and makes sure to go over things many times so you understand. Graded on 2 exams, 4/6 of the quizzes, and 20 homework questions every other week or so. Recitation is optional and they provide the questions from that for practice. He did provide extra credit at the end of the semester. Final is cumulative

Dr. Bazgir was one of my favorite professors. Warning, he does have an accent that makes it difficult to understand him at times but you get used to it. He is amazing at explaining concepts and tries his best to help you pass.

Ayoob has a heavy accent and is not tech savvy. There are only 2 exams and are heavily weighted. They are also not like the hw or quizzes. He will add more slides to the lecture and not say anything and you will scramble to find it. He does not take questions often and be ready to receive sass. He is funny, but the lectures are draining and a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Bazgir's class is straightforward. If you just show up to lectures you should be able to get a B. Some concepts can be unclear but if you go to office hours he will explain until you understand. Quiz retakes and Extra credit are offered but they aren't mentioned in the syllabus. He is very knowledgeable and actually cares about your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: heavy accent and fast lectures makes it harder to understand but if you ask questions he goes step by step until you get it. Go to office hours he will make sure you get hw correct

He has a very thick accent which makes it hard to understand his lectures. you will end up teaching yourself from the textbook. The grading is odd and there are only quizzes and few homework sets. He speeds very fast over important topics but his slides break them down to an easier level.

Go to his office hours(OH) & ask questions! He will help you with the homework problems at OH until you get it right, he cares a lot and is willing to help you. He simplifies hard topics very well. He tends to go fast in lectures and has an accent but he records lectures from the online class so you can watch those! Very kind, funny, and easygoing
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: lectures are very fast and confusing. The exams are harder than any of the reviews and quizzes. You are better off self teaching the materials than going to any lecture. To his credit though, I do believe that Prof Bagzir understands this and provides a very lenient grading scale.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Breezes over very complex and difficult topics too quickly. Doesn't explain very well. Heavy accent doesn't help either. If he slowed down it might be better. He posts the lectures which helps if you didn't pick something up in lecture. Orgo is hard no matter what but with this prof you will prob be watching a lot of youtube vids for help.

Organic chemistry is naturally going to be hard. The professor does have a thick accent and when you space out, it can be easy to miss the things he's saying. However, his explanations are good and digestible when you focus in lecture. Lectures for his online section are also recorded and uploaded, making it easy to find anything you miss.

He is quite hard to understand which wouldn't be a problem if he didn't speak so fast. He goes through very advanced topics too fast and to brief to for anyone to understand. 90% of your learning in this class will be through the text book or youtube. He is a good guy and he isn't bad. Just not very effective in lectures.

Horrible. You can NOT understand a thing he is saying. He has a very heavy accent, which makes it very difficult when trying to learn complex chemistry concepts. He does not care about learning. When students tried to ask question, he would ignore them. He is not tech savvy. He did not understand how to correctly post content online.

At first attending his lectures I had no idea what he was saying because of his accent but he really cares about his students. I asked him to record his lectures and that helped a TON. He can make very complex things become simplified and he even helped me gain some researchers when I asked him for help. Also go to his office hours I swear it helps

Literally, just pay attention. I get the feeling a lot of students may not pay attention because of his accent. If you pay attention, you will realize his explanations are very easy to understand. It's organic chemistry so obviously expect to put in some time outside of lecture as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: this man... oh god. in addition to being difficult to understand surface level, the man never explains ANYTHING. there is also no T.A.s like im sorry WHAT. a girl tried to ask a question and he signaled her to lower her hand because he doesnt take questions... save yourself.

This professor has the ability to simplify complex topics so students can understand and truly cares about the success of students. The practice problems and quizzes matched perfectly with the exams, and there were never any surprises. I took this class accelerated in 6 weeks instead of 16 and it was an easy 4.0.
She is the best professor I had my freshman year. She is very caring and wants to see her students succeed. She is very flexible with grades.

TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! She is so nice and always cares for her students. She is very accessible outside of class and responds to emails very fast. She uses a sheet of paper to mark attendance and it does not matter if you are a couple minutes late to class. Would take her again and am convinced that she is the best teacher of this subject. Grade-100%

Barb was a great professor. She really understands her students and the amount of work we have to do. We had deadlines on papers but she always moved them to about a week later. She took out a whole assignment because she thought we didnt have time. Definitely take her hybrid class, there was minimal work. And the papers were not even that long.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you can, take the hybrid class because I do not see the point of going to a two hour writing class twice a week with the work that she assigns to us. Everything is very straight forward and most of her unit schedules are clear. I disliked how our assignments kept getting pushed back and things were graded late. She rarely responds to emails.

We love Barb. Easily one of the best professors Ive had. She's super nice and understanding about any questions you might have. Deadlines aren't that important, as long as you send an email and ask for an extension, you'll get one. Not a harsh grader. Would 100% take a class with Barb again.
Not very accessible out of class. Very nice and lenient at times, but grading criteria is not as clear as it could be.
Barb is the best professor, extremely caring, and really enthusiastic. This has been one of my favorite classes to take.

Barb is the best, she'll work with you to make sure you do well and lets you know exactly what she's looking for with each assignment. DEFINITELY take WRA 101 with Barb!!!

Best professor ever! Really funny and really easy

Barb is seriously awesome.  She is in her office often and is always super helpful. Rarely gives homework.  Papers are given with more than enough time to complete. Definitely one of the best teachers in the university.
Barb is Awesome!

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. take any other class or switch your major, seriously. In my four years of undergrad I have never had a worse teacher. An EMBARRASSMENT to the university.

class should be renamed psychological torture 390
seriously find any other class to satisfy the credit. any. other. class.

Do not take any of this man's classes. Thinks he is "generous" while doing the bare minimum. Awful lecturer, awful human. Avoid at all costs, if this class is required: switch majors. Seriously, don't take

Do not take this class, or any of this man's classes. He is an awful professor who honestly acts like he wants you to bad. He is a staunch grader that won't round even at a .01%. Professor Barondess was an incredible instructor for spring 23. He understood and accommodated to the struggles of the semester. As god is my witness I almost jumped off the red cedar of how annoying this professor is at being off-topic while at the same time only having 4 exams that are insanely difficult. reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

Very rude and passive aggressive. Don't bother asking questions, because she won't give you an answer. Averages for all exams are 60% and she does nothing to help it. Take any other professor.
YOU WILL NEED TO RETAKE THIS COURSE IF YOU HAVE HER. VERY PASSIVE AGGRESSIVE. NOT UNDERSTANDING. NOT HELPFUL

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

she is very blunt and doesnt understand that for many students, this is their first time doing most of these experiments and expects everyone to understand the material just as well as her, also not great at giving constructive feedback and most assignments are graded harshly

Dr. Barnard is one of the most caring and respectable professors I know. Actually worst teacher I have ever taken

Dr. Barnard makes me want to jump into the Red Cedar. I think she made it her personal challenge to make her lab room as uncomfortable as possible. Barnard was never moving in the best interest of her students. she says if youre sick stay home... NEVER miss one of her labs. will probably ruin your grade. don't even bother asking her questions either- she will just belittle you or your group. rely on your ULA's.

Please listen to the reviews that say not to take this woman. I had her for lab & lecture. Was by far the worst teacher I've had with the worst attitude I've ever seen. Poop teacher. Condescending not helpful. Take some1 else.

In my opinion, Dr. Barnard was very condescending when I asked questions. The test are very hard, but I would suggest going to the LA's office hours because they are definitely the most helpful. I think the only reason I did somewhat okay in this class was because of the LAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Make sure to use the lecture slides as your primary study guide. If it showed up in the slides, it can be on the test! reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: To do well in this class you have to make sure you are understanding everything presented in the lectures as Dr. B goes through them. It was an easy A putting in the time starting 2 weeks before the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: At first, Dr. B may not be totally likable but she is very genuine if you put in the effort to get to know her. reviews.comment: A great professor- doesn't deserve the hate. Her class is tough, but the difficulty helps you learn the material better in the end. She is more helpful outside the classroom, so go to her office hours as much as possible. She is super down-to-earth and passionate abt chem! I highly recommend Dr. Barnard if you're a first year Briggs student!

reviews.comment: Dr. Barnard was a great teacher and is very passionate about chemistry. Her lectures are fast paced, so you have to keep up, but she explains concepts well and uses many analogies. reviews.comment: Chemistry is a very hard subject but she does her best to break down the material so it is easier to understand. She is very passionate about her job and it shows through her teaching. I would highly recommend her if you're a first year Briggs student.

Dr. Barnard is amazing! She is always pleasant in lecture and is extremely helpful outside of class too. It is a Briggs class so it is expected that it will be more difficult than standard university chemistry. She emphasizes the "why" to chemistry, not just the "what," which is extremely useful for future classes if you are a science major.

Dr. Barnard is a overall good professor. The content in chemistry can be difficult and she tries her best to teach it during lectures. Definitely take advantage of going to office hours if you need help! She also sometimes gives out a few extra credit points on exams which is a plus. If you put the work in you can easily get a 4.0.

Dr. Barnard is by far one of my favorite professors in Lyman Briggs. The content itself is challenging, but it's standard between all the chemistry professors. As long as you put the effort in (actually try), you can 4.0 the course. If you need help, see her during her office hours! Do not wait. She is extremely friendly and willing to help you.

I think she's a good lecturer and a pretty lenient professor overall. She is understanding and flexible to her students. badly organized, boring lectures

Obviously takes her research more seriously than teaching. Class was very poorly organized. Obviously takes her research more seriously than teaching. Class was very poorly organized. Worst most difficult professor to work with. Will not admit mistakes. Holds students to a higher standard then she is capable of attaining. Do not take any classes with this professor.

The workload is fairly balanced, and you don't really have to watch all of the movies he requires as long as you know some of the story. He's a pretty chill guy with fair grading and an easy class even if you don't like writing that much although the projects are a little annoying to do.

He is a really good guy and I really enjoyed his class, just not what I expected based off the syllabus. Lots of group work but it isn't anything hard, just takes some time. Dr. B is awesome! Such a nice guy and great to take if you have to take SSC/IDS 299. The off-campus assignments/projects were super interesting and eye opening to the community around Lansing. Overall, this class was great and an easy 4.0.
really easy gen ed. hes so chill i would def take this class again.

he is really passionate about what he does and it makes the material very interesting. His lectures are fun. if you want to pass the tests you MUST show up for the lectures The main homework was these journals & they ended up being the perfect building blocks for completing the Capstone I had him for Environmental Ethics ISS 310.

Very passionate professor and was very understanding when I had a problem with my group. His quizzes are quite difficult, but just study and you will be fine. Tophat is required and while attendance is not, you need to go to understand the content. Overall would recommend!

reviews.comment: Guys a beauty, grades super easy and doesn't give alot of homework. Take good notes and it's an easy 4.0.

I had Dr. Baylis for both ISS 215 and ISS 310. Both classes were easy, both consisting of tests, writing assignments, and small projects. Dr. Baylis is super passionate about his classes and is always willing to help and guide his students, no matter what it is. I didn't get either textbook and got 4.0 in both. Super understanding and a great guy!
Very caring professor and helpful when answering questions. Quizzes are pretty easy as long as you take notes on lectures, and despite having a lot of group assignments it's not a work-heavy course.

reviews.comment: This is easily the best professor I have ever had. most of the work is done as group project, He is laid back, chill, funny professor. He is literally the best professor

One of the best professors in MSU. I took his ISS 215 class. There are many readings and assignments but they are pretty easy. I still ended up with 4.0 even if I didn't put much efforts. Just read and do your tasks. You will still get 4.0.

Doc B is a fantastic professor! Even though every class is a lecture, he incorporates group work in your chosen group. He truly cares for his students if you build a connection with him.  10/10 would recommend for a beneficial ISS credit!!

I really enjoyed Dr. Baylis and his method. I struggle with lectures, but I never found myself really straying off from the content. I really enjoyed him.

Baylis was fantastic throughout the entire semester. He was so understanding, and patient. His class was extremely easy. There is a lot of busy work, but as long as you do it, it is quick and easy. Easy class for a 4.0 and the professor is amazing. 10/10 would take again.

Very caring and nice guy. Understands that many are taking to fulfill requirements, and I feel is accommodating to those students whilst challenging students who want to dive deeper. Very fair with grading, and tests are clear-cut as long as you take notes. Find a good group at the beginning and you're set. I learned quite a bit from his class.

Such a cool guy. There was no assignment that took more than 45 min to complete. Attendance is not mandatory, his tests are kinda hard but manageable, projects are easy. Honestly just pick a good group and it's an easy 4.0. He holds optional classes sometimes where he basically just chills with you. He's a cool ass guy and he's really funny. 10/10

Dr. Baylis is so nice and understandable, but there is a lot of group work that is most of your grade. He grades on completion and tests are online. Take notes during class and you'll get a good grade.

Mr. Baylis is such a sweet guy, and you can tell he has a passion for what he is teaching. All of his exams are online, and there are no trick question to confuse you. He is super sweet and his grading is very fair. Would 100% recommend to anyone.

Dr. Baylis is super passionate about what he's talking about. The only thing is that the exams are based on notes from the slides and lecture, so your notes need to be really good. One of the best ISS classes I have taken. He allows 2 attempts on the exams, the second attempt is just what you got wrong the first time. Such a great professor!

Amazing professor, if you go to his office hours you are able to understand the content. Very passionate about what he teaches and wants his students to succeed would recommend!

Don't worry about the time slot for the lecture, it's only for half a semester (ends when spring break starts). Bessette actually cares about you and is so funny to listen to. The chillest professor ever.

Dr. Douglas Bessette has been an excellent instructor who brings a wealth of knowledge and passion to his classes, especially in the field of clean energy and sustainability. Hilarious, knowledgeable, approachable, entertaining.

Easy course for ISB req
This is a great class and Professor Cooke is super knowledgeable.

Great professor and the class was very interesting. This was my favorite class.

No exams, just a course semester project due at the end of the semester which isn't the hardest thing ever. Group work, but have same group whole semester. Overall I'd take again.

the easiest class I've ever taken. Material isn't boring, grading is clear and uploaded into d2L, accepted late work for most assignments. Not that you'll need it, bc every assignment is pretty simple. If you get anything less than a 4.0 in this class and don't have extenuating circumstances consider dropping out of college

Literally got 100% in the class. So insanely easy, and you just show up once a week. I tell everyone to take this course for an easy 4.0. There's a lot of navigating on D2L and other websites, but the same stuff is basically due every week. Probably the best prof/class for a gpa boost.
Super easy class

Nice teacher but it took me forever to understand the layout of the class because we have SO many different websites relating to the class. But it's pretty easy once you understand how to use it. The whole class was based on this animal sex book, overall an easy class if you read the book. Attendance is only once a week and mandatory for a grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I hated her class, it basically had nothing to do with the title of the course, it took I believe 9 weeks to reach the first mention of topics related to the course. Only redeeming factor was that 80% of the grade is participation and graded by computer for 0 or 100%.

Great teacher if you love having the WORST class organization I've ever dealt with. I haven't finished the class yet, so I really can't say what my grade is. Taking ISB 204. Teacher will tell you to 'go somewhere' in the class website, and good luck to you finding it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: ISB 202 is an easy prerequisite. There are a few assignments that are teambased, but nothing this semester was difficult. Class structure makes it so that even with a bad group, you are still able to 4.0, since there are plenty of assignments and categories to be successful in.

Prides herself on being an online learning wiz? Worst online class I've ever had the displeasure of taking. Sure her D2l setup is pretty-- it's smoke and mirrors. Unhelpful prof, overcomplicated course, unnecessary and annoying group work, all busy work. If she ever reads these: Hi, It's summer gen-ed bio. No one wants to be here. Simplify things.

seems like a lot of work because of discussion posts and responses but overall super easy. group projects that build on each other and combine them for the final instead of an exam and drops one assignment in each "category." easy 4.0 as long as you do the work
This was an asynchronous class and the workload was a lot, but not necessarily difficult. Be sure to do the homework right away
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Overall, this class wasnt bad. In general, Prof Bierema was a relatively easy grader and assignments werent too hard. However, there are a TON of assignments. You will be bust every day of the week with this class. Also, a large part of your grade is dependent on group projects. These are pretty challenging and not an easy feat. However easyish A

was good at keeping me busy. lots of assignments due on different days of the week. had to post two discussion board posts each week (took about 2 hours to do both) before wed., and had to posts 3 responses, 3 different days of the week. group projects every week- not helpful at all. wasnt an option to work alone. she was organized and no exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very helpful, responded quickly to any questions. Discussion board each week, easy quiz every week online, content was very enjoyable and intriguing. 4 assessments total, easy projects. Met once a week, work in groups every class. Highly recommend, very nice and caring professor, easy A, and pretty interesting no matter what you major in.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Her class was decent. I feel like I didnt learn anything but it was an easy A. She is a great prof. and is very caring and understanding.

Great ISB class! This class only meets for an hour each week and the rest of the work is done on D2L. We had an online quiz and discussion board post due each week, as well as three responses to the discussion boards, but it was a reasonable amount of work. Bierma is super nice and helpful as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class only meets once a week so youre expected to attend every lecture. you work with the same group, so if you dont like who youre put with, say something immediately. Class is crazy easy but youre required to do online stuff beforehand that doesnt even correlate to what we talk about in class. theres 20 pts worth of extra credit!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is a very nice person, its a pretty easy class. You get put into groups for daily work, and you get participation every day for the group work. Try to be in a group that will write your name down for participation when you aren't there. Easy 4.0. Barely ever studied.

This class was very interesting and an easy A! You work in groups every class period and get credit for the work you complete. There are also modules before every class, but they are super easy. There are four total exams that are easy if you use your course pack to study. Dr. Bierema is very organized and clear about what she expects from you.

I had her for both LB144 and LB 145, and she was by far my favorite professor at MSU. She's super nice and really wants everyone to do well, the workload was extremely manageable, and the tests we're very similar to in class work. Would highly recommend!

You have an assigned group for the semester for in-class activities that cover biology principles, and you are scored for your participation in those activities. There are also modules (hw) you must complete for points before every class. The exams follow the content very well and are not difficult if you prepare. Professor Bierema is super nice!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: If you need to get you ISB credit, take it with her. She is very clear with what she expects on projects and is more than willing to help you understand. Worked in groups the whole semester, so going to class is necessary to get credit but she does give you plenty of skips. Pretty fair grader on tests and final project.
This class is super manageable. Work in groups for the whole semester. Homework is easy and not super complicated.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: In class you work in groups on case studies and video responses. Quick homework online after every class. Easy tests, I recommend this class.
AMAZING PROFESSOR. IF YOU GET A CHANCE TO TAKE HER, DO IT. YOU WILL THANK ME.

Rick is the greatest college professor I ever had the pleasure of meeting. He is just an absolute wealth of knowledge- not just about the industry but about so many things. He's someone who you want to learn absolutely everything you can from. One of the greatest resources not just in the MSU film program, but at MSU as a whole.

Once a week during class, you will watch a film. The discussions and analysis of the films is very interesting, but you do need to go to class, because there are weekly essays, along with the fact that attendance is graded harshly the more you miss. The professor is very nice and interesting.
I love movies, he made me love them more.
Professor Rick, goes above and beyond for both his students and lectures. I learned so much in this class, not only about film, but life in general. One of the best professors I've ever had.

The most insane class I have taken at MSU. Easy class, you watch a movie once a week and have a couple of one-pagers about the readings, but Prof. Blackwood is the highlight of the class. Not only are his lectures unhinged but he shares lots of stories from his past. While attendance is mandatory, you always want to show up to see what he says.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take this professor. I was legit excited to go to every one of his classes. He is very smart and knows what he's talking about, and he really for his students to learn.

Professor Blackwood was the most interesting professor I have had yet. Yes, the class was long, but we mainly watched movies and heard the professor's stories and insights on life.  I felt this class was an amazing opportunity to reflect on my life and goals. Homework was easy and engaging.

If you are looking for someone that will give you something meaningful for your time this is the man. Professor Blackwood, and those who work within his classes, really care about the material, and greatly encourage curiosity. While attendance is mandatory you're not wasting your time going. Read the material it seriously teaching good life lessons

Rick is an amazing professor who really cares about what and how we learned. Yes, class was early, but you were watching amazing movies all the time. Don't miss class because you'll miss out on great lectures and analyses that Rick provides throughout class. Would take it again just to have Rick as a professor again.

He was one of the most inspiring professors I've had at MSU. I found his IAH course deeply engaging and meaningful. He made complex topics feel approachable, encouraged open discussion, and always connected the material to real-world relevance. His passion for teaching and genuine care for students really stood out.

Prof Blackwood is very interesting, and the class itself isn't stressful at all despite all the content. Weekly readings, and biweekly one page papers that are graded on whether or not you did the reading. Lectures were long and sometimes droned on, but usually his extensive knowledge is fascinating enough to keep you awake and paying attention.

I enjoyed having Professor Blackwood, he has a lot of real-world experience to share from his days working in Hollywood. Lectures are very long, but they contain lots of wisdom, and I feel like I learned a lot from his class.

I enjoyed my time in this class. It was very interesting and we watched movies every Wednesday. We only had 2 papers and 3 one-pagers which were really only participation. The papers aren't even graded that harshly. Come to class every day and he will literally cancel your final and midterm. Wish he taught other classes so I could take them.

Showing up to these lectures was always the highlight of my week. He really cares about expanding your perspective and making you smarter. Movies in IAH 241G were triggering so be cautious of that. We had two papers and three one pagers which were easy if you did the readings and watched movies outside of class.
Professor Blackwood is an amazing professor. He really cares about his students and you will learn a lot.

Professor Blackwood is an interesting guy lots of life experiences. Fair grader and only assigned 2 longer-papers and a 3 short 1-2 page papers. Rarely gave quizzes and midterms as long as everyone showed up to class and was engaged in the material.Easy to get along with and enjoys what he's doing. The class was very worth it. Make sure to show up!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing class! He gives such good lectures you forget you're in class. He shows you movies and explains how they created them. He has amazing experiences in the real world, that he is more than willing to share with you! Highly recommend, you will not be disappointed with this class at all. I learned so much from this class!
Loved the class, great coursework, readings, and films. Enjoyed just about every lecture. Great class even greater professor.

This class was the one I looked forward to every week: Prof. Blackwood's stories and lectures were engaging and interesting, and I left each one feeling like I learned something. His screenwriting and filmmaking industry experience offered invaluable context to the class content. Class was discussion based and there was ample time to ask questions.
Seems paranoid around male students. Clearly writes her own reviews and has written her own Wikipedia page (lol).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: PHL344 was one of the best classes i took at MSU thanks to Dr.Bluhm. She is passionate and caring but also very clear and firm on her grading criteria, bc she is also very clear and thorough on her lectures and explains difficult concepts easily. Her course has changed my perspective on medicine and i recommend her course for anyone in pre-health.

Super interesting intro course for bioethcis! Dr. Bluhm makes the online course super easy to understand. Lots of reading, writing, and group discussion, but that is expected for an online bioethics course. Really fair grading and is super easy to get in contact with! She also gives great feedback. She really cares about her students! Easy 4.0.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Bluhm is a great professor and clearly cares about her students. The course is very accessible, and was one of my favorite classes of undergrad so far.
Very caring and sweet professor. Its the type of professor you want to take. I highly respect her, and she respects students back.

Class is graded based on three exams, in-class activities, and reading responses. Other than exams, it's pretty much graded on participation. Lectures can be a bit boring (probably due to long class periods and uncomfortable seats), but the material is still very interesting and valuable. She is very kind and easy to get along with.

This is an online asynchronous intro course for bioethics but it was still very interesting and valuable. Lots of readings, short reading responses, and discussion board posts. Graded pretty much on participation so long as you give a respectable effort. Course was organized and easy to follow along with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Bluhm was amazing for LB 326A, this class was an intersection of ethics and medicine which was really interesting to me.  Bluhm is really caring and wants all students to succeed. This semester we had 2 papers due per week with 3 larger assignments throughout the semester with no tests because of COVID. Overall, great prof!

Dr. Bluhm is thoughtful, compassionate, and an overall great professor. She makes herself available outside of class more than she should, she doesn't require camera's on or attendance in the first place, and loves her cats like nobody's business. Hard class, but if you put in the work and time, you'll succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Bluhm is a thoughtful, approachable, and overall great professor. I was a music major thrown into a class full of abstract neuroscientific vocabulary and I was able to succeed in this class. Definitely not easy and there is a lot of reading, but the class is valuable if you respect the time it requires.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She's very passionate and knowledgeable about bioethics and the class was very interesting. She creates a very good learning environment in the class that encourages discussion all sorts of issues, controversial or not. I definitely think that if you are doing anything involving bioethics you should take a class with her!

Dr. Bluhm was easily one of my favorite profs at msu. She knows a ton about bioethics and explains things very clearly with examples. Everything we discussed was so interesting. The tests are 7 essay questions but it is not hard to do well. There are a few extra credit points on the exams. This is a pretty easy 4.0.

Every HPS professor in Lyman Briggs teaches their course differently and Professor Bluhm taught hers from a bioethics perspective. I'm not even a health major but I found this course extremely worth-while. She is very knowledgeable in the field and navigates raw and controversial topics very easily. Definitely would take her again.

I LOVE Professor Morseau! She's genuinely one of the sweetest people ever! We had a lot of in class activities which we worked with the people around us on, but they were fairly easy. She also drops the lowest two of those so if you miss class then you're good. A discussion lead, three quizzes, and the final exam as well.

I loved Professor Moreseau. She truly cared about the content she was teaching and knew how to make it interesting. Discussion lead was super collaborative which made it less nerve wracking. 10/10 recommend this class!

Super nice and caring. Very laid back class. Class is graded on a few quizzes that are easy if you simply show up and pay attention,  4 in class assignments that are graded on completion (this is her form of attendance grade), a final exam and a discussion lead (not as scary as it sounds).

LOVED PROFESSOR MORSEAU! Had her for AIIS201 and was funny, understanding, and I looked forward to going to the class every week. We had different readings each class, and then went over it and had lecture. Extremely fun and would take it again!

Extremely rigid and stressful. 4.0 cutoff raised to 94. Attendance policy was not clearly enforced until around week 4, then grades were suddenly penalized with no drops or real makeups. Missing one class can ruin your grade. Heavy workload for a 2xx course and little openness to questions. Strongly avoid.
Really nice professor, very understanding. Material was covered in a way that was easy to understand. Also allowed for Zoom attendance, so very accessible. Would absolutely recommend!

WRA 210!!! Super easy grading. If you turn in the projects asked you will receive a 4.0. You have plenty of opportunities to submit late work and fix work in general to receive full credit. This class involves coding and learning the basics. Your final exam is the portfolio you create and it's super easy to receive a 100% on that!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He was one of the best professors I have had here at MSU. He really makes an effort to get to know his students and is incredibly understanding if you have stuff going on outside of class. Instructions for the assignments were clear and easy to understand. He really helped me a lot with my writing!

Two projects and attendance counts towards your grade, so don't skip! On-campus, the class was a breeze, online though. He made us take weekly quizzes and do an entire project with peer reviewing still. He's very unsure of himself and he wasn't prepared at all. Barely heard from him, due dates were very frequent. Try to find a more organized prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Two major projects and a final exam. Stuart is funny in that awkward nerdy way. He cares about your learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Good guy, know's his stuff. Seems a little unsure of either himself or the class, repeats "Make sense?" a lot.

This was his first time teaching the class, but I felt I was not challenged and his grading was not good. He graded more on the memo reflection than the projects themselves, which I found unfair. He's a nice guy - but I would take Laura Julier for this class, she will challenge you.

Professor Thompson is very passionate about what she teaches. Attendance is mandatory but you get three freebies. Guest speakers come each week to expand on content. There's weekly reflection papers for completion points and 3 noncumulative, open note + open book online exams. Also easy honors option, just an extra reflection paper.
Very kind professor. Very passionate about Social Work. Exams online and reflections due each Sunday but not hard at all.

Tina is an amazing prof! Her class was not difficult at all, she's very understanding, down-to-earth, and isn't a harsh grader. I definitely recommend taking her classes, she makes course materials easy to understand and doesn't sugar coat anything.
She is genuinely so sweet and cares a lot about what she does. Very much enjoyed having her class this year
Tina was absolutely amazing, and even convinced me to pursue SW as a career. I am applying to MSW programs simply because of her. I cannot recommend her classes enough, she really loves her job.

I loved this professor. The only complaint I have is that there is a lot of reading but you'll just have to face facts that you just have to skim a lot of things. She is a caring person, organized, fair grader, and very clear about her expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: The best MSW prof at MSU--- caring, helpful, passionate, and has clear instructions.

reviews.comment: Good. Good.
Nice.
love love love.
Very helpful and insightful on semester assignments-would not do my paper for me but showed me the right path to walk down to get the right grade. Blaschke and Rypkema are a good team.
She is a young teacher but is very good at becoming a great teacher. She is very helpful and insightful on questions I have asked her. Hands down a good teacher.

The professor was very nice and the class was easy 6 reflections and 6 open note quizzes. The only thing that was hard was the quizzes included a lot of stuff that wasn't talked about in class and very niche things from the book. The questions were also worded weird.

Kelley absolutely changed the trajectory of my college journey. As a psychology major, I was interested in taking this class, and now I am a double major in social work because of it. She brings in guest speakers, and she herself has a significant amount of experience in the field. Quizzes are easy and every other week, and papers every other week!

She was very sweet! There was one guest speaker a week, and homework was split between short online quizzes and short written responses. A very easy course, but she did a lot to keep it interesting. I had no problem reaching her outside of class hours, and she was flexible about attendance, grades, due dates, etc.

loved professor Blanck, most students weren't very interactive, but she was. The class is easy and catered to the social work major. she uses guest speakers to teach about real world experiences working in differing social work types, very accommodating. assignments are very easy. only downside is passing with a 93% which is only a 3.5

ignorant to how difficult the materials she has us work with are or doesn't care but either way in this class we had to work using foreign techniques to us w/o practice and are critiqued and graded. Graded on many aspects that it's hard to keep straight what needs to be added and hardly gives any in class time to work. WAY too much for a100 class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really enjoy Prof. Blesing's class. I overall enjoyed her helpful feedback and the class was very motivating for artistic expression, though sometimes you felt you needed to bend your work to fit some of her preferences. You can probably get through this class without purchasing the art kit, she supplies many of the needed tools and resources.

I had a great experience in Rebekahs class she is a wonderful professor. She pushes her students to dive deep and think critically about their projects. Almost every class period you will have an opportunity to work on projects/homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She was a really nice professor. I'm not a studio art major, so I was nervous about taking a sculpture class as a requirement for my major, but she was really helpful and provided good guidance throughout every assignment. The kit for the class was really expensive however, and we didn't use half of what was in it - buy materials as you go.

I enjoyed taking Rebekah's class. She seems passionate about presenting new projects. She gives excellent suggestions but has more or of a "figure it out as go" approach. I would love to take another one of her classes in the future :)
Good class with easy assignments, but gets cancelled all. the. time. it became disorganized quickly and confusing to stay on track with deadlines because class was cancelled so often.
You literally will not go to class, she canceled class every single week. I went to class maybe 5 times, IF that
Cancelled class last minute so many times.

She cancels all the time very last minute so don't take an 8 am class with her. Her class is very easy. She will make you read outload sometimes and work in groups or partners. All work is easy and there is never homework.

If you're into creative work and open to learn new perspectives, take this class! She is fun, caring, and despite some of the students making this class difficult for her because of circumstances unrelated to the class, she is empathetic and a kind grader. I loved her!

She was a good person, but the amount of times she cancelled class last minute was wild. Because my class was an 8:00 am, there was over ten times where I would be in the classroom and we would get an email saying class was cancelled, a few times even after class had started. The class itself was very disorganized, mostly due to many cancellations.

She was great! Super friendly and very engaging. Class was pretty easy, she would cancel class a lot but I was okay with it. Course work was simple and she was lenient on late work! Def recommend and would take a class with her again.

The professor is not all that bad. the class is easy and the writing assignments are not hard. For me, she did not come off as rude or have a bad attitude. She did however cancel class last minute a LOT or change it to Zoom that was extremely annoying. there is also a lot of reading in class and group discussions
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: If you can help it, don't enroll in a class with her as the professor! This professor is horrible at communicating and her attitude is also very unpleasant. The way that Professor Borha chose to run class this semester was always chaotic and unorganized to say the very least. Although the class itself is easy, she made it hard with her attitude.

Do NOT take this professor's class. She makes class online for no reason and lets you know the morning of. She never explains herself, adds random parts to the projects a day before it's due, and changes the due dates 100 times. She is very unclear about when things are due. Overall, this easy WRA 101 class is made complicated by this professor.

Do not take this class and avoid this professor if you care about your mental health and GPA. The workload is not worth 3 credits (6-8 quizzes a week, 6 essays, 4 exams) and the grading criteria for written exams is so stringent and arbitrary that even if you excel everywhere else and get the exam questions right it ultimately won't matter.

Don't look at any of these low reviews. You have 4 exams the entire semester and they are 2 essays and a hybrid true and false section, that are both done online at home. uses iClicker but not for accuracy just for attendance purposes. Honestly, i loved the class, and professor black is a great instructor.

Despite the horror stories I read when signing up for my PLS course, I enjoyed Dr. Blacks course. If you don't do the readings and look at lectures, this class will probably be impossible. Attending and taking notes, doing the readings, and basic review should be enough for almost anyone to 3.0 the course with average effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I LOVED him. One of my favorite professors I've had at MSU. Exams 1-4 are online, and the final was in person. He was able to keep my ADHD brain focused even during an 8:30 am lecture.
The class is super interesting but be prepared to get a bad grade even if you do the work and pay attention. The exam questions are meant to be trick questions he is literally out to get you
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Legit my favorite class this semester, all you really have to do is pay attention to the lectures and do the exams. Exams can be hard, but he makes it easy to get half credit on questions, and you can pretty easily do decent as long as you know what's going on. Overall great prof!

Dr. Black is SO kind, funny, and such a great teacher. I am a journalism student with no interest in political science, and I was able to make it through this class. His lectures are great, and he is just an overall very likable guy.

He is a hard professor- but if you are planning on working in Policy, his lectures and coursework are completely fair. Takes up a good chunk of your time but he is so willing to help and lend a hand when needed!!!!!

i am in his online PLS 320 class right now, and can already say Professor Black is one of the best professors I have had in my 3 years at MSU. His lectures are very informational and he always gives some "fun facts" which I find interesting. He has one of the best set-ups of an online class that I have seen, and it is clear what is expected of you!

Don't waste your time with him! Go add the class with someone else this guy is hard grader doesn't round up the grade! I had 1% left and he didn't round up?! Just take it somewhere else I would not recommend! 4 years of college and this is one of the weirdest experiences with an online class. Hopefully MSU does something about him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

His lectures were not only dated back in 2021, but they were just a boring yap-fest that made the subject not even remotely interesting and fun.  It also doesn't help that a majority of the lectures were him talking about his political science colleagues, which was super annoying.  AVOID!

His lectures were fantastic!! I took this online and loved it. Yes, there is work. If you actually watch the videos and read the writing will be insanely easy. The quizzes for each lecture are unlimited tries, and the midterm was multiple choice. This has been the best online class I have ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took the online version of this class during the summer semester, and I don't recommend it. Really one of the only professors I've had issues with during college. reviews.comment: Listen up, this class is NOT easy. Class is graded based on a midterm and final that include a multiple choice true/false section and 4 essays per exam and lecture/reading quizzes. Doing well is possible, but it will certainly test your limits!!! Make sure to do the reading and attend office hours. Prof is nice, but grading can be harsh at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ryan was a really good professor. He has you read a book over the course of the semester which I cannot say I loved but his mandatory lectures made up for it. His lectures are incredibly entertaining and he makes everyone laugh throughout. Overall, the class was decently easy and he is an amazing guy.

ISS 325- Video Games and Revolution: I took this course over the summer.. it's interesting and fun (easier if you're a gamer), but it is SO MUCH WORK! There are only ten days per module and you must play through anywhere from 7-20 hours of a game, read the millions of articles assigned, quizzes, and papers.. all in 10 days.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: You only have a midterm and a final to be graded on. Those exams consist of 4 essays and 60 multiple choice questions, on top of the "multiple choice answers" are true, false, probably true, probably false, or I'm not sure. All the exams are graded by his TAs, but he gives you the option to ask for a regrade. You are able to lose points on regrade.

reviews.comment: The worst professor I encountered at MSU. So many people in these ratings say how caring and engaging he is, but every lecture was recorded in 2021 and is outdated. 4 ULAs did all grading and made all tests. He put no effort into this course. Every lecture including his unimportant conscientiousness research will also be an additional hour.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Please do not make the same mistake I did and give him the benefit of the doubt. He is an awful professor and will destroy your gpa, mental health, and sanity. I wish I had never taken his class. We were graded off of two EXAMS only. People mentioned he liked papers, well not in this semester. AVOID IF POSSIBLE. AVOID. AVOID. AVOID.

This professor is the worst political science professor I have ever had. We were graded off of two things (the midterm and the final). He took forever to get back those grades and when he did, half of the class had failed. Believe me, I too thought he can't be that bad but he is. If you value your gpa or your mental health, AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!

super funny and easy!
amazing!

other professors recommended.

best prof ive ever had but i got a 2.0 cause of attendence... if you want to skip class, dont take hers

Professor Boateng is simply the best

Awesome professor, one of my favorites. Genuinely great guy and really good at giving engaging lectures.

Loved his class! Participation and just showing up is a huge part but his lectures are interesting. Really cool and definitely keeps it real. TAs are kinda harsh with grading but other than that I would take again!!

Show up to class, take the open book/note/internet quizzes, and there's half the class content. There are also a few big essays that are graded pretty harshly by the TAs, and if you don't like writing this course won't be for you.

Boucher's classes are extremely easy which is why I ultimately gave him a "good" rating. Worst class ever and unnecessarily hard for an ISS

reviews.comment: this is university required class which are typically easy and he makes this the hardest class ive ever taken. Hes a great guy but as a professor he is HORRIBLE! dont take this class with him. when he talks he tries to act all smart and uses words that no one understands what hes talking about. get ready to go to go random places outside of class

Prof. Boucher is insane. He makes succeeding in his class so difficult. He doesn't upload any grades on D2L so you have no idea where you're at in the class. reviews.comment: Just hope you have decent Ta's
This class in a nutshell: One of the TAs will tell you something and when you ask the other TA, it will be completely different.

The lab is run by the TAs and I'm not sure if anyone has ever seen the professor outside of the introduction video. You are required to have goggles no matter what otherwise they take points away from your grade but in all it's a straightforward class with a lot of writing in the course book.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: This lab was excruciating. The TA's have no idea what they're doing and are very unhelpful in answering questions. The projects have so much pointless writing that is expected to be done 1-2 days after lab. The grading really isn't very harsh, I found that throwing a bunch of words on a page will get you 100% pretty easily. It's a lot of work.

The TA's instructed each lab and were really unhelpful when you had questions. The lab manual was also hard to navigate which made labs even harder. There were also quick deadlines for each assignment, and lots of homework that was expected to be completed if you didn't finish everything in class on time. Just hope that you have a good group.
TAs are absolutely awful, don't know what they're doing themselves, and horrible graders.

Fully TA ran class and mine weren't good. The TA would take a LOT of points off for stuff that was not stated clearly in the course packet instructions or in class. ZERO late work tolerance. If your group is bad you are pretty much cooked and my group sucked. If you need either this class or physics lab for credit take physics!!!!

TAs and ULA will actually teach this class so I guess it depends more on them, but this class isn't super hard to do well in but it is SO boring. And if you get a bad group then youre cooked. I reccommend if you do not do well with your group, complain in the CATME surveys and they will likely change your group and label is as a "attendance change"

First off, she doesn't even teach the chemistry lab it's TAs and if you don't get a good TA, aka a TA that understands what to do for lab then have fun because you will be struggling and the TA's will say you are doing it wrong but won't tell you how to do it any better. I didn't look both ways crossing the road going to class that's how bad it is
Sucks, the lab book is unclear and every single TA grades differently. Told one thing, marked down, told to suck it up.

This class is a lot for a 1 credit class. I had two TA's that were lovely (the one was the sweetest ever) it's just how the course is set up. It feels like you're thrown to the wolves the very beginning and nothing is explained well. Utilize the help room!

I loved both my TAs in this class, so it wasn't too bad for me. However, I feel like it should be 2 credits. It's 3 hours long, but you have to do work outside it too (such as presentations and completing lab reports-- you usually don't get enough time in class to do this).

This class is not a lot of work, the professor does not teach the class but they are ran by god awful TAs that grade the notebook assignments harshly and not clear with what they say. Just make sure you are there and you have a good team because they grade individual assignments like it does not affect our overall grade.

Professor Busby's class is only run by TA's so it is really hard to gauge if you are going to like this lab or not. It is 3 hours long and you are STUCK with the teammates you get in the beginning, so play nice. I lucked out and got some pretty cool TAs but I know others who were miserable with theirs. Just try in the lab and you should be fine.

Hope you get good TA's bc your experience is dependent on them. Some are tough graders others are chill. Way too much work for a 1 credit class, need a good group or to be able to do all the work yourself. Prof was not present in any way. Labs were weird (have to design yourself & takes a while) but fun. Can't leave early even if ur done. Decent.

Way too much work for a one credit class though most labs let you leave early so its not a full 3 hours. Pray you get good TA's and a good group because it is entirely group work and its all written. The projects are relatively simple but my TA's told us the exact process for our projects, they were really nice but its pure luck.

This class was a lot of work outside of class for one credit. You have to get lucky and get a good lab group to do well because it is basically all group work. Work involves lengthy reports and presentations, but no exams. Put effort into the work and your grade should reflect that.

CEM 161 is not actually taught by Dr. Busby herself, but is instead taught by 2 TA's chose at random. Your grade in this class will likely depend on what 2 TA's you get and what 3 group members you get. Group members are chose at random. CEM 161 wasn't extremely difficult but does require a decent amount of effort and some knowledge from CEM 141.

Hope and pray you get a good group and good TA's. Class was okay, I got lucky with a TA who was not as strict, but I know friends who have had awful TA's. The projects have 0 instruction, and you have to figure it out on your own basically. Lots of work for a 1 credit class.

CEM 161 was very easy, but its because I had a great lab group. The TA's were funny, but hard to understand and did not explain things well. I don't think I saw Brittany once in the lab so I really have no opinion on her. She would take the smallest mistake on your "notebook" and deduct like 3 points. Rubrics were simple and clear though.

In theory, this class was perfect. However, the lack of documentation and instruction from the professors to the TAs made it very disorganized. TAs were looking for things that were not mentioned in resources. Also, the course provided no template or format for how reports were to be formatted. TAs were very nice though, and made class enjoyable.

Horrible TA's who don't give clear instructions and get mad when they see you doing something you're not supposed to. Pray you don't get TA's who like the power and mark points off for the littlest "error"

Hated every second of this lab. Useless TA's who were bad at explaining, no clear instructions until they see you doing something you're not supposed to. Very stingy when grading. Says on the syllabus "we do not expect any specific results" and how "it's for fun" but complains we did it wrong when we presented our project?
Never showed up to class once, which is expected in labs. Was very bad at emailing. Tough grading

Must have good TAs or you will not succeed in this class at all. Also, having a good group is key because the whole class is a group project. Some of the experiments are fun if you know what you're doing. They do take a lot of points off due to a very strict grading rubric. Overall the class is pretty fun and easy if you listen and pay attention.

This class was a lab led by 2 TAs,not Ms. Busby herself. Some of the experiments' instructions were unclear to be fully produced by students. At the start,the TAs were a little unhelpful and not encouraging but they got a little better towards the end. Make sure to write a lot in notebooks or the graders will take off many points for little things.

The class is led by 2 TAs, so how you do in the course is based on them and not Dr.Busby. During this course, we were not given clear instructions for how to do things, and that was a little frustrating. However, my TAs were very helpful during the process. There are 4 total projects (all group), 1 slide presentation, and 1 poster presentation.

I have reached out multiple times because Brittany is a coordinator for CEM161 lab. I have had issues with the TAs in my section and she was not helpful whatsoever. I felt that she did not care about the issues I was having as she told me there was nothing she could do and blamed me for things that I could not control.

You will not have Busby teaching because she is the overall director, but I think the overall chemistry labs could benefit from more guidance. Lab is led by two TA's who can be intense, you basically have to hope you have a good lab group or else the semester is going to be one big struggle, allowed to miss 2 labs, communicating with her was easy.

CEM 161 is literally the biggest joke. Like this class does not give you clear instructions on what to do during projects whatsoever, and then you'll get points taken off your grade even though the criteria isn't laid out. Also, Dr. Busby doesn't do any of the teachings. I had 2 international TAs, who taught the entire course

The TAs teach the class, so technically, how you do in the class is determined by them (most of them have thick accents...). But the TAs I had were very friendly and would help whenever asked (also easy graders). When I had an emergency and missed lab, I emailed the chemistry address, her, and Johanna Herman, and it was Busby who helped me.

Knowledgeable on the subject, but not a good professor.  Lectures are disorganized and hard to understand, study guides are long and lazily put together, and will take forever to grade any assignments.  Don't waste your time or tuition money with him.

This class was not super easy, but not too hard either. As other students said, exams make up a massive portion of your grade, so attending lectures and studying are important. Content is easy to understand, and lectures are a bit lengthy, but he usually ends class early. I would recommend this course!

I definitely recommend this teacher. 
-no required book
-attendance is mandatory (for credit, lectures: really interesting/vital to attend to pass)
-Heavily based on the three exams throughout the semester but, as long as you attend class regularly, and study your notes for a couple days prior to the exam you should be all good.

Very knowledgeable and a great professor! Great examples and associations made to promote learning. Very straightforward. 60% lecture attendance required for 3% of your grade. The lecture slides have everything; that's why I rated him a 4 instead of a 5, because he doesn't really elaborate on the slides; class is very much him reading off slides.

Brascamp is a very nice prof, and his class is pretty interesting. This class does have A LOT of content, so the exams can be a bit hard, but if you study, you will do fine. 60% of the lectures are mandatory for attending and there are studies you have to do, but they are easy. Exams are massive part of grade, so beware of that

I'm not going to lie…the material of this class is very easy. I was able to get a good grade on tests without attending lecture. If you aren't a good test taker, go to class, and trust you will be fine. (lecture can feel very boring and lengthy)
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is one of the easiest psych classes I have ever taken. The professor doesn't go in-depth, which is nice since it keeps the exams really straightforward. It is test-heavy, but honestly, the questions are super easy if you actually study and understand the material. He uses PowerPoints, SO if you miss class, you can just read the slides.

Professor Brascamp knows what they are talking about, and the lectures are very interesting. There isn't a lot of homework, and the material is easy to understand. He is super funny and makes the lecture fun to listen to.

I would recommend. Yes this class is hard and yes it is mainly lecture + exam-based. Brascamp's slides are amazing though, he is the first psych prof I've had that I genuinely learned from. He is passionate, gives tons of visuals, and explains very everything well. For exams, if you just study the slides and make a quizlet, u will be just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are very heavy in content and he moves decently fast through the slides. He doesn't do much extra talking outside of what is written on the slide. Attendance isn't mandatory but you do get extra credit for going to class. There are no quizzes, just experiments and SONA. You'll definitely need to prepare for exams, but they're not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Brascamp is very knowledgeable, but I found his lectures to be quite monotone. The material is pretty interesting but complex. Graded pretty heavily on exams which I found to be pretty difficult. Could do Sona/online experiments for credit, which was nice, but if you don't do good on the exams then you have a low chance of doing well

The lecture slides did not help you on exams, 80% of your grade is exams. There is no curve, the study guides are long and not helpful for the exams. It's basically a copy and paste of the slides. Not a good professor
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There are three exams and two homework assignments; if you're not a good test taker, I wouldn't recommend it. Attendance matters, but he also offers 4 points of extra credit. He's a nice guy, and he seems passionate about the material. I thought the material was interesting, but if you don't, this class will probably be a difficult snooze fest.

This class is all based on exams and attendance. If you fail one exam you're basically screwed over because there's barely anything else that goes into the grade book. Study guides are so unhelpful, notes are so hard to follow and the class material is so dry. Don't recommend this course.

The class is solely graded on exams. If you do poor on exams, you are not passing the class. No extra credit, his lectures are so confusing and the TA's notes do not help at all. No curve in grades, this was by far the worst class I have ever taken here. I'm an empath, so I feel Jan as a person, but this class was terrible.

I've had him for LIN 463 + PSY 200, both of his lecture slides are 80 pages long that jumble up the material. Theirs a disconnect between the exams & lectures, you are given a study guide but it's vague topics to focus on. Overall, I wish he was just more straight forward in his lectures to give better understanding since exams were difficult.
There are no quizzes or anything to aid in learning. Feedback is required for biological mechanisms to learn, no? Am I an ANN? No. So disappointed. In person tests that you don't get back.

reviews.comment: love him class was kinda hard for a psych class tho but prof brascamp is awesome and super understanding and supportive

Because of this, I at most could only get a 3.0 due to getting a 75% on the first exam. As with previous posts, he's a nice guy and clearly shows a passion for the field, but not a good professor.

Do not take this class. Prof is nice but formats the class in a way that makes it nearly impossible for ANYONE to do good in it. please dont take this man... i dont care what you read before. i read reviews and thought it was going to be so great but honestly having mandatory lectures (aka you wont pass) then exams that are 80% of your grade combined with "study guides" that are literally exactly whats posted on the slides just isnt it. he is a nice guy, but not best prof.

Professor Jan Brascamp was very nice and allowed extra credit through coglab. However, it is easy to mess up in this class there a were only 3 exams and they are very heavily weighted.

reviews.comment: absolutely awful, the lectures are tedious and redundant. the information on the slides are no help during the exams. dont bother going to the in person lectures because he just reads off the slides and goes on and on and on.
Tried his absolute best to make the most he could out of the course. I missed a quiz opening by a few minutes and he was extremely accommodating. His honors option is also really fun!!

Great professor. Tried his best to make lectures interesting with everything being online and exams matched the lectures. If you paid attention during lecture then you'd do fine on the exam. Coglab quizzes were also super easy if you actually did them and took notes. He's also super flexible about moving test times around. Grade reflected effort.

I took this class all online fall 2020. This class is super interesting. Make sure you watch the lecture videos, they help so so much! Also I suggest taking notes on the slides before you watch the lectures then add to your notes. The book isn't necessary at all. Professor Brascamp is super nice and the TA's are great. Definitely recommend.
I loved Brascamp. His lectures can be dry at times but he's really good at getting all of the information across. I definitely want to take him again if I get the chance. 11/10
Pretty nice professor. Course was a kinda hard. Wouldn't take again because content wasn't super interesting.

Awesome guy! Had a very good time in his class.

He is an extremely nice man who cares about his students. Class never goes the full amount of time and sometimes it makes the lectures rushed and boring, but the class is easy enough where you could never go to class and still 4.0.

Very chill professor, more than half way through the semester and we havent had a full length class yet. Answers questions through out lecture and his powerpoints are very well structured. You can tell he really cares about his students & is willing to help!
His socks are the best.

Coglab quizzes are easy; (10) HPR credits are easily attainable during a whole semester; he has entertaining lectures that are occasionally riddled with humor; he tries to answer questions the best he can and help students understand what he is teaching.

Lectures the whole 70 minutes and repeats himself all the time when trying to lecture. Honestly not as bad as everyone makes him out to be. His class is pretty boring and he takes it very seriously but as long as you actually go to class and do the assignments you're fine. Doesn't follow the syllabus or the assignment instructions for grading. Clearly doesn't even watch the projects because he marks people down for things that were actually included. Also does not respond to emails, and not willing to meet with you to discuss his mistakes.

Professor Ellis is a with-the-times professor and brings a lot of humor into his lectures. Sitting through lecture was tough sometimes, but the class expectations were light. Bit of a tough grader, but would take again.

This course started as fun and could have been great if he hadn't become insufferable and a rude person. Very disrespectful to his own students. If you plan to take this class, forget about it. It could have been an amazing course, yet this professor failed every student in the room.

He is honestly a pretty good lecturer and is pretty interesting

Dr Ellis is a great professor and incorporates humor into his lectures which makes this class interesting and worth taking. I spent around 30 minutes - 1 hour a week on homework for this course and still received a 4.0. A super nice guy and a good teacher.

Professor Ellis is a nice dude don't get me wrong but the lectures are painfully long and I personally think it's an issue when your social science of sports professor is asking the class questions about whether the big 12 still exists or not.
