I really enjoyed this class and Prof. Eisenlohr. She is very organized and knows what she is doing. The quizzes aren't that bad as long as you actually study for them (and maybe attend office hours) the labs were very engaging and very related to the rest of the class. I also found the material very interesting. The textbook is very helpful too.

Yeah she can be helpful at times, but lectures are useless. All she does is read off the slides with barely any class engagement. Quizzes are 50% of the grade and are all free response, and grading is very strict. Final is brutal and over content that she least covers. Can be rude at times as well and treats students as kids sometimes. Get ready.

Dr. Roraback was awesome! She was super understanding towards students and would always answer questions clearly. She doesn't give much homework, but when she does the material is always interesting. She prepared students for exams and was overall such an amazing prof. I recommend anyone who's taking IAH to take it with her!
She is very caring of her students, appreciates participation and very lenient on reading assignments! I would definitely recommend, not a harsh grader.

One of my favorite professors I have had! She is very sweet and is caring towards her students. Though attendance is mandatory, she understands things happen and is very lenient. The readings weekly are pretty long, but if you skim them and know enough to engage in conversation you will be fine. Exams are easy if you study with the guide provided.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sweet professor, boring class. Barely did any of the readings unless it came to the exams but still passed the class with a 4.0. Two papers which are extremely easy and two exams which are exactly like the study guide. She does not grade harshly at all and is really understanding and caring towards her students. Easy 4.0, take her for any IAH class

She is the sweetest professor I've had and my absolute favorite so far. The work isn't necessarily difficult, but it can be tedious at times. If you do a small portion of the readings and skim through a few chapters of your textbook you'll do fine. She gives you a detailed midterm study guide a week before the test, and there's no final exam.
This is a super easy honors course to take. Just do the readings, even though there's a lot, and you won't even need to study for the midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall Prof Roraback is a nice lady. I appreciate the somewhat easy A but a little work was required. She didnt seem to spread out the assignments nicely. Nothing for the first few weeks and then you were given 6 at once. Stressful near the end but she is very lenient with the due dates. Quality professor for a filler requirement class.

This class is an easy and enjoyable 4.0. Dr. Roraback is one of the sweetest profs I have ever had. She really cares about her students. There are before-class readings, so you have to review them so you can follow along and participate in class discussion. No final, just a paper, and one midterm. Speak up and participate in class discussion.

Such a sweet professor but her lectures are long and very boring (fell asleep a few times this semester). She takes attendance but you have 4 excused absences. I read maybe 1 thing she assigned this semester and still got a 4.0. Midterm and final exam study guides are the same as the questions provided on exams. I would recommend her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I LOVE her. Sweetest lady ever. such an easy honors option! go to class, take notes on what she says, dont even need to read the books or articles given. One paper about yourself, an exam where she gives you the concepts and page numbers that you need to know and a group project on creativity. class thats relevant and interesting too, loved it
Great professor! Class is kind of boring, but she is very caring and a good teacher. Her class was an easy A and not much homework or exams.

Allowed 4 skips during the semester. Assigns readings after every class. 4 hw assignments during the semester and if you do them you get 100% on them. Midterm and final are incredibly easy, she gives a study guide and theexam is the study guide. There is a final group project that is easy. Super nice and chill teacher. Class is boring, but easy 4.0

Wants students to do well! One of the easiest classes I have taken. Class consisted of short assignments, midterm, group project, and final. There was required readings which I didn't do, and still got 99/100 on midterm. Go to class and participate in discussions and it will be easiest class ever. Prof Roraback is such a sweetheart!
He has three eye clickers throughout the class period and the most boring lectures you can imagine. Easy 4.0 though if you show up, do the quizzes that are easy...

Class itself is very easy, listening to him talk for nearly 2 hours is hard. "Guest speakers" every Friday are either videos of CEOs from the early 2000s or someone from the HB school. As a non-HB major, don't take this class. Most of the answers are self explanatory but he never answered an email or mine or will reverse missed quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You don't need to study for this class at all, i guessed in all the of my exams and never got below a 75%, because a majority is what you're taught is basic common sense. I used this class mainly for doing homework for other classes and shopping. Elsworth reads directly off the slides which are almost exact copy-pastes of the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You have to attend his lectures every Friday as he takes attendance. They're super boring and just a guest speaker but you can do other work during them as they're not relevant to coursework. The homework is easy and quick and the exams repeat homework questions so they're not bad either. It's an annoying class but it's not difficult.

You have to go to his lectures every Friday. They're super boring but you can just do other work during the class because the lectures don't really have anything to do with the homework/exams. Homework was super easy, exams weren't bad and have same questions as the homework. It's an annoying class but not hard.

Love Elsworth, VERY nice but every class = 25 slides of paragraphs. Nothing bolded or highlighted that you NEED to know on the test + no study guide. He gives 100s on projects, papers but sadly the tests make up most of your grade and it's hard to do well on them. I would say to take notes but it's not even worth it. You will have a hundred pages.

Powerpoint slides contained multiple paragraphs and he just reads straight from them. The exams are extremely difficult because the multiple choice answers all seem like the correct answer. You have to take his class for HB major at MSU, which is horrible. Studying for the exams are impossible, but he does offer a lot of extra credit.

Elsworth wasn't the best. His weekly Friday classes would always be a random guest speaker talking about their experience in HB instead of him actually teaching the class, so unfortunately, his classes are pretty pointless. The class was easy; your only homework you'll have is a weekly quiz on D2L and Pearson Revel, excluding the midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is the easiest thing I've done in my life, definitely recommend easy A. Although the professor him self is pretty boring and just reads off slides in his lectures but it's only once a week so it's fine.

He is just very bland and copy/paste directly from the slides. Lecture content is just him reading off purchased slides. Exams just repeat the quiz questions. Content is so basic, just filled with busy work. Stay away if you can. He's been here about 30 years, but his slides and lecture content has barely changed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class itself was really easy all you needed to do was read one chapter and take an online quiz each week. The lectures are pretty boring and aren't covered in the quizzes or exams.

The amount of reading for this class is ridiculous. You have to pay for the textbook to be able to do your work and 100-page long slide shows you have to go through. He teaches nothing in class at all and also his class is points-based so make sure you do everything even the extra credit. This class was easy though!

I just received my final grade for this class and I am in complete shock. I got a 1.5 on the 4.0 scale for inexplicable reasons. I got a 48/50 on the midterm, I did almost every weekly quiz and attended every single class but somehow my grade appears as a 1.5 on sis? This teacher is extremely boring with almost zero personality,would not recommend
Easily the worst professor I have had in msu, shouts at people if they leave 5 minutes early, makes you buy a physical iClicker despite there being an app for it and he is very boring.

Be prepared for so much reading, like I'm talking 15 to 20 pages of a (dry) textbook, along with slideshows a week. You have two quizzes per week that you have to take, and missing even one can tank your grade. He does a lot of iClicker questions, and also has a lot of guest speakers. Textbooks are expensive and unneeded as you can guess a lot.

Just to sum it up - one subject that he covered contained 63 slides. All with long paragraphs with soooo much content. Its like he breaks up 10 page essays into slides and reads them to you in class. Its horrible. It also makes it hard to study for exams, because there is so much content to read
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super boring and pointless lectures. He seems to have no idea what the rest of the HB curriculum entails because he covered topics that I mastered in pre-req's. He takes the entire class period for each lecture and you will have to rush to finish his exams in time so never expect to get out early. Avoid him if you have any respect for your time.

God he is so horrid.  The most cold and closed off professor I've had.  He just rambles on and on for what seems like years and you walk out feeling like you've just wasted 80 minutes of your life.  He always goes off on tangents that don't even relate to what we're doing in class.  Avoid at all costs if you can

I took professor Elsworth's HB 100 and HB 207 courses. The first thing you should know is that the content covered is awful. It is a totally unnecessary class and I really did not learn much, but is required for Hospitality Students. As for prof's teaching its okay. He seems like a really knowledgeable person, but lectures are extremely dry.
lots of reading but easy class. weekly lectures and quizzes. gives 2 bonus quizzes. interesting class. quizzes are easy as long as you do the reading and reading assignment.

I went to this class once. The online access is $100, but you do not need to buy the textbook if you don't want to, everything is on Quizlet. Elsworth is super boring, but every week is a quiz, module, and guest speaker quiz. Takes about half an hour a week. Honestly, if he unlocked everything at once you could finish the entire class in a week.

I had a good experience with prof Elsworth, the class was 100% asynchronous and he had a very detailed weekly schedule put out every week. He pretty much gave you the quiz answers on his powerpoints so if you do the work you should get a good grade. He was also very kind to me when I had an issue with my grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Easy 4.o, everything is on quizlet. You have a weekly test that is very easy and study modules. Attendance is mandatory. Uses Iclicker questions. Overall great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is so boring. And sometimes for HB 100 specifically he just shows random videos that have no relevance. He also doesn't tell you about exams a couple days before you take it.

Took 12:40 to 2 pm, he is by far the most boring professor to listen to. The class consists of him standing in front rocking back and forth reading the slides, attendance is mandatory and he offers no extra credit. In my opinion he is pretty lazy and wants everything we turn in to be the right way OR he won't grade it! Also weekly quizzes:)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She isn't necessarily a bad professor but her way of lecturing is painfully boring. Attendance policy is overly strict when showing up to the class doesn't really offer much in the way of learning. An easy class just not very enjoyable in any way. Not a bad experience, but also not good

Professor Ellison was difficult to gauge, she was nice on occasion but there were times where a group member would go up to ask for clarification on an assignment and she was condescending in her response. Easy class if you do your work, you can easily get an A, but I found lectures disengaging even when I actually was interested in the material.

Overall, this class is manageable. The weekly quizzes and assignments were due at the same time every week, so remember deadlines; she does not give late credit. You work in groups pretty much all semester and have 2 big projects. Her instructions are not always clear and she can be difficult, but if you do your work, you will 4.0 easily.
Very boring lectures and everything is based on group work. Grade is based on weekly quizzes, weekly assignments, and two group projects.

Dr. Ellison is a really great professor, she is extremely kind and cares deeply about her course and the students taking it. The class was very easy, each week we would have a simple homework assignment due at midnight on Fridays, and a simple 5 question quiz on the 1st meeting of the week. The course is simple, you can get an A with little effort

Professor has a superiority complex and was very condescending to me and other students whenever we needed help. Her instructions are never clear when assignments are due when it comes to weekly assignments or the big projects. The material itself is not difficult; however, the professor is difficult to deal with.

Prof. Ellison is extremely nice but has incredibly boring lectures. You pretty much only get graded on 2 group projects and weekly quizzes. The only reason to take this class is that it is an easy 4.0.

Super easy class. Dr Ellison is honestly pretty rude, although she has a good sense of humor during lectures. There is no final assessment yet instead a final group project. The entire class is mostly group work and there are weekly quizzes. Most of the time lectures are pointless but  there is Clicker for participation each class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Ellison was the best professor I've had. She is SUPER chill and has a good sense of humor. She takes the time to learn everyone's name and is super respectful. Attendance is mandatory, but there are no exams. This class is heavy on group work, but not in a bad way. TAKE THIS CLASS!!

This is my favorite professor every. She is very chill, makes class fun and you'll actually want to go to class. She does use iclicker and attendance is mandatory. There is a lot of group work. There are 5 question quizzes, they are easy points if you do the short readings. It is just an amazing class and Dr. Ellison is awesome. Take this class!

Ellison is one of those professors that is able to teach a topic someone might find boring and make it into something interesting.Her sense of humor is hilarious and she is always finding new ways to teach, she is a bit of a harsh grader tho. You will also have lots of group projects and are constantly meeting with your group in and out of class.

I don't think the class itself is super hard but she is not understanding at all. She is really mean honestly and just likes to argue with everything you say. I had a terrible time in this class and I would never ever recommend her or her courses.
Lovely professor! She is the sweetest and I always looked forward to coming to this class. My only critique is about the course and having to work with the same group the whole semester.

I took the honors option and it was easy. I didn't read a single reading and guessed on all the quizzes and still got a 4.0. The only thing you have to worry about is the class presentations and group projects. She grades those pretty hard so try your best on those and come to class. She also has a funny sense of humor so that's also a plus.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ellison is an amazing professor and the course is integrated with various interesting topics (course is discussion heavy) that go well together. There are a few group projects so hope that you have a good team; she is a tough grader for projects. There is a weekly quiz that's 5 questions but it's lightwork and readings are usually easy too.

Dr. Ellison was a cool professor. Lots of group work, 2 presentations and 2 other "big" projects. Seemed intimidating at first, but the class wasn't too difficult, she just wants you to have discussions and think. She grades kinda strictly for projects, but it's not difficult to do well. I hate social science, but I still got smth out of her class.

Dr. Ellison was amazing. Funny and laid back. 5 question quizzes every week based on material learned the week before. We were put into groups of 4-6 and had about 5 assignment/projects that had to be completed as a group. She cares more about if you are learning something from the class rather than getting things "right". Very eye-opening.

She is a good professor, don't get me wrong. However, I feel like it is nearly impossible to get a 4.0 in this class, you are hardly graded on anything so a 5 point quiz can have a 1% impact on your grade. And she grades extremely strict. I would take her again compared to other professors, however I am sure there are better professors for ISS 305

She literally was my favorite professor ever, she used iClicker for attendance but you were allowed a few days to miss and still get a 4.0. She's super real, straightforward, funny, the content was easy. There is 1 group project to present and 1 solo that isn't presented. She had fun topics to talk about and made it fun to be a part of. Slay Brandy

Prof Ellison was remarkable and probably the best prof I had in the semester. We had lots of fun classes and museum visits. Assignments were not that tough and could be easily managed. I recommend taking her class.
I took Brandy for my seminar aboard and I loved the class the entire time. She was so caring and helpful for anything we needed help with. I would 100% take her class again.

Dr. Ellison is great! However, I took asynch in summertime (which I would not recommend). I missed a quiz once and she let me make it up by just writing a half page paper on any article! If you ask for help, she is VERY accommodating. This class taught me SO much and really helped improve my research abilities. Be prepared for group work though.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The hardest part of this class is the group projects but it can be easy depending on your team. Class was always fun and attendance was tracked. If you do the work you will 4.0 the class. Professor Ellison was always enthusiastic and willing to answer any questions.

Great professor who actually cares for the well being of her students. I missed an online module one week and she reached out to me through email making sure I was well. Easy class along as you keep up with online assignments.

So much reading and listening to podcasts. The professor told us at one point that the workload should take you 16 hours to complete. The work for the class opens every Thursday and is due on Mondays, leaving it to be done on the weekend. When class complained and asked for it to open sooner her response was pretty much I don't care.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Profesor Ellison is very easy going and understanding. Her projects are fun and interesting and allow you to be creative. You can miss class here and there but I always enjoyed going. It was relaxing and homework was never bad and very manageable. Definitely take her course if you can.

Easy class and chill Prof, however, a stupid amount of busy work, like way to much for this class. I on average have about 10-15 things due just for that class, while it is easy the sheer amount is what is insane, especially with heavier class loads.

Extremely chill and likable professor, I couldnt recommend her enough. The group projects are fine and easy if you have a decent group. Lectures were pretty interesting. She constantly gives opportunities for feedback so her class is always improving. Great class for first-year students.
Very laid back and did not have anxiety when going to her class. This course was not stressful at all, it was more of a breather class from all of my other ones.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: If you have the chance to take Prof. Ellison, do it. She is one of the best professors I have had and she is very personable. She is so caring of her students and her class is extremely interesting.
As long as your group works together you should do awesome in this class. The work took me maybe 20 minutes per week. The group projects are a little tough, but there is only 2. No final either!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: So I took this class completely online and it's a really easy course with a really easy professor. There is a lot a busy work (as I like to call it) but most times it takes less than an hour to do. Two group projects so hopefully you get good teammates because its random and no final exam. Prof is also lenient with due dates. Overall easy 4.0 class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: Heavy workload, reading heavy and very short powerpoints. Workload is repetitive and mostly busywork. Course format is difficult to follow. Laid out week by week in D2L but each week has some info for week before and after. Discussion board requirements are difficult to follow with two different charts to use to find when and what to post.

Don't waste your time, and money. Ellison apparently thinks making students read WaPo articles, and watch YouTube is teaching. I get that ISS classes are just mandatory courses in ideology, but this one was a waste of everyone's time.

Professor Ellington did a good job given the online format of the past semester. The lectures could have been more detailed, but aside from that I have no real complaints. She assigns a fair amount of work, but as long as you do it all you shouldn't have a problem.
Beware of discussion boards. Professor Ellison is super nice, but she definitely gave the appropriate amount of work for a 4 credit class, don't expect it to be light.
I found the class to be pretty fun and the professor is very receptive with questions and will provide you with feedback really quick. The quizzes get kinda annoying but they arent bad

The class sounds interesting but I found myself dozing off. The mini quizzes every Monday where you have to answer five questions got old real fast, even though I listened to the assigned podcasts and read the assigned reading I didn't do well on them until the class went online. Pray you have good teammates for the group projects.

Every Monday, there are 5 points quizzes. The material gets confused and can't even find it in the readings. If you do bad on these, like get 3 out of 5 everytime, you will be in bad situation. I hope her quizzes are more easy and not this confusing...

She is a very good professor. Not only is her class very interesting, but she keeps the lectures alive. They are not your typical "sit and take notes", but decently paced and interactive in a good way. Also, when having some sort of illness, she is very understanding. Even if you are without a note, she really does care about her students.

The topic was Education. NO EXAMS! Group projects include discussion panels (your group leads discussions on some aspect of Education) and a communication project (a brochure or infographic). At the end of the semester, we did a "class takeover" which was advocating for "social change" (change in some policy) in the class.
Class was boring, nothing serious. Just remember to read the online assignments for the weekly quizzes cuz I always forgot.  No exams at all, just a project and presentation :).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Boring class, pretty much just group work, no final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took HBIO295 but it wasn't an option. She was such an amazing teacher! Picky grader but you start to get a grasp of what she wants. The class is very interactive and interesting and I highly recommend

Be prepared to go into a writing class that is a LOT of work. The last thing I expected was to be learning writing techniques as a senior. However, I found Dr. TJ to be amazing. She knows what she is doing. I would 100% take her again and would recommend everyone to take her. It is hard to do poorly in this class as long as you do everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. TJ was exactly what every senior needs for their final writing class. She made it clear what needed to be done, was accessible outside of class, and made a personal connection with every student. This class is not SUPER easy because it is long writing, but trust their process and you will be rewarded. There is lots of extra credit as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: It is more of a writing class than anything else. None of the homework is helpful for learning or understanding the material, at all. It is all about writing and responding to discussion posts. Your main source of information is the textbook, how lazy. Evolution is my favorite subject and she made me hate every second of this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class is easy, but it's a ton of writing. Lots of discussion boards which is majority of your grade. There is only a final exam, so if you would rather write a lot than take exams I would recommend this class. You can pick and choose what you want to do each week, so class should be an easy 4.0 or 3.5 at least. Book is required for the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class structure is very lenient - you can choose which assignments you want to complete each week. The material is very interesting and the class itself is pretty engaging. Professor TJ herself is very well-versed and is a great professor. STEM profs can be too wrapped up in their research, but she's trained in pedagogy which is really nice.

I had professor Jennifer Lynn Ekstrom during the spring semester of 2025. Her lectures were insanely long, her attitude wasn't the best, and she was extremely nitpicky with the grading. She judged what students ate. She got mad when I mentioned my disordered eating and that "I didn't use the resources provided" and I couldn't because of the wait.

This class was beyond frustrating. There's a huge lack of communication, and dates for exams and such were often inconsistent. If you want to 4.0 the class, you NEED to do all the video lectures, assignments, extra credit, and GO TO THE EXAM REVIEWS AND USE THE PRACTICE EXAMS! If you can, save yourself and take the class in person another semester.

not as bad of a class as everyone makes it seem but it is a ton of work and you need to study for the exams. also DO THE EXTRA CREDIT, that's what helped me get a 3.5 even though I didn't do the best on the exams, exams are in person which is annoying considering its an online class, and don't buy the textbook, i did and it was a waste of money.

I will never be taking one of her classes again. This class has made me hate nutrition more than I ever thought was possible. She doesn't do any of her actual work, the TAs do everything. Exams are actually INSANE. Never received full credit on my discussion posts because she had to press ONE BUTTON. Save yourself the time and effort. Awful class.

Dr. Ekstrom will not respond to your emails, ever. I think she mainly has her TA's do a lot of the work. Don't get me wrong, she's a nice person. However, she expects you to study 100 vocab works and more than 50 learning objectives for just one exam, not even the final.
don't take this class as an elective. text book is unnecessary, quiz every week. doesn't answer emails. a lot of studying involved for it to be considered an elective.

this class is very hard and it requires alot of studying, however a 3.5 is possible if u do all the work and esp the extra credit work which is literally doing the hws before the due dates. do not buy the textbook not needed. they take forever to grade things but thats bcs its a huge class. also exams are in person!
DO NOT TAKE AS AN ELECTIVE!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was fine, pretty standard for an online class. The tests are a bit hard to prepare for because there are so many terms and things to remember. DONT BUY THE TEXTBOOK! I never bought it and it has had no impact on me. The grad TA for the class was extremely rude but that's not her fault so not part of the rating. Overall, just an ok class.

Lots of work to prepare for exams. Easy online work and quizzes every week as well as discussion posts. Exams are majority of points and require a ton of studying. Recommendation: do all possible extra credit assignments and go to the exam review questions. DO NOT TAKE AS AN ELECTIVE!
super hard for a 100 level, if ur not a science major it can be very challenging. exams are 20% 50 mc. discussion posts are long and require so much time. this class can be overwhelming

The ratings on here aren't as bad as it actually is. The exams aren't that hard and they do an exam review before every exam which is suuuper helpful because it covers everything that's gonna be in the exam. There are lots of notes every week but honestly, I could pass the exams by just going to the exam review and making a quizlet from it.

Weekly or biweekly quizzes and discussion posts. Professor is slow to respond to emails, don't expect quick replies. 3.5 or 4.0 is possible with hard studying, exams require memorizing 100+ terms, only 50 are on exam. If you have other demanding courses, the workload can be overwhelming. Book isnt helpful. Time management is key.
This class is a 3 credit course and was by far my hardest do not take this professor.

I think a lot of the negative reviews on here are more so about the class and not so much for the professor. The class is difficult, however a 4.0 is very achievable if you work for it. The only con is that she doesn't respond to emails very quickly. If you do all the homework and study you can easily get a 4.0

There are 3 exams, plus an option final to replace your lowest exam grade. We were provided 4 group study guides for each exam that had over 60 learning objectives and hundreds of terms (exams only had 50 questions). I believe in having to work for a grade, but this class had way too much work for its level. However, a 4.0 is achievable.
Do not take this class, this class is way too much work for a 100 level class, and it's online so its easy to forget about/not care for. This class is not worth it.

I would not wish this class upon anyone. Do not take this class. I got 100% on everything and did the class average on all exams but ended up with such a low grade. I wish she would have specified that the extra credit isn't really EXTRA more just a way to get a DECENT grade.

When I first saw these reviews I promised myself i would see if she's really this bad and come back and write a true review. Everyone is correct. If you plan to take this don't panic it is possible to do well it is just an insane amount of work for a 100 lvl class. Exams cover FAR too much content, she doesn't make the lectures, or grade anything.

I know this was an online class, but 6 hours of work a week is unobtainable. I had over 300 flashcards to memorize for every exam (she doesn't give a study guide, just learning objectives). Lectures are broken up, and not concise. D2L was not organized at all. For multiple weeks we had to watch a documentary on top of lectures. Doesn't answer email
A ton of work for a 100 level class. She also never responds to emails.

I know many reviews make HNF150 sound daunting, and while I don't think the professor is very involved in the class, it's doable. The first exam is a bit of a wake-up call as to how much information is required to be memorized, but chances are if this is a required class for you, that's something you'll have to get good at. Start studying early!

Dr. Ekstrom is not accessible outside of class. You send an email? You will not hear back. There are very few accommodations for anything. The lectures are useless. Lots of busywork. Exams are in person and heavy. I regret taking this class, and that is primarily due to the professor. This should not be labeled an intro/100 level class.

reviews.comment: Is Dr. E nice and personable? 100% She's nice enough and you can tell she is very passionate about biochemistry. However. The sheer amount of content is absurd. You prepare for hours and still run into random hyper specific questions on the exam that you have no idea how to answer. If you have to take BMB 401 I'm so sorry try to take it in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She isn't a rude professor by any means but... avoid taking online BMB401 if you can. I would rather take my engineering exams every class day rather than do these online lectures. They are slow, content heavy, and mind numbingly boring. Exams are open note, but don't expect your notes to help too much, questions rarely align to what your taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have to take this class sorry, if you don't...dont do it

The only grade you get in the class is based off 4 exams you take, that should tell you enough. Each lecture is just notes without any application;shows us how to do math yet never actually teaches us how to do it just gives us the equation. To some this class up, youre going to be teaching most of it to yourself because she isn't that great at it.

reviews.comment: This course has SO much material. Very hard to digest and to navigate throughout the course. Going to office hours is helpful as she provides tips. Is she rude? No. Since this is an online course, it's hard to study. She is very kind

I was warned about the sheer amount of content you need to know for this class but it was still more than I thought. Dr. Hefner's lectures are long and I think she could have explained things way better and in less time. I absolutely DO NOT recommend taking this class with a full-time courseload. Take this during the summer as your only class.
Check exams for errors. I think lectures could have been better organized and topics could have been explained much better than they were. The lectures were very tough to watch in my opinion.
Just glad it's over.

Dr. Hefner is a great professor, and makes amazing lecture videos that are easy to follow, however, this class is TOUGH. It's only graded off four exams, and there is minimal extra credit outside of the ones built into the exam. I would strong urge you to take this over the summer because of how much work needs to be put in, but it is 100% doable

reviews.comment: Every single exam had typos that students had to complain about so that they could be fixed. Also she is slow to respond to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is made up of recorded lectures, which are very disorganized and hard to follow. I avoided watching the lectures and instead just read the annotated slides and notes. Exams are open note but cover so much material that you spend a lot of time just looking for information. Class is doable but you're on your own for learning most of it.

It's a tough class with a LOT of content. The class is graded on 4x 100 point exams, but with the extra credit offered, a 4.0 was about 80%. The content is dense, but all the answers are somewhere on the slides and the tests were open note, plus the notes themselves are guided by focus questions. It takes a lot of bandwidth but not impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ignore these posts from 2024, they are just mad that she changed the exams to lockdown browser and they couldn't cheat anymore. In 2025 she has been very clear and consistent. She tells you exactly how to study and how often. Completely open note exams. I highly recommend typing out notes after writing on slides so you can use ctrl F for exams.
Seems like a very nice person but lectures and exams do not correlate and reads through lectures at light-speed so lecture video times are very misleading.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible professor. Graded on four exams and her lectures are SO boring. It is impossible to stay engaged during them and her exams are 10 times harder than the practice exams. I wish there was another prof option for this course but unfortunately there is not.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course content is dense; it is a difficult course. However, I enjoyed her lectures because she kept them engaging in her creative ways of teaching. She is clear in how she teaches and walked through the many processes in the course step-by-step. She gives mother energy and is very approachable. Would love to have her as a professor again!

Hefner has not responded to e-mails sent in past weeks, even with follow-ups. Constantly seems to be shifting or canceling her office hours due to random things, making it more difficult to access help. Additionally, no TAs are a part of this course, so you have no form of reaching out to anyone other than the professor. Tl;dr, bad communication.

Her exams are open note which is kind of nice if she didnt read off of the slides. I had 65 pages of notes for the first exam and only got a 56 on the exam. The exam questions are harder than her lectures, which are very dumbed down. The course is only graded on 4 exams so getting low scores on exams means a bad grade. DO NOT TAKE

I loved Dr. Hefner and her lectures! Yes the class is challenging and covers a lot of difficult material but, if you actively study, engage with lecture information, and go to her office hours when confused, you will succeed.

Reported grades wrong at the end of summer semester and I had to email the Biochemistry Department and the Dean of Biochemistry and Molecular Genetics to complain. I also emailed the College of Natural Science Dean and complained about incorrect grade reporting. Bad professor, bad exams, only graded on four exams. Messed up and exam and gave us EC
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yo, this class is hard. It's a lot of time and effort that will take a majority of your day. However, Hefner made those mundane tasks like a lecture seem less as hard. Her lectures are like podcasts, they keep you engaged the whole time. And she gives you so much extra practice that you are ready to come test day. The class is hard, but she isn't.

Because of the difficulty of this class Prof Hefner does not get the flowers she deserves. This was probably the hardest class I have taken in my 4 yrs of undergrad but no one could have taught me better than Prof Hefner. Amazing lecture videos that are engaging and easy (as easy as bichem can be) to understand
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Your entire grade is based on 4 exams... so if you're not a great test taker- beware. The exams are very in depth and require you to know basically everything on the 300+ slides for each exam. Highly recommend taking this class in the summer, I can't imagine taking biochem on top of other classes during the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Reported the wrong grade scale to the university, does not know how to use D2L causing our scheduled exam time to be delayed. Lectures are really good. reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I strongly recommend not taking this class in the spring/fall especially if you are taking any other remotely challenging classes, you need to set aside a LOT of time for this class. reviews.comment: Biochem lives up to its infamous reputation. Dr. H was kind and accommodating  any time I reached out with issues or conflicts. Yes, it is a hard class, but she is not a bad professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: this class is so difficult and covers an unreasonable amount of information, but I liked Dr. Hefner. her lectures are the highest quality I've seen from a professor and she's very nice. exams in this class are ridiculous though, you only get an hour and 5 minutes yet you have to read every single word in her lengthy questions

First of all, the exam format is awful, only having which is is false answer or which one is the true answer? Does not help determine our understanding in this course. Second, the grading is so limited towards 4exam scores.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Your grade will consist of four exams, and questions are often meant to confuse or trick you. Lots of material, but the exams are open note. Lectures were good ONLY IF they were made by Dr. Hefner, if they were old videos they were very poorly organized and hard to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall she is a nice professor however the class is designed poorly. The entire grade for this class is given via exams, and there are few ways to actually prep for all (4) exams. The setup of this class is not meant for learning. Hefner calls us lazy, but can't even make new lecture videos to replace the previous professor's lectures. The grading of the fall '23 sections were very disproportionate to the summer '23 sections as the summer class got an incredible amount of extra credit, whereas the fall sections got 5 points.

reviews.comment: This course is difficult, but she does a good job of making it manageable. Your grade is based on 4 exam scores only with 8.5  EC points on every one and they're open note. The lectures can be very long and tedious at times but there's many practice problems to help with studying! Overall, she turned a hard course into a much more enjoyable class
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Terrible. I hate this class so much. Has no respect for students aiming to succeed. Took away extra credit, when the entirety of the grades are based on 4 very challenging exams. DONT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Your only grades in the grade book are 4 exams, with 10 lectures(40min each on avg) in two weeks. She provides a lot of resources and is a great person. My only gripe is the way the exams are formatted. They are a bunch of "which statement is true/false" kind of questions. Causing me to look all over my notes for the right answer with limited time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Hefner is a good professor. This class is just very hard and can sour you on the entire class. I think the class is taught well and the lectures are easy to follow. Grades are exclusively on exams. The professor is very nice during office hours. TAs were helpful as well

Took every chance to make the class awful. Not understanding and very condescending in office hours. If you can't answer her questions in front of the 30 other people in office hours on the spot then she just skips you and better luck next time. Worst class I have ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class was a mess and so disorganized. Barely any of the lectures are hers. She is very condescending and does not care that most of her students don't understand what's going on. I only did well because I watched someone on youtube. It's sad we have teachers like this who use outdated lectures and don't care for their students. Avoid if u can

I honestly thought this class would be different. During the course halfway, we were down to just her. She said she'd step up but failed to do so. Yes, she offered extra credit, but she wasn't even nice enough to round grades. Yes her lectures were better than others, but she abandoned us and failed to help her students when needed the most.

This professor deserves a rating higher than 3.2; her class is tough, but it's a college class, and you can't expect an easy A. If you put in just a little more than the minimum amount of work, you'll be fine. She is a very kind professor who you can tell is passionate about history.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: lectures can be boring sometimes and she sometimes talks very fast so it is hard to keep up. You will not pass if you do not show up. She is a great professor and if you like foreign relations you will love this class. I though the papers were actually kinda fun. The quizees are kinda hard, DO THE READINGS. great professor!

When it comes to lectures, the slides give no information and the lectures are reliant on her talking about what is being discussed. She gives multiple readings, some literally being whole books that are 300 pages. When it comes to writing papers, her criteria is horrible and does not explain anything. Just terrible all around to be honest.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She graded way too hard when her instructions and rubrics were not at all specific. Way too difficult to figure out what she was asking for. A majority of students did an assignment wrong because she lacked the ability to instruct and she gives until the end of the day to redo it. Horrible all the way around

I would take this professor again in a heartbeat. I actually tried to see if she is teaching any other courses that apply to my major and was very upset that she didn't. A lot of reading, but that is expected. Two short group presentations that are very relaxed and both exams were take-home essays. Attendance was not required as long as you read.

Can't believe she doesn't have 5 stars. She was reading-heavy (expected for a 300 class), and her lectures could have been more entertaining, but she's an amazing professor. Due dates and assignments are incredibly reasonable. Genuinely happy to answer any question. In my top 3 for best educators I've had at MSU. Didn't take attendance either!

Professor Conroy-Krutz was extremely knowledgeable and passionate about her class. There was a lot of reading but that is to be expected from a History class. People on here complaining about her lectures want everything handed to them on a silver platter. If you do the readings and listen/participate during lecture, you will learn a lot.

Disagree with most of the reviews on here--she is great! Lectures are engaging, she knows her stuff, and most of the work in the class gets graded relatively easily as long as it's clear that you read the material and learned something from the lectures. She goes fast because there's a lot to cover, but it's not hard to follow or keep up. Big fan!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Respected

reviews.comment: She's an amazing professor! Her power points are a little vague, but all of your grades are from essays that you write, anyway. Lectures are really helpful for writing your essays. You do need to know a fair amount of U.S. history, but this is a 300 level history class, so it's obviously not a blow-off class. I learned so much valuable information.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Her power points are very vague. She talks way to fast for me to take notes and there is no slowing her down because she is alway behind her schedule. She gives a final exam as an in class essay exam in which you have only a commonplace book with quotes, for your notes. STAY AWAY unless you are in need of boring lecture.

This teacher seemed like she expected you to know the material prior to you attending the class. Her notes are just an outline and you literally have to take notes based on what she says in class. She goes too fast and it is really frustrating. She also expects you to read like 4-5 books during the course. STAY AWAY!!!

A very hard grader. If some people in class do not prepare she punishes the whole class by not explaining the materials. The amount of reading is unreasonable. PowerPoint’s are useless.  rambles, very philosophical,taking notes is hard. course is not organized. Responds to emails very late. Doesn’t acknowledge student’s progress and participation.

Katz cares a lot about her students and what they take away from her classes. Second time having her and I'd recommend with my dying breaths tbh. You'll enjoy the class a lot more if you're engaged and participate in discussions, and her study guides make it very easy to excel on the exams given out. Very helpful with papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's a good professor; knows exactly what she's talking about. However, if you plan on doing at least 5-10 hours of reading a week, this would be the class for you. The reading blocks were very excessive (4 days before class, having 30 pages to read. And 2 days in between classes, having 60 pages to read).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Very good and entertaining professor; provides multiple ways to succeed and cares deeply about the students and the topics covered.

Multiple writing assignments handwritten in class, but a very lenient drop policy allows you to miss classes a couple of times. Exams are strictly based on study guides provided (not many surprise questions).
Nice professor willing to help
The lectures help significantly, if you go and actively participate in class it is not only enjoyable but also engaging and easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: She is the best prof ever! so sweet and loves what she does and her students. Lectures are very interesting, and assignments are easy. Would take again 1000x over.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Katz is my favorite professor at MSU. She's kind, funny, and genuinely cares that her students have fun doing philosophy. Her grading is super clear in the syllabus. Make sure you're doing the readings and taking notes. If you can do the basics for this class, you'll be fine. Couldn't recommend her more.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Katz was funny and thorough at the same time. Tests were based entirely on the study guides, so if you fill those out it's incentive to do the readings and be prepared for the tests at the same time. Class itself was easy, though it was more philosophy than anticipated. I enjoyed it a lot, despite wanting more of the sci-fi aspect.

Katz was the best professor I have had so far. She is very passionate about philosophy and is very clear. She manages to be very interactive in such a big lecture. The study guide and the exams are close to identical, so make sure that you stay on top of that and ATTEND CLASS. You definitely won't pass if you don't come to lecture and take notes.

There is a lot of reading to endure in this class if you want to do well, but it's interesting. She goes over the readings the next day & explains it all very well, but if you miss a lecture you have to get notes from someone else as she leaves the slides pretty bare. She provides EC & is easy to reach outside of class & provides great feedback!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She was a very kind professor. Her lectures were very clear, and she made philosophy pretty interesting for a stem major. you can tell she is very passionate about Philosophy, and she's very experienced. Exams are completely based on the study guides, so if you don't get an A that's on you. Loved her class, highly recommend for IAH

For HST 201 our final was a 15 page paper. Prof. Elliott is very nice and caring, she gives great feedback on assignments preparing for the paper. She is very easy to get in contact with and responds to emails pretty quickly. She also made it clear that she is always willing to help and care for her students. Very passionate about her job.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Basically half your grade is one paper, but you spent most of the semester just working on it, so it was ok. Elliott is a great speaker, and the class was very entertaining. She would make us work in groups during class sometimes, which was fine but there were some students that made it suck. Clearly very passionate about Russian history.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Elliot was a very understanding proffessor. She did go through lectures pretty quickly but she does post them at the end of units, but just paying attention helps. There are no tests or quizzes, just 3/4 major writing assignments. She is really timely in replies and you can tell she really enjoys teaching this class. Recitations are also fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: So, shes a little rude, and she goes through notes a lot faster than some people are prepared for. But, Her assignments are very easy and clearly detailed. 4 assignments including the final. Compared to MSU's other ISS 210 course this one is MUCH easier. The other having almost weekly tests and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class was super easy. Lectures are not mandatory at all due to her slides being posted before the lecture. Recitation is mandatory but overall only 2 papers for the whole course and 1 test and the final exam. Super easy would take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 10/10 Professor that I'd recommend to everyone! She's enjoyable and makes her content easy to understand for the class! Her TA, Scott Bullock, is very understanding! As long as you go to lecture, take good notes, go to recitation, and participate you will surely pass with a 4.0!

Professor Elliot lectures every class and then recitation is set up to talk through her lectures and the assigned readings for the week, I found it to be easy because she posts the power points but I would definitely suggest still going to her lectures. There are pop reading quizzes and very few assignments, so try hard and meet the deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Elliott is very knowledgeable and can lecture the full class period. You have to take notes during the presentations as there is nothing written on the slides for you. She does have an accent that can be difficult to listen to for extended time periods. The assignments are reading and essays   and you have to participate in recitations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is a menace. He embarasses students and doesnt put effort into teaching students or making the classroom welcoming. He also does not care about his students especially those who struggle to obtain information or those who are of special needs. If you disagree with him he makes it a huge issue in class
Professor Engram was disrespectful and handled the school shooting awfully. He was often disrespectful to students in class. He has been one of my least favorite professors during my time at MSU.

Dr. Engram was a pretty good professor, The discussion posts are graded are very strictly and he won't tell you your grade until the end of the year. He does offer volunteering for extra credit which was very helpful.

Despite the tragedies Michigan State experienced in February, he remained indifferent: attempting to assign work during the allotted time away from campus, mandating attendance upon return, and violating numerous university policies. Although the nature of this course preaches empathy, his actions fail to embody his teaching.

Dr. Engram weighs discussion posts very heavily and gives you absolutely no idea of your standing in the category until final grades are released and you have no way of changing them. I submitted all but 1 weekly discussion post and somehow received less than a 50% in the category...NOT in line with the syllabus.

At the start of this course, I enjoyed Dr. Engram's. But after a while, I saw that he was extremely difficult, discouraging, and rude. I love the message he speaks on in the class and overall the class material was fine but due to his irrational expectations for students especially after we had all gone through a MASS SHOOTING, it's a no for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Engram is exactly what the kind of professor you fear getting in a course like this. He presents his agenda and is not interested in allowing class discussion on topics causing the class to be silent. He will then take your participation points away. Classic tyrant professor not pleasant to be in his class at all despite interesting topic

This professor is not understanding in the slightest, makes it very difficult to get good grades on things like participation! Take any other ISS class if you don't want to absolutely stress about grades.

I thought a lot of the content he spoke about in class was about his personal opinions not necessarily content from the book. The tests had all content from the book and readings so I was able to study, I just don't agree with his teaching style. I also felt it was hard to give my opinion because if it didn't align with his, it would be a problem.

I wish I could give him a zero. He started screaming at us when we had just returned to campus when we had returned from home because he was reported to the dean after he had tryed to have us take a test 2 days after the shooting. He did not support us students, we tried to express our thoughts and feelings and we were screamed at. Avoid him!!!!!

Though many may have negative things to say after the msu shooting, Dr.Engram is by far one of the professors I respect the most. He is so passionate about what he teaches, encourages students to engage in discussions and wants to help us grow. All of his exams are open note, open book. Eye opening course. Highly recommend.

After the MSU shooting, Dr. Engram displayed a lack of empathy towards the students and did not make any changes to the class syllabus, initially asking the class to take an exam two days after the shooting, also continuing to enforce a strict attendance policy. In class, he also tends to ramble and not provide facts or evidence of the things said

Not a super difficult class, but it is more complicated than it should be because of the D2L layout and instructions for assignments only being located in the syllabus. Pretty much no margin for error on assignments in this class due to tough grading. You really have no idea how you are doing in the class until the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Provided an outdated syllabus so it was SO hard to find information about the class, 5 absences and you were dropped from the course so watch for that. He wasn't as bad as people say about the shooting, he just wasn't lenient. Be prepared to sit through long lectures. 2 papers total in class and the Exams are open note and right off slides.

I love Dr. Engram. Signing up for his class wasn't what I expected it to be, but I was not disappointed. This class challenged me at first. I have never been one to raise my hand and participate in a lecture. Being in this class changed that. I now feel confident to share my input with the class. Every citizen in this country needs to learn this.

After other students and I went through the MSU shooting Prof. Engram showed no empathy at all in any of his emails. At first, he made our exam due 5 days after the shooting and then sent out demanding emails about how we must stay in attendance just the week after the shooting happened. Even before, he had always been very passive-aggressive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: On Feb 13th, there was a mass shooting at MSU and all the students were appalled by this horrific incident. He doesn't care how students feel, refuses to make any amendments to the syllabus, forces them to let student get back to the classroom on the following week, and showed no sympathy at all.
Hours after the school shooting, he told us our exam would still be due in 5 days.

If you like long, lecture-based classes (like myself), this course is great. Enders lectured for at least an hour a day and was accompanied by power point slides, which were later posted online. Don't be mistaken, however- this is a very difficult course. But if you want to learn about the ins and outs of congress, it's worth your time and energy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof was really nice,  but the course layout was not designed for success. Midterm was 30% of the grade, final 35% (cumulative). TopHat was used for lectures/quizzes. While it was nice because I didn't have to go to class, I had to pay for it and I didn't like that. No study guides for the exams and the final covered 472 pages of material. Not easy
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Instead of using iClickers like other teachers, Professor Enders had us buy a tophat subscription which was pretty annoying. Attendance was supposed to be counted, but due to errors with the app, it wasn't. There are online quizzes every other period, but with the app, you can take them online without showing up if you sign in at the same time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Pretty engaging lectures (will need to go and take notes to 4.0). Comprehensive study guides. Great professor.

He is a good professor, he is very passionate about what he is teaching and not to difficult. There was a textbook that was mentioned a little bit but I did not get it and was just fine. The attendance/participation was on iclicker.

Dr. Juenke is my favorite. His lecture slides are sometimes confusing and feel disorganized, but I also am the type of person who color codes everything so that could just be me. Juenke genuinely cares about his students. He remembers names and is extremely approachable. I didn't get a 4.0, but I enjoyed his class a lot: it felt meaningful.

Best Professor I have had so far. The lectures were engaging and he is incredibly nice. I wish I could take this class again or at least have him for another class. Sadly he only teaches this one, so if you end up with him as a Professor be aware that you probably will never see him again when the class is over.

Prof. Juenke did an amazing job maintaining political neutrality - for every Democratic example, he gave a Republican one, and vice versa. His lectures had humor and great examples. Occasionally, the quiz questions were about small details hidden in the lecture, but as long as you pay attention to the hour-ish lecture, you should be fine.

This was a really good class !! He takes IClicker attendance every class but you get 4 drops. there's weekly quizzes but if you pay attention to the lecture slides you'll be fine. There's also a lot of quizlets for the class. Overall great professor, very understanding, I would take his class again !!

Super fun and awesome lectures. I was a Pre dental major then switched to law because of how much he got me interested in the topics. Isn't biased towards either party. If you aren't into politics it's still a very fun class

Amazing Professor, he took the time to explain anything, made assignments clear, made an effort to connect with students, and incorporated real-world events as well as some humor. Had weekly readings and at-home quizzes on the readings and very few other assignments. A very kind and understanding professor I cant recommend him enough.

Dr. Juenke is my favorite professor so far. His class is lecture based and each week there is a short quiz about what we talked about. He is very clear in his teaching and explains things thoroughly. He is entertaining to listen to and clearly cares about all of his students.
